specs.name: LoginRequest
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x54E828], TCP; the port comes from the S2C 0x01 channel entry - the 2009 client has no hardcoded game port). Every Add and the Send load ECX from [0x54E828].

locations.role: SSO command-line parser (WinMain): splits the text after the first '"' at every " -"; argument 1 -> scene+0x48, 2 -> scene+0xCE, 3 -> scene+0x101; each is post-processed by FUN_0048b3d0; returns 0 (launch fails) unless all three are non-empty
ConnectToGameServer: Connect(g_sock_game, ip, port) from the S2C 0x01 channel entry selected by gs+0x15D8/+0x15D9 (entry status must be 3)
server-select window 0x73 ctrl 0xB -> FUN_00440c70 (status of the chosen channel must be 3)
S2C 0x01 handler calls FUN_00440c70 by itself when gs+0x404 != 0 (0x451B5A; set by system window 0x1AE control 5)
FUN_004604c0: init cash-shop object gs+0x754 (copies g_sock_game to +0x20)

FUN_00465770 (2008 analogue: MD5 hex of the account into app+0xD0A); strncmp(scene+0x131, gs+0xD6A, 32) @0x451C5B sets scene+0x21E, which is then forced to 0 (0x451C8E) - nothing of this reaches the wire
Sleep(1000) inside the receive critical section gs+0x368
S2C 0x02 success path: GetDataFromPacket(ulong) -> scene+0x154 (the value this packet echoes on the next login)

specs.grammar:
str[131] sso_account
u32 session_key

fields.name: sso_account
fields.meaning: First launcher (SSO) argument, exactly 0x83 bytes from the 134-byte scene buffer +0x48..+0xCD. LIVE-VERIFIED: the argument's trailing space is kept on the wire; the rest of the buffer is zero (scene is allocated zeroed) so the text is NUL-padded unless it is 131+ chars long. There is no password field any more: the 2009 client never sends the second/third SSO arguments (scene+0xCE, scene+0x101) on the game socket.
fields.dest_or_source: scene+0x48 (scene = [game_state+0x4F0] = [0x54F0C0]); written only by FUN_00440e00 (0x440E6x) from GetCommandLineA

fields.name: session_key
fields.meaning: Value the server returned as the u32 after account_flag_152 in the previous S2C 0x02 success (scene+0x154). On the first login of a process it is whatever scene+0x154 holds initially (0 in practice). LIVE-VERIFIED to be the value the client echoes; the server may use it to resume a session on reconnect / channel change.
fields.dest_or_source: scene+0x154 (Add(ulong) IAT 0x4C70E0); written only by the S2C 0x02 reader @0x4522CD

specs.semantics: Account login on the game socket, sent as the tail of the S2C 0x5A key-exchange handler. Sequence: GetDataFromPacket(i32 key) -> SetCodeKey -> FUN_004604c0 (cash-shop ctx init) -> MD5/strncmp bookkeeping that only touches scene+0x21E (local, forced back to 0) -> Sleep(1000) -> Add(0x01) + 131 bytes of the first SSO argument + u32 scene+0x154 -> Send. No ResetBuffer, no branches between the first Add and the Send. The 2008 account-ID/password pair from the login dialog is gone: authentication is by the launcher token.
specs.trigger: Automatic: every S2C 0x5A received on the game socket. The connect that leads to 0x5A is started by the server-select window 0x73 ctrl 0xB (FUN_00448730 -> FUN_00440c70) or automatically by the S2C 0x01 handler when a server was already chosen; system window 0x1AE control 5 (back to character select: gs+0x404 = 1, the S2C 0x01 handler then reconnects to the same channel by itself at 0x451B69) and control 6 (change channel: server-select window 0x73 opens, gs+0x408 = 1) end in the same connect.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x02 (2009 layout: u8 result; on 1: u32 account_id, u8, u8, i32 manner, u8 account_flag_152, u32 session_key, u8 char_count, 82-byte records, u8 transfer_status; see specs/s2c_carried.json 0x02 as corrected). When gs+0x408 (relogin flag) is set, the client reads only the result byte and immediately sends C2S 0x2B (key 0x452133/0x2B).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Launch requires all three SSO arguments to be non-empty (FUN_00440e00 returns 0 otherwise) and the X-Trap stubs at 0x49F420/0x49F440/0x49F460/0x49F480 (live-verified). The sso_account field is a raw 131-byte copy: a server must split at the first NUL and must NOT trim the trailing space if it compares with the launcher argument. Because of the Sleep(1000) inside the receive critical section the login arrives about 1 s after 0x5A and no other S2C is processed meanwhile. Every extra S2C 0x5A makes the client log in again. The Send argument (1) is not part of the body.
specs.references: Live-verified layout (orchestrator task facts). Compared with 2008 0x44D8BF/0x01 (str[41] account + str[21] password from the login dialog). S2C 0x02 reader for scene+0x154 confirmed at 0x4522BF..0x4522CD.
open_questions: What FUN_0048b3d0 strips from each SSO argument (it removes a marker substring; the live test showed the trailing space survives).
Whether the original server validated session_key or only the SSO token.
specs.verification: Read 2009 decomp FUN_00451960 case 0x5a (lines 4407-4427) and asm 0x451BE3..0x451CE5 (every Add typed by its IAT slot: 0x4C7120 u8, 0x4C7110 char*+len, 0x4C70E0 ulong), the SSO parser FUN_00440e00 (decomp) and the S2C 0x02 reader 0x4522BF..0x4522CD; compared with the 2008 handler 0x44D7CF..0x44D8BF. Layout agrees with the live-verified fact given in the task.
specs.diff_vs_2008: CHANGED: 2008 = str[41] account_id + str[21] password (62 bytes, from login-dialog edits). 2009 = str[131] SSO account token from scene+0x48 + u32 session_key from scene+0x154 (135 bytes); no password on the wire; source is the command line, not a dialog.

specs.name: WhisperChat
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x54E828], port <game port from the S2C 0x01 channel entry; 7022 was the 2008 hardcoded value>)

locations.role: "/message " (compares 6) and "/whisper " (compares 9) -> prefix_len=6 in BOTH cases (client bug)
first-switch case 2: validate and parse the target name into game_state+0x4B0 (17 bytes zeroed, then strncpy of 1..16 chars)
after the send: look the target up in UI window 0x6E (whisper list) and add it via FUN_004461b0 if absent

specs.grammar:
str[17] target_name
u8 msg_len
bytes[msg_len] message

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: Recipient character name, 1..16 chars, NUL-padded to 17 (always NUL-terminated on the normal path). On the whisper-tab path (no /w prefix) it is the previously stored target and can be all zeros if none was ever set.
fields.dest_or_source: game_state+0x4B0 (0x70EEB0(2008)): zeroed at 0x446C09, filled by strncpy at 0x446C96 from the name token after the /w prefix

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Byte count of the message that follows (no NUL counted). Explicit /w: input_length - space_index - 1. Whisper-tab mode: low byte of the full input length.

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Whisper text (EUC-KR/ASCII), not NUL-terminated on the wire.
fields.dest_or_source: EBX = input text + space_index + 1 (explicit /w), or the whole input buffer (whisper-tab mode)

specs.semantics: Private message to one character. After Send the client makes sure the target is in its whisper-history list (UI window 0x6E, FUN_004461b0) and sets the chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]=1, so later plain lines also go as whispers to game_state+0x4B0. The client does not echo the message locally. The echo comes from the server (S2C 0x09).
specs.trigger: The user types "/w name message" (also "/W", "/ㅈ ", "/message ", "/whisper ") and presses Enter, or types a plain line while the chat mode is whisper ([g_ui_root+0x44]==1). Chat macros and the UI 0x294 path reach the same code.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x09 (handler around 0x4511D9(2008)) to the sender: u8 result (0x66 "can not be found.", 0x67 "is rejecting whispers.", 0x65 or a channel number = delivered), then str[17] target, and on success u8 len + text shown as "<To: %s> %s". S2C 0x0A (0x456024) to the recipient: u8, str[17] sender, u8 len, text shown as "<From: %s> %s". The 0x09/0x0A layouts were only skimmed; confirm them with the S2C specs.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Common chat gates first: length>=1; Curse_Engine_Clean ("No cursing please"); manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40; [scene+0xF00]==6. Whisper gates: length > prefix_len, else "/w player_name message"; manner [scene+0xEE0] > -20, else "You can't whisper to others due to your low manner point."; the name ends at the first space within 16 chars, else "Character name must be within 16 characters." or the usage message; at least one byte after the space; target != own name (scene+0x206), else "You can't  send a message to yourself.". Whispers have NO 700 ms anti-spam check (normal and party chat do). QUIRK 1: "/message " and "/whisper " set prefix_len=6, so the name is parsed from index 6 ("/whisper bob hi" -> name "er"). QUIRK 2 (LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION, C35, chat_mail_gm#13): whisper mode with no stored target sends an all-zero 17-byte name but msg_len AND the message ARE present - observed payload 00 x17, 02, "hi" (20 B), not msg_len = 0 as previously documented. The server must still drop a whisper whose target name is empty. QUIRK 3: the whisper-tab path can send an all-zero target name if no target was stored. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.
specs.references: PySlayer has no C2S 0x02 parser but has S2C opcode_0x0A 'Whisper' (u8 1, name17, u8 len, text), which matches the EN 0x0A read order seen here. windslayer_server.py has no 0x02 dispatch branch.
open_questions: Full S2C 0x09 layout (the result codes other than 0x65/0x66/0x67, and whether a channel u32/u8 follows) was not traced here.
Which UI element sets [g_ui_root+0x44]=1 besides a successful /w (for example a chat-tab button). This decides how often the empty-target whisper-tab case can happen.
specs.verification: 2009 sweep (corpus_2009/fingerprint_c2s.py): send 0x4475C7 in FUN_004462e0 (2008 0x445ADD/0x02 in FUN_00444a90, function matched). Opcode Add(s) 0x447588; Add sequence (opcode type first) [u8, str[17], u8, str[?]] is identical to the 2008 builder's. Checked in the 2009 asm corpus (asm/004462E0_FUN_004462e0.asm) against the 2008 builder: the instructions on the opcode-Add -> Send paths are similar but not identical (shape similarity 0.92; field sources or conditions may have moved). locations/at_va: 11 2009 VAs (anchors = the matched Add/Send instructions; other VAs via identical aligned instruction runs of the matched function); 1 of the 2008 locations/at_va could not be placed in 2009 and were dropped: 0x445936 FUN_00444a90: aligned run too short to trust. specs.name: NormalChat
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x54E828], TCP <game port from the S2C 0x01 channel entry; 7022 was the 2008 hardcoded value>). Every Add and the Send at 0x445C66(2008)-0x44790E load ECX from [0x54E828].

locations.role: strncmp(text,"/\xA4\xB1 ",4) (EUC-KR jamo for the a key). Sets type=3, prefix_len=4 and [g_ui_root+0x44]=5 (0x446A37)
First switch case 3. Exact "/a \0" or "/\xA4\xB1 \0" shows "/p message to all" and returns 3 (0x447424). Otherwise sprintf_s(buf61 @esp+0x38, 0x3D, "%s", text+prefix_len) at 0x447287
Modes 0/3/>5: EBX=[esp+0x20] (text). The length stays strlen(buf61)
Final switch case 3 (table 0x445E7C(2008)/idx 0x445E90(2008)). Anti-spam: diff < 0x2BC jumps to 0x447740 "Do not Spam." (timer refreshed, no send). Otherwise [this+0x3E8]=now (0x445C72(2008))
Add(char* EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]): exactly msg_len raw bytes
Send(1) on g_sock_game, then refreshes chat UI windows 9/10 (FUN_00498120) and returns 0
Caller: chat macro slot this+0xE88+i*0x25 (12 slots), len=strlen
Caller: 64-byte stack copy of UI control 0x294 text (sprintf_s 0x40), sets [g_ui_root+0x44]=5 at 0x44D68D, len=strlen

specs.grammar:
u8 msg_len
bytes[msg_len] message

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Chat modes 0, 3 or anything >5: strlen of the prefix-stripped text, <= 60. Chat mode 5 ("All" tab, forced by a "/a " or "/ㅁ " prefix and by the 0x294 caller): low byte of strlen of the ORIGINAL input including the prefix. The two values are equal for a plain line of <= 60 bytes with no prefix.
fields.dest_or_source: stack byte [esp+0x18], set at 0x4458E2(2008) (strlen) or 0x445A61(2008) (mode 5, from arg2)

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Chat text (ASCII/EUC-KR), no NUL terminator on the wire in the normal case. In mode 5 with a prefix, the buffer holds the stripped text, then its NUL, then the rest of the original input, so the real message ends at the first 0x00. Example: "/a hi" -> 03 05 68 69 00 68 69.
fields.dest_or_source: EBX = the caller's text buffer after the in-place strcpy of the sprintf_s(61) result

specs.semantics: Public (area/all) chat line. The client strips a "/a " or "/\xA4\xB1 " prefix (and switches chat mode to 5) or takes the line as is, runs sprintf_s(61,"%s",text+prefix_len), copies the result back over the input, then routes by chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]. Mode 1 becomes whisper opcode 0x02 (send site 0x4475C7), mode 2 becomes party 0x6A (0x4476CB), and mode 4 becomes the friends path (0x4476D6, not this send site). Modes 0, 3, >5 and 5 reach this send, with the length rules above. After the 700 ms anti-spam check the client sends u8 len + raw bytes, then refreshes chat windows 9/10. There is no local echo; the line appears only when the server broadcasts S2C 0x16. Lines starting with '/' that are not client commands (for example "/heart") are sent as ordinary chat. Live capture "hi" -> 03 02 68 69 matches.
specs.trigger: The player presses Enter in the chat box (FUN_00446200). Also a chat macro hotkey (FUN_0043dde0, GetAsyncKeyState, 12 slots of 37 B at this+0xE88) and UI list control 0x294 in FUN_00448730 (0x44D6B3, forces mode 5). Chat-tab buttons in FUN_00448730 set the mode: 0x448A9E(2008)=1, 0x448B04(2008)=2 (after a party check), 0x448B64(2008)=4, 0x448BC5(2008)=5.
specs.expected_response: Server broadcast S2C 0x16 (handler 0x456800). It reads str[17] name first (0x45681D), then u8 len (0x456834), then str[len] into a 61-byte stack buffer (0x456874). It then checks text[0]=='/' for emotes like "/heart" and formats "%s : %s" (0x456A16). The client waits for nothing specific.
specs.gates_and_hazards: length arg > 0. Curse_Engine_Clean passes, else "No cursing please" (return -1). Manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40, else "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point." [scene+0xF00]==6, else a silent return. A GM ([scene+0x970]+0x12==1) matching a GM command sends a GM opcode (e.g. 0x06) instead. An exact "/a " or "/ㅁ " shows "/p message to all" and returns 3, so the IME text is kept. Anti-spam: a line within 700 ms of the last chat shows "Do not Spam." and refreshes the timer. The strstr for EUC-KR B0 AD C1 F8 C2 AF toggles game_state+0x404 locally with no wire effect. Client-side hazard: sprintf_s(61) at 0x447287 does NOT truncate (real CRT sprintf_s). A stripped text over 60 bytes calls the CRT invalid-parameter handler, likely a client abort. Server hazards: in mode 5, msg_len can include a 0x00 and leftover bytes, so cut at the first NUL. An S2C 0x16 with len > 61 overflows the receiver's stack buffer. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire grammar, u8 msg_len + bytes[msg_len] with opcode 0x03, and the asm confirms it. 0x4478E6 Add(u8 [esp+0x10]=3), 0x4478F3 Add(u8 [esp+0x18]), 0x447900 Add(EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]), 0x44790E Send(1), all on [0x54E828]. Both length rules are correct: mode 5 (0x445A54(2008)/0x445A61(2008)) uses the low byte of arg2 [esp+0x21C], and all three callers pass strlen of the original text (0x44622D, 0x43DE71, 0x44D6AB); otherwise strlen of the case-3 result is used (0x4458E2(2008)). A's example "/a hi" -> 03 05 68 69 00 68 69 is right, because the "/a " prefix always forces mode 5 (0x446A0A). On mode routing, B was complete (0, 3 and >5 all keep strlen: JZ 0x44544D(2008), JA 0x445459(2008), table 0x445E68(2008) entry 3 -> 0x44754D), while A's "0/3" left out >5. On the 60-byte cap, A was right: 0x4AC54D is real sprintf_s (-> __vsprintf_s_l) and does not truncate, so B's "truncated to 60" is wrong. The chat-tab writers of [g_ui_root+0x44] are 0x448A9E(2008) (1), 0x448B04(2008) (2), 0x448B64(2008) (4), 0x448BC5(2008) (5) and 0x44D68D (5); no writer of 0 or 3 was found. Both analysts were right that our server's 0x16 echo is misaligned: windslayer_server.py _handle_chat builds u8 0x01 + name17 + len + text, but the EN handler's first read (0x45681D) is char[17], so the leading 0x01 must be removed. PySlayer parse_0x03 (payload[1]=len, text follows) agrees with this spec. Our server's NUL-split parse happens to cope with the mode-5 tail.
open_questions: Initial value of chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44] after login (0 vs 5). It does not change the wire format, only whether msg_len counts the original length (they differ only for prefixed or >60-byte lines).
Is a custom CRT invalid-parameter handler installed? None was found, so a >60-byte stripped line probably aborts the client before sending.

specs.name: InputState_Loopback

locations.role: FUN_0042c310 (keyboard sampling, run only when scene+0xF00 is 4 or 6) writes scene+0x254/0x255 before the builder runs
FUN_0042e790 recomputes scene+0x257 (clears it at 0x42EB0E, sets 1..5 at 0x430B16-0x430EEE) before the builder runs
after the 0x04 loopback: CMP scene+0xF24,0; the 0x03 block runs only for non-hosts
Add u8 0x03 via CALL EDI (EDI=[0x4C7120] loaded at 0x424887)
Add u8 (byte scene+0x255 * 10 via IMUL CL) + byte scene+0x254
SendTo("127.0.0.1", port=[scene+0x244], reset=1) via CALL EBP (EBP=[0x4C7130] from 0x423779(2008))
receiver FUN_00424ae0 (from FUN_0045e230 case 3) decodes the input bytes

specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 input_a
u8 input_b

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Local player uid (account_id from S2C 0x02). The receiver looks up the entity with +0x84 == uid and +0x98 in {1,3}.

fields.name: input_a
fields.meaning:
(action*10 + dir) & 0xFF, computed with 8-bit IMUL.
- dir = scene+0x254. 8 = no horizontal input (reset every tick). FUN_0042c310 sets 2 when only key app+0xDE0 is held and 6 when only key app+0xDE4 is held; dash also uses 2/6.
- action = scene+0x255:
  - 0 = none
  - 1 = key app+0xDF4 (gated by FUN_0041d8a0 ammo/MP)
  - 2 = key app+0xDF0
  - 3 = key app+0xDE8
  - 4 = key app+0xDEC
  - 5 = key app+0xDF8 (gated)
  - 6 = double-tap dash (FUN_004281b0(0x50))
  - 7 = skill cast, set by the S2C skill-use confirmation; sticky until acknowledged.
The receiver writes action = a/10 to entity+0x8B4 and dir = a%10 to entity+0x8B3, and sets +0x15DC=1 if a != 8.

fields.name: input_b
fields.meaning:
(skill_variant*10 + status_code) & 0xFF.
- skill_variant = scene+0x256 (1..11 for action 7; cleared with 0x255).
- status_code = scene+0x257 (0..5): a local-player effect class recomputed each tick by FUN_0042e790, e.g. 1 for effect ids 0x192-0x19C, 2 for 0x8C6-0x8D0 / 0x908-0x912, 3 for 0x934-0x93E, 4 for 0xA10-0xA1A, 5 for 0x9D9-0x9E3. The builder never resets it.
The receiver writes b/10 to entity+0x8B5 and b%10 to entity+0x8B6.

specs.semantics:
The local player's input state, sent to the client's own socket every tick in normal maps, right after the 0x04 loopback snapshot (seq = snapshot seq + 1).

Destination: 127.0.0.1 : scene+0x244 (= 42907).

Conditions:
- scene+0xF90 != NULL and scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6.
- mode [scene+0xF88]+0x70 == 0.
- scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in EN).
- The local player pointer scene+0x970 is NOT checked on this path, so it is also sent at character select.

After the send, dir resets to 8. Action and variant reset to 0 unless action == 7, which stays until a received snapshot shows the local entity with action code 0x17..0x21 (FUN_0045e230 0x458CAx clears scene+0x255/0x256).

Receiver: FUN_0045e230 case 3 -> FUN_00424ae0(uid, a, b, src_ip, src_port). It finds the entity with uid match and +0x98 in {1,3}, stores the decoded digits in +0x8B3..+0x8B6 and +0x88 = scene+0xF1C. When the receiver is a host (never in EN) it also records src_ip/src_port in entity+0x6A/+0x80 and sets +0x14EA=1. If the receiver is in room phase 2, or phase 1 with F1C < 5100, actions 1/5/7 and input_b are zeroed.

Framing: 8-byte Fireway header (len|0x800|seq<<12; seq is the shared per-socket counter at CSNSocket+0x13A8, wrapping 255->0) plus the EncodebyArray checksum. The payload is XORed with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]. reset=1.
specs.trigger: Every FrameMove tick in map mode 0 (after the 0x04 loopback at 0x423787(2008)).
specs.expected_response: None. It is consumed locally by FUN_0045e230 case 3.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Loopback only. Do not bind UDP 42907 on the client PC.
- In the local field the player entity is usually +0x98==4, so the self-receive lookup (which needs +0x98 in {1,3}) usually finds nothing and the datagram is a no-op. It still consumes a sequence number.
- Byte math is modulo 256, but the maximum 7*10+8 = 78 and 11*10+5 = 115 fit.

fields.name: input_a

specs.semantics:
Input/keep-alive datagram from a non-host room participant to the room's UDP host. This is the only UDP traffic a non-host client produces in room maps; no snapshot is built.

Destination: IP string scene+0xF38 (host_ip from S2C 0x2F; SendTo uses inet_addr with gethostbyname fallback). The port is (u16 scene+0xF48 room_no + 10000) & 0xFFFF, passed through htons. scene+0xF48 is also written by the room-join UI at 0x44B8F5..0x44D79B.

Conditions:
- scene+0xF90 != NULL.
- scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6.
- mode [scene+0xF88]+0x70 != 0 (arena/team-battle maps; the map XML mode attribute).
- scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in EN).
- scene+0x970 != NULL.
- At least one of:
  - (a) local entity +0x98 == 3 (player-type entity, as created by room/player spawn packets). The datagram is then sent EVERY tick (at most every 30 ms).
  - (b) scene+0xF08 == 0: no room snapshot 0x07/0x08/0x09 accepted since S2C 0x2F reset it, so it is sent every tick until the host answers.
  - (c) scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C > 9000 ms: keep-alive. F20 is the previous tick's time; F0C is stamped on each send and by S2C 0x2F.

Input bytes are cleared at the end of every tick even when nothing is sent (dir=8; action/variant=0 unless action==7).

On the host side FUN_00424ae0 uses the datagram's source ip:port to register the peer (entity+0x6A/+0x80, +0x14EA=1) and stores the input digits in entity+0x8B3..0x8B6.

Framing: 8-byte Fireway header (len|0x800|seq<<12; shared per-socket seq at CSNSocket+0x13A8, wrapping 255->0) plus the EncodebyArray checksum/XOR (cencmsg.encode_by_array). reset=1.
specs.trigger: FrameMove tick in a room map (mode != 0) after S2C 0x2F provided host_ip/room_no, subject to the state/F08/9 s conditions above.
specs.expected_response: The room host must send UDP snapshots to the client's g_sock_map, i.e. the source address of this datagram, normally port 42907. Accepted opcodes are 0x07/0x08/0x09 (mode 1 only; header+records, the same layout as 0x04). They must carry map_code == the client's map+0x1B8. Each accepted snapshot increments scene+0xF08, which drops the 0x03 rate to the 9 s keep-alive unless the local entity is +0x98==3. HP/MP datagrams 0x06/0x0B/0x0A/0x10 are also accepted.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- No EN 2008 client can be the host (scene+0xF24 is never set), and every client binds 42907, not room_no+10000. A private server supporting arenas must therefore itself listen on UDP host_ip:(room_no+10000) and act as the host.
- host_ip must be NUL-terminated within 16 bytes. An unresolvable name makes inet_addr and gethostbyname fail; sendto then targets 255.255.255.255 without SO_BROADCAST, and the send fails silently.
- room_no + 10000 is truncated to 16 bits.
- If the local entity is +0x98==3, the flood is continuous (~33/s) regardless of host replies.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x2F: host_ip (scene+0xF38) and room_no (scene+0xF48) are described as 'Non-host peers later send UDP to this IP on port room_no+10000 (FUN_00424500 @0x4236E8(2008))'. PROTOCOL.md C2S 0x0D: 'Not sent in P2P room mode ([map]+0x70 == 1)'. The receiver's host-registration logic is FUN_00424ae0 at 0x424AE0-0x423A04(2008).
open_questions: Whether the original service ran a UDP room host/relay on host_ip:(room_no+10000), and which address it replied to. The client accepts snapshots from any source address.
Whether the original host sent 0x07/0x08/0x09 to the recvfrom source port or to the TCP-reported p2p_udp_port (42907). These differ only behind NAT.

specs.name: KeepAlive
specs.semantics: Periodic heartbeat that keeps the game connection alive. The payload is empty and the client expects nothing back.
specs.trigger: Win32 timer id 6, repeating every 240000 ms (4 min). The S2C 0x03 (enter world / map info) handler arms it and re-arms it (resetting the interval) on every 0x03, i.e. on every map load. It is killed on logout-to-server-select and on app cleanup.

specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate beyond the timer being active (sent inside the app critical section, whatever the UI state). Do NOT reply with S2C 0x05: per project notes that resets in-game state and kicks the client. The server may use the absence of 0x05 for more than about 4 minutes (plus slack) as an idle/dead-connection signal.
specs.references: Our server _dispatch: 0x05 consumed with no reply ('client heartbeat ~4 min'), which matches the 240000 ms timer. PySlayer has no C2S 0x05 parser.

specs.semantics: GM chat command "/manner <name> <points>" typed into chat (or a chat macro). Asks the server to change the named character's manner points by the signed amount (manner points are the value at scene+0xEE0 that blocks chat/whisper/trade/room use when low). Client does nothing locally besides clearing the chat input (function returns 0).
specs.trigger: GM (local entity word +0x12 == 1) submits chat text starting with "/manner " and longer than 8 chars, with a non-empty name token and a non-zero integer second token.
specs.expected_response: None awaited; fire-and-forget. No client-side follow-up state.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates in order: strlen>=1; ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text) must pass (else "No cursing please"); scene+0xEE0 (own manner points) > -40 (else "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point."); scene+0xF00 == 6 (else return, nothing sent); word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1 (GM flag of local player entity, filled by the u16 read at 0x4536A5 in S2C 0x07) else the text goes to normal chat parsing at 0x4469BB; strlen > 8. Hazards: name token > 16 chars overflows the 17-byte stack buffer; the i32 local [esp+0x20] is NOT initialized on this path, so if the second token is not a number sscanf leaves stack garbage and it is sent if non-zero. Offset of the second sscanf assumes exactly one space after the name.

specs.length: 2 + (L - 8), where L = strlen of the typed line (the caller-supplied length). Total body with the opcode is L - 5 bytes.

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: GM command selector, constant 0x01 = notice/announcement. Related sites in the same function: 0x0A = /manner (site #15, 0x446482), 0x00 = /업데이트 'update' (site #16, 0x4464DF)

fields.meaning: (L - 8) & 0xFF, the number of text bytes that follow
fields.dest_or_source: MOVZX ECX,BL; SUB CL,8; PUSH ECX at 0x44651D-0x446523 (EBX = caller-supplied strlen)

fields.name: notice_text
fields.meaning: The raw line starting at byte index 8, right after the full '/notice ' prefix, with no NUL terminator and possibly CP949 multibyte text: '/notice hello' sends 'hello' (5 bytes). The 2008 client compared only '/not' and skipped 4 bytes, so it sent 'ice hello'.
fields.dest_or_source: ADD EBX,-8; PUSH EBX (N); ADD EBP,8; PUSH EBP (src = text+8) at 0x446532-0x446539

specs.semantics: A GM asks for a server-wide announcement. The client sends [06 01 len text...] and returns 0, which makes the chat-submit caller clear the input line. The client shows nothing locally. The server should broadcast the text as a system notice. The client has an '[Announcement] ' string at 0x6F5710(2008) for display, but this spec does not identify which S2C packet carries it.
specs.trigger: A GM (the 2008 gate was the flag word ==1 at [[scene+0x970]+0x12]; not re-derived for 2009) submits a chat or macro line that starts with the full 8 bytes '/notice ' (strncmp(text, '/notice ', 8) at 0x4464EE, string at 0x52BAC0) and is longer than 8 (CMP EBX,8 at 0x4464FA). The /manner and /update checks come first in 2008 (order not re-verified for 2009).
specs.expected_response: None awaited. The server presumably broadcasts an announcement S2C to all players (opcode not determined here).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates, in order: L > 0 (signed); Curse_Engine_Clean(text) passes, so the notice text itself is profanity-filtered (on failure 'No cursing please' and nothing is sent); manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40; [scene+0xF00] == 6; GM word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1; not '/manner ' (8-byte strncmp); not exactly '/업데이트' (10-byte compare including NUL); strncmp(text,'/notice ',4)==0; L > 4 (unsigned JBE). Server hazards: (1) payload keeps the 'ice ' leftover when the full '/notice ' is typed, so strip it if wanted; (2) the prefix is u8 but the appended count is the full L-4. If L-4 >= 256 the prefix would wrap and a server trusting it would desync. Macro callers (L<=36) and the sprintf caller (L<=63) cannot reach that. The IME chat buffer limit was not measured, so a server should read the rest of the packet body rather than trust text_len.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: No real dispute on the wire format. Analyst A (decomp+asm) and Analyst B (asm only) gave the same grammar (u8 sub-command 0x01, u8 length (L-4), then L-4 raw bytes from text+4), the same socket (g_sock_game) and the same gates. The signatures 'u8 u8 bytes[text_len]' and 'u8 u8 bytes[msg_len]' differ only in names. The asm confirms both: 0x4464EE strncmp(EBP,"/notice ",4); 0x4464FA CMP EBX,4 / 0x4464FD JBE; 0x44650F PUSH 6 / 0x446511 Add(u8); 0x446519 PUSH 1 / 0x44651B Add(u8); 0x44651D MOVZX EAX,BL, 0x446520 SUB AL,4, 0x44652A Add(u8); 0x446532 ADD EBX,-4, 0x446535 PUSH EBX, 0x446536 ADD EBP,4, 0x446539 PUSH EBP, 0x44653A Add(char*,N) via IAT 0x4C7110; 0x446548 Send(1) with ECX=[0x54E828]. Their examples also agree: A's '/nothello'->'hello' and B's '/not hello'->' hello' both follow from the 4-byte compare and 4-byte skip. A left the sub-command, length and text Adds out of locations; B listed them. I also resolved B's open question on the length wrap as far as statics allow: EBX is the caller's strlen (0x44622D, 0x43DE71, 0x44D6AB), the macro and sprintf callers are bounded at 36 and 63, and only the IME chat buffer bound is still unknown. Other references: the 0x06 opcode is a GM command family in this function (06 0A <17-byte name> i32 = /manner at site #15; 06 00 = /업데이트 at site #16; 06 01 = notice). PySlayer has no client_packets parser for 0x06, and our server (windslayer_server.py) has no handling of C2S 0x06.
open_questions: Maximum length of the IME chat buffer ([0x54E840]+0x104), which decides whether text_len can wrap past 255 for typed input. Macro and sprintf callers cannot.
Whether the original server stripped the 'ice ' leftover or GMs typed '/not <text>'. The 4-byte compare of an 8-byte literal looks like a leftover from a Korean command string.
Which S2C opcode the server used to broadcast the announcement (the '[Announcement] ' prefix at 0x6F5710(2008)).

fields.name: realtime_delta_ms
fields.meaning: Real-time (timeGetTime) milliseconds covering the last 10 sends. A counter at scene+0x978 goes up by 1 per send; when it reaches 10 at send time this is now minus scene+0x974 and the counter resets. Otherwise it is 0, including the first packet. Probably a speed-hack check.

fields.name: map_code
fields.dest_or_source: [[0x70EED8(2008)]+0x1B8], low 16 bits of the map object's u32
fields.meaning: Current map code (map loader FUN_00407800 @0x407BA3 computes a + b*100 from the map file name, e.g. 101). The capture shows 0x0065 = 101.

fields.name: logic_elapsed_ms
fields.meaning: Logic-clock ms since the last 0x0D send. scene+0xF1C goes up by 30 each logic frame (0x417E23(2008)), so the value is a multiple of 30 (capture: 30). scene+0x24C is set to scene+0xF1C after each send (0x42E716).

fields.name: state_lo
fields.meaning: Packed input/state bits. Bits 0-1: player+0x8B3 (01 = value 2, left; 10 = value 6, right; 00 = other, 8 = none). Bits 2-4: player+0x8B4&7 (vertical/jump input; 4 = Up). Bits 5-8: player+0x8B5&0xF. Bits 9-11: player+0x8B6&7. Bits 12-15: player+0x94C&0xF (action_event). Bits 16-19: player+0x950&0xF (interact_event). Bits 20-21: player+0x8D0 (01 = 2, 10 = 6, 00 = other). Bits 22-31 are never written and hold stale scratch bytes (scene+0xEF8 is reused as the parse buffer by the S2C 0x1B/0x2A handlers), so they are garbage.

fields.name: state_hi
fields.meaning: Bits 0-11: player+0x958&0xFFF (a timer; 600 is set on the target at 0x4184A8). Bits 12-31 are stale garbage.

fields.name: event_source_uid
fields.meaning: UID of the entity tied to the action event (e.g. the item-hit path writes the thrower's uid into the victim's +0xD80 at 0x4184A2). Present only if player+0x94C != 0.

fields.name: f64_1338
fields.meaning: Action parameter double (x-like). Unknown meaning; compared against in FUN_00414210. Present only if 0x8B6==4 and 0x94C is 9 or 7.

fields.name: f64_1340
fields.meaning: Action parameter double (y-like), same condition as f64_1338.

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: UID of the entity this player interacted with (0x418496: the other entity's +0x84). Present only if player+0x950 != 0.

fields.name: pos_x
fields.meaning: Local player world X. Sent ONLY inside the interact_event block. Ordinary movement packets carry no position.

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: Local player world Y (interact_event block only).

fields.name: target_dx
fields.meaning: target.x - self.x (computed at 0x4184B2).

fields.name: target_dy
fields.meaning: target.y - self.y (computed at 0x4184C4).

fields.name: flag_8db
fields.meaning: Copied from target+0x8DA in the item-hit path (0x4184D6). Meaning unknown.

fields.name: flag_8e7
fields.meaning: Flag: 0 in the item-hit path (0x4184DE), 1 in other paths (0x417178). Meaning unknown.

fields.name: timer_dac
fields.meaning: A per-entity counter that goes up by 30 per frame (0x416450(2008)) and is handed between entities on contact. Meaning unknown.

fields.name: target_action_event
fields.meaning: The target's +0x94C (action event) captured at interaction time (0x4184F6).

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Only when interact_event == 0xC (thrown-item/projectile hit, item word from the record checked against 0xA31..0xA3B at 0x4182B6). The item id that hit.

specs.semantics: The local player's input/state sync. The client sends its current input bytes and event state plus the logic time elapsed since the last send; remote clients simulate the movement from these. Position is included only in the interaction-event block. No state is changed from the server side. On the client, after sending, scene+0x24C = scene+0xF1C; the previous-input snapshot (player+0x8B7..0x8BA = 0x8B3..0x8B6) is updated every tick whether or not a packet is sent. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C12, world_movement_npc#00/#01 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): (a) For the LOCAL player a bad (IP-octet) seed in the spawn record does NOT produce a ~28-packet stream: the client resets +0x8B3/+0x8B4/+0x8B5/+0x904 from real input immediately, and only +0x8B6 = 1 survives ~1.5 s after a map-change 0x07 (7 non-idle sends). After a spawn the client emits a burst of about 5 idle 0x0D, so a server sanity check should allow <= 5, not <= 2. The idle-default rule still matters for the REMOTE records in S2C 0x04/0x05/0x07 and for 0x1A. (b) A basic melee swing is lo bits 2-4 (+0x8B4) = 1 with +0x904 = 4 - NOT an action_event: +0x94C stays 0 for a plain attack, so the 22-byte event_source_uid form is never produced by one. +0x8B4 values: 0 idle, 1 basic attack, 3 jump, 4 down/portal/drop-through. Bits 20-21 (+0x8D0) and hi bits 0-11 (+0x958) are live during jumps. (c) The interact tail for interact_event 0xC is confirmed at 45 bytes: u32 target_uid, f64 pos_x, f64 pos_y, f64 dx, f64 dy, bool, bool, u32 timer, u8 action_event (= 9), u16 item_id.
specs.trigger: Checked every 30 ms logic tick from FUN_0042c920 (possibly several times per rendered frame during catch-up), when scene+0xF00 == 6 (in world), [0x70EED8(2008)]+0x70 == 0 (not a P2P room), and player (scene+0x970) != 0. (1) Sends at once if any of player+0x8B3..0x8B6 changed since the last tick, or player+0x950 != 0, or player+0x94C != 0 (also sets scene+0x250 = 1). (2) Otherwise nothing if logic_elapsed < 210 ms. (3) If not idle (idle means 0x904 == 8, 0x8B3 == 8, and 0x8B4, 0x8B5, 0x8B6 all 0), sets scene+0x250 = 1 and sends about every 210 ms. (4) If idle and scene+0x250 != 0, clears it and sends one final packet. (5) If idle otherwise, sends only when logic_elapsed >= 15000 (keepalive).
specs.expected_response: Nothing to the sender. It must NOT be echoed back: echoing desynced the cipher, per memory. For multiplayer the server should relay to other players on the map as S2C 0x1B (handler 0x45712B: u32 uid, u32, bytes[8] state, if(ae) u32, if(vb==4 && ae in {9,7}) f64 f64, if(ie) f64 f64). The 0x1B conditional tail is NOT the same as 0x0D's, so the relay must re-encode rather than copy the bytes.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Variable length: the server must parse the conditional tails using bits of the packet itself. The client tests the full ints (player+0x94C, +0x950, byte +0x8B6), but the packet carries only 4/4/3 bits of them. The equivalence holds only if those values fit (all observed writers use values <= 0xD). The upper 10 bits of state_lo and upper 20 bits of state_hi are stale garbage and must be ignored (capture: 53 40 / 60 64 75). Not sent in P2P room mode ([map]+0x70 == 1), which appears to use a UDP path instead (FUN_0042dcf0, not traced).
specs.references: Capture '00 00 00 00 65 00 1E 00 00 00 00 02 40 53 00 60 64 75' decodes exactly: realtime_delta 0, map 101, elapsed 30, state_lo 0x53400200 (0x8B6=1, other fields 0, garbage high bits), state_hi 0x75646000 (0x958&0xFFF = 0), 18 bytes, no tails. PySlayer parse_0D agrees on offsets (payload[5:7] u16 'sub_opcode' = map code; payload[7:9] == 0xD2 = elapsed 210; keycode payload[0x0B] = first state byte). Our server's _handle_world_sync docstring wrongly says the payload 'begins with two f64 world coords': positions appear only in the interact_event tail. The memory atlas note calling 0x0D a 'heartbeat' is wrong (it is S2C 0x0D in sub_handler_3, a different message).
open_questions: Exact meaning of player+0x8B4/0x8B5/0x8B6/0x8D0 values and of action_event (0x94C, values 1..13 seen) and interact_event (0x950, values 1, 9, 0xB, 0xC seen).
Meaning of f64_1338/f64_1340, flag_8db, flag_8e7, timer_dac; appears related to item/PvP contact mechanics.
Meaning of the second u32 in the S2C 0x1B relay (probably logic_elapsed_ms) and whether the relay should carry the 0x0D realtime_delta.
Whether scene+0xF1C can be resynced by the server (FUN_0042dbf0 writes it at 0x42DC58), which would affect logic_elapsed.

Which action actually produces the 22-byte event_source_uid tail? Live (world_movement_npc#00) proved +0x94C stays 0 for a basic attack, so the tail must come from skills or grabs; the 45-byte interact-0xC tail is already confirmed.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to equip the bag item <item_id> with its stone list. Sending changes no client state. The equip is applied when the server sends S2C 0x1D (u32 uid, u16 item, u8 n, u16[n], u16; handler 0x45804E writes equip grid entity+0x13C/+0x16E and recomposes the sprite). The bag entry is removed by a bag-remove packet (our server uses S2C 0x23). Live capture matches: double-clicking Wooden Stick 179 sent 'B3 00 00 00 00' = item 179, stone_count 0, extra 0.
specs.trigger: Double-clicking/activating an equipment item in the inventory window (window 9) with no NPC-shop/storage/stall context active. Also pressing a quick-slot hotkey (or HUD quick-slot button) that holds an equipment item, at most once per 1000 ms per slot.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x1D equip (same body layout prefixed by u32 uid) plus a bag removal (0x23). Also error chat on failure (server-defined).
specs.gates_and_hazards: All client-side, each showing a message and not sending on failure. scene+0x970 local entity non-null (silent). def+0x1D4 gender: ==1 requires scene+0x130 != 0 and ==2 requires scene+0x130 == 0, else 'You can not equip other gender's item.'. scene+0x979 (level byte) >= def+0x1D8 (Lv), else 'You need higher level'. entity+0x904 not in {1,4,0xE,0xF} and < 0x18, entity+0x15B4 not in {1,4,0xE,0xF} and < 0x18, and scene+0x258 (pending skill) == 0, else 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.'. def+0x168+entity.class(+0x110)*4 (Job[class]) != 0 or def+0x168 (Job[0]) != 0, else 'You can't equip other class items.'. Hazard: an unanswered C2S 0x15 skill leaves scene+0x258 set and blocks this packet permanently. The quick-slot path updates its 1000 ms timestamp even when a gate rejects.
specs.references: This is the only 0x0F send site in the client. Our server's _handle_equip_item reads only u16 item_id and ignores stone_count/stones/extra. That is safe for parsing but loses stone data, and its 0x1D reply does not echo stones. The docstring 'u16 item [, u8, u16]' is correct only for stone_count == 0. PySlayer parse_0F has the same n==0-only layout and wrongly asserts payload[0]==0x0D. It matches the captured 5-byte payload.

specs.expected_response: Most likely S2C 0x1E (handler 0x458E07, shared with 0x24): u32 uid, u16 item_id, u8 n, n x u16 enchant, u16 enchant_last. It calls 0x427F00 to clear the entity's equip slot (+0x13C / +0x16E), recomposes the sprite (0x4282C0) and, for the local player (uid == scene+0x220) with opcode 0x1E and bag capacity byte scene+0x3A9 <= 45, puts the item back in the bag with its attribute words. Our server's own notes also call 0x1E the remove/unequip opcode.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks, in order: (1) slot index - 3 <= 0x18; (2) bag capacity byte char+0x361 (char = ctx+0x18 = scene+0x48) <= 45 AND at least one empty word in bag[0..cap) at char+0x380 (0x4261F0), otherwise a modal notice 'You have no more slots for the item.' (0x49EBC0) and no packet; (3) 0x470C70 and 0x470C90 abort (no message) when ctx+0 == 0x259 and ctx+0x20 or ctx+0x1C is set (a special UI mode, probably a personal shop); (4) 0x470850 finds the selected Equipment record and its catalog entry; (5) the local player entity (char+0x928) has action state +0x904 not in {1,4,14,15} and < 24, the same for +0x15B4 (4 = attacking), and word scene+0x258 == 0; otherwise chat notice 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.' (0x495E30) and no packet; (6) catalog type +0x154 == 1 (equipment), otherwise nothing. No local pending state: double-clicking again before the server answers sends another 0x11, so the server must check the item is still equipped.
specs.references: Captured C2S 0x0F equip 'B3 00 00 00 00' (u16 179, u8 n=0, u16 0) confirms this shared shape (builder 0x44FE20 uses the same loop, reading from rec+2). PySlayer parse_0F reads a fixed u16,u8,u16 and ignores the n-word loop; PySlayer has no 0x11 parser. Our server: _dispatch has no inbound 0x11. Its _build_en_opcode_1D_equip docstring states '0x1E is the REMOVE/unequip opcode', which matches the expected response. Do not confuse this with the server-notes '0x11 + account_id' UDP broadcast on the map/tertiary socket: that is a different message on a different socket.

specs.length: 4 (payload after the opcode). The datagram is 13 bytes on the wire: 8-byte Fireway header + opcode + u32.

fields.name: account_id
fields.meaning: Local account/player uid. It was read earlier in the same S2C 0x02 packet into scene+0x220. Receivers do not check it: case 0x11 only requires its own scene+0x220 != 0 and discards the value.

specs.semantics:
A one-shot LAN broadcast the client sends right after a successful login. Its purpose is to learn the client's own IP address. The client's socket is bound to 0.0.0.0:42907, so it normally receives its own broadcast, as does every other client on the LAN. FUN_0045e230 case 0x11 then zeroes scene+0x224..0x233, copies the recvfrom source IP string into scene+0x224 (p2p_ip) and sets scene+0x244=42907. Both values are later sent to the game server in the TCP enter-world request (p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port).

Destination: 255.255.255.255:42907 (sin_addr=0xFFFFFFFF, htons(0xA79B)). SO_BROADCAST is switched on just before this send and off right after it.

Framing (common to all g_sock_map sends): the socket was created by CreateSockets at 0x440804 as Create(port 0xA79B, type 2=UDP, encode=true, header=true). NoEncode is not imported by the exe, so the encode flag always applies. Each SendTo emits exactly one datagram of 8 + payload_len bytes, where the payload is opcode + fields.
- Header dword0 (SetHeader 0x10002150): bits 0-10 = (payload_len+8) & 0x7FF; bit 11 (0x800) = 1; bits 12-19 = seq; bits 20-31 = 0.
- Sequence: the counter at CSNSocket+0x13A8 starts at 0 (Init / Initial_Socket), is incremented before every SendTo on this socket, and wraps 255 -> 0. The first datagram therefore has seq 1. One counter is shared by every UDP kind (this broadcast, the loopback 0x04/0x03, and 0x03 to the room host).
- Header dword1 plus payload come from CEncMsg::EncodebyArray (0x10006B20), which is identical to cencmsg.encode_by_array. With T = the Fireway table at 0x1000B138 (low byte of each 4-byte entry): chk = (T[seq] + sum(plain[i] & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF, and every payload byte ^= T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF].
- The client's TCP Send uses the same header and cipher code.
- A third SendTo argument of 1 zeroes the 0x7F8-byte payload buffer after the send.
specs.trigger: S2C 0x02 (login result) with result==1, after the character list and transfer status are parsed. It runs once per successful login.
specs.expected_response: None. No server or peer reply is expected. The only effect is on receivers of the broadcast (normally the sender itself), whose case 0x11 handler records the source IP.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates:
- Sent only in the result==1 path of S2C 0x02, and always sent there.
- The receiver ignores 0x11 until scene+0x220 != 0.

Hazards:
- The u32 is not compared with the receiver's own uid. A 0x11 broadcast from another client on the same LAN overwrites scene+0x224 with that client's IP (last writer wins).
- If broadcast delivery or loopback fails, scene+0x224 keeps its previous value, which may be empty.
- A server process on the client machine must not bind UDP 42907. The client's own bind at CreateSockets 0x440804 would fail and the socket-creation error path runs.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x02 (login result) already mentions this broadcast. PROTOCOL.md C2S enter-world fields p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port (scene+0x224 / +0x244) are what this datagram feeds. In server/windslayer_server.py, UDPMapServer (a logger/decoder for this datagram) is defined but deliberately not started in main(): the comment notes that binding 42907 breaks the client. No server action is needed. Fireway SendTo(ulong) body 0x10003E38-0x10003F4F: htons(port), raw ip into sin_addr, sendto(sock, buf, len+8, 0, &sa, 16), and reset if arg3 != 0.
open_questions: Whether the original server-side infrastructure ever listened for this broadcast. It cannot cross routers, so it is most likely a pure self-discovery trick.
On Windows hosts with several interfaces, which source IP recvfrom reports for the looped-back broadcast. This decides the p2p_ip value.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to delete one character from the account. The client sends the selected character's 17-byte name and the 21-byte confirmation password/SS#, shows 'Waiting for the server to response.', and then always calls FUN_0042acd0(this+0x700).
specs.trigger: On the character select screen (window 0x12), the Delete button (control 2) needs character count != 0 and a selected character in idle pose (+0x15A8==0x214, +0x904==8). FUN_004640e0 then opens password dialog 0x201 owned by 0x235. Confirming that dialog raises window 0x235 / control 2, which builds and sends this packet. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_004640e0 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x1F [u8 result]. The handler at 0x45759B first closes message window 0x16. Results: 1 = success (FUN_00423fe0 removes the character whose uid is [this+0x3F8]+0x84 and clears the selection), 2 = 'Server process is running. Please try again in a few minutes (DB)', 3 = 'You can't delete a character created within 24 hours.', 12 = 'Invalid password. Please check your password again.'. Results 4..11 do nothing. S2C 0x1F [u8 result] closes the waiting box. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_004640e0 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: character count != 0, and a selected char entity with +0x15A8==0x214 and +0x904==8. If the entity check fails, no packet goes out and it jumps to 0x44D43B. Hazard: if window 0x201 is missing or has fewer than 5 controls, the client calls Add(NULL,0x15). Whether Fireway handles NULL is unknown (possible client crash), but the normal flow always has the dialog. Leaves a modal waiting box that needs S2C 0x1F to clear.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to cast skill <skill_id>. The client has already checked cost, cooldown and state locally and sends nothing else (no target). Right after Send it sets scene+0x258 (u16 pending/casting skill) = skill_id. That field locks out further casts (gate at 0x44C0E1(2008)) and also equip/unequip (FUN_0044fe20 gate 0x44C3B3(2008) and the 0x11 path), until the server clears it. For ids 0x0A31..0x0A3B (Booby Trap Lv1-10 and Puppet, 0x0A3B) the client adds its own integer X/Y. S2C 0x3B reads a matching u16,u16 pair for the same id range (0x452E2B(2008)).
specs.trigger: Pressing a quick-slot hotkey (game_state+0xE38[0..7], page byte game_state+0x10BC, 2x8 slots; HUD quick-slot buttons send WM_KEYDOWN for the same keys via FUN_0044ed10). Also activating a skill icon in the skill window (window 5) or an inventory entry whose def Type == 3. Quick-slot path requires scene+0xF00 == 6 (field mode), no item-stall session, no trade modal, and game_state+0xD84 == 0.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x25 (handler 0x458429, local path 0x458ADC -> 0x453D7F(2008)) clears scene+0x258 and starts the cooldown (FUN_00426cc0(2008) with def+0x1EC and game_state+0x364). S2C 0x5F (0 bytes, handler 0x457794(2008)) only clears scene+0x258, so it works as a reject/cancel. Other players are told via S2C 0x3B (u16 id, u32 caster uid, [u16 x, u16 y for 0x0A31..0x0A3B], ...). HP/MP cost updates go via S2C 0x28/0x44.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Branch taken only when def+0x154 (Type) == 3. Gates, in order: def+0x1DC > 0 (signed); scene+0x970 local entity non-null; scene+0x258 == 0 (no pending skill); scene+0x255 != 7 (S2C 0x25 sets 7 for some buff-skill ranges); entity+0x15B4 in {6, 8, 0xC} (8 = idle; attacking/jumping blocked). If def+0x168 (Job[0] traveler flag) == 0 and entity+0x112 == 0: shows 'You can't use the skill with elementary traveler weapon.' and does not send. entity+0xA0 (cur MP) must be >= |def+0x15C| (MP column, stored negative), else 'MP low.'. For ids 0x124..0x12E or 0x8DC..0x8E6 only, entity+0x9C (cur HP) must be > |def+0x158|, else 'Not enough HP.'. Cooldown: def+0x1EC (CT ms) + last_use_tick <= game_state+0x364 (now), unsigned, else silently nothing. HAZARD: if the server never answers with S2C 0x25 or 0x5F, scene+0x258 stays set. The player can then never cast another skill and gets 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.' on every equip attempt. No ResetBuffer: the packet starts with the Add(0x15) in this function (callers add nothing before).
specs.references: PySlayer parse_15 reads only u16 and ignores the trailing booby-trap X/Y. Its game_server handles Type 3 by sending a buff packet plus HP/MP deltas. Our windslayer_server.py dispatches 0x15 to _handle_use_item, which returns early for any type != 0. Skills get no 0x25/0x5F reply, which triggers the scene+0x258 lock described in gates. It only reads u16, so the 6-byte booby-trap variant parses harmlessly. The item DB confirms the id ranges: 0xA31-0xA3A 'Booby Trap' (Plants an invisible bomb on the field), 0xA3B 'Puppet', 0x124-0x12D Attack Boost, 0x12E Defense Boost, 0x8DC-0x8E5 Heaven Strike (HP -47/MP -47), 0x8E6 Aura of Advance. Note: the client's HP-cost range is inclusive of 0x12E and 0x8E6, one past each skill family.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to accept (take) the quest shown in the NPC quest dialog. Note the 0x26 handler only uses a slot if quest reward gold (+0xDE8) < 0, or it has required items (+0xD0C != 0), or a required count (+0xDF8 != 0); otherwise it calls FUN_00427910 instead (talk-only quest).

(0x489A5D) and no send; the dialog + window 0x236 are closed in both the send and the no-space cases. specs.semantics: Creates an arena room (window 0x2B, from the F-key ARENA list) or a Play&Chat room (window 0x479, from the P-key list). Both variants build the same 27-byte body in the same order and share the Send at 0x44DBE8. After sending, the client opens the modal 'Waiting for the server to response.', which only a server reply can close.
specs.trigger: Control 3 ('Create') in the arena create-room dialog (window 0x2B) or in the play-room create dialog (window 0x479).
specs.expected_response: A reply is required to close the 'Waiting for the server to response.' modal. The most likely candidate is the room-enter result (S2C 0x2F reads game+0xF70/+0xF48); not verified. On failure, S2C 0xA2 has 'The number of the play rooms are excessive...'. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x34 RoomJoinResult (or S2C 0x2F on a successful enter, 0x30/0xA2 on a create failure).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Arena: FUN_00445c00 blocks when manner < -20, already in arena or play room, in flea market, level < 5, in party play (window 0x75 state 1), waiting for battlefield, not standing still, hunting, stall open, or in cash shop. Play room: FUN_00444590(2008) (same checks minus the level-5 rule). A title that fails Curse_Engine_Clean shows 'No cursing please' and nothing is sent. Title length and emptiness are not checked. If an edit control is missing, FUN_0049eec0 returns NULL, and Curse_Engine_Clean and Add(char*,N) dereference it (crash). Novice-only rooms (type 3) cannot have a password, but that is enforced in the password UI, not on this send path. Text fields are raw edit buffers, so a server must stop at the first NUL and ignore trailing bytes. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C23, pvp_arena#05): both variants are 27 B and match the grammar field for field. max_users comes from a dropdown of {2,4,6,...,20}, so clamp it to 2..20 (design F3.3's 2..16 is wrong). The map dropdown order is 9801 "Popola Arena", 9802 "Marble Mount." (EN wording, not "Ohaengsan"), 9803 "Amakusa", 9804 "Balderan". room_type 3's EN caption is "For Beginners". round_time_min is only ever 3 or 5 from the arena dialog and 1 from the play-room dialog. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x34 (or 0x2F/0x30/0xA2 on failure).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on every Add call, its width and its order: u8 0x18, 17-byte title, u8, u8, 5-byte password, u16, u8 (27 bytes). The asm confirms this at 0x449969(2008)-0x4499ED(2008) (arena) and 0x44DB6C-0x44DBDE (play room); both jump to 0x44DB9B -> Send(1) @0x44DBE8. Stack offsets check out: CSNSocket::Add is thiscall and pops its own arguments, so [ESP+0x1C]/[ESP+0x24]/[ESP+0x10]/[ESP+0x18] are read at the same ESP where they were stored. The only disagreement is whether the 5-byte password is typed bytes[5] (A) or str[5] (B). Both describe the same 5 raw bytes. The source is FUN_0049eec0 (CALL FUN_004979d0; ADD EAX,0xD1), the same edit-control text accessor that supplies the 17-byte title, which both analysts typed as str. The password is user-typed, NUL-terminated text, so B's str[5] is the correct DSL type. Wire length is identical either way. Neither our server (no 0x18 branch in _dispatch) nor PySlayer (no C2S parser) handles it. PySlayer's S2C 0x33 room entry (name[17], u16 room no, u8 maxuser, u8 curuser, ...) supports the max_users name.

fields.name: ground_item_uid
fields.dest_or_source: ground-item node +0x12 (word). Node comes from the list at scene(*0x54F0C0)+0x1C. FUN_00424cb0 wrote the value (param_6) when S2C 0x12 spawned the item.
fields.meaning: instance id of the ground item (dropped loot) to pick up. The same id is matched by S2C 0x13 (FUN_00441630 compares node+0x12).

specs.semantics: The player asks to pick up one ground item. The client does all range, ownership and bag-space checks first. It sends at most one 0x1F per key event: the first item in the scene ground-item list that passes all checks. The client does not change the item locally. It waits for S2C 0x13 to set node+0x16=2, set node+0x1C=picker, and, when the picker is the local uid, add the item to the bag and print "you've received %s. (Count:%u)".
specs.trigger: Pickup key held during any key-down message. The key is the bound slot at game_state+0xDFC, copied from COption+0x68 (registry "Key3", default 'W' 0x57) by FUN_00487b90. FUN_0043d870 runs from MsgProc on WM_KEYDOWN when the UI did not consume the key and chat does not have focus (g_ui_root+8==0, g_ui_root+0x30==0). It also runs on WM_SYSKEYDOWN with Alt/F10. It then calls GetAsyncKeyState(pickup key).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x13 (handler 0x4565B3): u16 ground_item_uid, u16 count, u32 picker_uid. Broadcast it to everyone on the map so other clients mark the item taken. If validation fails there is no known error reply; the client simply keeps the item on the ground.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates, in order: (1) scene+0xF00 == 6 (in-game). (2) NOT (game_state+0xD7C != 0 && game_state+0xD5C == 0x259). (3) FUN_00472e10() == 0: UI window 0x28C/modal state is not 3. (4) app+0x9E == 0 (device not lost) and app+0x9D != 0 (app active). (5) The pickup key is down. (6) scene != 0 and scene+0x970 (local player entity) != 0. Per item in the scene+0x1C linked list: skip null nodes and nodes with state byte +0x16 == 2 (already picked). Range: (player u16@+0x15A4 - node.x u16@+0x0E)^2 + (player u16@+0x15A8 - node.y u16@+0x10)^2 < 625 (unsigned). Ownership: node+0x1C owner == 0, or == scene+0x220 (local uid), or node+0x24 + 15000 < scene+0xF1C (15 s loot protection). Otherwise the item is flagged as not owned. Bag space by node+0x18 category (from item def +0x154): 0 = capacity byte scene+0x3AA <= 45 and FUN_00426110 (qty node+0x14 <= 999; a same-id stack at ids scene+0x63E / counts scene+0x698 with count+qty < 1000, or an empty slot). 1 = capacity scene+0x3A9 <= 45 and an empty slot in scene+0x3C8 (equipment, no stacking). 2 = capacity scene+0x3AB <= 45 and FUN_00426190 (qty <= 99; a stack at ids +0x7A8 / byte counts +0x802 below 100, or an empty slot). Any other category is never sent. If nothing is sent: an owned in-range item with no bag space and game_state+0x3DC != 0 shows "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory." and clears +0x3DC (MsgProc sets it back to 1 on WM_KEYUP). Otherwise, if some in-range item was not owned, it shows "You don't have ownership of this item." HAZARDS: holding the key auto-repeats WM_KEYDOWN, so the client can send 0x1F for the same uid many times before 0x13 arrives. The server must be idempotent: grant once, ignore uids already picked. The uid is only 16 bits on the wire (node+0x12 is a u16), so ground uids must fit in u16.
specs.references: PySlayer: no C2S parser for 0x1F. Our server: this is the "pickup-request opcode still unidentified" noted near windslayer_server.py:1925. Ground drops (0x12) are deferred because of it. DISCREPANCY in our _build_opcode_13 (line ~1724): it packs the second u16 as the item id, but FUN_00441630 uses that value (param_4) as the COUNT, both for the bag add (e.g. MOVZX EAX,[ESP+0x64] at 0x4416CA) and for the "(Count:%u)" text. The item id comes from the ground node (node+0x00). Our GROUND_ITEM_UID_BASE 0x00200000 truncates to 0x0000 on the wire, so it is unsafe as a u16 uid.

Stacking items (catalog type 0 or 2) do not send from here: they open the quantity dialog (UI 0x74, default value = rec+0x0E), and on OK FUN_00472f40 sends the same opcode from send site #66 (Send at 0x473B5B, Adds at 0x473DE9..0x473E0D) as: u16 item_id, u16 entered_qty, u8 0, u16 0.

When owner_uid == local uid (char+0x1D8 = scene+0x220), the client takes the item out of its bag (0x470F00) and adds it to its own trade grid (0x49E830, window 0x4E). Otherwise it appends the item to the partner-offer list (win+0xBC). If the partner has no room, send S2C 0x4D ('There are no more spaces in the other player's item slot.').

specs.semantics: Asks the server to cancel the current trade. It is sent when the player clicks the X close button (control 2, text 'End') or the 'Cancel' button (control 4) in the trade offer window 0x4E 'Exchange', or the same two buttons in the final window 0x291 'Confirm Exchange'. Before sending, the client disables controls 2 and 4 of that window so the click can't repeat. The window stays open until the server answers. There is no body. The positive buttons are control 3 in each window: 'OK' in 0x4E sends 0x23 + u64 gold, and 'Trade' in 0x291 sends 0x25 + gold + items. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#04, trade#12): the EN captions differ from the KR lng strings quoted in the references - window 0x4E is captioned "TRADE" (not "Exchange") and window 0x291 is "Comfirming Trade" [sic] with list headers "Items to Send" / "Items to Receive" and ctrl 3 labelled "Trade".

specs.expected_response: S2C 0x49 'Trade has been canceled.' (handler 0x478C75). It closes windows 0x4E and 0x291 with FUN_00497c70(win,1,1) and returns the items staged in the window's +0xAC/+0xB0 list to the bag. The server should send 0x49 to both players. The client does not block waiting for it.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only gate: the UI root [ctx+0xC] must be non-null (0x472F6B). There are no trade-state checks. If the server never replies, controls 2 and 4 stay disabled and the window can't be closed. Only S2C 0x46 (trade open, 0x478568) enables them again (EDI=1 at 0x46DFEE(2008)). A server must not treat 0x24 as a confirm or lock: those are 0x23 and 0x25. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, trade#05/#06): live proof - after the first Cancel click both Cancel and the caption X are disabled and produce ZERO packets, so the TRADE window cannot be closed at all until the server answers. RECOVERY: send S2C 0x49 (it closes 0x4E/0x291 and returns the staged items). The server must always answer 0x24.

specs.semantics: Final accept of a player-to-player trade. After both sides lock (S2C 0x48 for self and for the partner), the client opens the confirmation window 0x291. Pressing OK disables the button and sends the whole deal as this client sees it: its own gold and item list, then the partner's gold and item list. Each item is id, quantity, a variable-length option list, and word +0x0C.
specs.trigger: Event 3 (OK button) on dialog 0x291. S2C 0x48 opens that window once button 3 of trade window 0x4E is disabled (own lock) and ctx+0x24 == 1 (partner locked).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x4A (trade completed) or S2C 0x49 ("Trade has been canceled."). Pairing comes from the handler strings; the payloads were not followed here.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs ctx+0x0C != 0. Button 3 is disabled BEFORE the dialog null-check, so if FUN_004979b0(0x291) returns null nothing is sent but the button stays disabled. The gold values are round-tripped through text with _strtoi64. A null text pointer from FUN_00497b50 would make _strtoi64 hit its invalid-parameter path. Counts are u8; the own trade grid is capped at 12 slots. Events 2/4 on the same dialog send C2S 0x24 (zero payload) instead. SERVER HAZARD: our server's _dispatch (windslayer_server.py:644) treats inbound 0x25 as UseSkill/attack (_handle_attack). A trade-confirm packet would be misparsed as a hit list. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C25, trade#13): the misparse does NOT stop at the first list - the attack parser read past my_item_count and produced one bogus target per offered item on BOTH sides (2 bogus targets from a 1+1 deal), so the exploit surface is every item id in either list, not just the sender's.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A gave u64 my_gold, u8 count, items{u16 id, u16 amount, u8 n, n*u16, u16}, u64 partner_gold, u8 count, items{same}. Analyst B did not report this key, because the path reaches the shared Send at 0x473E14 only through JZ 0x473E0F @0x46AB27(2008) or JMP 0x473E0F @0x474DBC. The asm confirms A in every detail. 0x474ADF PUSH 0x25 -> Add(uchar). 0x46A9AD(2008) FUN_00497b50(EDX=0x1D) -> FUN_004ad334 (_strtoi64 base 10) -> PUSH EDX, PUSH EAX -> Add(u64) [0x4C70C4] @0x474B37. Count loop over [dlg+0xB0] -> Add(uchar) @0x474B6E. For each node with data: Add(ushort) [data] @0x474BA2, Add(ushort) [data+0xE] @0x474BAC, option count (<5, stop at zero) Add(uchar) @0x474BDD, Add(ushort) loop @0x474BFD, Add(ushort) [data+0xC] @0x474C18. Then EDX=0x1E -> u64 @0x474C83, list [dlg+0xC0] with the same pattern @0x474CBD..0x474D68, then Send(1). Own/partner list identity comes from S2C 0x48 @0x47892B: uid == self marks dialog 0x4E list +0xB0; otherwise gold goes to label 0x1F, ctx+0x24 = 1 and list +0xC0 is marked. The lists are copied to dialog 0x291 +0xAC/+0xBC containers (heads +0xB0/+0xC0) at 0x478AA7/0x478AEE. The dialog id was decoded from the table: 0x291 -> 0x474A85. Not in PySlayer. Our server has an inbound 0x25 handler with a DIFFERENT meaning (skill/attack hit list). The only literal PUSH 0x25 + Add(uchar) opcode site in the corpus is this one, so the server's 0x25-as-attack assumption should be re-checked.

Payload layouts of S2C 0x49 and 0x4A were not traced in this task.

specs.semantics: Takes an item back out of the player's own trade offer. The client has already put the item back in its bag (0x470FC0: type 1 into the first empty bag slot, type 0 via 0x424FB0 into the consumable bag, type 2 via 0x4252A0 into the etc bag), refreshed the Inventory UI (0x46EF40) and removed the offer node. The packet tells the server so it can update the trade and notify the partner.
specs.trigger: The player drags an item out of their own side of the Trade window (window 0x4E) and drops it on the Inventory window (9) or on empty space (destination 0).
specs.expected_response: No reply to the sender is needed: its UI is already updated. Send S2C 0x4C (u8 slot_index; handler 0x478F33) to the trading PARTNER only; it removes node #index (0-based, 0x45F5E0) from the partner-offer list (win+0xBC). Do NOT send 0x4C to the sender: it would delete an entry from the sender's view of the partner's offer.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks: source 0x4E and destination 9 or 0; Trade window sub-controls 3 and 2 both non-zero (0x49DD90); a catalog entry exists for the dragged item id at ui_root+0x14 (0x404750 on [scene+0xF84]); the Trade window exists. For each own-offer node, it matches when node word+0x00 == dragged id AND the 12 bytes at node+0x02 equal ui_root+0x16 (0x428900). On a match, 0x470FC0(type, ctx, item_id, qty) must return non-zero before the packet is sent. HAZARDS: (1) if 0x470FC0 fails (bag full: type-1 bag capacity byte char+0x361 > 45 or no empty slot), the node is STILL unlinked and freed but no packet goes out, so the item disappears from the client's trade UI while the server still holds it as offered (desync). (2) The loop does not stop after a match. Several identical offers (same id and attributes) are all removed, one 0x26 each, and the index counter keeps counting removed nodes, so every later packet's trade_slot_index is based on the list as it was BEFORE any removal. A server that removes by index should process them against the original order, or match by item_id plus attributes.
specs.references: Our server: no inbound 0x26 in _dispatch. S2C 0x26 in our server is the quest GRANT, the opposite direction and unrelated. PySlayer: no 0x26 client parser. The body mirrors S2C 0x4B's item layout plus a slot index; S2C 0x4C carries only that index to the partner.
open_questions: Did the retail server send any confirmation or refresh (for example S2C 0x48) to either party after a removal? Nothing in the client needs one.

specs.semantics: Room-list subscription: one opcode for all three room lists. Opening a list asks the server for its contents; closing any of them tells the server to stop list updates. Replaces the 2008 opcodes 0x2C/0x2D (arena open/close) and 0x74/0x75 (play-room open/close), which no longer exist in the client.
specs.trigger: Opening (state 3/4) or closing (state 1) window 0x2A (F key), 0x478 (P key) or 0x4C4 (dungeon list, from its NPC/menu), including the forced closes when a room game starts (S2C 0x2F closes 0x2A, 0x478 and 0x4C4 and so emits list_type 0 if one was open).

specs.gates_and_hazards: Not sent when the window already has the requested state. The open gate [map+0x7C] == 1 (room map) blocks the packet; the close path has no gate, so an unsolicited list_type 0 can arrive right after the server sends S2C 0x2F. specs.name: DeathReviveRequest
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x54E828], TCP <game port from the S2C 0x01 channel entry; 7022 was the 2008 hardcoded value>)

locations.role: control id == 0 -> ignore (the only check before per-window dispatch)

the only other writer of +0x94C = 0xD, next to the dying flag +0x1388 = 1 and level-based exp-penalty math (table 0x6F0EAC(2008)), so state 0xD = dead
S2C 0x08 map load hides window 0x79 when not in arena

specs.semantics: Bare opcode, no body. It is sent when any control on window 0x79 is clicked. S2C 0x3E opens that window and puts the local player into motion state 0xD. State 0xD is the death state: FUN_0041b160 sets it together with the dying flag and the exp-loss calculation. So window 0x79 is the death dialog and 0x2E asks the server to revive or return the player. The handler never checks which control was clicked, so every button sends the same packet.
specs.trigger: Clicking any nonzero control on window 0x79 (the death dialog opened by S2C 0x3E).
specs.expected_response: Probably a map (re)load: S2C 0x08 hides window 0x79 outside arenas, then the spawn/enter sequence. Not verified for EN. This is a different packet from the S2C 0x2E map/channel enter. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, combat_skill#21): the client sends this the moment the death dialog's only button is clicked and closes the dialog itself, so the server MUST answer with the revive sequence (HP via S2C 0x28/0x44 plus the map-enter sequence S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07) - otherwise the player stays dead with no UI and no way to retry.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No client-side gate beyond control id != 0. The handler ignores the control id, so a multi-button dialog cannot tell the server which choice was made. Window 0x79 stays open until the server sends something that hides it (S2C 0x08 outside arena), so the player can click repeatedly and send duplicates.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the body is empty. Add(u8 0x2E) at 0x44CD22 goes directly to JMP 0x44A9CE and Send(1), with no other Add. A's grammar "" and B's "stop" both mean zero bytes. The correct grammar is empty (length 0). On naming: A's 'revive request' is supported by more evidence than B's generic 'Window79Confirm'. The value S2C 0x3E writes (+0x94C = 0xD) is also written by FUN_0041b160 @0x41B1B3, right next to the dying flag (+0x1388 = 1) and the per-level exp-penalty code, so 0x79 is the death dialog. A's cross-reference 'PySlayer answers respawn with S2C 0x2E' is for the other direction and a newer KR build; do not assume a server reply opcode from it. Our server has no C2S 0x2E branch in _dispatch.
open_questions: Whether the server should revive in place or send the player to town. The client sends no choice.
Which S2C sequence the original server sent in reply (0x08 map reload is the most likely, since it hides window 0x79).

specs.socket: game: CSNSocket* at CMessenger(app[+0x4E4])+0x74. FUN_0046f860(2008) copies g_sock_game [0x54E828] there (0x46F934(2008)), so it is the same TCP <game port from the S2C 0x01 channel entry; 7022 was the 2008 hardcoded value> socket.

S2C 0x0B friend-list handler on the same messenger object (likely reply)

specs.semantics: Opcode-only request from the messenger (friend list) subsystem. Earlier in the same S2C 0x03 handler, FUN_0046f860(2008) re-initializes CMessenger: it clears the friend-list state and copies the local name from player+0x48+0x1BE and fields +0x1D8/+0x1CF. At the end of the handler, after the map is loaded, the UI is refreshed and timers 6 (240000 ms) and 0xB (7000 ms) are armed, the client sends a bare 0x2F on the messenger's socket (the game socket). Nothing is Added before or after the opcode. The only other Add(0x2F) in the binary is this one. It is fire-and-forget: the client does not wait for a reply before continuing to the 0x63 send.
specs.trigger: Automatic, at the end of every S2C 0x03 (world/map info) handler, i.e. after each map load, both on entering the world and on map change. Always immediately followed by C2S 0x63.
specs.expected_response: Probably S2C 0x0B friend list, handled in SubHandler3 on the messenger object and read through messenger+0x74: u8 unk (messenger+0xD1), u8 count, repeat(count){ str[17] name, u8 unk, u32 unk, u8 state }. The client does not require a reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sent only if [app+0x4E4]+0x74 != 0, i.e. FUN_0046f860(2008) found a UI root, an app pointer and g_sock_game. app+0x4E4 itself is dereferenced without a null check here and at 0x44E52F(2008), so it must exist (allocated at app init). Because this runs on every 0x03, a server that answers 0x2F with a friend list resends that list on every map change.
specs.references: The live capture shows 0x2F with 0 bytes sent right after a map loads, which agrees. windslayer_server.py _dispatch consumes 0x2F with the log 'arena query — ignoring'. That label is WRONG: the packet comes from CMessenger (friend list), not the arena. The arena room list is C2S 0x2C/0x2D. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x2F.py is an unrelated S2C 0x2F (the same number means something else in the other direction); PySlayer has no C2S 0x2F parser. Our server comment 'no heartbeats arrived after 0x2F+0x63' matches the send order.
open_questions: Name is inferred from the owning object (CMessenger, whose S2C handlers 0x0B-0x10/0x60-0x62/0x78/0x7A-0x7E carry friend-list, 1:1 chat and mentor strings); no UI string names 0x2F directly. Friend list vs. full messenger sync (friends + mentor) is not proven.
Whether the original server answered with 0x0B, and whether other messenger packets (e.g. 0x7B mentor info) also followed, is unknown.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to send a friend request to another character. After sending, the client prints "Requesting <name> to be a friend" (0xFF00C800) in the system chat. It does not add the friend locally.

specs.expected_response: S2C 0x0C (friend add result, handler 0x47BEED): u8 result; if result is 1 or 0x0B: str[17] name, u8 channel, u32 friend_uid, u8 state, then the entry is added to the list with "<name> has been registered in your friend list."; otherwise: str[17] name and an error dialog chosen by code (2 not online, 3 refused, 4 friend function off, 5 target list full, 6 already in list, 7 your list full, 0x15 generic error). The target receives S2C 0x0D (u32 requester_id, str[17] requester_name), which opens dialog 0x17C, and answers with C2S 0x31 {u32 id, str[17] name, u8 accept} (FUN_0047b330).
