specs.name: FriendDelete
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game via CMessenger+0x74; messenger+0x74 is loaded from [0x54E828] at 0x46F86A(2008) and stored at 0x46F934(2008) by FUN_0046f860(2008) on S2C 0x03; ECX=[ESI+0x74] before every Add/Send in the builder)

locations.role: Builder with a custom calling convention: ESI = CMessenger ([game_state+0x4E4]), EDI = friend name pointer, [ESP+4] = friend_id (u32), RET 4. Gate: [ESI+0x74] != NULL (0x47B0E6) and EDI != NULL (0x47B0EA); otherwise it returns without sending.
MOV EAX,[ESP+4] / PUSH EAX / CALL [0x4C7114] Add(unsigned int): u32 friend_id
PUSH 0x11 / PUSH EDI / CALL [0x4C7110] Add(char*,17): exactly 17 name bytes

Tail call. MOV [ESP+4],1 at 0x47B11C overwrites the caller's argument slot with 1, then JMP [0x4C712C] runs CSNSocket::Send(1) on ECX=[ESI+0x74]. Send's RET 4 returns straight to the caller at 0x480E2E and pops the slot. This is the only JMP into any Fireway IAT slot in the binary.

Only caller. 0x480D70: FUN_004979b0(ui_root=[messenger+0x70], id 0x17A) gets the dialog, saved at [ESP+0xC]. 0x473015(2008): FUN_004979d0(window 0x17A, control 4) gets the control; EDI = control+0x50 (text buffer), or 0 if the control is missing. If the dialog is NULL it jumps to 0x481250 ('Please select a character name. ') and sends nothing. Otherwise it pushes [dialog+0x134], sets ESI=EBX=messenger and calls the builder. Afterwards (0x480E2E-0x473062(2008)) it sets [ui_root+0x5A4]=1 and calls FUN_00448730(0x17A,0,1,0,1) to close the dialog, even if the builder skipped the send.

Prepares the confirm dialog. If window 0x176 +0xEC (selected row, 1-based) == 0: 'Please select a character name. ' and dialog 0x17A is closed (0x472B08(2008) -> 0x473055(2008)). Otherwise FUN_0045f5b0(list window+0xAC, index-1) returns the friend node (EDI).
The only code that writes dialog 0x17A +0x134: [dialog+0x134] = friend_node+0x18 (friend_id from S2C 0x0B/0x0C)
FUN_00498120(window EAX=0x17A, control 4, EDI=friend_node): memsets control+0x50 to 0 for 0x81 bytes, then strcpy's friend_node+0x00 (name) into it
Generic route: FUN_00480430([game_state+0x4E4] messenger, window id, button id) when FUN_00489aa0 does not consume the event
Handler for the response S2C 0x0E FriendDeleteResult

specs.grammar:
u32 friend_id
str[17] friend_name

fields.name: friend_id
fields.dest_or_source: Dialog 0x17A +0x134. Written at 0x4806FA from friend_node+0x18, the friend_id the server sent in S2C 0x0B (friend list) or 0x0C (friend added).
fields.meaning: Server id of the friend to remove, echoed exactly as the server gave it. The same field is used by C2S 0x33 chat invite and matched by S2C 0x60 status updates.

fields.name: friend_name
fields.dest_or_source: Text buffer (+0x50) of control 4 of dialog 0x17A. FUN_00498120 at 0x48070D zeroes 0x81 bytes, then copies friend_node+0x00 (the 17-byte name from S2C 0x0B/0x0C, stored in a zeroed 0x28-byte node).
fields.meaning: Character name of the friend to remove, NUL-terminated and zero-padded to 17 bytes. Stale bytes are not possible on the normal path because the buffer is memset first.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to remove a friend from the player's friend list. The client changes nothing locally when it sends: the list node, the count (messenger+0xD0) and the '(count/capacity)' label only change when S2C 0x0E arrives. The body is fixed at 22 bytes: 0x32, u32 friend_id (LE), 17 name bytes. There is no ResetBuffer call; the packet is built with Add calls and flushed with Send(1), like the other messenger sends (0x30/0x31/0x33/0x34/0x5C). Flow: the player selects a row in the friend list window 0x176 and clicks button 9. The UI script opens confirm dialog 0x17A; the code copies the selected node's friend_id into dialog+0x134 and its name into control 4. Clicking button 2 (OK) of dialog 0x17A sends this packet and closes the dialog.
specs.trigger: Friend list window 0x176 ('My Friends'): select a friend, click button 9 (Delete). Then click button 2 (OK/Yes) in confirm dialog 0x17A, which probably uses UILng 8001 'Would you like to delete the character from your Friend List?' and 8002 'Name of Friend's' (inferred). This is the only trigger: FUN_0047b0e0 has one caller (0x480DC9), and window id 0x17A appears only in FUN_00480430.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x0E FriendDeleteResult (handler 0x47C1F1): u8 success, str[17] name. If success != 0: popup '<name> is deleted from friend list.', then FUN_0047fde0 unlinks every friend node whose name exactly matches (strcmp) and redraws window 0x176 and the (count/capacity) label. If success == 0: popup 'Deleting <name> from your friend list failed. Please again in a few minutes.' The server should echo friend_name byte-exactly, because removal is by name, not by friend_id.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Send-time gates, in order: (1) dialog 0x17A must be found in the ui_root+0x5C0 window list; otherwise 'Please select a character name. ' and no send. (2) messenger+0x74 must be non-NULL; it is NULL until the first S2C 0x03. (3) Control 4 of dialog 0x17A must exist (EDI != NULL). If (2) or (3) fails, nothing is sent and there is no message, but the dialog still closes. Nothing checks that friend_id is non-zero or that the name is still in the list. Open-time gates (button 9 of 0x176): a row must be selected (+0xEC != 0), otherwise the message is shown and 0x17A is closed. HAZARD: if FUN_0045f5b0 returns NULL or dialog 0x17A is not found, +0x134 and control 4 are not refreshed, so OK would send whatever an earlier use left there. The code does not reset them. In the mentor tab (FUN_0047b3e0 else-branch), buttons 8 and 9 of window 0x176 are put in state 3 (FUN_0049e070(0x176,9,3)), which probably disables them, so deletion should only be reachable from the friend tab.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x0B/0x0C (friend_id source) and S2C 0x0E (FriendDeleteResult: 'Reply to C2S 0x32 (delete friend: u32 friend_id, str[17] name), sent from the delete-confirm dialog 0x17A'), which matches this derivation. Sibling messenger sends in the same class with the same register convention: 0x47AE8B/0x30 FriendAddRequest, 0x47B383/0x31, 0x47B1B8/0x33, 0x47B3CB/0x34, 0x46FFD8(2008)/0x5C (FUN_0046ff70(2008), the function right before, ESI/EDI convention). Missing from protocol_spec.json because the Ghidra scout only annotated plain CALL [0x4C712C] sites and this one is a tail JMP. PySlayer: server_packets/__init__.py imports opcode_0x32 inside try/except but the file does not exist; there is no C2S parser. Our server (windslayer_server.py, wsproto.py) has no 0x32 handling and no friend system. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C43, social_friend#06): captured live byte for byte - payload 21 B "02 00 00 00 42 6F 62 00*14" = u32 friend_id (2) followed by str[17] "Bob", exactly the grammar above. (This spec was missing from the earlier protocol_spec.json snapshot that the verification matrix was written against; it is present and correct in this corpus.)
open_questions: Whether the original server keyed the deletion on friend_id or friend_name (the client sends both; the S2C 0x0E reply removes by name only).

The mapping of window 0x17A and button 9 to UILng strings 8001/8002 ('delete from Friend List') is inferred from lng ordering (0x17C->8006, 0x17D->8007) and the S2C 0x0E strings, not from a parsed UI definition file.

specs.name: MessengerRoomChat
specs.socket: game (CMessenger+0x74, which FUN_0046f860(2008) copies from g_sock_game [0x54E828] while handling S2C 0x03 at 0x452C01; the constructor FUN_0046f670(2008) sets it to 0)

locations.role: builder: checks, adds the opcode, length and text, then calls Send
caller: the Enter/IME result in the messenger chat window 0x177 (reached from FUN_0049cf10 at 0x49DBE6 when window 0x177 is open and CIME::IsStringResult is true)
caller: chat-macro hotkey (12 key slots at +0xe58, macro text slots of 0x25 bytes at +0xe88) while the focused window is 0x177
S2C 0x61: the matching room-chat broadcast the client displays

specs.grammar:
u8 text_len
str[text_len] text
specs.length: 1 + text_len (text_len = strlen(text) & 0xFF; no NUL is sent)

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: Length of the chat text in bytes. It is the low byte of the strlen the caller passes (param_2); Add(uchar) pushes EBX, so only BL is sent.
fields.dest_or_source: caller's strlen of the text. From FUN_00446280 it is strlen(CIME+0x104). From FUN_0043dde0 it is strlen of the macro slot (player+0xe88+idx*0x25, at most 36).

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Chat text for the messenger chat room. Exactly text_len raw bytes with no terminator (Add(char*,N) with N = movzx BL at 0x47B2C0).
fields.dest_or_source: CIME result string (DAT_0070e708+0x104) or the macro text slot

specs.semantics: Sends one line of chat into the messenger/friend conversation room the player is currently in (room id held at CMessenger+0xcc). The client does NOT show its own line locally. It waits for the server's S2C 0x61 relay, which prints "<name> : " and "  text" in window 0x177. The line is colored 0xffc766a6 when the name equals the player's own name (CMessenger+0x7c), otherwise 0xff3277cc.
specs.trigger: The player presses Enter with text in the messenger chat window (UI 0x177, 'Messenger Window'), or presses a chat-macro hotkey while window 0x177 is the focused window (g_ui_root+8 == 0x177) and that window's state (+0x3c) != 1. Otherwise the macro goes to normal chat through FUN_004462e0.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x61 to every member of the room, the sender included: str[17] sender_name, u8 len, str[len] text. It is only processed while CMessenger+0xcc (room_id) != 0.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No send when: CMessenger socket (+0x74) is NULL, the text pointer is NULL, or CMessenger+0xcc (room_id, set by S2C 0x0F result=1) == 0. Also no send when ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text) returns false; the client then prints 'No cursing please' (color 0xfffdf34c) to the chat log. After the IME path the client calls CIME::ResetResultString and memsets player+0x14d8 (0x3d bytes). HAZARD for the relay: the S2C 0x61 handler reads len bytes into a 64-byte stack buffer and then sprintf_s("  %s") into a 0x3d (61) byte buffer. The server must relay len <= 58, otherwise sprintf_s hits the invalid-parameter handler (client abort), and len >= 64 also leaves the text unterminated.

specs.semantics: Sent when the Item Mall (cash shop) main window, control 0x1CF, receives notification 3. This is almost certainly its close/exit button. The client first hides all Item Mall sub-windows (FUN_0045cc20(2008)). It then reports the net result of the session's item moves between two lists of 28-byte cash-item records. List 1 is account cash storage (main+0x700+0x28), filled by S2C 0x6A and appended to by S2C 0x6C purchases and 0x79 gifts. List 2 is the character's cash-item inventory (main+0x700+0x4), filled at login by S2C 0x6F entries with flag==0. S2C 0x6A (mall open) snapshots both lists (+0x48 and +0x58). While the window is open the player moves records between the lists: storage->character via control 0x1FC notification 0xCA, which checks per-category slot limits ('You have no more slots for the item.') and duplicates ('The item is already in your inventory. You can't store it any more.'); character->storage via control 0x1FD notification 0xC9. On close the client sends each list's additions compared to its snapshot, keyed by record+0x00 (u32 serial). Removals are never sent explicitly. The server should treat each list-A serial as 'now in storage' (moved off the character, or a no-op for items bought or gifted this session) and each list-B serial as 'now on character' (moved out of storage). Record layout as the client uses it: +0x00 u32 serial, +0x04 u16 item id, +0x06 u8 kind (0/1/2), +0x08 u16, +0x0A u16, +0x1A u8 (3 = event item). Only the serial goes on the wire.
specs.trigger: The player closes the Item Mall window (control 0x1CF, notification 3). The windows hide even if the socket is null.
specs.expected_response: None awaited: no waiting dialog and no state change that depends on a reply. The temporary vectors are freed right after Send.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Built only if [main+0x700+0x20] != NULL. FUN_004604c0 sets it during the S2C 0x5A key/login-start handler. SubHandler4 also ignores mall packets unless +0x14 and +0x18 are set there. The opcode Add is inside the null-check, so nothing is appended to the buffer when the socket is null. The snapshots +0x48/+0x58 are rebuilt ONLY by S2C 0x6A, and neither the snapshots nor the live lists are updated after this send. If the window is reopened without a fresh 0x6A and closed again, the same serials are re-sent, so the server must make applying them idempotent. Items bought (0x6C) or gifted (0x79) during the session appear in list A even though they never left storage. A deletion (0x6E) removes a record only from the live storage list, so it produces no serial; only the flag reports it. Counts are i32 while the elements are u32; element pointers are never NULL, so the counts always equal the number of u32 entries that follow.
specs.references: PySlayer has no C2S 0x42 parser. PySlayer's server_packets/opcode_0x42.py is an unrelated S2C builder for the KR build (u32,u32,u16), and S2C 0x42 is not C2S 0x42. Not handled by our windslayer_server.py _dispatch (no 0x42 branch). The Item Mall meaning comes from strings used in FUN_00465890/SubHandler4: 'Item is added to your wish-list.', 'You have no more slots for the item.', 'You failed to delete the item.', 'You are short of cash.', 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash...'.
open_questions: Notification 3 on control 0x1CF is inferred to be the close/exit button, because it hides all mall windows; there is no UI layout file to confirm it

Which C2S request opens the mall and makes the server send S2C 0x6A (not in this batch). The correctness of the diff depends on 0x6A being sent on every open.

Which window shows which list (0x1FC vs 0x1FD) does not affect the wire format. List A = account storage (+0x28, from 0x6A) and list B = character cash items (+0x4, from 0x6F flag 0) are inferred from the slot-limit and 'already in your inventory' checks on the storage->character move.

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Tells the server to delete all stored messenger messages, the 126-byte records that S2C 0x78 adds to the CMessenger+0x34 list. Closing the received-messages window 0x3FE with ctrl 2 or ctrl 9 opens the confirmation box. Pressing OK there (message box 0x16, ctrl 2, owner 0x3FE, phase 6) sends the bare opcode. The client then clears everything locally: the HUD window 3 ctrl 8 indicator goes to state 3, window 0x3FE is hidden, the message list is freed and the count label is refreshed. No message ids are sent.
specs.trigger: Close the messenger messages window (0x3FE ctrl 2 or 9), then press OK in the 'All the messages will be deleted...' confirmation.
specs.expected_response: None. The client clears its list without waiting for a reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs game phase [[scene+0x4CC]+0xF00]==6 and the message-box owner to be 0x3FE. If CMessenger+0x74 is NULL, neither the send nor the local clear happens. The server should drop the stored messages, or they will come back on the next S2C 0x78. C2S 0x44 has nothing to do with S2C 0x44 (setMP).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree on everything that matters: a bare opcode from FUN_00480430 (Add u8 0x44 at 0x48049A, Send at 0x4804A8), gated on dlg==0x16, ctrl==0x64 and a non-NULL socket, with the only real caller at 0x44930B. The disagreement was notation only ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm confirms there is no other Add. The caller code at 0x44924C-0x44930B checks phase 6 (SUB 3/SUB 2/SUB 1), ctrl 2 and owner 0x3FE, then does PUSH 0x64; PUSH EDX(=0x16); PUSH [scene+0x4E4]. EDX survives FUN_00497b20, which does not touch EDX. A is right that the UI clear is inside the socket-non-NULL branch, because the JZ at 0x480492 skips to 0x48399A. The 0x3FE switch table decoded from the binary maps ctrl 2 and ctrl 9 to the confirm prompt at 0x47324E(2008). The other caller FUN_0044ed10 only passes (0x176,7). The generic dispatch at 0x44E589 passes the real ctrl id, which would have to be 100 on window 0x16. 'stop' is used as the zero-byte DSL form. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.

specs.socket: game (g_sock_game 0x54E828, cached at [app+0x700+0x20] by init FUN_004604c0)

locations.role: control 5 action: minimize game + ShellExecute item_filling.html

specs.semantics: Asks the server to re-send the account's Wind Cash / mileage balance. The body is just the opcode byte. It is built with Add(u8 0x46) at 0x46D62E and Send(1) at 0x46D639, and nothing else is added (no helper or caller adds to the buffer). The object is the cash-shop (item mall) controller at app+0x700: +0x18 = UI root, +0x20 = game socket, +0x588 = cash, +0x58C = mileage.
specs.trigger: UI event: window 0x1CF (cash shop / item mall; its handler uses the wish-list strings) receives control 0xA8. The FUN_00465890 switch was checked against tables 0x461564(2008)/0x461538(2008) and 0x4615C0(2008)/0x461598(2008): (0x1CF, 0xA8) goes to 0x465942, and 0x1CF is the only window id that reaches that switch. It only sends if [app+0x700+0x5AC] != 0. That flag is set to 1 when the player presses control 5 in the same window. Control 5 closes windows 0x1F7-0x1FA, minimizes the client (PostMessage WM_SYSCOMMAND SC_MINIMIZE) and opens http://windslayer.kr.games.yahoo.com/item/item_filling.html, which is the cash top-up page. So this is the 'refresh balance after topping up' action.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x70 (SubHandler4 @0x46B9A1): u32 wind_cash -> [app+0x700+0x588], u32 mileage -> [+0x58C], u8 first_purchase_bonus (non-zero shows the 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash. 500 mileage...' dialog). The client then calls FUN_00462100 to refresh the display and clears the +0x5AC flag.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sent only while [app+0x700+0x5AC] != 0. The flag starts at 0 (FUN_004604c0 at session init), is set only by the charge-cash button (control 5), and is cleared only by S2C 0x70. Until a 0x70 arrives, every control-0xA8 event sends another 0x46. If the player never presses charge-cash, control 0xA8 does nothing. There are no dialogs and no 'waiting' UI. Pressing charge-cash minimizes the game window and opens a dead Yahoo KR URL in the browser.

Double-clicking a cash-inventory item opens confirm dialog 0x3F4, unless it is one of the special items that have their own dialogs: 0x766/0xCF8 (dialog 0x3FD), 0x767 (0x3F1), 0xC8E/0xC8F/0xCA2/0xCA3 (0x3FA), 0xD31-0xD35 (0x3FF), 0xD65-0xD6A (0x472 / FUN_00497af0), 0xD6C/0xD6D and 0xF6F/0xF70 (FUN_00472760). Pressing OK (button code 2) sends opcode 0x48 plus a u16 item id, with no ResetBuffer before the Adds. The client then shows a modal 'Waiting for the server to response.' box. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x72 CashItemUsed (echoing the real cash_item_serial).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only reached for widget type [+0x154]==5 items found in the cash item list by FUN_00464c10 (entry +4 short == key, +8 short != 0, and not (+6 byte==2 with +0xA short != 0)). Dialog button must be 2 (OK) and window 0x3F4 must exist. Skill-type items already registered show 'The item is already registered. Please check your skill list.' and send nothing. After sending, the modal waiting box stays until the server replies, so the client appears stuck if the server ignores 0x48. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x72.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A reported send site 0x469072 carrying opcode 0x48 as 'u16 item_id' (2 bytes after the opcode). Analyst B did not report this key because it only followed the linear 0x49 path into the shared Send. Analyst A is correct. The asm shows case 0x3F4 of the dialog switch (raw jump table 0x4617B4(2008)/0x4617E0(2008) resolves dialog 0x3F4 to 0x46951D). At 0x46951D it checks SUB EAX,2 / JNZ, then FUN_004979b0 with a NULL check. Then 0x469586 MOV ECX,[EBX+0x20]; 0x469589 PUSH 0x48; 0x46958B CALL [0x4C7120] Add(uchar). Then 0x469591 MOVZX EAX, word [ESI+0x134]; 0x469597 PUSH EAX; 0x469598 CALL [0x4C7118] Add(ushort). Then 0x46959E JMP 0x46906D, which does MOV ECX,[EBX+0x20]; PUSH 1; 0x469072 CALL [0x4C712C] Send. So the full packet is 48 + u16. The decompiler agrees (case 0x3f4: Add 'H', Add *(ushort*)(iVar9+0x134), goto LAB_00460a6d). The same Send VA also carries 0x49 (u8 0x49 + 17-byte string via 0x469055-0x469067), which is a separate key. Not handled by PySlayer client parsers (no parse_0x48) or by windslayer_server.py.

The server cannot tell the skill-registration variant (opener param_5==2) from a normal use, because the wire bytes are identical. It has to work that out from the item type.

specs.semantics: Apply a Stat Reset cash item. Dialog 0x3FA shows the four current stats and the number of points the item can reset (window+0x40). Buttons 3/4/5/6 decrement the displayed str/dex/int/tol value (never below 0) while total removed < item points and update the remaining counter (ctrl 11); nothing is sent for those. Button 0xC (confirm) sends 0x4A with the item id and the per-stat number of points removed, if any points were removed, then shows a modal waiting box. Removed points presumably return to the free stat-point pool server-side.
specs.trigger: Using a Stat Reset item (0xC8E/0xC8F/0xCA2/0xCA3) opens dialog 0x3FA; player decrements stats and presses confirm (param_3 == 0xC).

Not fully verified. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x76 StatRedistributeResult (18-byte form to the requester).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Not sent if total displayed == total current (nothing removed). Deltas are u8 (value mod 256) but bounded by item points (<=20). The client never checks base/minimum stats beyond >=0, nor that deltas sum to exactly the item's points (only <=), so the server must validate: sum(deltas) <= points of item_id, each resulting stat >= class minimum, and the player owns item_id. Opener requires item points (param_4) != 0. Modal waiting box stays until the server replies. No ResetBuffer before Adds. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C13, premium_cash#21): the client's own cap is the u16 quantity at +0x08 of the 28-byte cash record delivered by S2C 0x6F, not the item def's Cash_V. The server must validate sum(removed) <= record.quantity (and treat Cash_V only as the value stamped into quantity when the record is created). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x76.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to broadcast a megaphone message using a megaphone cash item from the inventory. The item id tells the server whether it is a Super Megaphone (whole world) or a normal Megaphone (whole channel). After sending, the client closes the megaphone window straight away and shows no waiting dialog, so it does not need a direct reply. The server should check that the player owns the item, use up one charge, broadcast the message, and update the item count.
specs.trigger: The player double-clicks a Megaphone or Super Megaphone item (ids 3377-3381), types in window 0x3FF (edit control 6) and clicks the send button (control 3).
specs.expected_response: No reply packet is required (window closes, no modal). The broadcast and item-count update presumably come in a separate S2C packet, but it was not found in this pass.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks before sending: text is not empty ('Please enter the contents.'); Curse_Engine_Clean(text) passes ('No cursing \r\n\r\nplease.'); low 16 bits of window+0x40 are not 0 (otherwise it returns silently with no dialog). Opening window 0x3FF any other way leaves +0x40 at 0, so nothing is sent. Hazard: unbounded strcpy of the edit-control text into a 61-byte stack buffer. If the control allows 61 or more characters the text is not NUL-terminated inside the 61 bytes sent (and the stack overflows). No ResetBuffer is called; the buffer is assumed empty after the previous Send. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.
specs.references: No match in PySlayer (no parse_0x4C). Not handled in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. The scout guess (0x48 + u16 + str) was wrong: the Add(0x48)+u16 at 0x460E06(2008) belongs to window 0x3F4 and jumps to site #52's Send at 0x460A6D(2008). Item names come from data/en/items_en.json and the PySlayer gamedef items table (Type 5 cash items).

locations.role: Friend window 0x176, ctrl 0x1C (switch 0x48052F, verified from table 0x47374C(2008)/0x473724(2008)). If the CMessenger+0x14 list (head +0x18) has an entry, it opens window 0x200 and sets ctrl 4's text to entry+0x00 (name).

Calls FUN_0047fee0, which frees the CMessenger+0x14 list (+0x18/+0x1C/+0x20) and refreshes the friend UI via FUN_0047b3e0. Then FUN_00448730(0x200,0,1,0,1) closes the window.

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Asks the server to dissolve the local player's mentor relationship. Friend window 0x176 button 0x1C opens confirm window 0x200 only if the client has a mentor entry in list CMessenger+0x14 (filled by S2C 0x7A), and shows that mentor's name in ctrl 4. Button 0x1B next to it is the register-mentor path, which requires a novice ('Only a novice can register a mentor.'). When OK (ctrl 2) is pressed and the name label is not empty, the client sends the bare opcode, frees its local mentor list at once, refreshes the friend window and closes window 0x200. No name or uid is sent, so the server works out the mentor from its own records.
specs.trigger: Friend/messenger window 0x176 button ctrl 0x1C, then OK (ctrl 2) in confirm window 0x200.
specs.expected_response: None. The client removes the mentor locally before any reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs window 0x200 to exist and its ctrl 4 label to be non-empty, otherwise the client shows 'Please select a character name.'. If window 0x200 exists but ctrl 4 does not, FUN_00497b50 returns NULL and the strlen loop at 0x4811D0 dereferences NULL, crashing the client. No send (and no local clear) if CMessenger+0x74 is NULL. The client drops the mentor whatever the server does, so if the server refuses it must send the mentor data again to resync.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: the bare opcode, with Add(u8 0x50) at 0x4811F1 and Send(1) at 0x4811FF in FUN_00480430's dlg==0x200/ctrl==2 branch. The only difference is notation ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm shows no Add between the socket gate at 0x4811E1 and Send. The name read from ctrl 4 at 0x4732F9(2008) is only used for the empty-string check and is never Added. Decoding switch table 0x47374C(2008)/0x473724(2008) from the binary confirms ctrl 0x1C goes to 0x4808FC (the opener) and ctrl 0x1B to 0x480883 (the novice-only register-mentor path). S2C 0x7A writing the list at LEA ESI,[EBX+0x14] (0x4716C4(2008)), and FUN_0047fee0 freeing +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20, are verified. A's confidence was medium only because window 0x200 has no text string. The control flow (mentor list present, then name shown, then list freed) supports 'remove mentor', so high confidence is justified for the wire format. B's NULL-dereference hazard is real, since FUN_00497b50 returns 0 when the control is missing. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.

specs.semantics: Password re-confirmation gate. When the player opens a protected feature (cash-shop gift, some NPC service windows) the client first shows password dialog 0x201. Clicking OK (control id 2) sends 0x51 with the password and the id of the window that should open on success, then closes dialog 0x201 (no 'waiting' box). Control id 4 on this dialog only refocuses the edit box (FUN_0049e710(0x201,5)).

CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_004640e0 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F. Target window ids seen live: 0x1A7 (bank), 0x1F9 (cash-shop purchase continuation) and 0x235 (character delete confirm). Always echo the id the client sent.

No ResetBuffer before the Adds (relies on the prior Send having cleared the buffer). strcpy of the edit text into the stack buffer is unbounded (edit length limit not verified). specs.semantics: Opcode-only request that asks the server for the card deck ('dictionary') contents. The send is unconditional and comes right after the messenger 0x2F send, at the very end of the S2C 0x03 handler. It goes through the card-deck object's socket pointer (app+0xDC4, the same object passed to SubHandler5). That object only handles S2C 0x8A: u8 count stored at (player+0x48)+0xE30, then u16 ids. It then refreshes the Card Deck UI ('%u / %u (%u%%)'). S2C 0x8B error code 2 says 'Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again.', which ties this data to the login/world-entry fetch. No other Adds; the only Add(0x63) in the binary is this one. Fire-and-forget.
specs.trigger: Automatic, at the end of every S2C 0x03 (world/map info) handler, i.e. after each map load, immediately after C2S 0x2F (or in its place when the messenger gate fails).
specs.expected_response: Probably S2C 0x8A card deck list: u8 count, repeat(count){ u16 card_id }. It is stored at player+0x48+0xE30/+0xE32 and handled in SubHandler5_ifelse. The client does not require a reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate. [app+0xDD0] is only set by FUN_0045f760 in the S2C 0x02 success path (result==1). If a server sends S2C 0x03 without a prior successful 0x02 on this connection, ECX may be NULL or stale and CSNSocket::Add would fault (crash). SubHandler5 ignores 0x8A/0x8B unless cardobj+0x0 (app) and +0x4 (ui) are non-null, which is also set in that 0x02 path.
specs.references: The live capture shows 0x63 with 0 bytes after a map load, which agrees. windslayer_server.py _dispatch answers C2S 0x63 by sending S2C 0x63 with an EMPTY body. That looks wrong: the client's S2C 0x63 handler (0x45CCF2) is unrelated. It reads u16 + u8 and formats '%s(%u/%u)' / '%u Players' (a player-count display), so an empty body means reading past the end. The natural reply is S2C 0x8A. PySlayer has no C2S 0x63 parser; its server_packets list has no 0x8A either.
open_questions: Name and reply are inferred from the owning object (card-deck/dictionary object at app+0xDC4, its S2C 0x8A/0x8B handlers and strings); wire format (0 bytes) is certain, semantic name is medium confidence.

S2C 0x03 already reads a u8 into player+0xE78 (= player+0x48+0xE30, the card count slot) at 0x452668; it is unclear whether 0x8A is still needed to fill the u16 id array or whether 0x03's byte is an unrelated field sharing that offset.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to register a card item in the character's Card Deck (a collection book). Client flow: (1) inventory action case 0x65 in FUN_00472f40 on a selected inventory item calls FUN_0045f9f0. That function checks that the item def has +0x154==2 and +0x14C!=0; otherwise it shows 'This item cannot be registered.'. It also scans the local deck list (byte count at charData+0xE30, u16 ids from +0xE32; charData = main+0x4CC+0x48); a duplicate shows 'This card is already registered . You can't register it again.'. If both checks pass, it stores the id in control 0x292 +0x134 and opens dialog 0x292. (2) When the user confirms dialog 0x292 (notification code 2), FUN_0045fad0 sends [0x64][u16 card_item_id] and shows the modal 'Waiting for the server to response.'.
specs.trigger: The player uses the card-register action on a card item in the inventory (FUN_00472f40 case 0x65), then confirms dialog control 0x292 (notification 2). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C47, quest_cards_misc#07): the user gesture behind FUN_00472f40 case 0x65 is DRAGGING a card from the bag (Miscellanies tab) onto the Card Deck window (window 8, hotkey B) - neither a right-click nor a double-click is involved. The confirm dialog 0x292 then reads "Once the card is registered to the Card Deck, it cannot be returned back to your inventory."
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x8B (handled in SubHandler5 @0x45FB80). Its grammar is: u8 result; if(result==1){ u8 new_count  u16 card_item_id }. On result 1 the client sets charData+0xE30=new_count and writes card_item_id at charData+0xE30+new_count*2, so new_count is the 1-based slot and equals the new total. This happens only if the item lookup and FUN_00470f00(card_item_id,0,1) both succeed (probably consumes the card from the inventory). The client then refreshes the deck UI and prints 'Registered %s in the Card Deck.'. result 2 = 'Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again.', result 6 = 'Already registered.', anything else = 'Failure to register card. Please try again in a few minutes.'. The 0x8B handler first calls FUN_00497c70(0x16,1,1), which probably dismisses the waiting box. S2C 0x8A (u8 count; repeat(count){u16 card_item_id}) replaces the whole deck list. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x8B CardDeckRegisterResult - this one box does have an OK button, so an unanswered 0x64 is not a soft-lock, but nothing is registered.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs [main+0xDC4+4] (g_ui_root copy) != 0, which FUN_0045f760 sets during the S2C 0x02 handler. FUN_00448730 only reaches this handler if [main+0xDC4] != 0 and the item-mall handler FUN_00465890 returned 0. The socket pointer is not null-checked here. After sending, the client shows a blocking 'Waiting for the server to response.' message box. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C47, quest_cards_misc#07): the waiting box (dialog 0x16) HAS an OK button, so an unanswered 0x64 does NOT soft-lock the client - the player closes the box, nothing is registered and the card stays in the bag. (Drop "soft-locks" from the design-doc note.) control0x292+0x134 is not cleared after the send, so confirming the dialog again would re-send the same id. The duplicate check runs only against the client's local deck list, so the server must also reject duplicates (result 6).
specs.references: No C2S parser in PySlayer (its client_packets only cover 0x03,0x0B,0x0C,0x0D,0x0F,0x15,0x1A,0x2B,0x2C,0x7E). PySlayer has server builders opcode_0x8A/0x8B in __init__ (KR). Not handled by our windslayer_server.py _dispatch (no 0x64 branch). The UI strings in FUN_0045f9f0 and SubHandler5 confirm the Card Deck meaning.

specs.semantics: Reinforcement completion request. FUN_004722e0 runs every frame. When progress window 0x293 is in state 3 and more than 5000 ms have passed since [this+0x60], and both reinforcement slot words (+0x64 stone, +0x66 equipment) are non-zero, the client finds window 0x28C and the first node of its equipment list. It then sends 0x68: equipment id, stone id, and the 6 option words of the equipment record copy. The server decides the result. After Send, if [this+8]!=0, the client runs window 0x28C controls 3 and 4. The two slot-clear handlers in FUN_00472f40 zero +0x64 (0x46BE08(2008)) and +0x66 (0x46BE35(2008)). Then, as on every other exit from this block, it resets the timer [this+0x60]=0 and closes window 0x293.
specs.trigger: The player places a reinforceable item and an elemental stone in the Reinforcement window (0x28C, near the smithy) and presses Reinforce (FUN_00472f40 @0x47624C). The packet goes out on the first frame more than 5 s later.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x8E (SubHandler1 @0x479446): u8 result, u16, u16, then if result==1 { repeat(6) u16, u16 }. Result dialog is window 0x29B: 'Reinforcement Successful.' / 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.' / 'Reinforcement Failed.'. The client has already cleared the slots and closed the progress bar; the busy flag [this+0x2C] is cleared by the 0x8E handler.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Send-time gates: window 0x293 is in the UI list with [win+0x3C]==3; elapsed > 5000 ms (unsigned delta, converted to float); FUN_004979b0(0x293) != 0; word+0x64 != 0 and word+0x66 != 0; window 0x28C exists; its list head [+0xB0] and node data [node+8] are non-null. If any 0x28C lookup fails, NO packet is sent, but the timer is still reset and window 0x293 closed. [this+0x2C] busy then stays 1 until a 0x8E arrives, which a server will never send unprompted, so reinforce/refine stays locked. HAZARD: 0x67 and 0x68 share window 0x293 and timer +0x60. The opcode is chosen only by whether +0x64/+0x66 are non-zero, not by which button started the bar. Start-time gates (FUN_00472f40 / FUN_004729b0): the stone must be present, the equipment must be present and reinforceable, and stone level <= equipment level. Opening the window zeroes +0x64/+0x66.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: There is no real disagreement. Both analysts described the same 16-byte wire format, u16 [this+0x66] equipment id, u16 [this+0x64] stone id, then six u16 words from the equipment record at +2..+0xC. A wrote it as repeat(6) and B as 8 flat u16s, which is why the 'structural signatures' differ. The asm confirms both: 0x47242C push 0x68 / 0x47242E Add(uchar); 0x472434 movzx eax,word[edi+0x66] + 0x47243B ebx=[0x4C7118] Add(ushort) + 0x472442 call ebx; 0x472444 movzx ecx,word[edi+0x64] + 0x47244C call ebx; 0x47244E add esi,2 (esi=[node+8] from 0x47241E); 0x472451 mov [esp+0xC],6; body 0x472460 movzx edx,word[esi] / 0x472467 call ebx / add esi,2 / dec counter / jnz 0x472460; 0x472478 Send(1). Equipment is added BEFORE stone, as both said. The node walk at 0x4723F8-0x472409 starts with ECX=0 and takes the index-0 (head) node at once. The canonical grammar uses repeat(6) because the code is a counted loop over contiguous record words; the bytes are identical to B's expansion. Minor corrections: the socket is [this+0x14] loaded from g_sock_game at 0x46EB69 (both right). A's post-send claim that controls 3 and 4 empty both slots fits the two slot-clear blocks at 0x46BE08(2008) (+0x64=0) and 0x46BE35(2008) (+0x66=0). The exact control-number-to-block mapping was not traced through FUN_00472f40's switch. B's narrower claim ('control 4 clears the stone slot') is also not contradicted. The naive scout (Add8(0x68) only) was wrong. PySlayer has no C2S 0x68 parser. windslayer_server.py does not dispatch 0x68. The S2C 0x8E success path reads exactly 6 u16s (loop counter 6 at 0x4794C4), which supports the 6-word block.
open_questions: Meaning of the 6th option word (record +0x0C): it is sent, but the client's 'has a free slot' check only covers +0x02..+0x0A.
Which of FUN_00472f40 controls 3 and 4 maps to the +0x64 clear (0x46BE08(2008)) and which to the +0x66 clear (0x46BE35(2008)); not traced through the switch table.
Meaning of the two unlabeled u16s and the trailing u16 in S2C 0x8E (outside this C2S spec).

specs.semantics: Party chat line for the server to relay to party members. The sender name is embedded in the text by the client. Two client paths reach this send. (A) Prefix path: the input starts with "/p " (3 bytes) or "/\xA4\xC4 " (4 bytes). The client sets type 0x6A and chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]=2, checks party membership, rejects an exact "/p " or "/ㅔ " with a usage popup, formats "%s : %s" (own name, text+prefix_len) into 88 bytes, copies it back over the input and refreshes chat UI windows 9/10. (B) Chat-mode path: a plain line while [g_ui_root+0x44]==2 (party tab or an earlier /p). The line is type 3, so it first goes through case 3 (sprintf_s(61,"%s") copy-back), then the mode switch reformats it as "%s : %s" and changes the type to 0x6A. Both paths then pass the second party check and the 700 ms anti-spam check, and send u8 len + raw bytes. There is no local echo. The function returns 0, so caller FUN_00446200 resets the IME result and clears this+0x14D8.
specs.trigger: The player presses Enter in the chat box (FUN_00446200, IME result string at [0x54E840]+0x104) on "/p message" or "/ㅔ message", or on any plain line while the chat mode is party (set by the party chat tab at 0x448B04(2008) in FUN_00448730 or by an earlier /p). It can also come from a chat macro slot (FUN_0043dde0) or the UI list control 0x294 (FUN_00448730 @0x44D6B3) if their text starts with "/p ".
specs.expected_response: The client waits for nothing. The S2C opcode used to show relayed party chat was not identified. S2C 0x6A (sub-handler 4 @0x46AAAC) reads u32,u32,i32+list and is not chat. The only other user of the "%s : %s" format is the S2C 0x16 normal-chat handler (0x456A16).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates, in order: the length arg is > 0 (0x446311). Curse_Engine_Clean passes, else "No cursing please" and return -1. Manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40, else the low-manner popup. [scene+0xF00]==6, else a silent return. A GM ([scene+0x970]+0x12==1) goes through GM command parsing first. The party check FUN_00498050(g_ui_root, 0x75) walks the control list at g_ui_root+0x5C0 and returns ctrl+0x3C, or 1 if the control is missing; ==1 means not in a party. This check runs twice on path A (0x446E69, 0x447645) and once on path B. An exact "/p " or "/ㅔ " shows "/p message to party" and returns 0x6A, so the IME text is kept. Anti-spam blocks a send within 700 ms of the last chat. Client-side hazards: sprintf_s at 0x4AC54D is the real CRT sprintf_s (via __vsprintf_s_l) and does NOT truncate. Output over 87 chars, or over 60 chars in case 3 on path B, calls the CRT invalid-parameter handler, likely terminating the client. The copy-back is an unbounded strcpy of up to 88 bytes into the caller's buffer. For a macro slot (37 B at this+0xE88+i*0x25) this overwrites the next slot(s). For the 0x294 caller it is a 64-byte stack buffer. Server note: the embedded "name : " is client-controlled and spoofable. Use the session character name instead. In theory, text_len can be 0 with EBX=[esp+0x20]=0 (0x446EC4 -> 0x445433(2008) -> 0x44754D), sending "6A 00". That needs length arg <= prefix_len without matching the exact usage strings, which cannot happen because all 3 callers pass strlen. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C41, chat_mail_gm#00, party#06): a length-prefixed text field carries EXACTLY the prefixed number of bytes and NO trailing NUL - the client terminates the string itself. (The wsproto codec forced a NUL into the last byte of str[<length field>], which is only correct for a fixed str[N]; every length-prefixed text in the campaign had to be sent with len+1 or as raw hex to work around it. The grammar here is correct as written.) Live capture: "/p hi there" produced payload 13 + the raw 19-byte string "TestHero : hi there" with no NUL and no local echo. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49, party#06): the "not in a party" refusal is a system-notice line in the floating overlay, not a modal popup.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire grammar, u8 len + bytes[len] with opcode 0x6A, and the asm confirms it. 0x4476A3 Add(u8 [esp+0x10]), 0x4476B0 Add(u8 [esp+0x18]), 0x4476BD Add(EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]), 0x4476CB Send(1), all on [0x54E828]. The disagreement was only about preprocessing detail. B was right that the chat-mode-2 path first runs case 3 (0x447224, sprintf_s(61,"%s") copy-back): the jump table at 0x445DE8(2008) sends type 3 to 0x447224, and only after that does 0x44545F(2008) use the mode table (0x445E68(2008), mode 2 -> 0x44594C(2008)). A's "same formatting" left this step out. B was wrong to call that step truncation to 60: 0x4AC54D is sprintf_s -> __vsprintf_s_l with (buf,size,fmt,arg) and no _TRUNCATE count, so over-length input triggers the CRT invalid-parameter handler, as A said. Both were right about the party check (FUN_00498050 returns ctrl 0x75's +0x3C, or 1 if absent), the usage popup and the 700 ms anti-spam. B's len-0 corner case matches the code but cannot be reached. Added here: the in-place copy-back overflow hazard for macro slots and the 0x294 list caller. Other references: no PySlayer parser for C2S 0x6A, and windslayer_server.py _dispatch has no 0x6A branch.

Is there a custom CRT invalid-parameter handler? None was found by name in functions.tsv, so an over-length sprintf_s probably terminates the client.

AddToHead(uchar 0x6B) opcode (prepended last, so it is the first byte)

fields.name: recipient_count
fields.dest_or_source: Loop counter BL (copied to [ESP+0xC]), prepended with AddToHead(uchar) after the body is built, so it comes right after the opcode on the wire
fields.meaning: Number of (channel, id) recipient entries that follow. Always >= 1, because the packet is not sent when it is 0.

fields.name: friend_channel
fields.dest_or_source: friend_entry+0x14 (CMessenger CPList head at +0x08; entry pointer = node+0x08; filled by S2C 0x0B/0x0C/0x60)
fields.meaning: Channel byte of the friend. An entry is included only if entry+0x20 (presence) is 0 or 4 and this byte is non-zero.

fields.name: friend_id
fields.meaning: Friend's character id (the key S2C 0x60 matches on), naming the recipient

fields.name: msg_len
fields.dest_or_source: arg1 = movzx byte [ESP+0x18] in FUN_004462e0 = strlen of the sprintf_s result (0x445751(2008) or 0x445A2F(2008))
fields.meaning: Byte length of message. No NUL is counted or sent.

fields.name: message
fields.dest_or_source: arg2 = chat input buffer (EBX), overwritten with the formatted string
fields.meaning: Display line "<own char name> : <text>", built by the client from player_record+0x206 and the typed text. Exactly msg_len bytes, with no terminator. CP949 text.

specs.semantics: Friend chat. FUN_0047ac40 walks the CMessenger friend list (list head at messenger+0x08, next pointer at node+0, entry at node+8) in list order. For each non-null entry with presence [+0x20] of 0 or 4 and a non-zero channel byte [+0x14], it Adds u8 channel and u32 id and increments BL. If BL != 0 it Adds u8 len and the len text bytes, then AddToHead(count) and AddToHead(0x6B), so the wire order is 6B, count, entries, len, text. Then it calls Send(1). No ResetBuffer is called here; the socket buffer is assumed empty. The text already contains the sender's name. The client prints its own copy locally before this function runs, so the server must not echo it back to the sender.
specs.trigger: A chat line starting with "/f " (0x529F98) or the Korean-IME form "/\xA4\xA9 " (0x529F74), or any plain chat line while sticky chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44] == 4 (set by an earlier /f).
specs.expected_response: The client waits for nothing. A server should relay S2C 0x91 {u8 len, str[len] text} (receiver at 0x45D009, same color 0xFF8EE085) to each listed recipient that is really online, and send nothing back to the sender.
specs.gates_and_hazards: FUN_004462e0 gates: Curse_Engine_Clean ("No cursing please") at 0x444AC9(2008). Manner points [player_record+0xEE0] must be > -40 (CMP -0x28 / JG at 0x444AF9(2008)), otherwise "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point." A bare "/f " with no text shows the "/f message to friends" hint and sends nothing. Anti-spam: [main+0x364]-[main+0x3E8] < 700 shows "Do not Spam." (0x4476E4). The local echo happens at 0x44776E. Then [messenger+0x74] must be non-zero (0x447779), i.e. S2C 0x03 has already initialized the messenger. FUN_0047ac40: an empty list returns before any Add (0x47AC4E). If entries exist but none qualify, BL stays 0 and nothing is Added or sent, even though the line was already echoed locally. Hazard (not reachable in practice): the entry Adds happen before the count test, so 256 qualifying friends would wrap BL to 0 and leave stale bytes in the socket buffer, and more than 256 would send a wrong count. Receivers copy len bytes into an 88-byte zeroed buffer (memset 0x57 plus a 0 byte), so a server relaying S2C 0x91 must keep len <= 87. sprintf_s uses a 0x58 buffer, so the client-built text is <= 87 bytes.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts derived the same wire layout: after the opcode come u8 count, then count x (u8 channel, u32 id), then u8 len, then len text bytes. The "structural signature" difference is only in typing and truncation. A typed the text as bytes[msg_len]; B typed it as str[text_len], and B's signature string simply dropped the final field. The asm at 0x47ACA1-0x47ACE9 settles it. arg1 (EDI = [ESP+0x14]) is pushed once for Add(uchar) at 0x47ACAC, then pushed again as N together with arg2 ([ESP+0x18]) for Add(char*,N) at 0x47ACBE. After that come AddToHead(BL) at 0x47ACD5, AddToHead(0x6B) at 0x47ACDF and Send(1) at 0x47ACE9. There is no NUL and no other field, so both layouts are correct. Because the payload is client-formatted display text (sprintf_s "%s : %s" at 0x4470F4 and 0x4474E2, with strlen stored at 0x445751(2008) and 0x445A2F(2008)), str[msg_len] (exactly len bytes, no terminator) is the right DSL type; on the wire it is identical to bytes[msg_len]. On the one factual point where they differ, A is right and B left it open: the delivery packet is S2C 0x91. Its handler at 0x45D009 reads u8 len (IAT 0x4C70F0) and then len chars (IAT 0x4C70EC) into an 88-byte buffer, and prints them with color 0xFF8EE085. That constant appears in only two places in the corpus: the /f local echo at 0x447761 and 0x45D0E0. A's manner-point gate is confirmed (CMP [rec+0xEE0],-0x28 / JG at 0x444AF9(2008)). Socket: CMessenger+0x74 = g_sock_game, loaded at 0x46F86A(2008) and stored at 0x46F934(2008), as both analysts said. Other references: PySlayer has no C2S parse_0x6B (its S2C 0x6B is unrelated). Our server's _dispatch has no 0x6B branch. Not in the memory notes or the opcode atlas.

It is not proven that friend_id (entry+0x18) shares the id space of entity uid (+0x84) or the character DB id.

fields.name: trap_skill_id
fields.meaning: Skill id of the trap that fired, level-specific, always 0xA31..0xA3B (2609..2619, 11 levels of one trap skill). It is the u16 at +0 of the owner's effect slot.
fields.dest_or_source: word [slot+0x00], slot = owner_entity+0xE84+i*0x18 (i=0..20); the same value is also copied to owner+0x8D4

specs.semantics: Sent when a trap the player placed is set off. Every 30 ms tick the client walks the owner entity's 21 effect slots at +0xE84 (each 0x18 bytes: +0 u16 skill_id, +6 u16 x, +8 u16 y, +0xC i32 remaining ms, +0x14 u32 caster uid). For a slot whose skill is 0xA31..0xA3B and still has time left, it builds the hit box with GetColRect(sprite 0xE1, x, y, 0x1E, 2). It then finds the first entity in the scene list whose collision box (FUN_0041dc70) overlaps that box. On a hit the client locally: sets owner+0x950 = 0xC (a catch/grab state that FUN_00412c60 turns into 9 on the next tick); links the two entities (owner+0xD78 = owner+0xD64 = victim uid, victim+0xD80 = victim+0xD60 = owner uid); sets victim+0x958 = 600; stores the victim-owner dx/dy in owner+0x1328/+0x1330; sets owner+0x8D4 = skill_id (FUN_004194f0 uses it as the damage source, see the push 0xA31 at 0x4197F6); and zeroes the slot timer. It then sends [0x6C][u16 skill_id] on the game socket. The packet tells the server that this trap fired. Because it carries no victim uid, the server has to work out the victim itself, or get it from the grab block of the next C2S 0x0D.
specs.trigger: Automatic, from the fixed-step sim tick FUN_0042c920 -> FUN_00416ab0. Sent when a monster (or, in PvP, an enemy-team player) walks into a trap placed with a 0xA31..0xA3B skill (placed via C2S 0x15 with x,y). No user click is involved.
specs.expected_response: The client does not wait for any reply. A server should probably apply the trap's effect/damage to the caught entity and remove the consumed trap slot on the owner (for example via its effect-removal / skill-hit S2C). The client zeroes only the slot timer and never clears the slot itself.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Victim eligibility, evaluated in scene-list order with the first match used: victim != owner; and either (victim +0x98 == 3 AND room_info+0x70 == 1 AND victim team +0x14EB != owner team) or (owner +0x98 == 3 AND victim +0x98 == 4 AND victim +0xE64 (gamedef category) >= 3, i.e. an AI monster). The branch 'owner +0x98 == 4 AND victim uid == scene+0x220' can never match here because the owner is already required to be state 3. Also required: victim +0x904 (action) not in {0x14, 0x10, 0x16}; if victim +0xDF0 > 0 or action in {3, 0x17}, the victim must be state 4; the boxes must overlap; victim +0x94C == 0 (not already caught). At most one 0x6C per owner per tick, because owner+0x950 becomes nonzero. The caller only runs this function when room_info+0x70 == 0, so in practice the owner must be a state-3 entity whose uid == scene+0x220. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C28, combat_skill#22): there is NO reachability problem - in normal field play (scene+0xF00 == 6) the local player spawned by S2C 0x07 IS a state-3 entity and C2S 0x6C fires. Live facts to use instead: the trap slot needs +0xC > 0 and the client counts it down from the skill's Con (7020 ms), so a trap is live for about 7 s client-side; MP cost -16 per placement; one trap slot only (a re-cast replaces it). Victim eligibility has an unexplained extra condition: server-spawned 0x1A monsters (action_state 0, +0xDF0 = -20) were never caught, even at the trap's exact x,y, while client-revived monsters (action 0xC, +0xDF0 = 0) were caught instantly. Nothing on the client stops the same trap from being re-reported once the server refreshes the slot timer.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to teleport the player to the chosen map, using one charge of a Region Warp Stone. The client packs the region-window slot (v/10000) and the map id (v%10000) into one int, but only the map id goes on the wire. After OK the client clears the item id on that region window and closes it. It shows no waiting dialog.

specs.gates_and_hazards: No packet is sent if the u16 item_id is 0 or dest_map_id <= 0; the region window is still reset and closed when v/10000 >= 1. Region windows opened without a warp stone have +0x134 == 0, so confirmation window 0x471 never opens (0x44B6BB(2008)). specs.semantics: Buys more friend-list slots at the Frenaiga NPC service window 0x47B. On OK (ctrl 2) the client checks gold >= 50,000 and friend capacity (CMessenger+0xD1) < 50, then sends the bare opcode. It does not deduct gold or raise capacity locally; the server must do both and report back with S2C 0x9D. No amount or slot count is sent, so the server decides the increment and the price. CMessenger+0xD0 is the current friend count and +0xD1 the capacity; S2C 0x0B fills capacity first.
specs.trigger: OK (ctrl 2) in the Frenaiga friend-slot expansion window 0x47B.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x9D (handler 0x47D408): u8 result. result==1: u8 new_capacity -> CMessenger+0xD1, u64 gold -> info+0x228 (gold HUD refresh), message box 'You added him/her on your friend list...', and window 0x176 ctrl 0x13 label '(count/capacity)'. Otherwise: 'You failed to added him/her on your friend list.'
specs.gates_and_hazards: The client requires gold >= 50000 and capacity < 50; the server must check both again. CMessenger+0x74 is not NULL-checked on this path, so the client crashes if the messenger was never initialised (S2C 0x03). The 50000 check is only a minimum-gold gate; the actual cost comes from the server through the u64 gold in 0x9D.

The difference was notation only ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm shows no Add on this path between the capacity gate at 0x481A4B and the Send tail. The shared tail at 0x4736FE(2008) only reloads ECX=[EBX+0x74] before Send, so the u32/str[17] Adds of the 0x6D branch (0x4736C9(2008)-0x4736F6(2008)) are not on the 0x73 path. The naive scout wrongly merged the two branches. EDI is still 1: it is set at 0x472928(2008) and not written on the route 0x47292D(2008) -> 0x472DC1(2008) -> 0x47320A(2008) -> 0x473615(2008) -> 0x481A16. On the expected response A is right and B's 'not identified' is superseded: S2C 0x9D at 0x47D408 reads u8 result, then u8 into CMessenger+0xD1 (0x47D43A/0x47D441) and u64 into info+0x228 (0x47D464), and prints '(%u/%u)' from +0xD0/+0xD1. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.

specs.name: PortalEnterRequest
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x54E828], TCP <game port from the S2C 0x01 channel entry; 7022 was the 2008 hardcoded value>)

locations.role: per-tick UI/world updater (EBX = game_state 0x54EBD0), called from FUN_0042c920 once per logic tick
call FUN_00407350(this=[scene+0xF88], EAX=trunc(posX), EDI=trunc(posY), &event, &value_num), which finds the map line underfoot
line lookup; returns the 0-based index in the map's line list (list at +0x58 built by FUN_00406680)

specs.grammar: u32 portal_line_index

fields.name: portal_line_index
fields.dest_or_source: return value of FUN_00407350 (EAX to ESI), Add(ulong) 0x4C70E0
fields.meaning: 0-based position, among ALL entries of the current map's collision-line list ([scene+0xF88]+0x58, built layer by layer, sprite by sprite, line by line in FUN_00406680), of the first line with type 0, event != 0, y1 == trunc(posY) and x1 <= trunc(posX) <= x2. Sent only when that line's sprite 'event' attribute == 1 (portal). This is the 'portal_code' used by PySlayer/our portals.json (capture 0x17 = 23 on map 101).

specs.semantics: Asks the server to use the portal the local player is standing on. The client does not change map by itself; it relies on the server's change-map/spawn packets. The line's value_num attribute is fetched but NOT sent.
specs.trigger: Player presses Up while standing on a portal. The check runs every logic tick and requires: scene+0xF00 == 6; [0x70EED8(2008)]+0x70 == 0 (not a P2P room); player (scene+0x970) != 0; player+0x8B4 == 4 (Up input); player+0x904 == 8 or 0xC; and app+0x364 (now, ms) > app+0x470 + 2500 (2.5 s cooldown). When these gates pass, app+0x470 = now whether or not a packet goes out.
specs.expected_response: Server change-map sequence: S2C 0x08 (new map code) then S2C 0x07 re-spawn at the destination (PySlayer). Our server also sends 0x03/0x0A/0x28/0x44. The send site has no client-side wait dialog or timer. The reply is the mandatory map-enter sequence S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07 (-> 0x0A/0x28/0x44 -> 0x1A), live-captured for the 101 -> 102 portal. Do NOT answer with a bare 0x08: it destroys the local player and hangs the client on the loading overlay (C1).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Latent client bug: if no line matches, FUN_00407350 returns 0 without writing the event out-param. The caller then tests an uninitialized stack slot ([ESP+0x14], also written at 0x42EB91 with entity+0x15B4). If that stale value is 1, a spurious 0x7E with index 0 is sent. The server must validate (map, index) against its portal table and ignore unknown entries, as our server already does. Match requires the truncated Y to equal the line's y1 exactly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C17, world_movement_npc#04/#06, shop_storage#20): EN portal indices differ from the KR-derived portals.json. Live: 101 -> 102 = 23 (0x17), 102 -> 101 = 31 (0x1F) (portals.json also carries an unused 102_26), 102 -> 103 = 17 (0x11) - portals.json only has 102_14, which is why every map past 102 is unreachable on the EN client. Map 201 additionally has an event portal tile to 9701 (flea market) at (2600,1600) with no portals.json entry at all. The map-101 portal trigger is at world (~1412, 814) - the MIDDLE depth tier: Up moves one depth tier back, Down moves one tier forward and fires the portal. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C18, world_movement_npc#04): the 2.5 s cooldown holds for presses made INSIDE the window, but input made during the ~1.5 s map load is NOT dropped - a second Down press made then fires another 0x7E right after the cooldown expires (observed 3.06 s apart), bouncing the player back through the arrival portal. The server should ignore a 0x7E that arrives within ~3 s of a transfer (or while the arrival spawn still sits on the destination's reverse portal tile).
specs.references: Agrees with PySlayer parse_7E (up32u(payload[1:5]) = portal_code, looked up per current map) and our _handle_change_map (struct '<I', key f'{cur_map}_{portal_code}'). The capture '17 00 00 00' matches.
open_questions: Semantics of player+0x904 values 8 vs 0xC (both allowed for portal use).
Whether the real server also checked player position or line validity; the client provides only the index.

Instance-dungeon flow (2009): list window 0x4C4 open -> C2S 0x2C u8 5 -> S2C 0xC2 (+0xC1); create dialog 0x4C5 -> C2S 0x18 room_type 5; join a row -> C2S 0x1A (u16 room, u8 5) or, with password, C2S 0x1C (.., u8 5, str[5]); join by number (0x4C4 ctrl 8 -> dialog 0x49) -> C2S 0x1B (u16, u8 5); world entrance objects of kind 5 -> C2S 0x1B (u16, u8 5); room window 0x4C6: ready -> C2S 0x1D u8 1, exit dialog 0x4B -> C2S 0x1D u8 3/4, kick -> C2S 0x2D, start (master) -> C2S 0x95; server -> S2C 0x2F (room_mode 5 + dungeon_ref), stages via S2C 0xA5, objects via 0xA7, result via S2C 0x36 kind 5.
specs.references: No 2008 counterpart (2008 used byte 0x95 only in the dead room-host packet 0x4284D3/0x95).
specs.verification: Read 2009 decomp FUN_00448730 lines 569-576, asm 0x44E1D6..0x44E219 and FUN_004446c0 (decomp) for the ready flags.

fields.name: version_code
fields.meaning: Client-version gate. Accepted only if == 14 (0x0E; LIVE-VERIFIED for the 2009 client, 2008 used 3) or >= 0xEA61 (60001: notice/refusal mode). Anything else: nothing more is read and the launcher runs its HTTP auto-patcher (dead CDN).

fields.name: notice_len
fields.meaning: Byte length of the notice text that follows (0 allowed). malloc(notice_len+1), zeroed.

fields.name: notice_text
fields.meaning: Launcher notice (no NUL on the wire; the buffer is zero-terminated by the client). Shown in launcher control 0x403; if version_code >= 0xEA61 also shown in popup FUN_0049ebc0.
fields.dest_or_source: heap buffer -> SetDlgItemTextA(gs+0x3E4, 0x403) at 0x451AED; freed at 0x451B29

fields.name: server_count
fields.meaning: Number of world servers. Server records are 0xA8 bytes from gs+0x1338 and run into gs+0x15D8 (selected server/channel bytes) at index 4; the UI loop draws 4 -> keep <= 4.

fields.name: server_status
fields.meaning: World status, stored zero-extended as u32. UI (FUN_00442080): < 1 hidden, 1..2 greyed, 3 selectable, > 3 hidden. 1 = no channel data follows for this server.

fields.name: channel_slot_count
fields.meaning: Number of channel slots (loop bound). Slots are now 16-byte records at gs+0x133C+i*0xA8+j*0x10 (+0 u32 state, +4 u8 channel_no, +6 u16 user_count, +8 u32 ip, +0xC u32 port); only 10 fit before this byte -> keep <= 10. Every slot 1..count that is not listed is marked state 2 = "Channel - N (inspection)".

fields.name: channel_entry_count
fields.meaning: Number of channel entries actually present on the wire.

fields.name: channel_no
fields.meaning: 1-based channel number of the next entry. The first is read unconditionally when channel_entry_count != 0 (even if channel_slot_count == 0); later ones only after a matched entry while entries_read < channel_entry_count. Must be strictly ascending and <= channel_slot_count or the remaining entries are NOT consumed.
fields.dest_or_source: temp (stdcall arg slot [esp+0x28]); copied to slot+4; slot state (+0) set to 3

fields.name: user_count
fields.meaning: Channel population/load. UI colour = user_count/200: 0 green, 1 yellow, >= 2 red.

fields.name: game_server_ip
fields.meaning: Game server IPv4 for this channel (ulong overload). LIVE-VERIFIED: host order (127.0.0.1 = 0x7F000001, LE bytes 01 00 00 7F). Passed to CSNSocket::Connect(ip, port) in ConnectToGameServer 0x440C70.

fields.name: game_server_port
fields.meaning: NEW in 2009. Game server TCP port for this channel (uint overload); ConnectToGameServer passes it to Connect instead of the 2008 hard-coded 7022. LIVE-VERIFIED.

specs.semantics: Version-server reply. Global gate: the whole OnReceive is skipped while [this+0x418] != 0 (2008: +0x408). The 2009 handler first kills timer 0xC (the version-reply timeout used by the in-game server change). It reads version_code; if it is not 14 and < 0xEA61 the launcher starts its auto-updater and nothing else is read. Otherwise it reads the notice and calls ParseChannelList (0x440A00), which fills the per-server (0xA8-byte) / per-channel (16-byte) tables, closes the version socket, copies the previously chosen server gs+0x15DA to gs+0x15D8 if that server has status 3, and - NEW - when gs+0x408 is set (in-game "change channel" path, FUN_00448730 case 0x1AE param 6) hides every server except the current one; then it redraws the list ("Channel - N", "Channel - N (inspection)", load colours). The notice goes to launcher control 0x403. version_code >= 0xEA61: popup with the notice, then the disconnect message. version_code == 14: SetTimer(launcher, 8, 300) enables and blinks Start. NEW tail: if gs+0x404 is set (in-game "change server" path, case 0x1AE param 5, which reconnected to the version server) the client connects to the remembered server/channel (gs+0x15D8/0x15D9) at once, without a Start click. Canonical well-formed wire per channel entry: u8 channel_no, u16 user_count, u32 ip, u32 port (11 bytes, was 7).
specs.trigger: Immediately after the client connects to the version server (TCP 7011); the server sends it once and the client closes the socket. Also sent again when the player uses the in-game change-server/change-channel action, which reconnects to the version server (FUN_00440880).
specs.expected_response: None on the version socket. If version_code == 14 the user picks a server/channel and presses Start (or, on the in-game change path with gs+0x404 set, the client connects by itself) -> ConnectToGameServer TCP to game_server_ip:game_server_port, where the server must send 0x5A.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Top-of-dispatch gate [this+0x418] != 0 drops the packet. Wrong version_code -> the launcher tries to download patches from a dead CDN (LIVE-VERIFIED: 14 is required). server_count > 4 overflows into gs+0x15D8.. (selected server/channel); channel_slot_count > 10 overwrites the slot_count/entry_count bytes and the next server record. Non-ascending or out-of-range channel_no silently leaves the remaining entries unread. A port of 0 or a wrong port now breaks the game connection (2008 ignored it). notice_text is copied into a fixed popup buffer on the >= 0xEA61 path (keep it short). The in-game server-change path (FUN_00440880) reconnects to a HARD-CODED version server "207.211.84.46":7011 - a patched client must redirect that string too. On the gs+0x408 path every other server is hidden client-side.
specs.references: 2008 entry 0x01 (handler 0x44D663, parser 0x4404D0) read u16 3-gate + 7-byte channel entries with port 7022 hard-coded at 0x44080E. The 2009 channel entry layout (u8 channel_no, u16 user_count, u32 ip host order, u32 port) and version_code 14 are LIVE-VERIFIED facts for this client. PySlayer (newer KR) also carries a port in the channel entry but adds a further u8 and uses version 4 - do not copy the KR layout. 2009 UI refresh FUN_00442080 has the same status/colour semantics as 2008 FUN_004414d0.
open_questions: Exact return-value contract of ConnectToGameServer 0x440C70 (decompiled as void) that the gs+0x404 auto-connect tail tests with TEST EAX,EAX was not traced; on either path the "Waiting for the server to respond." popup follows.
What distinguishes server_status 2 from 1 beyond parsing (both display greyed) is still unknown.
specs.verification: Read 2009 handler 0x4519F1 and ParseChannelList 0x440A00 in decomp and annotated asm end to end; GetDataFromPacket calls resolved to overloads through the 2009 PE import table (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 u8, 0x4C70F4 u16, 0x4C70F8 f64, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7100 int, 0x4C7104 ulong, 0x4C7108 uint, 0x4C710C u64), including register-indirect CALL ESI/EDI/EBX reads; compared statement by statement with 2008 handler 0x44D663 / parser 0x4404D0. Folded in the live-verified version_code 14 and u32 port. Grammar validated with wsproto.Grammar; 19-byte example length computed with wsproto encode.
specs.blind_confidence: n/a (single-pass 2009 port; no independent blind derivation)
specs.diff_vs_2008: CHANGED: accepted version_code 3 -> 14; each channel entry gains a trailing u32 game_server_port (7 -> 11 bytes) that ConnectToGameServer now uses (no hard-coded 7022); channel slot records 12 -> 16 bytes and server records 0x80 -> 0xA8 (client-side only). New client behaviour: KillTimer 0xC on entry, hide-other-servers filter when gs+0x408 is set, and automatic ConnectToGameServer when gs+0x404 is set (in-game change server/channel).

specs.semantics: 2009 login result (FUN_00451960 case 2, 0x451CF0). result != 1: close the game socket; if gs+0x404 != 0 reload main99_01.hmi and FUN_004405B0; show the dialog for the code (see result). result == 1 and gs+0x408 != 0 (relogin / change-channel pending): hide windows 0x16/0x73, FUN_00441C60, gs+0x400 = 0 and immediately send C2S 0x2B {u8 gs+0x524, u8 gs+0x528, u8 gs+0x52C, u8 gs+0x534, u8 gs+0x530, str[16] scene+0x228, u32 scene+0x248, str[17] scene+0x20C, u8 scene+0x152} plus SetTimer(2, 5500 ms); nothing else of the packet is read. result == 1 and gs+0x408 == 0: FUN_0043D810, gs+0x16F8 = 0, hide 0x16/0x73, load ./hs/main99_02.hmi, window 0x12, scene mode 5 (FUN_004405B0 with EDI=5), scene+0xF84/+0xF88 = 0, then the header reads; scene+0x130 is forced to 1; for each record a 0x16B8 entity (FUN_00423D00) is filled, posX int +0x165C = 110*(i+1), posY +0x1660 = 300 (f64 copies +0x1298/+0x1328), alive +0x9C = 3, uid +0x88 = 30000000+i, +0x962 = 1, HP +0xA0 = 100, level +0x9D from exp (FUN_004415D0), +0x9E = 99, FUN_00422FC0 adds it to the scene (not as local player) and +0x940 = 4. Then transfer_status -> gs+0x170A, scene+0xF30 = 0, three subsystem resets (FUN_00489750, FUN_0046EB60, FUN_0045F760), GetPeerName -> gs+0x1690 and the UDP broadcast u8 0x11 + u32 scene+0x224 to 255.255.255.255:42907 (0xA79B) on the map socket.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x01 login (after 0x5A). Also re-sent after character creation to refresh the list (our server does this).
specs.expected_response: Normal success: no TCP reply; UDP broadcast u8 0x11 + u32 account_id to port 42907. Relogin success (gs+0x408): C2S 0x2B enter-world immediately (layout in semantics). Failure: none (socket closed by the client).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Global drop gs+0x418. A success 0x02 with gs+0x408 set is a relogin: the client reads only the result and sends C2S 0x2B by itself, so the server must be ready to take a 0x2B right after 0x02 on a change-channel reconnect (the full 0x02 payload may still be sent; it is ignored). The 2008 hazards very likely still apply (entities appended on a second success 0x02; level derived from exp) - not re-tested on 2009. Bad password must now be result 0x14 (0x11 means "ID does not exist").
specs.references: Our _build_login_success is wire-compatible (12-byte header, 75-byte records, u8 3, plus 16 ignored trailing bytes) but MISLABELS fields: the byte it calls 'level' is job_branch (entity+0x111; sending level=1 shows 2nd-job name e.g. 'Berserker'), the first u32 'look' is total_exp, the 6 u32 'fields' are 3 u32 ranks + 3 i32 rank changes, 'unknown_1' is the cash first-purchase flag, 'has_premium' is the gender flag, 'premium_flags' is manner points, the trailing byte 3 is transfer_status. It uses results 0x0B (short payload) and 0x11 (bad password) correctly. protocol.md error list is incomplete (see result field). PySlayer KR 0x02 differs: extra header bytes and per-char layout (bool, u8, u16 job, u32 exp, ...) with 0x2AD8-byte entities - do not copy. RegisterLocalPlayer uid gate (scene+0x220) agrees with project_local_player_spawn.md.
