fields.name: channel_id
fields.meaning: Current channel/server number of the local character; byte right after the 17-byte char name at scene+0x20C. Compared against mentor_channel.

fields.name: map_code
fields.meaning: Map xml code (e.g. 101). Used only to build the map path sprintf("%s%s%02u_%02u.hmi", prefix, "stage", map_code/100, map_code%100) and load it.

fields.name: game_clock_ms
fields.meaning: Synchronized game clock in ms (scene clock, +30 per logic tick). Also written by S2C 0x08.

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Gold (inventory "%I64u").

fields.name: exp_total
fields.meaning: Cumulative experience (exp bar vs cumulative curve table).

fields.name: fame_points
fields.meaning: Fame/honor points; converted to a rank icon.

fields.name: winnie_points
fields.meaning: Shown as "%u" in the stats UI. Name from PySlayer.

fields.name: battle_win
fields.meaning: Battlefield wins.

fields.name: battle_lose
fields.meaning: Battlefield losses.

fields.name: battle_ko
fields.meaning: Battlefield KOs.

fields.name: battle_down
fields.meaning: Battlefield downs.

fields.name: gender
fields.meaning: NEW in 2009. Local character gender flag. The same scene byte is set to 1 by S2C 0x02, toggled by the character-creation UI (FUN_00448730 cases 0x1E/0x1F: 1 -> default part ids 0x65/0x66, 0 -> 1/2), sent in C2S 0x0E (create character) and copied into the preview entity gender byte +0x11B (0x457404). Which value is male/female is not confirmed.

fields.name: mentor_id
fields.meaning: Mentor character id; 0 = no mentor (sub-block skipped). Non-zero allocates a 0x24-byte messenger entry (+0x18 = id, +0x20 = 1) prepended to the messenger mentor list.

fields.name: mentor_name
fields.meaning: Mentor character name (only if mentor_id != 0). Exactly 17 raw bytes.

fields.name: mentor_channel
fields.meaning: Mentor online status/channel (only if mentor_id != 0). 0x66 = offline -> entry+0x14 = 0, state (+0x1C) = 1; equal to channel_id -> state 0; any other value -> state 4 (online on another channel).

fields.name: unk_e90
fields.meaning: Unknown scene flag (2008 unk_e78 at scene+0xE78; same position in the packet). PySlayer KR analog sends 10.

fields.name: active_quest_id[5]
fields.meaning: CHANGED: 5 active quest-log slots (2008: 3). 0 = empty.

fields.name: active_quest_progress[5]
fields.meaning: CHANGED: per-slot progress counters for the 5 active quests (2008: 3). The 5 "ready to complete" flags scene+0x2B7..+0x2BB are zeroed first (0x452D05), not read.

fields.name: equip_tab_slots
fields.meaning: Equipment inventory tab capacity (1..45).

fields.name: consume_tab_slots
fields.meaning: Consumable tab capacity (<= 45).

fields.name: etc_tab_slots
fields.meaning: Etc/material tab capacity (<= 45).

fields.name: completed_quest_count
fields.meaning: Number of completed-quest records. Arrays hold 85 entries; NO bounds check.

fields.name: completed_quest_id
fields.meaning: Completed quest id (array memset 0xAA bytes first).

fields.name: completed_quest_times
fields.meaning: Times that quest was completed (array memset 0x55 bytes first).

fields.name: equip_item_count
fields.meaning: Items in the equipment tab (index = slot). NO bounds check, max 45.

fields.name: item_id (equip)
fields.meaning: Equipment item id for slot i.

fields.name: option_count
fields.meaning: Number of option u16s that follow; not stored. Max 5 (a 6th lands on record+10 and is overwritten by item_extra; 7+ overflows into the next record).

fields.name: option_value
fields.meaning: Option word j of the 12-byte equip record.

fields.name: item_extra
fields.meaning: Last word of the 12-byte equip record; meaning unconfirmed.

fields.name: consume_item_count
fields.meaning: Items in the consumable tab. NO bounds check, max 45.

fields.name: item_id (consume)
fields.meaning: Consumable item id slot i.

fields.name: quantity (consume)
fields.meaning: Stack count.

fields.name: etc_item_count
fields.meaning: Items in the etc tab. NO bounds check, max 45.

fields.name: item_id (etc)
fields.meaning: Etc item id slot i.

fields.name: quantity (etc)
fields.meaning: Stack count.

specs.semantics: Full enter-world / (re)load-map character state on the game socket. Before reading: fade-out (FUN_0043d810), this+0x16F8 = 0, windows 0x16/0x13 closed, KillTimer(2). Reads the fields above in order (scene = [this+0x4F0]); between gender and mentor_id it resets the messenger (FUN_0047a1a0). After the reads it clears the unsent 4th item tab, refreshes the friend/inventory/quest/stat UI panels, builds the stage path from map_code and loads the map (a failure only logs), resets the scene (FUN_0042dcf0), destroys every entity including the local player (FUN_00424130), frees the scene lists (FUN_00428750), shows the map name (truncated to 20 chars + "...") in UI texts 4 and 0x17, spawns the map-file NPCs (FUN_00445970), resets the window-0xB HUD buttons, shows the character name (scene+0x20C) in text 0x4E, sets game mode scene+0xF18 = 7, SetTimer(6, 240000) and SetTimer(0xB, 7000), and finally sends three zero-length C2S packets: 0x2F (messenger friend list, messenger socket, only if initialised), 0x63 (card deck list, [this+0xE34]) and NEW 0x8A (messenger socket, only if initialised). Wire changes vs 2008: a bool gender after battle_down, and 5 active-quest ids + 5 progress bytes instead of 3 + 3.
specs.trigger: Send in response to C2S 0x2B (enter game) and on every map change (2008 live-proven sequence 0x08, 0x03, 0x07, 0x0A, 0x28, 0x44, 0x1A). Must be followed by S2C 0x07 containing the local player because 0x03 destroys every entity.
specs.expected_response: Client immediately sends C2S 0x2F (0 bytes, only if the messenger socket is set), C2S 0x63 (0 bytes) and, NEW in 2009, C2S 0x8A (0 bytes, messenger socket, only if set). 2008 LIVE-VERIFIED map-enter sequence (0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07 -> HP/MP -> 0x1A) is expected to hold; not re-verified on 2009.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No opcode-specific gate (generic OnReceive gate [this+0x418]). No bounds checks on list counts: completed_quest_count > 85, any item list > 45 or option_count > 5 corrupts adjacent client state. Tab capacities must be 1..45. The 5 quest ready flags are zeroed and not sent (re-send S2C 0x59 for quests that are ready). mentor_channel 0x66 = offline. Destroys every entity including the local player: without a following 0x07 the client stays on the loading overlay (2008 live finding). A 2008-format 0x03 (64 bytes) sent to the 2009 client misparses from the gender byte on: mentor_id shifts by one byte and the quest/tab/list fields desync.
specs.references: Our server _build_pyslayer_opcode_03 (2008 layout: 3+3 quest slots, no gender byte) must be updated for 2009. PySlayer opcode_0x03.py (newer KR) already had the extra bool before mentor id and 5 quest slots - the 2009 EN client adopted exactly those two KR changes, but NOT the KR " " offline marker (2009 EN still tests 0x66), the KR 48-byte item records or the KR trailing u32. Scene offsets shifted: channel +0x217 -> +0x21D, clock +0xF1C -> +0xF34, gold +0x270 -> +0x278, stats +8, tabs +0x3A9 -> +0x3BB, item arrays +0x18.
open_questions: Which gender value is male and which female (0x130 = 1 selects default part ids 0x65/0x66 in character creation) is unconfirmed.
Purpose of the new zero-length C2S 0x8A sent after 0x03 on the messenger socket (not present in the 2008 client) was not traced.
scene+0xE90 (unk_e90) purpose unknown, as in 2008.
item_extra and option_value meanings unconfirmed, as in 2008.
specs.verification: Read 2009 handler 0x452A3D..0x453583 in decomp and annotated asm; GetDataFromPacket calls resolved to overloads through the 2009 PE import table (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 u8, 0x4C70F4 u16, 0x4C70F8 f64, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7100 int, 0x4C7104 ulong, 0x4C7108 uint, 0x4C710C u64), including register-indirect CALL ESI/EDI/EBX reads; compared read-by-read with 2008 handler 0x44E38F (loop bounds checked in asm: 2008 CMP EAX,0x2A4 / CMP EAX,3 vs 2009 CMP EAX,0x2B2 / CMP EAX,5). Grammar validated with wsproto.Grammar; minimum length 71 computed with wsproto encode.
specs.blind_confidence: n/a (single-pass 2009 port; no independent blind derivation)
specs.diff_vs_2008: CHANGED: new bool gender after battle_down (before mentor_id); active quests 3 -> 5 (repeat(5) u16 ids then repeat(5) u8 progress). Min length 64 -> 71. Everything else identical in order and width. Behaviour: additionally sends C2S 0x8A after 0x2F/0x63.

u32 uid

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Player uid. Matched against entity+0x84 of scene entities whose state byte +0x98 is 3 (player) or 1 (spectator). Monsters (+0x98==4) and unknown uids are ignored. The local player (state 3, uid == scene+0x220) also matches.
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 offsets; 2009 map in notes] sender: scene+0x220 (0x423692/0x4237A2); receiver: compared at 0x42388B

fields.name: input_a
fields.meaning: Primary input, encoded action*10 + dir (u8 arithmetic). Ones digit -> entity+0x8B3 = input direction. The sender resets scene+0x254 to 8 every tick (8 = no direction); the key handler sets 2 or 6 (0x42B05E/0x42B045). Tens digit -> entity+0x8B4 = action state. 7 = skill cast (scene+0x255 is kept across ticks only when ==7, 0x4237FF); 4 = Up per the portal-trigger spec.
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 offsets; 2009 map in notes] sender: scene+0x255*10 + scene+0x254 (0x4236A5); receiver: entity+0x8B4 (tens), entity+0x8B3 (ones)

fields.name: input_b
fields.meaning: Secondary input, encoded variant*10 + sub. Tens digit -> entity+0x8B5 = action sub/variant (scene+0x256 = skill variant). Ones digit -> entity+0x8B6 = sub-state (scene+0x257, values 0..5 written by FUN_0042cf20).
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 offsets; 2009 map in notes] sender: scene+0x256*10 + scene+0x257 (0x4236BF); receiver: entity+0x8B5 (tens), entity+0x8B6 (ones)

specs.length: Body is 7 bytes including the opcode, so the datagram is 15 bytes and header size = 0x00F. Fixed length. If the datagram is short, the GetDataFromPacket bounds check fails: the target is left unchanged, 'Error occured in Fireway (0x10/0x16)' is logged, and parsing continues.
specs.semantics:
[2009] 2009 UDP dispatcher FUN_0045E230 (listener thunk FUN_0048B260) = 2008 FUN_00458640: same switch shape (opcode-3, index table 0x45F1E0, jump table 0x45F1C0), same per-case read fingerprints for 0x03, 0x06..0x11, EXCEPT that 0x04 has no case (falls to the default, i.e. ignored) and the arena snapshot header is re-packed (see UDP-S2C:0x07). Gates/offsets: drop flag gs+0x418, map object gs+0x4FC with map_mode +0x7C and map_code +0x1C4, scene gs+0x4F0, local uid scene+0x224, local entity scene+0x988, entity uid +0x88, HP +0xA0, MP +0xA4, popup slots +0x11B4..+0x11C8 (2008 gs+0x408/+0x4D8/+0x70/+0x1B8/+0x4CC, scene+0x220/+0x970, entity +0x84/+0x9C/+0xA0/+0x1114..+0x1128). Fireway framing: the 2009 Fireway.dll is a different build (sha256 c26665b6...) but GetUDPHeader (0x10003BC0), UDPBufferManager (0x10004340), DecodebyArray (0x10006E20) are instruction-identical except that a duplicate sequence number is now dropped without SetLastError(0x130).
[2008 description follows; offsets are 2008 values]
DATAGRAM FRAMING (Fireway CSNSocket UDP; applies to every UDP opcode on port 42907).

One datagram = 8-byte header + body.
- hdr0 (u32 LE):
  - bits 0-10 = size = 8 + body_len. The receiver trusts this, not the recvfrom length; the dispatcher gets len = size - 8.
  - bit 11 (0x800) = ENCODED flag. It is set by SetHeader when encryption is on and NoEncode is off. The server's NO_ENCODE_FLAG name for this bit is backwards.
  - bits 12-19 = seq (u8).
  - bits 20-31 = unused: the sender leaves them 0 and the receiver ignores them.
- hdr1 (u32 LE) = checksum, checked only when bit 11 is set.
- Encoding (EncodebyArray 0x10006B20 / DecodebyArray 0x10006BC0, static and key-independent; SetCodeKey is never called on this socket). T[i] = low byte of the dword at Fireway 0x1000B138 + 4*i (= cencmsg._STATIC_TABLE).
  - body[i] ^= T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]
  - checksum = (T[seq] + sum(plain[i] & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF
  - The decoder accepts when hdr1 - ((T[seq] + sum + T[seq+0x25]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq.
  - cencmsg.encode_by_array/decode_by_array implement exactly this.
- Sender (client SendTo 0x10003C60/0x10003DF0): pre-increments a per-socket seq (+0x13A8: 1..255, then 0), sets size and bit 11, encodes, and sends exactly size bytes.
- Receiver: GetUDPHeader drops a datagram only if its seq equals the last accepted seq on this socket (any source; initial last_seq = 0 from Init). Unlike TCP there is no ordering requirement, no size sanity check, and no socket close. A datagram with bit 11 clear is accepted as plaintext even though this socket encrypts.
- Dispatch: FUN_00458640 returns if owner+0x408 (WM_CLOSE flag) != 0. Otherwise it locks owner+0x368, reads u8 opcode at offset 0 and handles exactly one message per datagram.

OPCODE 0x03 (player input).
- Reads u32 uid, u8 input_a, u8 input_b. FUN_00423850 finds the player/spectator entity with that uid.
- Writes the decoded digits into entity+0x8B3..+0x8B6: dir, action, variant, sub. These are the same input slots that FUN_00412100 fills for remote players from the TCP movement queue; the entity update FUN_00413920 consumes them.
- Stamps entity+0x88 = scene+0xF1C (room clock, +30 per tick).
- Sets entity+0x15DC = 1 (activity flag) unless input_a == 8.
- No map-mode gate: accepted in field and arena modes.
- Scene bytes +0x254..+0x257 are read ONLY by the UDP sender FUN_00423260. In field mode the client sends this datagram to itself every tick (127.0.0.1:42907), so field-mode local-player keyboard input reaches the local entity only through this UDP loopback. In arena mode a non-host sends it to the room host instead (no loopback).
- EN-only dead code (host flag scene+0xF24 is never set):
  - During countdown (F04==1 && F1C<5100) or round end (F04==2), actions 1/5/7 are zeroed, and so are the input_b digits.
  - The first packet from each peer stores its source ip (str16 at entity+0x6A) and port (+0x80) and sets +0x14EA=1. The host then unicasts snapshots there (0x423759).
specs.trigger:
Generated by clients every logic tick in FUN_00423260, called from FUN_0042B260 when scene+0xF90 (map socket) != NULL.
- Field mode ([map]+0x70==0), non-host: loopback to 127.0.0.1:[scene+0x244] (0x4237FD).
- Arena mode ([map]+0x70==1), non-host: sent to host_ip:(room_no+10000) from S2C 0x2F. It goes every tick while the local entity +0x98==3; otherwise only while scene+0xF08==0 (no snapshot yet) or as a keepalive when scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C > 9000.
- A server or room host emulator would send it to the client's ip:42907 (p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port from C2S 0x2B).
specs.expected_response: None. The client sends no reply. In arena mode the host is expected to answer with snapshot datagrams 0x07/0x08/0x09 (not traced here).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates:
- owner+0x408 == 0 (the game is not closing).
- Header accepted: seq != last accepted seq; if bit 11 is set, the checksum must be valid.
- uid must match an entity with +0x98 in {1,3}.

Hazards:
- SEQ COLLISION: the dedupe is per socket, not per peer, and the client's own loopback datagrams (2 per tick in field mode: 0x04 then 0x03) land on the same socket. A server datagram whose seq equals the last accepted seq is dropped silently. The only trace is a log line 'Error occured in Fireway (304)'. Never use seq 0 for the first datagram after socket init. Resending with a different seq is safe because this message sets absolute state.
- If bit 11 is set with size field < 8, DecodebyArray loops over (size-8) treated as a huge unsigned count and the client crashes. With bit 11 clear, size < 8 just yields len < 0, opcode 0, no-op.
- A datagram longer than 4078 bytes overflows Fireway's stack buffer (memcpy uses recv length, 0x100041E8). Keep size <= 0x7FF.
- If the size field is larger than the bytes actually sent, the missing bytes read as 0.
- There is no source-address filter: any host can inject input for any player uid, including the receiver's own local player (overridden until the next loopback tick).
- FUN_00423850 dereferences scene+0xC without a NULL check. Safe in practice because the scene exists before the socket is created (0x4402E9).
- u8 packing overflows if action > 25.
- Blocking UDP loopback on 42907 (firewall, port already bound by a second client) removes field-mode local input.
specs.references:
- Byte-identical to the client's own UDP 0x03 sends at 0x4236F5/0x4237FD (Add u8 0x03, Add u32 [scene+0x220], Add u8 [+0x255]*10+[+0x254], Add u8 [+0x256]*10+[+0x257]).
- cencmsg.py encode_by_array/decode_by_array match Fireway 0x10006B20/0x10006BC0.
- PROTOCOL.md: S2C 0x07/0x05 name the same entity fields input_dir_8b3/action_state_8b4/action_sub_8b5/action_sub_8b6.
- Portal trigger spec: +0x8B4==4 means Up.
- C2S 0x93 spec: the idle check uses +0x15DC.
- windslayer_server.py has no UDP sender; its UDPMapServer class is never started, and it correctly notes that 42907 is the client's own bind.
open_questions: In arena mode a non-host client never loops 0x03 back to itself. Does the original room host (external, at host_ip:room_no+10000, since the in-client host flag is dead in EN) relay 0x03 to every client, or is movement purely snapshot-driven (0x07/0x08/0x09)? Not decidable statically.

Exact meaning of each digit value: dir codes besides 2/6/8, action codes besides 4 (Up) and 7 (skill), and the scene+0x257 sub-state (0..5). Consumers are in FUN_00413920/FUN_00412360 and were not fully traced.
entity+0x88 (last-input room-clock stamp) has no reader found other than the reset in FUN_00428090. Its purpose (idle timeout?) is unconfirmed.
specs.verification: audited: 2009 UDP dispatcher FUN_0045E230 case 0x0045E2C4 vs 2008 FUN_00458640 case 0x004586D4: jump tables decoded, read fingerprint differs (walker misses the pre-switch IAT register; decomp shows u32,u8,u8), normalized decomp diff read by hand; Fireway.dll 2008 vs 2009 export functions compared. 2008-only VAs dropped: 0x458661 (Gate: owner+0x408 != 0 -> return without reading or locking. This flag); 0x458688 (EnterCriticalSection(owner+0x368). The lock is shared with the UI thre); 0x4586AD (u8 opcode at offset 0 (IAT 0x4A4094); switch(opcode-3) with index tabl); 0x459BBA (LeaveCriticalSection. One message per datagram; trailing bytes are ign); 0x4236F5 (Client sender, arena non-host: same 7-byte body to host_ip scene+0xF38); 0x4237FD (Client sender, field mode non-host: same body to 127.0.0.1:[scene+0x24)
blind_open_questions: Did the original arena relay/host on room_no+10000 forward C2S UDP 0x03 payloads to other clients as S2C UDP 0x03? This is inferred from port and uid-lookup design, not provable from the client alone.
Are entity+0x8B3..0x8B6 values set by UDP 0x03 honored on normal field maps (map mode 0), or overwritten each tick by the snapshot path FUN_00412100? The ordering was not traced.
Exact meaning of the input_b digits (entity+0x8B5/+0x8B6), and the full action code list for the input_a tens digit.
What happens if uid is the local player (scene+0x220)? Could it override locally generated input state?
scene+0xF24 was proven write-only-zero by displacement scan. A block copy (memcpy/rep movs) into the scene covering +0xF24 was not ruled out.
specs.diff_vs_2008: identical wire (u32 uid, u8 input_a, u8 input_b, decomp lines 48-53); receiver FUN_00424AE0 = 2008 FUN_00423850 with offsets moved (entity +0x93F..+0x942, uid +0x88, alive +0x9C) and one more host condition (map object +0x2E0 == 0 in phase 1); the field sender FUN_00424500 now sends it to 127.0.0.1:[scene+0x248]

specs.semantics: Other player(s) appear. Byte-identical format and per-record processing to 0x07 (shared handler 0x453588): new entity, buffs applied, FUN_00422fc0 registers the entity into the scene list after the position is read, the remaining state is read over the registration defaults, then the pet block (remote records only) and FUN_00447f40 spawns the player's pet. After the loop the opcode check fails, so no game-mode change and no UI refresh. A record whose uid equals scene+0x224 still becomes the local player and reads no pet block.
specs.trigger: Send to clients already in a map when another player enters their map/view (one or more records).
specs.expected_response: none from this handler
specs.gates_and_hazards: No uid de-duplication (every record creates a new entity). Do not send the receiver its own uid in 0x04 (it would re-register as local player). CLIENT-STATE-DEPENDENT LENGTH: the trailing has_pet block exists only for records whose uid != the receiver's login uid (scene+0x224); the server must build each record per receiver - the local player's own record has NO has_pet byte, every other record has at least 1. Getting it wrong desyncs every following record. skill_count > 30 overflows the skill array. Buff ids 0xA31..0xA3B carry 4 extra bytes. cur_hp = 0 renders the player dead. Use idle defaults for the state-machine fields (anim_substate 8, action_state 8, direction 2, input_state 8,0,0,0, rest 0). Because pos_x/pos_y are now read before FUN_00422fc0, registration sees the real position. 2008 live findings carried over (not re-verified on 2009): remote spawn position used verbatim (send floor-level y), input/state bytes must be idle defaults, all-zero appearance gives an invisible body. A 2008-format record misparses from appearance_part onward (14 vs 17 parts).
specs.references: Same shared handler as 0x07 (see 0x07). PySlayer opcode_0x04.py/0x07.py KR layout (17 appearance, 15 equips, positions before state, trailing str[13]) now largely matches the 2009 EN client in those points, but KR cash slots (10 x 3 words) and KR IP bytes still differ from 2009 EN (10 x 2 words, idle input bytes); do not reuse PySlayer blindly. Our server has no S2C 0x04 builder.
open_questions: Which S2C removes a remote player (2008: probably 0x06) is outside this batch.
gm_hidden semantics were not re-traced for 2009.
Exact meaning of has_pet beyond "pet info follows" (it is stored at pet+0xA and later tested by FUN_00447f40 for the pet sleep state).
specs.verification: Same analysis as 0x07 (shared handler 0x453588; opcode-7 branch at 0x453E75). GetDataFromPacket calls resolved to overloads through the 2009 PE import table (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 u8, 0x4C70F4 u16, 0x4C70F8 f64, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7100 int, 0x4C7104 ulong, 0x4C7108 uint, 0x4C710C u64), including register-indirect CALL ESI/EDI/EBX reads; compared with 2008 shared handler 0x44EF72. Grammar validated with wsproto.Grammar; lengths computed with wsproto encode (383 local / 384 remote minimum).
specs.blind_confidence: n/a (single-pass 2009 port; no independent blind derivation)
specs.diff_vs_2008: CHANGED (same as 0x07): gm field > 1 now carries guild_name str[17] + 2 u16 emblem words; appearance 14 -> 17 u16; equip slots 16 -> 15 (x 7 u16); cash slots 9 x u16 -> 10 x (u16 id + u16 attr0); pos_x/pos_y moved from after direction to right after the skill list; new trailing pet block (bool has_pet [+ u8 pet_level + str[13] pet_name]) read only for records whose uid is not the receiver's own uid. Entity 0x15F0 -> 0x16B8 bytes, all state offsets shifted.

Fireway framing: the 2009 Fireway.dll is a different build (sha256 c26665b6...) but GetUDPHeader (0x10003BC0), UDPBufferManager (0x10004340), DecodebyArray (0x10006E20) are instruction-identical except that a duplicate sequence number is now dropped without SetLastError(0x130).

HP sync with a damage number for arena/room maps. Execution order (asm 0x4595B9-0x4596B0):
1. Check the map object (owner+0x4D8 non-NULL) and map+0x70 == 1.
2. Read u32 uid and look it up with FUN_004189f0 (stop if NULL).
3. Read u16 cur_hp, then u16 popup_value.
4. Opcode 0x06: entity+0x1114 = popup_value.
5. entity+0x9C = cur_hp.
6. If uid == scene+0x220: local entity (scene+0x970, if non-NULL) +0x9C = cur_hp, and FUN_00443690 redraws the HP text and gauge (it is called even when scene+0x970 is NULL).
7. FUN_0042fd20(owner) runs. It needs scene and scene+0x970 non-NULL and walks every entity. For each non-zero slot +0x1114/+0x111C/+0x1124 whose byte +0x98 is >= 3, it mallocs a 0x20-byte record {[0]=kind, [1]=value, [2]=0 age, [3]=0x14, [4]=0x28, [5]=entity+0x15A4, [6]=entity+0x15A8, [7]=style 0/1/2}, pushes it onto owner+0x430 (FUN_00459df0) and zeroes the slot. The slot is zeroed even when +0x98 < 3. Kind in mode 1 is 0 if entity+0x14EB (team) equals the local player's +0x14EB, else 1; outside mode 1 it is 0 if +0x98 == 3, else 1.
Opcode 0x06 uses style 0, drawn immediately by FUN_00430aa0.
HP 0 does NOT change the alive state (+0x98); the snapshot datagrams carry that. The handler sends nothing and does not use the source ip/port. No code in the EN client emits UDP 0x06; the original sender was an external battle/relay host.

FRAMING (Fireway UDP; g_sock_map = Create(0xA79B, type 2, encode +0x13B5=1, header +0x13B6=1)):
- Datagram = u32 h0 (LE) + u32 h1 (checksum) + body. Exactly one message per datagram; the dispatcher parses one opcode and ignores trailing bytes.
- h0 bits 0-10 = total length including the 8-byte header (max 0x7FF). Bit 11 (0x800) = encoded. Bits 12-19 = seq.
- UDPBufferManager 0x10004180 zeroes a 0xFEE-byte stack buffer, copies the datagram in, calls GetUDPHeader, then hands the listener body = buf+8 and len = (h0 & 0x7FF) - 8. The length comes from the header, not from recvfrom, and reads past the real data return 0.
- GetUDPHeader seq rule: if last_seq (+0x13AC; 0 at construction, 0x100019A2/0x100019E6) is >= 0xFF, it becomes -1. Then seq == last_seq -> drop (err 0x130); otherwise last_seq = seq, set before decoding. last_seq is per socket and shared by every sender, including the client's own loopback datagrams.
- Bit 11 clear: body accepted as plaintext with NO checksum check.
- Bit 11 set: requires +0x13B5 != 0 and +0x13B4 == 0, else drop 0x133. +0x13B4 is set only by NoEncode, which the exe does not import. DecodebyArray XORs each body byte with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] and requires h1 - ((T[seq] + sum(plain_i & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq, else drop 0x12F. T = low byte of each dword in the table at 0x1000B138; this equals cencmsg.py encode_by_array.
- Every field read is CSNSocket::GetDataFromPacket (this = g_sock_game, used only for its error callback), little-endian. A short read leaves the destination untouched, does not advance, and logs through listener slot 6.

Example plaintext datagram (seq 1, uid 1, hp 500, popup 37): 11 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 00 F4 01 25 00.
specs.trigger: The arena authority (battle server or host at the S2C 0x2F address; not emitted by the EN client) applies ordinary damage to an entity in a map-mode-1 room.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Silently ignored unless owner+0x408 == 0, owner+0x4D8 != NULL and map+0x70 == 1. In normal field maps use the TCP HP packets.
- The uid must exist in scene+0xC. uid 0 always fails.
- Seq: never repeat the seq of the previously accepted datagram on this socket, which also includes the client's loopback traffic. The first datagram after socket creation must not use seq 0. Plaintext (bit 11 clear) is accepted, but the seq check still applies.
- h0 length must equal 8 + body length. Too short: reads fail and stale stack values get written. Too long: extra reads return 0.
- cur_hp is u16 and not clamped. HP 0 does not kill; send the state via snapshots.
- The popup is assigned, and each arrival flushes. A popup shows only if entity+0x98 >= 3 and the value is non-zero, and it needs scene+0x970 non-NULL (otherwise the slot stays pending).
- No source-address validation.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the wire bytes (u32, u16, u16), the stack slots ([esp+0x30] -> +0x9C, [esp+0x18] -> +0x1114) and the jump-table routing (re-decoded from the binary: idx[3]=2 -> 0x4595B9). The dispute was the grammar, and analyst A is right. The asm exits to 0x459BB5 BEFORE any field read when owner+0x4D8 is NULL or map+0x70 != 1 (0x4595C1/0x4595CB), and exits after the uid read when FUN_004189f0 returns NULL (0x4595FF), so the cur_hp/popup reads are conditional. The verified TCP spec encodes such client-state gates in the grammar (TCP 0x40 'if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) { stop }', TCP 0x20 'if(client_in_battlefield_map) { stop }'); B's flat grammar drops them.
B's claim that FUN_0042fd20 'also runs every tick' is wrong for this mode: FUN_0042b260 at 0x42B4BA CMP [map+0x70],0 / JNZ 0x42B4CC calls the flush only in mode 0 (A correct).
B is right, and A silent or imprecise, on these framing details: initial last_seq = 0 (Fireway ctor 0x100019A2 XOR EAX,EAX -> 0x100019E6), so seq 0 is dropped as the first datagram; the zeroed buffer is 0xFEE bytes (byte [buf]=0 plus memset(buf+1,0,0xFED) at 0x100041C4-0x100041D5); and the checksum mask is applied before seq is added (0x10006C41 AND 0x0FFFFFFF, 0x10006C47 SUB, 0x10006C4C CMP with the seq byte). A's formula is numerically equivalent for real lengths.
The kind/style decode of FUN_0042fd20 (0x42FD69-0x42FE5A, [7]=EBP=0) was verified. Local counterpart: FUN_00418ac0 0x419EEA. The server has no UDP sender for this opcode.
open_questions: Which process originally emitted UDP 0x06: a dedicated battle server at the S2C 0x2F host_ip:port+10000, or a host peer build not present in the EN client.
Exact digit sprite sets for popup kinds 0/1 in FUN_00430aa0 (not asm-verified).

Per record: new 0x16B8-byte entity (alive +0x9C = 3), identity/looks/stats/equipment read, buffs applied (FUN_004262b0), skills read, then pos_x/pos_y, then FUN_00422fc0 registers the entity (local player if scene+0xF40 == 0 and uid == scene+0x224 -> scene+0x988/+0xF00; otherwise scene list insertion and defaults; if it returns nonzero the stats/HP/party panels are refreshed via FUN_00444ca0/FUN_00444af0/FUN_0043d790), then the motion snapshot, HP (+0xA0), MP (+0xA4), state bytes and shop block are read over the defaults. specs.semantics:
[2009] 2009 UDP dispatcher FUN_0045E230 (listener thunk FUN_0048B260) = 2008 FUN_00458640: same switch shape (opcode-3, index table 0x45F1E0, jump table 0x45F1C0), same per-case read fingerprints for 0x03, 0x06..0x11, EXCEPT that 0x04 has no case (falls to the default, i.e. ignored) and the arena snapshot header is re-packed (see UDP-S2C:0x07). Gates/offsets: drop flag gs+0x418, map object gs+0x4FC with map_mode +0x7C and map_code +0x1C4, scene gs+0x4F0, local uid scene+0x224, local entity scene+0x988, entity uid +0x88, HP +0xA0, MP +0xA4, popup slots +0x11B4..+0x11C8 (2008 gs+0x408/+0x4D8/+0x70/+0x1B8/+0x4CC, scene+0x220/+0x970, entity +0x84/+0x9C/+0xA0/+0x1114..+0x1128). Fireway framing: the 2009 Fireway.dll is a different build (sha256 c26665b6...) but GetUDPHeader (0x10003BC0), UDPBufferManager (0x10004340), DecodebyArray (0x10006E20) are instruction-identical except that a duplicate sequence number is now dropped without SetLastError(0x130).
[2008 description follows; offsets are 2008 values]
Framing: see UDP-S2C:0x04. It is the same Fireway 8-byte header (size|0x800|seq<<12, checksum, static-table XOR body; plaintext with 0x800 clear is also accepted). A datagram is dropped iff its seq equals the last accepted seq on the socket. Length is taken from the header.

Arena ('P2P room', map_mode==1) snapshot for room phase 0 (waiting/intermission). Same wire grammar as 0x04, but accepted only when map_mode == 1. After the map-code check: (1) toggle the round-timer control in windows 4 and 0x17 based on the PRE-packet scene+0xF04 (==1: zero +0x18 of the 3rd child; else FUN_00489320(ui,4|0x17,3,3)); (2) scene+0xF08++ (snapshots received since S2C 0x2F); (3) if scene+0xF04 != 0: FUN_00428090(scene,0). For a non-host (scene+0xF24==0, always true in EN) this only sets scene+0xF04 = 0. Then FUN_00442EE0 (blue/red/spectator status text), FUN_00443280 (team-balance notice) and FUN_004307C0 (camera follows the local player if it has a team, else picks a player to spectate via FUN_004305B0); (4) if timer != owner+0x1524: countdown/Fight! messages for timer 1..5 and the clock text F37*60-timer in windows 0x480/4/0x17 control 3; (5) owner+0x1524 = timer, then the per-record loop exactly as described for 0x04 (snap/interpolate position, facing, cast-echo clear, anim toggle, attack FX, action change via FUN_0042B860, +0x15AC timers, +0x15A0/+0x1598/+0x159C). Arena-only additions inside the action-change block: new action 0x10 prints '[<name>]is down.' colored by team (+0x14EB 1 = 0xFF5D9DFF, 2 = 0xFFFF5D5D), plus 'Revival in 20 seconds.' for the local player when room type scene+0xF70 >= 5. In attack FX idx 0x1F the extra 0x37/0x54 effects are skipped in arena.

WHO SENDS IT: the arena room HOST (FUN_00423260 with scene+0xF24 != 0). Each tick it sends the opcode from its scene+0xF04 (0 -> 0x07, 2 -> 0x09, else 0x08) to every peer entity's +0x6A ip / +0x80 port, which it learned from that peer's UDP 0x03 hello (FUN_00423850). In the EN client scene+0xF24 is never set non-zero, so the host is external: host_ip:room_no+10000 from S2C TCP 0x2F. Non-host arena clients do NOT build snapshots. They only send 0x03 (u32 uid + two action/dir bytes) to that address every tick, so in arena maps the display state of ALL entities, the local player included, comes from these host datagrams.
specs.expected_response: None directly. The client keeps sending UDP 0x03 hellos/inputs to host_ip:(room_no+10000) every tick.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: owner+0x408 == 0; map_mode == 1 (no NULL check on [owner+0x4D8]); hdr>>18 == map code; records apply only to existing entities with +0x98 >= 3 and a matching 25-bit uid. Phase code runs only when scene+0xF04 != 0 (the transition), but scene+0xF08++, the UI toggle and the timer block run on every accepted arena snapshot. Hazards: the 9-bit timer caps at 511 s, so for round_time_min (F37) > 8 the clock can never reach 0. The same short-read and stale-record behaviour as 0x04 applies. A server emulating the host must make count equal the number of records (the in-client host code counts only +0x98==3 entities in arena but writes records for qualifying state-4 monsters too). Seq collisions with other datagrams drop packets.
specs.trigger: Arena host tick while the host's room phase scene+0xF04 == 0.
specs.references: FUN_00428090 phase setter (writes scene+0xF04 @0x428BA5). Host sender FUN_00423260 @0x4232AE/0x423759. S2C TCP 0x2F supplies host_ip/room_no/round_time_min (scene+0xF38/+0xF48/+0xF37) and resets scene+0xF08. Not implemented in the private server.

fields.name: reason
fields.meaning: NEW (replaces the 2008 separate opcodes 0x5E/0xA3/0xA4). Popup before the map change: 1 = "Connection to PVP server was lost. Please check your internet connection." (2008 0x5E); 2 = "You were kicked out." (new); 3 = "The room has deleted due to inappropriate room name. ..." (2008 0xA3); 4 = "Your manner point has reduced due to creating a room with inappropriate room name." (2008 0xA4); any other value (0, 5..255) = no popup. Send 0 for a normal map change.

fields.name: map_code
fields.meaning: Map id; path = sprintf("%s%s%02u_%02u.hmi", prefix, "stage", map_code/100, map_code%100).

fields.name: game_time_ms
fields.meaning: Scene game clock in ms (same field S2C 0x03 sets).

specs.semantics: Full map change. NEW: first reads a reason byte and shows the matching popup (the 2008 client used separate opcodes 0x5E/0xA3/0xA4 for three of them; those opcodes no longer exist in the 2009 dispatch). Then reads map_code and the scene clock and performs the same sequence as 2008: closes window 0x259 if needed, builds the map path, fades out, remembers whether the old map was a PvP map ([[this+0x4FC]+0x7C] == 1, else closes window 0x79), closes window 0x236 and any modal window, unloads/loads the map, resets the scene (FUN_0042dcf0), closes windows 0x2A, 0x4C4, 0x480, 0x4D, 0x47A, 0x47E, 0x4B, 0x4C6, sets the map-name label on windows 4 and 0x17, destroys every entity, clears scene+0xF88/+0xF84 and refreshes the stat panel if the old map was PvP, spawns the new map's NPCs and sets game mode 7. The local player is NOT recreated.
specs.trigger: Server sends when the player changes map (portal C2S 0x7E, teleports, returning from dungeons/arena), with reason 0; with reason 1..4 when the player is thrown back to the field for that cause.
specs.expected_response: No direct Send. Must be followed by 0x03 and 0x07 (2008 LIVE-VERIFIED mandatory sequence 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07 -> 0x0A/0x28/0x44 -> 0x1A; a bare 0x08 leaves the client on the loading overlay).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No precondition checks. The old 6-byte 2008 packet is misparsed by 2009: its map_code low byte becomes the reason, and the clock is taken from shifted bytes. All entities are destroyed - without a following 0x07 the player stays invisible (2008 live finding). The fade blocks the network thread. Trailing bytes are ignored.

Our server _handle_change_map sends u16 map + u32 + u32 (2008 layout) and must prepend u8 0.

Arena snapshot for room phase 1 (round start countdown and fighting). Grammar identical to 0x04/0x07; accepted only when map_mode == 1 and the map code matches. Common arena steps: timer-control UI toggle by old scene+0xF04, scene+0xF08++. Phase transition (only if scene+0xF04 != 1): FUN_00428090(scene,1). For a non-host this does: if old F04 == 0, reset the round counters (F5B=1, F5C..F60, F71, F72 = 0); if scene+0xF08 > 1, reset every entity's HP/MP to max (+0x9C=+0x110C, +0xA0=+0x1110), clear buffs (+0xE84 0x1F8 bytes, +0x107C 0x90 bytes), recompute stats (FUN_0041ACE0) and possibly clear +0x14ED/+0x14EE/+0x14F0; recount living team members into F73/F74; F04 = 1. The handler then recounts F73 (team 1) / F74 (team 2) for entities with +0x98==3, team != 0, HP > 0. If this packet's timer == 0 it prints the start message (room type F70 >= 5: '<round#>Starting the Round.'; F70 <= 3: 'The battle is starting.') and 'The round will start in 5 seconds.'. The local player gets HP/MP = max, then HP/MP gauges, team status, team balance notice and camera target are refreshed, and the stat panel too if F08 > 1. Then the common countdown block (timer changes 1..5 -> messages/sound, clock F37*60-timer), owner+0x1524 = timer, and the per-record loop (see 0x04). The loop adds, for 0x08 only: when an entity's action changes away from 0x16 and F70 >= 5, restore that entity's HP/MP to max and refresh the gauges and team UI (round-mode respawn). The arena 'is down.'/'Revival in 20 seconds.' messages apply as in 0x07.

Sender: arena host FUN_00423260 when its scene+0xF04 is not 0 or 2, to each peer's learned UDP address (see 0x07). Its header timer is trunc(scene+0xF1C * 0.001), the only case where the timer is non-zero.

(4) Short reads, stale records and seq-collision drops as for 0x04.

Heal/restore in arena/room mode (asm 0x459856-0x459B43). UDP relay form of TCP S2C 0x40 (same wire layout), but it writes remote entity HP/MP and adds the revive-camera call. Execution order:
1. Map gate.
2. Read u32 uid; lookup (EDI; stop if NULL).
3. Read bool has_hp, then bool has_mp.
4. If has_hp:
   a. If the target is the local player (scene+0x220 == entity+0x84), scene+0x970 != NULL and its HP +0x9C <= 0 before the update, call FUN_004307c0(EDX=owner). If the local team byte +0x14EB != 0, it sets the camera/follow target scene+0xEE8 = local entity. Otherwise, if scene+0xEE8 is NULL or its team is 0, it calls FUN_004305b0(owner, 0x27).
   b. Read u16 hp; entity+0x9C = hp; if local, (scene+0x970)+0x9C = hp and FUN_00443690.
   c. If has_mp == 0: malloc a 0x20 record {[0]=0x0A, [1]=0x37, [2]=0, [3]=target uid, rest 0}, push it to owner+0x430 (FUN_00459df0), and Play_Sound(0x37, x=+0x15A4, y=+0x15A8, owner+0x1044, +0x1048, +0x104C, +0x1050, 0).
5. If has_mp:
   a. Read u16 mp; entity+0xA0 = mp; if local, (scene+0x970)+0xA0 = mp and FUN_00443780.
   b. Queue record {0x0A, 0x58, 0, uid = scene+0x220}. This is the LOCAL player's uid even for a remote target (client quirk).
   c. Play_Sound(0x58) at the target's position.
6. Always (even with both flags 0): queue record {0x0A, 0x54, 0, target uid} and Play_Sound(0x54) at the target.
Type-0x0A records are drawn by FUN_00430aa0 case 0x0A at the uid's entity. There are no damage numbers and no FUN_0042fd20/FUN_00430020 call. The alive state +0x98 is not changed.
No emitter in the EN client.

FRAMING: identical to UDP-S2C:0x06.
- 8-byte header: u32 h0 (bits 0-10 total length incl. header, bit 11 encoded, bits 12-19 seq) + u32 checksum; one message per datagram; listener len = (h0&0x7FF)-8.
- Seq equal to the per-socket last_seq (initial 0; reset to -1 once >= 0xFF) is dropped.
- Bit 11 clear = plaintext, no checksum. Bit 11 set = XOR T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] with checksum h1 - ((T[seq]+sum(plain&0x5F)+T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq (cencmsg.py encode_by_array).
- owner+0x408 != 0 drops all. LE reads; a short read leaves stale stack values and does not advance.

Example plaintext (seq 2, uid 1, HP 800, MP 300): 13 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 0A 01 00 00 00 01 01 20 03 2C 01.
specs.trigger: The arena authority reports that an entity was healed or used HP/MP recovery (potion or heal skill). This includes healing a dead local player (the camera refocuses).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Map mode 1 only (owner+0x4D8 != NULL, map+0x70 == 1). owner+0x408 busy drops the datagram. The uid must be in scene+0xC.
- Both bools come before either u16; do not interleave. Send the bools as 0/1 (the client tests byte != 0).
- h0 length must match the flags: if a flag is set but its u16 is missing, a stale stack value is written as HP/MP.
- Each datagram mallocs 1-3 effect records and plays 1-3 positional sounds (0x54 always, even with both flags 0), so do not send per tick.
- Effect 0x58 always attaches to the local player's sprite.
- Reviving via hp does not change alive state +0x98; send the snapshot state as well.
- HP/MP u16, unclamped.
- Seq rules as UDP 0x06.

The dispute was the grammar, and analyst A is correct. The exits at 0x45985E/0x459868 (map gate, before any read) and 0x45989E (lookup NULL, before the bools) are part of the parse and must be stops. The verified TCP S2C 0x40 grammar in protocol_spec.json uses exactly 'u32 uid / if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) { stop } / bool has_hp / bool has_mp / if(has_hp != 0) { u16 hp } / if(has_mp != 0) { u16 mp }'; B's version drops the stops.
On FUN_004307c0 behaviour B is more precise: 0x4307E6-0x4307FC calls FUN_004305b0(owner,0x27) only when scene+0xEE8 is NULL or its team byte is 0, not merely 'may call'.
Effect record fields verified at 0x459994-0x4599AD / 0x459A71-0x459A8A / 0x459AE8-0x459B01. The 0x58 record uid is taken from [scene+0x220] at 0x459A55.

1. Map gate.
2. Read u32 uid; lookup (stop if NULL).
3. Read u16 cur_mp, then u16 popup_value.

5. entity+0xA0 = cur_mp.

Result of a friend-add attempt. On success (1 or 0x0B) the client builds one friend node, appends it to the friend list without checking capacity or duplicates, redraws window 0x176 (count/capacity) and shows a green notice "<name>has been registered in your friend list.". On failure it formats the matching message into a 128-byte buffer and opens popup window 0x16 (FUN_00489da0). No packet is sent back. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#02): the 24-byte SUCCESS form (result 1 + str[17] name + u8 channel + u32 friend_id + u8 status) is accepted and renders correctly - the grammar here is right; the wsproto encoder was building the 18-byte failure layout for result 1. Result of a messenger personal/group chat-room invite or join. Subtype 1: the client stores room_id at mgr+0xCC and reads member_count. If the count is 0 it returns. Otherwise it opens window 0x177 (FUN_00483430 0x177,3,1). If the window can't be fetched it returns without reading the names. Otherwise it sets window+0x134 = room_id, appends each name to the window member list, and calls FUN_00489960(0x177,9). If the count is at most 2 it also adds '<last name> has entered.' in color 0xFF00A2A2 via FUN_00472430. Any other subtype reads target_name and shows a modal popup through FUN_00489da0(text,3,3,0,0). Subtype 8 first calls FUN_004723c0, which sets the friend's status (+0x20) to 1 (offline) in the friend list headed at mgr+0x8. It does the same for the single head node at [mgr+0x18] if its name matches, removes and frees matching entries in the list headed at mgr+0x28, and refreshes the UI with FUN_00470270. The client sends nothing back.
specs.trigger: Server reply to C2S 0x33 (chat invite: u32, str[17] name): a failure subtype (2-6, 8), or subtype 1 once the room is formed. It is probably also sent to the invitee after it accepts an S2C 0x10 prompt with C2S 0x34, and to existing members when someone joins (count 1 -> 'has entered.'). Those last cases can't be proven statically.
specs.expected_response: none (afterwards the client may send C2S 0x35 room chat)
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 gate at 0x4708DE: [mgr+0x68] and [mgr+0x70] must be nonzero. S2C 0x03 (FUN_0046f860) resets mgr+0xCC. HAZARDS: subtype 0, 7 or 9+ passes the uninitialized 0x80-byte buffer [esp+0x40] to the popup (garbage text and a possible over-read), so only use 1-6 or 8. Subtype 1 with a count > 0 stores room_id even if window 0x177 can't be fetched. Member nodes are not zeroed and the list isn't cleared or de-duplicated, so every name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes, and resending the full list may duplicate rows. target_name/member_name with 17 non-NUL bytes makes sprintf %s read past the buffer.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A's grammar was 'u8 subtype; if 1 { u32 room_id; u8 member_count; if count==0 stop; repeat(count) str[17] } else str[17]'. Analyst B's was the same without the explicit stop. On the wire they are identical: with count 0, repeat(0) reads nothing, so both consume 1+4+1+17n or 1+17 bytes. A's explicit early exit matches the code exactly: 0x470E7A CMP byte [esp+0x13],0 / 0x470E7F JBE 0x471FF6, which does MOV EAX,1 and returns, so that form is kept. The field widths were verified in the asm: u8 via IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x470E3F and 0x470E74, u32 via 0x4A40C8 into [EBX+0xCC] at 0x470E60, and the 17-byte char reads (PUSH 0x11, IAT 0x4A4098) at 0x470EEF in the loop (0x470F03-0x470F11, movzx count, JL) and at 0x470FA6. The analysts also disagreed on details that don't affect the wire. (1) Node zeroing: A said not zeroed and was right. FUN_0048b484 is operator new (a _malloc/_callnewh loop) with no memset, and only 17 bytes are written, so B's 'zeroed node' is wrong. (2) Subtype 8 side effects: each analyst was partly right. The code at 0x4723C0-0x47242B marks the friend found by FUN_00472180 in the list headed at [mgr+8] (+0x20=1) and also compares only the head node of [mgr+0x18] and marks it (B saw this, A didn't). It then calls FUN_00472340, which removes and frees matching entries from the list headed at [mgr+0x28] and refreshes via FUN_00470270 (A saw this, B didn't). (3) Jump table 0x472148, dumped from the binary: 2->0x471068 (0x6F4CD0 'in other channel'), 3->0x470FC4 (refused), 4->0x471016 (rejecting), 5->0x471120 (room full; sprintf '%s' at 0x4A6318, then shared popup), 6->0x471116 (in conversation, jumps into 0x47101B), 7->0x47113C (default, uninitialized text), 8->0x4710BA (not on line). Both analysts had this mapping right. Neither PySlayer (its 0x0F is the C2S equip) nor our server covers this packet.

FRAMING: identical to UDP-S2C:0x06.

Framing: same Fireway UDP framing as the UDP-S2C:0x03 spec. 8-byte header: u32 size|0x800(encoded)|seq<<12, then u32 by-array checksum. The seq must differ from the last accepted seq on the socket. Plaintext (bit 11 clear) is also accepted.

Purpose: local P2P endpoint self-discovery.
- Right after a successful login, the client broadcasts {0x11, account_id} to 255.255.255.255:42907 from its own socket, which is bound to 0.0.0.0:42907. The broadcast is delivered back to that socket.
- Handler steps:
  1. Checks that a scene exists and that account_id (scene+0x220) is set.
  2. Consumes the u32 and ignores it.
  3. Zeroes the 16-byte string scene+0x224 and copies in the datagram's SOURCE IPv4 dotted string, i.e. the client's own outgoing interface address as seen by the stack.
  4. Forces scene+0x244 = 42907.
- Uses of these values:
  - The client reports them to the game server as p2p_ip (str[16]) and p2p_udp_port (u32) in C2S 0x2B EnterWorldRequest.
  - FUN_00423260 uses scene+0x244 as the loopback SendTo port.
- No other code writes scene+0x224. The scene ctor memset (0x411FAE, +0x48..+0xEE7) leaves it all zeros until this datagram arrives. scene+0x244 is also set to 42907 at 0x4400D9 and 0x476526.
specs.trigger: The client itself: S2C login result==1 handler (0x44DFBC-0x44E012), once per successful login. Nothing on the server side needs to send it. It could also arrive from any other host broadcasting on the LAN (another client logging in) or from a deliberate unicast.
specs.expected_response: None. The learned endpoint is reported later in C2S 0x2B (key 0x42F904/0x2B, fields p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates:
- owner+0x408 == 0.
- UDP header accepted (seq != last accepted seq; valid checksum if bit 11 is set).
- scene != NULL and scene+0x220 != 0. Before login the datagram is consumed with no effect.

Hazards:
- NO SENDER VALIDATION. Every 0x11 datagram from any source overwrites p2p_ip with that sender's address. A server unicasting 0x11 would set p2p_ip to the SERVER's IP, not the client's. Another client logging in on the same LAN rewrites this client's p2p_ip to the other machine's IP. The server should not send this opcode.
- If the broadcast loopback is blocked (firewall, no interface or broadcast route, port 42907 bind failure), p2p_ip stays empty (all zeros) in C2S 0x2B.
- The IP string always fits in 16 bytes because Fireway builds it with inet_ntoa, so the unbounded strcpy cannot overflow.
- Generic UDP framing hazards (see UDP-S2C:0x03): seq collision drop, crash on an encoded datagram with size < 8, overflow above 4078 bytes.
specs.references:
- PROTOCOL.md C2S 0x2B EnterWorldRequest: p2p_ip is 'learned from its UDP 0x11 datagram's source address'; captures show '127.0.0.1' and '10.5.0.2'.
- PROTOCOL.md S2C login result: the broadcast of 0x11 + account_id to 255.255.255.255:42907.
- windslayer_server.py _fake_map_server (disabled) once sent 20x UDP 0x11 + 64 zero bytes as a guessed 'map-server response' and saw UI errors. Statically, 0x11 only rewrites scene+0x224/+0x244, so it is not a map-server response.
- The server's UDPMapServer class is never started, and there is no UDP send path.
open_questions: The earlier live experiment (20 UDP 0x11 datagrams to 127.0.0.1:42907) was followed by 'cascading UI errors'. Static analysis of case 0x11 shows no UI side effects, so those symptoms were probably coincidental or caused by concurrent TCP experiments. Unverified.
Whether the original server actually used p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port from C2S 0x2B to broker arena P2P, or the room host at host_ip:room_no+10000 learned addresses from datagram sources instead.

The windslayer_server.py comment near line 841 attributes 'cascading UI errors' to a 20x UDP 0x11 experiment. This UDP handler has no UI calls, so the cause lies elsewhere (unverified).
Did the original server use C2S 0x2B p2p_ip for anything, such as NAT detection or arena host selection?

specs.name: SetBaseStat
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 stat_index
u16 value

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: uid (entity+0x84) of the entity whose allocated base stat is set
fields.dest_or_source: stack local; FUN_00419450 lookup key (entity+0x88), compared to scene+0x224

fields.name: stat_index
fields.meaning: 0=Strength (+0xE6), 1=Dexterity (+0xE8), 2=Intelligence (+0xEA, drives max MP), 3=Spirit (+0xEC, drives max HP). Values > 3 write nothing, but the derived-stat recalc and stat-window refresh still run

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: new ABSOLUTE allocated base-stat value (assignment, not a delta)

specs.semantics:
2009 (asm 0x459557..0x459731): reads u32 uid, u8 stat_index, u16 value; FUN_00419450 entity lookup (null -> stop). switch(stat_index) jump table 0x45E1FC: 0 word +0xF0 @0x4595E5, 1 +0xF2 @0x4595F6, 2 +0xF4 @0x459607 then FUN_004294E0 max-MP recalc (no level test) + party MP bar (+0xA4/+0x11B0), 3 +0xF6 @0x4596C2 then FUN_004292A0 max-HP recalc + FUN_0043D6A0 party HP. Then FUN_0041B830 derived stats @0x459707 and, if uid == scene+0x224, FUN_004431A0 stat window @0x459727.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
All three fields are always read first. entity = FUN_004189f0(scene, uid); if it is null, stop (break at 0x4547EF). Switch on stat_index (jump table 0x4585E4, verified: 0->0x45480A, 1->0x45481B, 2->0x45482C, 3->0x4548F0; >3 -> 0x45492D):
- Case 0: word +0xE6 = value.
- Case 1: word +0xE8 = value.
- Case 2: word +0xEA = value. If level +0x99 != 0, FUN_00427f40(0) recomputes max MP (+0x1110) and clamps cur MP (+0xA0) down to it. Then the party frames UI 0x75..0x78 are scanned; on the frame whose +0x134 == uid, if max MP != 0, text 2 = '%u/%u' (+0xA0, +0x1110) and bar 2 = ratio.
- Case 3: word +0xEC = value. FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recomputes max HP (+0x110C) and clamps cur HP (+0x9C) only if it exceeds the new max. If the low word of max HP != 0, FUN_0043d3f0(uid, (u16)max_hp, (u16)cur_hp) updates the party HP display.
All paths that found the entity then run FUN_0041ace0(scene, entity), which recomputes derived stats including the equipment bonuses +0xF0..+0xFC. If uid == scene+0x220 (the local player), FUN_00442510 redraws the stat window: 'Lv.%u', each stat as '%u' or '%u+%u' (base + bonus), and remaining stat points = total(level) - (E6+E8+EA+EC), where FUN_00440e10 total(L) = 9 + 4*min(L-1,28) + 5*max(0,L-29), or 0 if L > 99.
specs.trigger: Server reply to the client's stat-point allocation (C2S 0x04 in our server), or any server-side base-stat resync.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: The entity must exist, otherwise the packet is consumed (7 bytes) and ignored. The value is absolute: our server's hard-coded value 4 overwrites the real stat. Remaining points are derived client-side from level minus the sum of the four stats, so wrong values also corrupt the displayed free points. The packet never writes cur HP/MP directly; it only clamps them down after the max recalculation, so using 0x14 as a 'monster HP' packet is wrong. Case 2 skips the MP recalc when level == 0. Case 3's party HP update tests only the low 16 bits of max HP.

FUN_00442510 local stat window refresh if uid == scene+0x220 [2008 0x00454959; handler-region call-anchor(1)]

switch(stat_index) jump table 0x45E1FC [2009, identified by hand]
case 0: word entity+0xF0 = value (STR) [2009, identified by hand]
case 1: word entity+0xF2 = value (DEX) [2009, identified by hand]
case 2: word entity+0xF4 = value (INT); FUN_004294E0 max-MP recalc @0x459612 (no level test) [2009, identified by hand]
case 3: word entity+0xF6 = value (SPI); FUN_004292A0 @0x4596D4, party HP FUN_0043D6A0 @0x4596F6 [2009, identified by hand]

specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analysts A and B agree on the read sequence: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 at 0x45479F, [ESP+0xE0]-12 = [ESP+0xD4]), u8 stat_index (IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x4547BA, [ESP+0x88]-12 = [ESP+0x7C]), u16 value (IAT 0x4A4090 at 0x4547D2, [ESP+0x70]-12 = [ESP+0x64]). A appended `if(entity_by_uid(uid) == null) { stop }`. The asm shows the entity lookup (CALL 0x4189F0 at 0x4547E6) and its null break (JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4547EF) come after all three reads, and no later path reads the packet. The condition gates side effects only, so B's grammar `u32 uid / u8 stat_index / u16 value` is the correct canonical form, and A's trailing stop is redundant (wire-equivalent, but a mis-modelled structural branch). The switch targets were confirmed from the raw jump table 0x4585E4 (0x45480A, 0x45481B, 0x45482C, 0x4548F0). Both analysts are right that values > 3 write nothing but still reach FUN_0041ace0/FUN_00442510 via JA 0x45492D. B's remaining-points claim is confirmed by the FUN_00442510 decomp (FUN_00440e10() - EC - EA - E8 - E6). The stat names come from strings 0x6F3C58 Strength, 0x6F3C4C Dexterity, 0x6F3C3C Intelligence, 0x6F3C34 Spirit, referenced via table 0x701760..0x70176C. Cross-refs: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x14.py = p32u uid, p8u type, p16u value (matches EN). The KR Hex-Rays case 0x14 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 4222) reads a u32 plus four u16 deltas: a different build, not applicable to EN. windslayer_server.py _handle_set_stats (line 957) uses the correct layout but uid = account_id and a hard-coded value 4. The comments at lines 88 and 1817 calling 0x14 an HP/monster-HP packet contradict the binary.

specs.semantics:
2009: str[17] sender, u8 len, str[len] text are always read; the emote-alias / chat-log / bubble processing runs only if FUN_00484190() == 0. FUN_00484190 = the NEW 2009 client-side blacklist lookup (list at mgr+0x38, count +0x40; match by uid at node+0x18 or by name); UI text "Blacklisted user can't use this."
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Ordinary (say/map) chat. If text starts with '/', known emote aliases are rewritten to their canonical form (for example /love, /l -> /heart; /:) -> /pleased). If the result matches an entry of the emote UI list 0x294 (1-based index i), it is an emote: no chat-log line, and ANY scene player entity with that name - the LOCAL player included (live C34, chat_mail_gm#01: an echoed emote plays on the sender's own character) - gets entity+0x94 = 0x118+i with the timestamp in +0x90. Otherwise the client appends "name : text" (white) to the chat log, and a remote player entity (alive state 3) with that exact name gets a speech bubble (text copied to entity+0x1D, time to +0x8C).
specs.trigger: Server broadcast in response to C2S 0x03 chat (u8 len + text) from any player on the map.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: STACK OVERFLOW: text goes into a 61-byte buffer; text_len > 61 overflows and 61 leaves no NUL. Keep text_len <= 60. sprintf_s into 0x58 bytes: a 16-char name + ' : ' + 60-char text = 79 fits, but a 17-byte name with no NUL runs into the following stack bytes and could exceed the buffer (sprintf_s invalid-parameter crash). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C34, chat_mail_gm#00/#01): bubbles and emotes attach to ANY scene player entity carrying that name, including the local player, so echoing a line back to its sender plays the emote (and presumably the bubble) on the sender's own character. Wire text_len EXCLUDES the terminating NUL - the client NUL-terminates by itself, and a raw text_len = 5 payload with no NUL printed correctly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C41, chat_mail_gm#00, party#06): a length-prefixed text field carries EXACTLY the prefixed number of bytes and NO trailing NUL - the client terminates the string itself. (The wsproto codec forced a NUL into the last byte of str[<length field>], which is only correct for a fixed str[N]; every length-prefixed text in the campaign had to be sent with len+1 or as raw hex to work around it. The grammar here is correct as written.)
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x16.py = pstr(name,17) + u8 len + text: exact match. KR Hex-Rays case 0x16 (u32 + strings) is newer and differs. OUR SERVER IS WRONG: _send_chat_line (windslayer_server.py:1486) and _handle_chat (:897) prepend an extra u8 count=1. The client then reads name = 0x01 + first 16 name bytes and text_len = name padding byte 0x00, so every server chat line shows as '\x01Name : ' with empty text. The code comment claiming 0x451AF0 reads a leading count is disproved by the asm (first read is the 17-byte char buffer at 0x451B0D). Fix: drop the leading count byte.

specs.name: SuppressDisconnectNotice

locations.role: handler block (whole body: one MOV then break) [2008 0x00451D7E; dispatch]
reader: Fireway error 0x83 callback shows 'Transferring to server failed.' only if flag==0 [2008 0x004788E0; function-signature]

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics:
2009: sets dword gs+0x16EC = 1 (2008 gs+0x1528), which suppresses the next disconnect notice (FUN_00451800 checks it).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Reads nothing. Sets game_state(0x70EA00)+0x1528 = 1 (absolute 0x70FF28). That flag means 'disconnect already handled'. While it is set, the client shows no disconnect dialog and does not start the 5-second WM_CLOSE timer: not on socket close (FUN_00478880), not on Fireway error 0x83 (FUN_004788e0) and not on a later 0x5D. In short: 'the server is about to drop you on purpose, don't show an error or close the game'. Every write to +0x1528 in the corpus sets it to 1. Nothing clears it, so the suppression lasts for the rest of the process.
specs.trigger: Send just before the server closes the game socket on purpose (e.g. a server/channel transfer or logout) so the client doesn't show 'Connection to Server got disconnected' and close itself 5 s later.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No preconditions. Hazard: the flag is never reset, so after one 0x17 the client silently ignores every later disconnect, including 0x5D kicks and real network drops. It will not show a dialog or close itself. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, quest_cards_misc#18): live-verified - after an empty 0x17 the following S2C 0x5D produced NO dialog and the client did NOT exit (still in world 10 s later, normal HUD). RECOVERY: nothing clears the latch except a full client restart, so a session that has received 0x17 can never be told about a disconnect again.
specs.references: Matches the KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x17: *(v3+13360)=1, same 'no payload, set flag' behaviour at the KR struct offset). Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py.

The exact situations where the original server sent 0x17 are unknown. Logout and server transfer are guesses from what the flag does.

[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
1) Store gold at player_info+0x228 and refresh the inventory gold label. This happens even if the rest fails. 2) Read item_id and count, zero a local 12-byte option block (6 u16 words), read opt_count, then opt_count u16s into words 0.., then one u16 into word 5. 3) Look up the item definition by item_id; if none (item_id 0 or past the end of the catalog), stop quietly (returns 1). 4) Remove the item according to its type (def+0x154): type 0 subtracts count from u16 stacks (the whole thing fails if total owned < count); type 1 (equipment) removes the first slot whose id matches AND whose 12 stored option bytes equal the packet's block exactly, then shifts later slots down; type 2 subtracts count from u8 stacks; any other type fails. 5) Only if removal worked: show system chat 'Sold <count> (<item name>).' and refresh the inventory UI. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.

specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH HAZARD: the opts array is 6 words on the stack and opt_count is never checked. opt_count >= 6 writes past word 4 (word 5 is later overwritten by opt_extra) into other locals; opt_count >= 63 reaches the /GS cookie at [frame+0xB0], and the client terminates when the handler returns. Keep opt_count <= 5. Equipment matching: an item added with 0x18 has an all-zero option block, so it can only be removed with opt_count=0 and opt_extra=0 (or with the exact nonzero words the client stored). Equipment removal also fails if the tab capacity byte player_info+0x361 > 45; types 0/2 fail if their capacity byte (+0x362/+0x363) > 45. count=0 on a type 0/2 item removes nothing and shows no message. The chat line needs the chat window ([ui+0x59C]) to exist.
specs.references: Matches PySlayer opcode_0x19 (u64 gold, u16 idx, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16, u16) and our server's _build_opcode_19 (15 B, opt_count=0). Memory note 'combat model: 0x19=SELL' agrees. Our server's comments call the loop list 'extra'; it is really option words 0..4 of the item option block, and the trailing u16 is word 5 (the C2S 0x3C encoder in FUN_00469090 builds the same block: u8 n (non-zero words among the first 5), n*u16, then u16 word 5; non-equipment sends u8 0 + u16 0).

C2S 0x0D builder that packs the same 8-byte blob from the local player (confirms bit layout) [2008 0x0042C940; function-signature]

specs.length: 16 base (uid 4 + hold 4 + blob 8); +4 if action!=0; +16 more if action in {7,9} and sub_b==4; +16 if move_flag!=0. Max 52. Only 4 bytes are consumed if the uid is unknown.

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (remote player or monster). If no entity in the scene+0xC list has it, the handler stops reading.
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] stack [base+0x210] -> FUN_004189f0 lookup

fields.name: hold_ms
fields.meaning: Command timing. Monsters (+0x98==4): when dequeued it goes into entity+0xE48 and counts down 30 per tick before the next queued command is popped, so it's how long this action lasts. Remote players (+0x98==3): it's a delay before the command applies (0 means 30 ms).

fields.name: state_blob
fields.meaning:
Packed state, read as u32 b0 (bytes 0-3) and u32 b1 (bytes 4-7), little-endian.
b0 bits 0-1 facing: 1->2, 2->6, 0/3->8 (cmd+0x4A -> entity+0x8B3).
b0 bits 2-4 motion (cmd+0x4B -> +0x8B4).
b0 bits 5-8 motion_8b5 (cmd+0x4C -> +0x8B5, players only).
b0 bits 9-11 sub_b (cmd+0x4D -> +0x8B6, players only).
b0 bits 12-15 action (cmd+0x4F -> +0x94C).
b0 bits 16-19 move_flag (cmd+0x4E -> +0x950/+0x8EA, players only).
b0 bits 20-21 facing2: 1->2, 2->6, else 8 (cmd+0x50 -> +0x8D0).
b1 bits 0-11 param12 (cmd+0x44 -> +0x958; the client writes values like 50/250/600).
Other bits are ignored. The 8 raw bytes are copied into scene+0xEF8, which is also the local player's C2S 0x0D scratch buffer.

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: Present only if action!=0. Uid of the action target.
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] cmd+0x08 -> entity+0xD80 (0 when absent)

fields.name: target_x
fields.meaning: Present only if action!=0 and sub_b==4 and action is 7 or 9. Target point X (e.g. a ground-targeted skill).

fields.name: target_y
fields.meaning: Target point Y (same condition as target_x).

fields.name: pos_x
fields.meaning: Present only if move_flag!=0. Position X the entity snaps to when the command is applied (non-monster entities only).
fields.dest_or_source: cmd+0x10 -> entity position (2009 entity pos_x is +0x1298; consumer not re-traced)

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: Position Y (same condition).
fields.dest_or_source: cmd+0x18 -> entity position (2009 entity pos_y is +0x1328; consumer not re-traced)

specs.semantics:
2009: same reads and conditions (target_uid when action nibble != 0; target_x/y when bits 9-11 == 4 and action 7/9; pos_x/pos_y when reaction nibble != 0). Entity lookup FUN_00419450, entity+0x963 = 1, blob -> scene+0xF10. The per-tick consumer that copies the node into the entity was not re-traced; 2009 entity position lives at +0x1298/+0x1328.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Queues a movement/action command on an existing entity. The client allocates a zeroed 0x58-byte command, sets entity+0x8D7=1, reads hold_ms and the 8-byte state blob, bit-decodes the blob into the command, and reads the optional target and position fields. It forces cmd+0x04=0 and appends the command to the entity's FIFO at +0x1350 (FUN_00459df0).
FUN_00412100 consumes the queue once per tick for entities with +0x98>2 and uid != local uid (and only while scene+0xF88+0x70==0). When +0xE48 reaches 0 it pops the head.
Monsters (type 4): +0xE48 = hold_ms.
Other entities: if move_flag is set, pos goes to +0x11F8/+0x1288 and cmd+0x40 to +0xDAC.
Then for everyone: +0x8B4 = motion, +0x8B3 = facing.
Players only (type 3): +0x8B5, +0x8B6, +0x8EA/+0x950 = move_flag, +0xD78 = 0, +0x1328/+0x1330 = 0, +0x1338/+0x1340 = target point, +0x8DB, +0x8E8, +0x8D4 and +0x8E7 from unset cmd bytes (0).
Finally for everyone: +0x94C = action, +0xD80 = target_uid, +0x958 = param12, +0x8FF = 0, +0x8D0 = facing2.
This is the server-side echo of another client's C2S 0x0D movement packet (FUN_0042c940 packs the same blob from the same entity fields), and it's also the way to drive monster actions from the server.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#23/#24): a type-3 remote entity advances physics ONLY while entity+0xE48 > 0, i.e. while a node is pending. A single walk node with nothing queued behind it sets +0x8B3 2 but does not move the entity; each new node moves it for ~210 ms using the PREVIOUS node's facing. A relay must therefore STREAM 0x1B continuously - one node per received C2S 0x0D with hold_ms = that packet's logic_elapsed_ms. Measured stop-node latency behind a pending walk: 1.08 s. For an immediate stop use 0x2A.
specs.trigger: The server relays another player's C2S 0x0D movement/action to nearby clients (turning its state into uid + hold + blob + optional target/pos), and sends server-driven monster AI actions (move/attack) for mobs spawned with server_controlled=1.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Unknown uid: only the 4-byte uid is consumed and the rest is ignored (safe).
Commands sent for the LOCAL player's uid are queued but never consumed (FUN_00412100 skips uid==scene+0x220), so they leak memory.
Commands for monsters don't apply pos_x/pos_y directly (type-4 branch only sets +0xE48). Movement must come from motion/facing plus the client's physics, or the position is ignored.
The blob overwrites scene+0xEF8, which the local client reuses for its own 0x0D. The bits the client doesn't recompute (b0 bits 22-31, b1 bits 12-31) will echo back in the next C2S 0x0D.
If you queue many commands with large hold_ms, the backlog stays until the entity is removed.
The client needs entity+0xE48==0 before it pops a command. A monster spawned with server_controlled=1 and a big cmd_hold_ms delays its first command.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C29, world_movement_npc#24): monster motion codes (lo bits 2-4 -> +0x904): 0 -> action 7 then walk 12 (82.5 px/s); 1 -> 4 (melee attack loop); 3 -> jump 10/9/11; 5 -> 1 (attack loop); 6 -> 5 wind-up then 6 dash. With server_controlled = 1 the physics STOPS when the hold expires, EVEN MID-AIR, so a server-driven monster needs a follow-up command before its hold runs out.
specs.references:
C2S 0x0D (FUN_0042c940 @0x42CAAF..) uses the identical blob encoding: +0x8B3->bits0-1 (2->1, 6->2), +0x8B4<<2 (mask 0x1C), +0x8B5<<5 (0x1E0), +0x8B6<<9 (0xE00), +0x94C<<12 (0xF000), +0x950<<16 (0xF0000), +0x8D0->bits20-21, +0x958&0xFFF in the second dword. It likewise sends target uid if +0x94C!=0 and f64 x2 if +0x8B6==4 and action is 7/9. The C2S form carries extra fields (u32 time delta, u16, u32 tick delta, and when move_flag is set u32 +0xD78, f64 x4, bool...) that the S2C form drops.
The captured C2S 0x0D blob '00 02 40 53 00 60 64 75' decodes to facing 8, action 0, move_flag 0 plus garbage high bits, which is consistent.
KR Hex-Rays case 0x1B has the same structure (uid lookup, 0x58 alloc, u32, 8-byte blob, the same conditionals) but DIFFERENT bit widths (KR: 2-5, 6-10, 11-13, 14-17, 18-21, 22-23). Use the EN widths above.
Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py. The memory notes say monster movement is unsolved; this opcode is the likely candidate.
open_questions: Exact meaning of action codes (+0x94C values 5,6,7,9,0xA,0xD,0x10 seen) and motion/sub_b values. They need a trace of FUN_00413920/FUN_004158d0 state machines.

[RESOLVED by live verification world_movement_npc#24, 2026-09-17] Live: a monster under server_controlled = 1 does move from motion + facing plus client-side physics while its hold (+0xE48) is non-zero; walk code 0 gives 82.5 px/s. Physics stops the moment the hold expires, even in mid-air, so continuous commands are required. Original question: "How a monster actually moves under server control: FUN_00412100 doesn't apply pos for type 4. Does motion/facing plus per-frame physics move it, or is there another move opcode? Needs dynamic verification."
Whether hold_ms units are ms (30 subtracted per ~30ms tick is assumed).
The consumer's gate scene+0xF88+0x70==0 (a map/mode flag); when it is nonzero no queued commands are applied.

blind_open_questions: Real-world meaning of the bit groups: +0x8B3 direction codes 2/6/8 (value 4 cannot be carried), +0x8B4/+0x8B5/+0x8B6 action states, skill_kind values, sync_kind values and the 12-bit param +0x958.

What [scene+0xF88]+0x70 means (consumer and AI are disabled when it is non-zero).

specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate: result 1 adds a char-select-style entity to whatever scene is current. If sent outside the char-select screen it would inject a bogus entity (uid 30000000+n, alive=3) into the world scene. No max-character check in EN (KR checks 12 slots), so over-creating just keeps placing entities further right. Only 1 byte is read; the KR build reads a 2nd u8 and has a result 5 ('nickname available'). Do not send the KR 2-byte form (the extra byte would be ignored here, but the length changes). After an S2C 0x1F delete the surviving entities keep shifted uids/positions, so a 0x1C create can produce a uid or x that collides with an existing character.

[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Equip-change notice for any entity. The 12-byte item option block is u16[6] = 5 stones + tail, with the wire encoding u8 n, n*u16, u16 tail. The client looks up the item (must be Type 1 equipment) and the entity by uid, and aborts silently if either is missing. It writes item_id into the entity's equip grid at the slot derived from itemdef+0x1CC (kind) and +0x1F0 (alternate grid), stores the block, remembers the previously equipped item and its block, recomposes the sprite and recalculates stats. For remote players that is all. For the local player (uid == scene+0x220, bag slot count scene+0x3A9 <= 45): it removes the bag entry at scene+0x3C8/+0x422 that matches item_id AND the exact 12-byte block, and aborts if there is none. It then puts the previously equipped item (if any) with its block into the first empty bag slot, refreshes the inventory (window 9) and equipment (window 7) windows, and updates the game_state+0x700 lists for items with itemdef+0x1F0. On the current quickslot page, slots holding item_id with the same block are swapped to the old item and old block, and the quickslots are saved to HKCU\Software\Hamelin\WindSlayer\<name>. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C33, item_inventory#03/#05): 0x1D ITSELF removes one matching copy from the bag (this is the root cause of the "item equipped and still in the bag" reports when the option block does not match - and of double removal when the server also sends 0x23). The equip-tab removal COMPACTS the bag (later slots shift down) and the swapped-out item is appended to the first empty slot, i.e. the end of the list after compaction. EN Kind 11 (Wooden Stick, item 179) maps to equip grid index 5 = the Equipment window's Weapon & Shield slot 1.
specs.trigger: Send in response to C2S 0x0F EquipItem. The live capture 'B3 00 00 00 00' is u16 item 179 followed by the same block encoding (u8 0 stones, u16 tail 0), so echo the client's block. Also broadcast to other players so they see the change.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: catalog entry must exist with +0x154==1; entity with uid must exist; the local bag/UI path needs uid==scene+0x220, scene+0x3A9<=45, and an existing bag entry with a byte-identical 12-byte block. If that match fails, the grid and sprite ARE already changed but the bag, windows and quickslots are not, so the item shows both equipped and still in the bag. If the bag is full the old item silently disappears client-side (the add result is ignored). There is no bound on stone_count: the wire stays aligned (exactly n u16 are consumed), but n==6 loses stone 6 to the tail and n>=7 writes past the block into stack [S+0x230..]. Those first 12 bytes get re-zeroed; n>=13 clobbers unrelated locals up to S+0x422, below the cookie at S+0x1304, so no crash is expected. Keep stone_count <= 5. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.
specs.references: Our server's _build_en_opcode_1D_equip (windslayer_server.py ~2171) sends u32 uid | u16 item | u8 0 | u16 0, which matches this grammar; it is sent from _handle_equip_item. That docstring says 0x1D 'does NOT touch the bag (+0xf84)', but +0xF84 is the item CATALOG. For the local player 0x1D DOES remove the item from the bag list at scene+0x3C8 when the block matches, which may double up with the follow-up 0x23. The unused _build_en_opcode_1D (~2143) is wrong for this handler: it sends class as item_id and N=14, which overflows the 12-byte block. The memory note in reference_combat_render.md ('keeps the item IN THE BAG') conflicts with this static reading unless the bag entry's block was non-zero or the local gate failed. KR Hex-Rays 0x1D (doc line 5035) parses a different item struct via sub_40A010, so it is not comparable byte-for-byte. The 5-stone naming comes from FUN_004411A0 'QuickSlotStone%d%d' (inner loop < 5).

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: uid of the entity whose equipment changes. If it equals scene+0x220 (local player), the item is also put back into the local equipment bag tab
fields.dest_or_source: stack local; entity lookup; compared to scene+0x224

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item id of the equipped item to remove (1-based item table scene+0xF84). The def must have def+0x154 == 1 (equipment category) or the whole packet is ignored

fields.name: option_count
fields.meaning: number of option/enchant u16 values that follow. The client's 12-byte item-option record holds 5 option slots (bytes 0..9) plus option_extra (bytes 10..11), so send <= 5. The record is zeroed first, so fewer than 5 leaves zeros. No bounds check: a 6th value lands on bytes 10..11 and is then overwritten by option_extra; values 7+ spill into unused stack locals (no crash, just discarded)
