fields.meaning: item option/enchant value i (PySlayer calls these 'enchant'); fills record bytes 2*i
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] 12-byte record at stack [base+0x23c + 2*i]

fields.name: option_extra
fields.meaning: trailing u16 of the 12-byte item record (record bytes 10..11); meaning unknown (PySlayer 0x03 sends it unnamed)

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical (0x1E/0x24 still share one handler); level!=0 test before MP recalc removed; local check scene+0x224, bag-count test scene+0x3BB < 0x2E (2008 +0x3A9).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Removes an equipped item from an entity and, for the local player, returns it to the bag. Steps: (1) Look up item_id in the item table; it must exist with def+0x154 == 1, otherwise nothing happens. (2) If the entity is found: FUN_004269a0(entity+0x13C equip id grid [25 u16], entity+0x16E option records [25 x 12 bytes], item_id, &record) finds the slot whose id == item_id AND whose 12-byte record matches exactly (memcmp) and zeroes it. Then FUN_00426d50 rebuilds the body sprite, FUN_0041ace0 recalculates stats, FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recalculates max HP (clamping current HP), and if level != 0 FUN_00427f40(0) does the same for max MP. (3) If uid == scene+0x220 (checked even when the entity lookup failed): for opcode 0x1E, if bag capacity byte scene+0x3A9 <= 45, FUN_00423FF0 (mode EAX=1 'add') puts item_id plus the 12-byte record into the first empty slot of the equipment bag tab (u16 ids at scene+0x3C8, records at scene+0x422; the same arrays the 0x13 pickup path writes). If the item is a cash item (def+0x1F0 != 0), FUN_0045d170(game_state+0x700, item_id) updates the cash-item list. For both 0x1E and 0x24 it then refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290 on game_state+0xD5C) and the equipment window (FUN_00441a10).
specs.trigger: Server confirmation that an item was unequipped (moved from the equipment grid back into the inventory), sent to the owner and to observers so the sprite updates.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: DUPLICATION HAZARD: the return value of the removal (FUN_004269a0) is ignored. If item_id or ANY of the 12 record bytes (5 options + option_extra) differ from what was stored at equip time, the equip slot is NOT cleared, but the local player still gets a copy added to the bag. The server must echo exactly the option values it used when equipping (e.g. 0x1D / 0x07). If the bag is full, FUN_00423ff0 silently adds nothing. Equipment-category gate def+0x154 == 1. The local-bag branch needs uid == scene+0x220. option_count > 5 corrupts the record (see field notes). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C10, item_inventory#04): a block mismatch produces a THREE-WAY desync, not just a bag duplicate: (1) the bag gains a duplicate carrying the WIRE block, (2) the equip grid and the Equipment window KEEP the item, and (3) the sprite recompose still drops the item's visual (the character is drawn with an empty hand). Echo exactly the 12 option bytes used at equip time. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.

Reply to the character-delete request. Always dismisses the message box (window 0x16) first. Result 1: takes the selected character entity pointer at game_state(0x70EA00)+0x3F8 and, if it is not null, calls FUN_00422B90(scene, entity->uid). That frees the entity from the scene list and, in char-select mode (scene+0xF00==5), shifts entities by x -= 110 and uid -= 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): FUN_00422B90 walks the scene list FROM ITS HEAD and shifts every entity that comes AFTER THE FIRST MATCH IN LIST ORDER. The character-select list is HEAD-INSERTED (the last-loaded character is first), so the characters that actually move are the ones with LOWER slot indices (drawn to the LEFT); higher slots keep their x and uid, a gap is left behind, and slot 0 can end up at x = 0 / uid 29999999. After a delete the client no longer satisfies uid = 30000000+index or x = 110*(index+1). It then clears the selection. Result 2 shows 'Server process is running. Please try again in a few minutes (DB)', result 3 the 24-hour message, and result 12 'Invalid password'.
specs.trigger: Send after C2S 0x12 DeleteCharacter. Send site 0x44AB49: u8 0x12, str[17] name of the selected entity (game_state+0x3F8), str[21] password buffer (or zeros). The client only sends it when the selected entity has +0x15A8==0x214 and +0x904==8, then shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Result 1 is harmless when nothing is selected (null check). The handler deletes whatever is selected on the client, not a name from the packet, so the server must answer the request actually made. KR's success path reads an extra date struct and shows a 1-week message; EN reads nothing more, so do not append data. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08): after a successful delete the client-side uid/x invariants are broken (see semantics), and a following S2C 0x1C create - which derives uid = 30000000 + n and x = 110*(n+1) from n = scene+0x14 - can COLLIDE with a surviving character. The server should re-send the whole character list (a fresh success S2C 0x02 after a fresh login, never a second 0x02 in the same char-select session, see C6) rather than rely on the client's post-delete layout.
specs.references: KR (PySlayer doc line 5080) has the same u8 result switch, but its success path reads more data. EN reads 1 byte only. Our server does not dispatch C2S 0x12 and never sends 0x1F. The error strings are from strings.tsv (0x6F6680, 0x6F6BBC, 0x6F4E38).

fields.name: guild_points
fields.meaning: NEW IN 2009. Guild points credited with this exp gain. Present ONLY for opcode 0x21 (not 0x7F), only when exp_delta > 0, and only when the receiving client's own local entity has guild_id (entity+0x12) >= 2 (0 = no guild, 1 = the GM marker value). The client just prints "(+%u) guild points are gained." - the value is not stored anywhere
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x270]; only used by sprintf_s at 0x459236

specs.semantics: Local-player exp update; the whole packet is ignored (0 bytes read) if no local player is registered (scene+0x988 == 0; scene = [this+0x4F0]). exp_delta > 0: FUN_00429210(old_total+delta) checks for a crossed level threshold; on a level-up it opens UI event 0xA2 (FUN_00497c70(0xA2,3,1)), queues level-up effect 0x24 on the local uid (scene+0x224) via FUN_0042cd90, plays sound 0x24, sets local entity+0x9D (level) = FUN_004415d0(new_total), recomputes max HP/MP with full refill (FUN_004292a0(..,1), FUN_004294e0(1)) and refreshes the stat window (FUN_004431a0). It then posts "You've received (+%d) experience points." (FUN_00495e30, color -1). NEW: if the local entity's guild id (entity+0x12, u16) is > 1 it reads a u32 and posts "(+%u) guild points are gained.". exp_delta < 0: clamps the delta to -total, FUN_00429240 level-down check (level from new total, HP/MP recalculated without refill, MP clamped to max, stat window refresh), then "Lost (%d) EXP.". Always afterwards: scene+0x280 += delta and FUN_00443780 redraws the exp bar. The handler is shared with 0x7F (mentor exp): for 0x7F with delta > 0 a u32 mentee uid is read instead of the guild points (party list [this+0x508]+0x28), and 0x7F never reads guild points.
specs.trigger: Server grants or removes exp for the local player (monster kill, quest reward, death penalty). For a guild member the retail server evidently appended the guild points earned by that exp gain.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: The extra u32 depends on CLIENT state that the server must mirror: the receiver's own local entity+0x12 (guild id). That value is set by the local spawn packet and by S2C 0xB4 (guild join: writes entity+0x12, +0x16A1 name, +0x16B2/+0x16B4 emblem) and cleared by S2C 0xB6/0xB7. If the server believes the player has no guild (id 0/1) but the client has >= 2 (or the reverse) the packet is one u32 short/long - Fireway then reads garbage/leaves trailing bytes. Only positive deltas carry the u32. As in 2008, the packet is dropped (exp NOT accumulated) if the local player is not registered, and level-ups are computed client-side from scene+0x280, so the server total must match the client baseline.

specs.name: SetLevel
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 level

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: uid (entity+0x84) of the player (local or remote) whose level is set
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] stack [ESP+0x10C] (IAT 0x4A40C8 u32); used as effect target, entity lookup key (FUN_004189f0), and compared to party-frame window +0x134

fields.name: level
fields.meaning: new ABSOLUTE level. 0 = packet ignored after reading

specs.semantics:
2009: reads u32 uid, u8 level; level==0 -> no-op. Else FUN_0042CD90 queues the level-up effect, FUN_00419450 lookup; if found: byte +0x9D = level, FUN_004292A0 / FUN_004294E0 recompute max HP/MP, sound 0x24 at +0x165C/+0x1660, party frames 0x75..0x78 HP/MP text (+0xA0/+0x11AC, +0xA4/+0x11B0), local player -> FUN_0048AC00 (quest list filtered by +0x9D/+0x118/+0x119), then FUN_00447E10.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Both fields are always read. If level == 0 (0x4545B5) nothing else happens. Otherwise: (1) FUN_0042b580(0x24, uid, 0,0,0, 1, 9, 0) queues a deferred event record (type 9, id 0x24, target uid), which is the level-up effect. It runs before the entity lookup, so it is queued even if the uid is unknown. (2) entity = FUN_004189f0(scene, uid). If the entity is missing, jump to step 6. (3) byte entity+0x99 = level; FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 1) recomputes max HP (+0x110C) and sets cur HP (+0x9C) = max (full heal). It does this only when level is 1..99 and class byte +0x110 <= 6; otherwise it writes nothing. Then FUN_00427f40(1) with ESI=entity recomputes max MP (+0x1110) and sets cur MP (+0xA0) = max, again only if level < 100 and class < 7. (4) CSpriteControl::Play_Sound(0x24, entity+0x15A4, entity+0x15A8, gs+0x1044, gs+0x1048, gs+0x104C, gs+0x1050, 0) plays the level-up sound at the entity's screen position. (5) Scan the party-member frames, UI ids 0x75..0x78 (FUN_004830f0). For the first frame whose +0x134 == uid: if max HP != 0, write text 1 = sprintf('%u/%u', +0x9C, +0x110C) and set bar 1 = cur/max. Then, if max MP != 0, write text 2 = '%u/%u' (+0xA0, +0x1110) and set bar 2. If max HP == 0, both HP and MP updates are skipped. (6) FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) always runs when level != 0, whether or not the entity or a party frame was found (0x454694 / 0x454780). It walks a record list filtered by the LOCAL player's level range (+0xDEC/+0xDF0 of each record), class/job and prerequisite ids, which looks like an available-quest list rebuild. The local stat window (FUN_00442510: 'Lv.%u', stat points) is NOT refreshed, the exp counter scene+0x278 is not changed, and no packet is sent back.
specs.trigger: Server-side level-up of any player: broadcast to observers and party members, and send to the owner to apply the new level to the avatar and play the effect.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: level == 0 makes the packet a no-op after both fields are consumed (still 5 bytes). The entity must already be spawned for the level/HP/MP to apply; the effect event is queued regardless. The effect and sound play every time, even if the level did not change, so pairing this with a 0x21 exp update that already levels the client plays them twice. Levels > 99 are stored in +0x99, but max HP/MP are not recalculated. Because 0x442510 is not called, the local HUD 'Lv.' label and remaining stat points stay stale until another refresh (e.g. 0x14 or 0x21 paths). The KR build returns early when the entity is missing; EN still runs the FUN_004781c0 refresh. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (login_character#14): besides the stat window, the HUD level label (top-left "LV") is NOT refreshed by 0x22 either.

locations.role: FUN_0042b580 queue event type 9 id 0x24 on uid [2008 0x004545D8; handler-region call-anchor(1)]
FUN_004189f0 entity lookup; null -> 0x454775 (list refresh only) [2008 0x004545EB; handler-region call-anchor(1)]
FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 1) max HP + full heal [2008 0x0045460E; handler-region call-anchor(1)]
FUN_00427f40(1) max MP + refill [2008 0x00454620; handler-region call-anchor(1)]

record list rebuild filtered by local player level/class/prereqs [2008 0x004781C0; function-signature]

specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analysts A and B agree on the wire bytes: u32 uid (GetDataFromPacket IAT 0x4A40C8 at 0x454597, dest [ESP+0x118]-12 = [ESP+0x10C]) followed by u8 level (IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x4545AF, dest [ESP+0x59]-12 = [ESP+0x4D]). The only structural difference is that A appended `if(level == 0) { stop }`. The asm shows the level==0 test (CMP byte [ESP+0x4D],0 / JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4545B5) comes AFTER both reads, and no path in the block reads anything else. The condition therefore gates side effects only, not how many bytes are consumed. A's trailing stop is redundant and misleading, so B's grammar `u32 uid / u8 level` is the correct canonical form, and the gate belongs in gates_and_hazards. On semantics: both correctly say FUN_004781c0 also runs when the entity is missing (JZ 0x454775 at 0x4545F4 falls into the call at 0x454780). B's label 'party list refresh' for FUN_004781c0 is not supported. Its decomp iterates records gated by the local player's level (+0x928 -> +0x99) against per-record min/max, class and prerequisite ids, which is consistent with an available-quest list, not a party list. B's note that 0x427D40 no-ops for level > 99 or class > 6 is confirmed by the FUN_00427d40 decomp. Cross-refs: windslayer_server.py _send_level packs '<IB' (matches). Its docstring's 'refreshes the HP/MP bars' refers only to party frames, and cur HP is full-healed by the flag=1 recalc. PySlayer Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x22 (line 5283) reads u32 + u8 the same way, but returns early when the entity is missing.
open_questions: FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) exact identity: it looks like an available-quest list rebuild (records filtered by level range, class/job, a prerequisite id checked against 0x55 u16 ids at +0x262, and 3 ids at +0x256), but the owning UI was not traced.
Deferred event type 9 / id 0x24 queued by FUN_0042b580 is assumed to be the level-up visual; the consumer (FUN_00459df0 queue) was not traced.
specs.verification: audited: 2009 handler 0x00459343 (primary@0x451960) decomp + asm compared with the 2008 handler 0x00454582 (normalized decomp diff, then conditions and destinations read by hand); read fingerprint identical (2 reads 2008). 2008-only VAs dropped (no unique 2009 match): 0x004545B5 (CMP level,0 / JZ 0x44D7AD (break) - after all reads); 0x00454600 (entity+0x99 = level); 0x0045465D (Play_Sound 0x24 at entity +0x15A4/+0x15A8); 0x004546A9 (matched frame: HP '%u/%u' text+bar, MP text+bar); 0x00454780 (FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) level-gated list refresh)

fields.meaning: How many option words follow (0..5)

FUN_00467140(type, item_id, &opts, count) remove [2008 0x0046DE2A; handler-region call-anchor(1)]

specs.semantics:
2009: identical (audited; normalized decomp identical).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Same as 0x19 but with no leading gold field and no chat message. Reads item_id, count and the option block (u8 n, n u16 words into words 0.., u16 into word 5). Looks up the item definition (none -> stop, handled). Removes the item with FUN_00467140 using the same type rules as 0x19: type 0 subtract from u16 stacks, type 1 remove the matching equipment slot (option bytes must match), type 2 subtract from u8 stacks. On success refreshes the inventory UI; on failure nothing visible happens.
specs.trigger: Whenever the server takes an item out of the bag without selling it: consumed, used by a quest, destroyed, moved to storage or equipped (our server sends it after the 0x1D equip).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same stack overflow as 0x19: opt_count must be <= 5 (>= 63 corrupts the /GS cookie and kills the client). Equipment is removed only when all 12 option bytes match the stored slot; items granted by 0x18 have zero options, so send opt_count=0 and opt_extra=0. Fails if the tab capacity byte (player_info+0x361/+0x362/+0x363) > 45, if count=0 for stack items, if fewer than count are owned (types 0/2), or if the type is 3 or higher.
specs.references: Our server's _build_opcode_23 (u16 item, u16 count, u8 0, u16 0 = 7 B) has the right format. One correction to its comment: FUN_00404210 does not look up a bag element. It returns the item definition from the global catalog [scene+0xF84] (name at +0, type at +0x154), and is NULL only for item_id 0 or an id past the catalog. Whether the item is actually in the bag is decided later by FUN_00467140 against player_info's tab arrays. The memory note '0x23 didn't remove bag in test' fits the item not being in the matching tab array (or an option mismatch), not a catalog miss.

fields.dest_or_source: stack local; entity lookup; compared to scene+0x224

fields.meaning: equipped item id to remove; def must exist with def+0x154 == 1

fields.meaning: number of option u16s (send <= 5; same record-overflow behaviour as 0x1E)

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical (shares the 0x1E handler 0x458E07); same 2009 changes as 0x1E.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Same handler as 0x1E: removes item_id (with a matching 12-byte option record) from the entity's equip grid +0x13C/+0x16E, rebuilds the sprite, recalculates stats and max HP/MP. For the local player (uid == scene+0x220) it refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290) and the equipment window (FUN_00441a10). Unlike 0x1E it does NOT add the item back to the bag and does NOT update the cash-item list (FUN_0045d170): the opcode check at 0x45424F skips both. So the item simply disappears from the equipment.

fields.name: item_or_skill_id
fields.meaning: windslayer.hii record id (a consumable item or a skill). The client looks up the record and applies its effect to the LOCAL player. No uid is read.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local; key into the hii table (FUN_00404750)

specs.semantics:
2009 (FUN_00451960 case 0x25/0x3B, 0x458429): id -> hii record (FUN_00404750); none -> stop. Type 0 (rec+0x154==0): FUN_00424FB0 consumes one bag unit (cooldown checked), inventory refresh FUN_0046EF40, effect 0x29 + sound 0x29, then the common tail. Type 3: straight to the common tail. Common tail: FUN_00444CA0 stats panel; if local entity scene+0x988 exists and (map_mode [[gs+0x4FC]+0x7C] != 1 or scene+0xF90 == 5): MP (+0xA4) += rec+0x15C clamped to [0, +0x11B0] - except when the delta is negative and entity+0x174 != 0 and entity+0x25A == 1, where MP is set to a computed value (FUN_004C1EF0); HP (+0xA0) += rec+0x158 clamped to [0, +0x11AC] when FUN_00426D40 allows it; rec+0x160 != 0 refreshes HP bar and party bars.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Server confirmation that the LOCAL player used an item or skill. There is no uid, so it always applies to the local player. The client looks up the id in its hii table (FUN_00404210). If there is no record, nothing happens. Otherwise it switches on rec+0x154:
(type 0, consumable) FUN_00423b70(qty=-1, ids=scene+0x63E, counts=scene+0x698, cooldown_ts=scene+0x6F4, id, bag_size=byte scene+0x3AA, cooldown=rec+0x1EC, now=this+0x364, check=1) removes one unit from the client-side bag and stamps the cooldown. If the item is not in the bag or is still cooling down, the handler exits with no effect. On success it refreshes the inventory window, then plays effect 0x29 on the local uid and sound 0x29.
(type 3, skill) Starts the local cast animation by writing scene+0x255=7 and scene+0x256=variant. Those bytes go out on the UDP P2P state as action*10+dir. Variants by id range: 1 = 0x104-0x10E, 0x150-0x15A, 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x200-0x20A, 0x22C-0x236; 2 = 0x10F-0x119, 0x15B-0x165, 0x1B3-0x1BD, 0x1C9-0x1D3, 0x20B-0x215, 0x242-0x24C; 3 = 0x13A-0x144, 0x166-0x170, 0x1DF-0x1E9, 0x216-0x220, 0x237-0x241, 0x7A1-0x7AB; 4 = 0x24D-0x257, 0x76A-0x774, 0x780-0x78A, 0x796-0x7A0, 0x7C2-0x7CC, 0x7D8-0x7E2; 5 = 0x258-0x262, 0x775-0x77F, 0x78B-0x795, 0x7CD-0x7D7, 0x7E3-0x7ED, 0x9FA-0xA04, 0xA3C-0xA46; 6..10 = further families; 11 = 0xB3B-0xB45.
Special skill ids: 0xAD6-0xAD7 and 0xC2C-0xC2D pick the variant from the player's active buff slots. 0xAD8-0xAE2 is a party heal: effect and sound 0x10E on self and on every party member in scene+0x25C..0x26C, and rec+0x158 is added to each member's HP. 0x1F5-0x1FF plays effects 0x54 and 0x37 plus sound 0x54 when mode==0. 0xC2 opens UI message 0x259. 0x876-0x880, 0x881-0x88B and 0x88C call UI helpers FUN_00467fa0, FUN_00467ea0 and FUN_004687f0.
Then for every type-3 id: scene+0x258 (pending skill) = 0, FUN_00426cc0 stamps the skill cooldown, FUN_00441c20(0) and FUN_00443ac0 refresh the quick slots.
(common tail for types 0 and 3) FUN_00443840 refreshes the stats panel. If local entity scene+0x970 exists and [[0x70EED8]+0x70] != 1: MP += rec+0x15C (clamped 0..max) and MP bar refresh; HP += rec+0x158 (clamped 0..max, only if FUN_004258d0(id)=1, i.e. id not in 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x24D-0x257, 0x8C6-0x8D0, 0x8F2-0x8FC, 0x997-0x9A1, 0x9C3-0x9F9, 0xA5D-0xA67, 0xAF9-0xB03, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB25-0xB2F) and HP bar refresh. If rec+0x160 != 0, the HP bar and party HP bars refresh too.
HP/MP deltas come from the client's own hii record: potions have positive values, skill costs are negative. The packet carries no amounts.
Other record types (1/2/4/5/6) do nothing.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C27, combat_skill#03): for id 0x88C, FUN_004687f0 is NOT an unconditional "open the Reinforce UI" - it first checks the distance to a smithy and otherwise shows the modal "Too far for Reinforcement. Go near the smithy."
specs.trigger: Reply to the local player's C2S 0x15 UseItemOrSkill (u16 id [+u16 x,u16 y for 0xA31..0xA3B]) when the use is accepted. Send it for consumables (type 0) and for non-buff skills (type 3). For duration/buff skills, S2C 0x3B with target_uid = caster also runs this same self logic, so use one or the other, not both. To reject a skill cast, send 0x5F.
specs.expected_response: none (client sends nothing back)
specs.gates_and_hazards:
2009: no pending-skill gate exists - C2S 0x15 skill sends are gated client-side by scene+0x259 != 7, a 1000 ms global delay (scene+0x260), rec+0x1EC cooldown (-10% with a buff) and MP/HP checks, so the server does not need to answer every cast with 0x25/0x3B/0x5F (0x5F is gone in 2009). The tail checks scene+0x988 != 0, so the 2008 null-local-entity crash no longer applies.
[2008]: 1) Unknown id (not in windslayer.hii) or a record type other than 0/3 is silently ignored.
2) Type 0: needs the id in the client-side bag (scene+0x63E) and the per-slot cooldown rec+0x1EC to have elapsed. Otherwise the whole handler aborts with no heal.
3) Type 3: C2S 0x15 skill sends are blocked while scene+0x258 != 0 (set on send at 0x44C248) and while scene+0x255 == 7 (cast animation). If the server never answers a skill cast with 0x25 (or 0x3B for self) or 0x5F, the player can never cast again until a map reload (FUN_0042c360 clears it).
4) CRASH: the type-3 tail at 0x453D98 does LEA on [scene+0x970] with no null check and FUN_00426cc0 reads [+0x29A]. Never send a type-3 id before the local player entity exists (after 0x07 spawn).
5) HP/MP are applied as client-side deltas. If the server also pushes absolute 0x28/0x44, send those AFTER 0x25, or the delta double-applies on top of the absolute value.
6) The HP/MP change is skipped when [[0x70EED8]+0x70] == 1 (probably team/arena room mode, unverified).
7) Plays effects and sounds; no dialogs except id 0xC2 (UI 0x259).
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C27, combat_skill#03): the CAST LOCK scene+0x255 = 7 clears BY ITSELF within 3 s with no TCP packet, so no unlock packet (S2C 0x5F) is needed just to clear the cast animation. The pending-skill gate scene+0x258 is the one that really needs an answer (0x25 / 0x3B / 0x5F), and it is what blocks further casts and equip changes.
specs.references:
PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x25.py sends exactly u16 skill, which matches EN. PySlayer sends opcode_25(300) after consumable use and calls opcode_25(500) 'set_maxhp_and_maxmp', both guesses. project_status.md's '0x25 set max HP/MP' inherits that misnomer. The KR Hex-Rays handler (doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x25/0x3B) reads extra bool/flag fields that EN does NOT read.
Our server: _handle_use_skill (windslayer_server.py:1409) builds the correct EN body (struct '<H') but is dead code: nothing calls it, and inbound 0x25 goes to _handle_attack. _handle_use_item (C2S 0x15, line 1111) sends only 0x28/0x44 absolutes, never 0x25, so the client bag count never decrements and skill casts would stay pending.
reference_combat_model.md says 0x25 feeds the +0x3C8 damage-number pool with a scene+0x220==uid gate. This block has no uid read for 0x25 and no +0x3C8 access; only 0x3B compares a uid with scene+0x220.

Meaning of the mode flag [[0x70EED8]+0x70]: ==1 skips HP/MP deltas and changes party-buff handling (team byte +0x14EB), ==0 selects local/single behaviour in UDP code. Likely room/PvP mode, unverified.

locations.role: quest-table lookup QuestTable[id-1] (ctx+0xC, vector at +8/+0xC), returns record in EAX or 0 [2008 0x0040A840; function-signature]
append quest_id to completed-quest list char+0x262 (85 x u16) / count char+0x30C (u8, cap 99) [2008 0x004264A0; function-signature]

specs.grammar: u16 quest_id

fields.name: quest_id
fields.meaning: Quest index into the client's hs/windslayer.hqi quest table (1-based). 0 or unknown id = packet ignored after the read.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local; written into the first empty active slot char+0x260+2*i (i<5) with ready flag char+0x26F+i cleared (2008: 3 slots at +0x256)

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical; FIVE active quest slots u16[5] at char+0x260 (2008 three at +0x256); the matching ready flag char+0x26F+i is cleared.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Quest-accept result. After reading quest_id the client looks up the quest record (FUN_0040a840). If the record is null, nothing happens (the handler still returns 'handled'). Otherwise:
(a) If record.Money(+0xDE8, i32) >= 0 AND record.Demand_id[0](+0xD0C) == 0 AND record.ReqPro(+0xDF8) == 0 (a quest with no requirements), the quest is NOT put in the active log. FUN_004264a0 adds it to the completed-quest list instead (char+0x262 u16[85] plus count bytes char+0x30C: a new entry gets count 1, an existing one gets count+1 capped at 99, and a full list is shifted left before appending).
(b) Otherwise the quest goes into the first active slot i (0..2) whose u16 id at char+0x256+2i is 0. The client writes the id and clears the ready flag at char+0x25F+i. The progress byte at char+0x25C+i is NOT reset. There is no duplicate check, and if all 3 slots are full nothing is stored and there is no message.
In both cases the client then grants the quest's Send items itself: for i=0..9, stopping at the first zero id at record+0xC94+4i, it calls FUN_00440920(ctx+4, id, 0, count=record+0xD34+4i). That adds the item to the bag and prints "you've received %s. (Count:%u)" (or "You've learned skill(%s)." for type-3 items). Finally it refreshes the quest window (FUN_00478380). Quest record layout (confirmed from hqi loader FUN_00409FE0): +4 name, +0xC94 Send ids[10], +0xCBC Reward ids[20], +0xD0C Demand ids[10], +0xD34 Send_Num[10], +0xD5C Reward_Num[20], +0xDAC Demand_Num[10], +0xDE4 Exp, +0xDE8 Money, +0xDF4 Repeat, +0xDF8 ReqPro, +0xE08 SNPC, +0xE0C ENPC.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x16 AcceptQuest (u16 quest_id, send site 0x477330). The client sends it only after checking that an active slot is free ("You can only take 3 quests at a time...") and that the bag has room for the Send items. The client does not add the quest optimistically; it waits for this packet.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Returns without reading if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null (the sub-handler chain then continues). Hazards: (1) Sending 0x26 twice for the same quest fills two active slots. (2) The client grants the hqi Send items ITSELF, so a server that also sends S2C 0x18 GetItem for those items (0x18's handler at 0x46DEDE calls the same FUN_00440920) duplicates them in the client bag. (3) A no-requirement quest (Money>=0, no Demand, ReqPro==0) goes straight to the completed list, so the server must not expect it to be active. The client's turn-in code (FUN_00477af0) only turns in quests that are in active slots. (4) The client's slot choice is the first empty slot, so the server's slot numbering for 0x59 must copy that rule exactly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, quest_cards_misc#09): one client session exited GRACEFULLY about 2 s after a 0x26 "1a 00" injection followed by a Q keypress (the server logged a clean close with no crash event). It was NOT reproduced in two later sessions with the identical packet, so treat it as an unexplained termination risk rather than a rule; recovery is a restart.
specs.references: PySlayer opcode_26: p16u(random), which agrees on u16 / 2 bytes. Our server's _send_quest_grant packs '<H' quest_id, which matches. Live capture: accepting quest 26 got S2C 0x26 with a 2-byte body, with no desync. Disagreement: reference_gamedef_db.md says 'EN client has NO live quest granted opcode'. That is wrong; this is that opcode. Our _handle_accept_quest also sends 0x18 for each q['send'] item, which likely duplicates the client-side hqi Send grant (PLAUSIBLE; depends on EN hqi Send columns).
open_questions: Whether the EN hqi quest 26 (starter) has ReqPro/Money/Demand set. If all are empty, 0x26 files it straight into the completed list instead of the active log. The live observation 'shown as Accepted' could be either tab.
For no-requirement quests, how the original server delivered Exp/Reward items (0x27 would increment the completion count a second time).

specs.grammar: u16 quest_id

fields.name: quest_id
fields.meaning: Quest being completed. It must exist in the client's quest table or the packet is a no-op. All rewards come from the client's local hqi record, not from the packet.

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical; checks the 5 active slots char+0x260..+0x268 and clears progress char+0x26A..+0x26E; gold reward -> player_info+0x230; NEW chat line "[%s] Quest Completed.".
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Quest turn-in result. The client applies all of the completion bookkeeping itself, from its local quest record:
1. Look up the record; if null, return.
2. Clear every active slot whose id == quest_id (id=0, progress byte char+0x25C+i = 0).
3. FUN_004264a0: add quest_id to the completed list char+0x262 (count 1, or count+1 capped at 99).
4. If record.Money (+0xDE8, i32) != 0: gold64 at char+0x228/0x22C += sign-extended Money, and the gold label is refreshed. If Money < 0 the chat shows "Gave %u Gold." (color 0xFFFD4C87); otherwise "You've received %u Gold." (0xFF00C800).
5. For i=0..9 while Demand_id[i] (+0xD0C+4i) != 0: look up the item in the item table at [ctx+4]+0x4D4. If found, call FUN_00467140(type=item+0x154, inv=[ctx+4]+0xD5C, u16 id, 0, u16 count=+0xDAC+4i) to remove it from the bag (types 0/1/2 only). On success, chat "Gave %u item(%s)." and refresh the inventory UI (FUN_00465290).
6. For i=0..19 while Reward_id[i] (+0xCBC+4i) != 0: FUN_00440920(ctx+4, id, 0, count=+0xD5C+4i) grants the item ("you've received %s. (Count:%u)" / skill learned).
7. Refresh the quest window and the NPC quest-dialog list.
EXP (+0xDE4) is NOT applied here; the server must send it separately (S2C 0x21).
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x17 TurnInQuest (u16 quest_id), sent by FUN_00477af0 when talking to the quest's ENPC (+0xE0C). The client checks Money/gold, progress >= ReqPro, Demand items present and reward bag space ("There isn't empty space in the inventory.") before sending.
specs.expected_response: none (server should follow with S2C 0x21 exp if the quest gives exp)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Skipped if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null. An unknown quest_id is a silent no-op. The client does NOT check that the quest was active, so sending 0x27 for a non-active quest still adds gold, removes Demand items, grants Rewards and bumps the completion count. Double-sending doubles rewards. Duplication hazard: the client already adds Money and Reward items and removes Demand items locally. A server that also sends S2C 0x18 GetItem for the rewards (the 0x18 handler calls the same FUN_00440920) duplicates reward items in the client bag. Gold can stay consistent if 0x18 carries an absolute gold total. Gold is not clamped, so negative Money can underflow the u64 if the server skips the gold check. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C21, quest_cards_misc#11): live-confirmed that double-sending re-grants the items and gold and bumps the completion count again; the one exception is a type-3 skill reward that is already learned, which prints nothing the second time. Duplicate 0x27s duplicate items, gold and completion count - not skills.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Our server's _send_quest_complete packs '<H' quest_id, which matches the wire format. However: (a) our server fires it from C2S 0x16 (treated as accept OR turn-in), while the real client sends turn-in as C2S 0x17 (send site 0x477F15), which our _dispatch does not handle, so real NPC turn-ins get no reply; (b) _complete_quest also sends 0x18 per reward item (plus gold_gain), likely duplicating the client-side hqi Reward grant (PLAUSIBLE; depends on EN hqi Reward columns matching the KR gamedef).
open_questions: Whether EN hqi Reward/Money/Demand values match the KR gamedef.sqlite3 rows (item-id drift like 377->179), which determines what the client grants locally.
Whether the original server sent 0x18 inventory syncs after 0x27, or relied solely on the client-side grant.

blind_open_questions: Mapping of def+0xCBC (20 entries) vs def+0xD0C (10 entries) to gamedef 'reward'/'demand' columns is inferred from the helpers used (grant vs negative-count removal) and the chat strings.

specs.name: SetLocalHp
specs.grammar: u16 hp

fields.name: hp
fields.meaning: New ABSOLUTE current HP of the local player (not a delta)
fields.dest_or_source: zero-extended into (*(scene+0x988))+0xA0, local-player cur HP (2008 (scene+0x970)+0x9C); HUD refresh FUN_00444AF0

specs.semantics:
2009: identical; target is now (scene+0x988)+0xA0 (2008 (scene+0x970)+0x9C).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Reads one u16 (IAT 0x4A4090, stack local [esp+0xE8]). If the local-player entity pointer [scene+0x970] is non-null, writes movzx(hp) to entity+0x9C. Then always calls FUN_00443690 (ESI=game_state): if the local entity exists, sprintf("%d/%d", +0x9C, +0x110C max HP) into HUD text slot 6 (FUN_004838c0(6)); if max HP (+0x110C) != 0 it sets HP globe fill ratio (FUN_004891e0(2, cur/max, 2)) and a HUD state FUN_00489320(2,1, ratio>0.2 ? 3 : 0) (low-HP indicator). No effect, no sound, no reply.
specs.trigger: Whenever the server changes the local player's HP: enter-world / map change right after 0x07 (otherwise player shows 0 HP and is effectively dead), potion use, damage taken, regen.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No uid in packet: always targets the LOCAL player only. If [scene+0x970] is null (before RegisterLocalPlayer) the value is silently dropped. Max representable HP is 65535. Handler does not trigger death at 0; however the entity-update loop (FUN_00413920, action 2/0x11 end) calls FUN_0041a230 when +0x9C < 1, so hp=0 can start client-side death flow later. HUD ratio skipped if max HP (+0x110C, set by 0x07) is 0.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x28.py (setHp, single p16u) matches EN exactly. The newer KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x28) is DIFFERENT: u8 subtype (1=HP,2=MP,3=...) + u16 + i32 max etc. - do not port that. Our server _send_hp (windslayer_server.py:1566) struct '<H' matches; used at enter-world (732), item use (1180), map change (1265). Memory note 'player needs 0x28/0x44 on spawn' consistent.

specs.name: EntityDie
specs.length: 16 (client consumes only 4 if uid not found)
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) {
  stop
}
u32 respawn_tick
u32 respawn_x
u32 respawn_y

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: entity (player or monster) that dies; looked up with FUN_00419450 in the scene list; unknown => stop

fields.name: respawn_tick
fields.meaning: absolute respawn deadline on the client scene clock (2009 scene+0xF34). Type-4 template entities auto-respawn when (int)(respawn_tick - clock) < 0 AND the current map's [scene+0xFB4]+0x2E0 flag is 0 (new 2009 extra gate in FUN_00414210 case 0x16)
fields.dest_or_source: read DIRECTLY into entity+0xEF8 (ulong&; IAT 0x4C7104 via CALL EDI)

fields.name: respawn_x
fields.meaning: respawn/home X; converted unsigned->f64

fields.name: respawn_y
fields.meaning: respawn/home Y; converted unsigned->f64

specs.semantics: Unchanged behaviour with 2009 struct offsets. After a successful lookup and BEFORE reading the rest: entity+0x96E=0, +0x971=0, action +0x994=0x10 (dying), action timer +0xE9C=0, +0x95B=8 (if not already 8). Then respawn_tick goes straight into +0xEF8 and x/y (FILD + 2^32 fixup = unsigned) into f64 +0x13B8/+0x13C0. The entity update loop FUN_00414210 plays the death animation (action 0x10) then action 0x16 (dead). In 0x16: type-4 entities (+0x9C == 4) revive client-side when (int)(+0xEF8 - scene+0xF34) < 0 and [scene+0xFB4]+0x2E0 == 0 (FUN_0042a220); on an arena map ([scene+0xFB4]+0x7C == 1) the room host (scene+0xF40 != 0) in modes > 5 revives after +0xE9C >= 20000 with HP/MP refill (FUN_0042a1c0); otherwise, when scene+0xF40 != 0 and entity+0xF16 != 0, the entity is revived with HP += 10 and buffs cleared. HP is NOT set to 0 by this packet.
specs.trigger: Server-side death of a monster or player (HP reached 0).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unknown uid => only 4 bytes consumed, no-op. Re-sending for a dead entity restarts the dying animation. specs.name: RemoteEntityMoveStateSync (keyframe: flush queue + target + position)
specs.length: 16, 17, 33 or 34 bytes: 4 + 8 + 4 + [1 if action nibble is 9 or 10] + [17 if the position block is read]. Nothing is read after the position block, so always sending it gives 33 or 34 bytes.

fields.name: mover_uid
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] stack local [esp+0x1D4]. Passed in EDX to FUN_004189f0, which walks the scene entity list (scene+0xC) and matches entity+0x84. uid 0 or an unknown uid gives null, and the handler stops.
fields.meaning: uid of the entity whose movement/action state is being synced (another player, not the receiver)

fields.name: move_bits
fields.meaning: Same bit packing as the 8 bytes inside C2S 0x0D, so the server can relay them verbatim. Read as move_bits_lo = u32 LE of bytes 0-3 and move_bits_hi = u32 LE of bytes 4-7.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[1:0] horiz_input
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x4A: 1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, 0 or 3 gives 8. Applied later to entity+0x8B3.
fields.meaning: horizontal key/direction state; 8 = neutral. The C2S packer maps 8B3: 2 to 1, 6 to 2, anything else to 0.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[4:2]
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x4B, later entity+0x8B4
fields.meaning: vertical/jump state (a live jump capture had value 3)

fields.name: move_bits_lo[8:5]
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x4C, later entity+0x8B5
fields.meaning: input state byte 8B5 (unknown)

fields.name: move_bits_lo[11:9]
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x4D, later entity+0x8B6
fields.meaning: input state byte 8B6 (a live walk capture had value 1; the C2S packer checks for value 4 on grab)

fields.name: move_bits_lo[15:12] action
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x4F, later entity+0x94C
fields.meaning: Current action: 0 = none, 1-5 = attacks, 6-10 = grab/throw family, 0xD = death (FUN_00412360 case 0xD sets state 0x10, HP 0 and clears buffs). Values 9 and 10 add the extra u8.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[19:16] reaction
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] low nibble of byte scene+0xEFA, stored at node+0x4E. When consumed it goes to entity+0x950 if scene+0xF24 != 0, otherwise to entity+0x8EA.
fields.meaning: Reaction/being-hit state. HAZARD: a nonzero value makes FUN_00412100 copy node+0x10/+0x18 (zeroed by memset) into the entity position, so keep it 0.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[21:20] facing
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x50: 1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, anything else gives 8. Later entity+0x8D0.
fields.meaning: facing direction used for the action

fields.name: move_bits_hi[11:0] action_time
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x44, later entity+0x958. Also used to adjust the node delay when target_uid == local uid.
fields.meaning: action timing/frame value (C2S source entity+0x958)

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: Target/victim uid of the action. The C2S 0x0D packer only sends entity+0xD80 when action != 0, so the server should write 0 when there is no action.

fields.name: action_flag
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] node+0x52, later entity+0x8FF
fields.meaning: only present when the action nibble is 9 or 10 (grab/throw). FUN_00412360 case 9 checks it to trigger a buff/effect.

fields.name: pos_x
fields.meaning: mover world X

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: mover world Y

fields.name: airborne
fields.meaning: In-air flag. FUN_00413920 sets it to 1 together with state 10 (jump) and clears it on landing.

specs.semantics:
2009: identical read sequence and conditions. entity+0x971 = (opcode != 0x9E) (2008 +0x8E4), entity+0x963 = 1 (2008 +0x8D7); command node 0x58 bytes with the same field layout; queue flush uses entity+0x13F4 (2008 +0x1354); local-target delay math uses entity+0xE3C and scene+0xF14 (2008 +0xDAC / scene+0xEFC).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Server-to-client counterpart of C2S 0x0D: it syncs another entity's input and action state.

After the entity is found, the handler:
- Sets entity+0x8E4 = 1 (it is 0 only for 0x9E) and entity+0x8D7 = 1.
- Mallocs and zeroes a 0x58-byte node and sets node[0] = 0x3DE (990).
- Decodes the 8 bits into the node, zeroes node+0x30/+0x38/+0x08/+0x04, then reads the target, the optional u8 and the optional position block.

Only 0x2A then does these steps:
- Frees every pending node in the entity's move queue (entity+0x1350; head at +0x1354) and sets entity+0xE48 (hold timer) = 0.
- Sets node[0] = 960, or 0 if it was 30 or less.
- If target_uid == local uid, clears the action fields as described above and sets node[0] to 960 minus max(entity+0xDAC, action_time), clamped at 0.

The node is then appended to the queue with FUN_00459df0.

FUN_00412100 consumes the queue each tick, only for entities with state byte +0x98 > 2 whose uid != local uid:
- node[0] is the longest time (in 30 ms steps) the node waits.
- The node applies at once if the entity is idle (904 == 8, 8B3 == 8, 8B4/8B5/8B6 == 0, 950 == 0, 94C == 0).
- Applying it copies the node into entity 8B3/8B4/8B5/8B6/94C/950/D80/958/8FF/8D0 and D78/1328/1330/8DB/8E8/1338/1340/8D4/8E7. The EN 0x2A leaves all of those except the decoded bits, target and 8FF at 0.
specs.trigger: Send to the other players on the same map when a player's C2S 0x0D arrives. This is the correct relay: echoing 0x0D is known to desync. Use 0x2A for an authoritative state (it flushes the queue and carries target and position); use 0x9F/0x9E for buffered updates.
specs.expected_response: none LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#26/#27/#28): 0x2A applies within one sample (<17 ms measured) because it flushes the pending queue and sets +0xE48 = 0, so it is the only "apply now" relay. 0x9E / 0x9F / 0x1B all append BEHIND the pending nodes (0x9E measured 750 ms, 0x9F 1.81 s, 0x1B stop 1.08 s). Use 0x2A for authoritative keyframes and stops, 0x1B for the streamed relay.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- An unknown uid or uid 0 is silently ignored and nothing more is read.
- NEVER send it with mover_uid == the receiver's own uid. The local entity would be found, its position overwritten (a teleport), and nodes queued for the local uid are never consumed (FUN_00412100 skips the local uid), so memory leaks.
- The position block depends on client-only state (mover state 0x10 = dead) and on target_uid == receiver uid. Nothing is read after it, so always appending the 17 bytes should be harmless because trailing bytes are ignored. Omitting it is only safe when target_uid == receiver uid.
- A nonzero reaction nibble (bits 16-19) snaps the remote entity to (0,0) when the node is consumed, because the node x/y at +0x10/+0x18 stay 0.
- Needs a valid scene (this+0x4CC), so send it in-world only.
- Bits 22-31 of lo and 12-31 of hi are ignored. Live C2S captures carry stale garbage there.

specs.references:
- Bit mapping matches the C2S 0x0D packer FUN_0042c940 exactly: 8B3 in bits 0-1, 8B4 in 2-4, 8B5 in 5-8, 8B6 in 9-11, 94C in 12-15, 950 in 16-19, 8D0 in 20-21, 958 in hi bits 0-11.
- Live C2S 0x0D captures decode consistently: walking bits_lo 0x53400200 gives 8B6 = 1; jumping 0x7240000C gives 8B4 = 3; bits_hi & 0xFFF = 0 in both.
- KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c, case 0x2A/0x9E/0x9F) has the same skeleton but a DIFFERENT layout. It adds a u16 before the target uid and a u16 after it, uses wider bitfields (action at bits 14-17, facing at 22-23), adds action 14 to the u8 condition, and uses a state check of 23. Do not port the KR layout.
- windslayer_server.py has no builder. The project memory confirms that echoing 0x0D broke the cipher.
open_questions: Which opcode the original server chose for normal walking versus actions (0x2A, 0x9F or 0x9E). The client semantics suggest 0x2A for authoritative/action states and 0x9F/0x9E for buffered input changes.
C2S 0x0D carries no x/y unless the reaction state is nonzero, so it is unclear where the original server got pos_x/pos_y for 0x2A (server-side simulation, or the last known spawn/position).
Exact meaning of entity bytes 8B5/8B6 and of the 12-bit action_time value.
Whether the (0,0) snap for a nonzero reaction nibble is real in practice or is masked by other state (not verified at runtime).
specs.verification: audited: 2009 handler 0x00459C3D (primary@0x451960) decomp + asm compared with the 2008 handler 0x00454E6D (normalized decomp diff, then conditions and destinations read by hand); read fingerprint identical (7 reads 2008). 2008-only VAs dropped (no unique 2009 match): 0x00455002 (opcode==0x2A branch: target, optional u8, position block, queue flush); 0x00412100 (per-tick queue consumer that applies node fields to the entity)
blind_open_questions: Exact gameplay meaning of 0x2A vs 0x1B. The hit/knockback reading is inferred from the position override and the special case when source == local; the handler itself has no strings.
Meaning of action nibble values 9/10 (which carry action_extra) and of the w1 12-bit parameter (+0x958).
Fireway GetDataFromPacket behaviour when reading past len (throw, clamp or garbage) is not visible in this binary.

specs.semantics: List of arena players. For each entry the client allocates a new 0x16B8-byte entity, zeroes it and sets state +0x9C=3, reads the fields above (name ... skill list), inserting each buff with FUN_004262b0. cur HP/MP are taken from the NEW hp/mp words (entity+0xA0/+0xA4) - 2008 instead set them to max after registration. After the skill list FUN_00422fc0 registers the entity (scene list; local player when uid == scene+0x224). The team/next_team/K/D/score tail is read after registration; state +0x9C becomes 3 (team != 0) or 1 (spectator). NEW pet tail: for the receiver's own entry (uid == scene+0x224) nothing is read and the pet record pointer entity+0x1628 = FUN_00462c80(slot-15 item id) from the local pet list; for every other entry a bool is read and, when nonzero, a 0x1C-byte pet record is allocated at entity+0x1628 (if absent) and filled with level (+0xB) and name (+0xD), and +0xA = summoned. FUN_00447f40 then spawns/updates the pet companion entity (entity+0x1638) from the slot-15 pet item's template. For opcode 0x2B nothing else happens (no scene-state change, no HUD refresh). There are still no position fields.
specs.trigger: Add or sync arena match participants while the client is already in the arena scene, when no HUD/scene transition is wanted. Compare 0x2E (same format + transition), 0x2C (one player) and 0x2D (remove by uid).
specs.expected_response: none (the handler sends nothing)
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- RECEIVER-DEPENDENT BYTES: the pet block is present for every entry EXCEPT the one whose uid equals the receiving client's login uid (scene+0x224). The server must build 0x2B/0x2E per recipient; broadcasting one byte string to several clients desyncs every client whose own uid is in the list (or any client not in it).
- guild_id > 1 inserts 21 bytes; guild_id 1 (GM) does not.
- No uid dedupe: every entry creates a new entity.
- skill_count > 30 overflows the skill array at entity+0x2AE.
- Buffs beyond the slot capacity or with unknown ids are dropped but their bytes are consumed.
- Names (17) and pet names (13) must be NUL-terminated inside their fixed length.
- As in 2008 (live D4), 0x2B does not rebuild the roster window until a later 0x2E/0x2C/0x37.

specs.semantics: Single-player spawn into an arena/room game. Allocates a 0x16B8 entity (ctor FUN_00423d00), memsets it, state +0x9C=3, parses name ... skill list (no buff loop, as in 2008), registers it with FUN_00422fc0 (local player if uid == scene+0x224), reads team (state 3/1) and next_team, then sets cur HP +0xA0 = max +0x11AC and cur MP +0xA4 = max +0x11B0 (full HP/MP; unlike 0x2B/0x2E there is no hp/mp on the wire). NEW: reads the pet bool (+ level/name) unconditionally, filling the 0x1C-byte pet record at entity+0x1628. Finally FUN_00443bc0 (team text), FUN_00444220 (roster sort/balance), FUN_004446c0 and FUN_00447f40 (pet companion spawn).
specs.trigger: Server sends to everyone in an arena/room game when a player enters it.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No mode gate; no uid dedupe (a second 0x2C for the same uid makes a ghost). skill_count must be <= 30. guild_id > 1 inserts 21 bytes. Unlike 0x2B/0x2E the pet bool is present even for the receiver's own uid - do not reuse the 0x2B per-entry encoder blindly (0x2C has no hp/mp words, no buff loop, no K/D/score, and an unconditional pet block).
specs.references: 2008 entry 0x2C (handler 0x4503E1, 313 + 2*skill_count). Changes mirror 0x2B except hp/mp (absent here) and the pet gate (unconditional here).

specs.name: ArenaRoomListReset

locations.role: handler block (prologue: clears the list, then falls through into the 0x32 parser at 0x45565E; there is no jmp) [2008 0x004555E6; dispatch]
per-room check: can the local player enter this room [2008 0x00444770; function-signature]

specs.grammar:
u8 room_count
repeat(room_count) {
  str[17] room_name
  u16 room_no
  u8 max_players
  u8 cur_players
  u8 room_level
  u8 room_type
  bool has_password
}

fields.name: room_count
fields.meaning: number of rows in this packet (0..255). The loop counter is compared with movzx, so the count is unsigned.

fields.name: room_name
fields.meaning: room title. Exactly 17 bytes are copied and the client adds no terminator, so send at most 16 chars plus a NUL. Printed with %s.

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: room number: shown as %03d, sent back in C2S 0x1A/0x1C, and compared with the requested room number [game+0x4CC]+0xF48 in 0x34 result 4. Join-by-number only accepts 1..128.

fields.name: max_players
fields.meaning: room capacity, the second number of '(cur/max)'. Result 4 of 0x34 copies it into cur_players.

fields.name: cur_players
fields.meaning: current occupants, the first number of '(cur/max)'

fields.name: room_level
fields.meaning: level bracket of a type-0 room. Shown as 'Lv.%d'. The local player (level byte at player+0x99) may enter only if room_level-2 <= level <= room_level+1. The client's join prompt clamps the range to 1..99 ('To enter Lv.%u room, your level must between Lv.%d and Lv.%d.'). Ignored for types 1-3.

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: 0=level-bracket room ('Lv.N'); 1='ULMT'; 2='STD'; 3='Novice' (novice-only room, novice icon sprite 0x11B); 4=play/chat room, which the arena list never stores. Also derives room+0x18 = (type in 1..3) and room+0x1C = (type in 2..3); for type 1, +0x1C is left uninitialized.

fields.name: has_password
fields.meaning: room is locked: draws lock sprite 0x7D (not for Novice rooms). When joining from the list, the client then opens password window 0x4A instead of sending C2S 0x1A.

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical (0x33 clears the list then falls into the 0x32 parser - the reverse of the 2008 code order); 0x54-byte room struct, see 0x32.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Starts a new ARENA room list (window 0x2A). Prologue at 0x4555E6: (1) RemoveHead + free every room in the list at game+0x440 (head +0x444, count +0x44C); (2) if window 0x2A exists, clear its UI rows (FUN_0047d700, no free); (3) set label control 0x14 of window 0x2A to '0/0'; (4) FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1), which clicks message box window 0x16 and dismisses the 'Waiting for the server to response.' popup. It then parses rows exactly like 0x32. Per row: allocate a 0x24-byte room and read the fields. If room_type==4 the row is dropped without being stored or freed (memory leak). Otherwise flag = FUN_00444770(local player, room), meaning the player can enter. Enterable rooms go to the head of the list at game+0x440 (FUN_00459d30), the rest to the tail (FUN_00459df0). The row is added to window 0x2A's UI list (at the head if enterable) only if it passes the current filter: the text of combobox control 0x15 is compared with item controls 0x16=all, 0x17=rooms with +0x18==0 (type 0), 0x18=type 1, 0x19=type 2, 0x1A=type 3. After the loop it counts the enterable rooms in the whole list and sets label 0x14 to sprintf('%u/%u', enterable_count, total_count[game+0x44C]), then FUN_00489c50(0x2A,1) refreshes the scroll. Enterable means: player+0x110==0 (novice, no class change) and type==3; or player+0x110!=0, type!=3, and either type is 1/2 or the level is inside the bracket. Rows the player cannot enter are drawn grey (0xFF999999).
specs.trigger: Send when the player opens the F-key ARENA room list; the client opens window 0x2A itself and sends C2S 0x2C with no payload. Also usable as a full refresh.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH: for every row, and for every stored room in the final count loop, the handler calls FUN_00444770 with ECX=[[game+0x4CC]+0x970] and reads [ECX+0x110] with no null check (the renderer does check it). Sending 0x33 with rooms, or with an already non-empty list, before the local player object exists will access-violate. Send it only in-world. Do not send room_type 4 here (leak, never shown). Name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes, or %s runs into the uninitialized byte +0x11 and room_no. The handler does not open window 0x2A; if the window is not loaded, the UI steps are skipped but data is still stored.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x33.py uses the same byte layout (name17, u16, u8 maxuser, u8 curruser, u8 ??, u8 ??, u8 IsLocked). The two '??' bytes are room_level and room_type; PySlayer sends type 1 (ULMT). PySlayer game_server answers C2S 0x2C code 1 with 0x33. The EN client sends 0x2C with no payload (scout plus live capture), so the code byte PySlayer and our server's _handle_room_query read does not exist in EN. Our server only logs 0x2C and never sends 0x33. Its comment 'answering with 0x33 unprompted opens the arena UI' is not supported by this handler, which never opens a window.
open_questions: Whether dismissing message box 0x16 via FUN_00446300(0x16,0,1,0,1) has side effects when no popup is showing (the server comment says an unprompted 0x33 opened the arena UI)
Use of the derived flag room+0x1C (set for types 2/3) was not traced
Whether the server is expected to split lists above 255 rooms into 0x33 plus 0x32 continuations

specs.name: RoomJoinResult
specs.grammar:
u8 result
u8 room_type

fields.name: result
fields.meaning:
1=message 'Incorrect password.'; 2='Invalid room #.'; 3=password required: close the wait box and open password window 0x4A (FUN_00489960(0x4A,5) + FUN_00483430(0x4A,4,1)); 4='The room is full
(Please try again in a few minutes.)', and the client finds the row in window 0x2A whose u16 room_no equals the requested [game+0x4CC]+0xF48 and sets cur_players = max_players; 5=accepted: close the wait box and flush the room list (see room_type); 6='Your level is not appropriate.'; 7='Only novice can enter a
[novice-only room].'; 8='A novice can only enter 
[Novice only room].'. 0 or >8: nothing happens.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local (switch 1..9): 1 Incorrect password, 2 Invalid room #, 3 password prompt, 4 room full, 5 accepted (room_type 4 -> play-room list flushed, 5 -> no flush, else arena list flushed), 6 level not appropriate, 7/8 novice-room messages, 9 NEW "Already started."

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: echo of the joined room's type. Read only by result 5: if ==4, the play-room list is flushed (window 0x478 UI rows cleared, label 0x14='0', list at game+0x450 freed); otherwise the arena list is (window 0x2A UI rows cleared, label 0x14='0/0', list at game+0x440 freed). Always present on the wire.

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical (u8 result, u8 room_type); NEW result 9 = "Already started." (removes the requested room, room_no == scene+0xF64, from the arena list); result 5 now also has a room_type 5 branch (no list flush); requested room_no at scene+0xF64 (2008 +0xF48).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Server's answer to a room join request (C2S 0x1A / 0x1B / 0x1C, which all show 'Waiting for the server to response.' in message box window 0x16). Both bytes are always read, then the handler switches on result via jump table 0x4585F4 (1->0x455C6A, 2->0x455CA4, 3->0x455CC1, 4->0x455DE6, 5->0x455CF6, 6->0x455C87, 7->0x455E5A, 8->0x455E77). Error results 1,2,4,6,7,8 call FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0), which rewrites the text of the same message box 0x16. Result 3 dismisses the box (FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1)) and opens the password prompt, which later sends C2S 0x1C with the stored room_no/type and the 5-byte password. Result 5 dismisses the box and frees the relevant list data. Actually entering the room is presumably driven by other packets; not traced.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x1A (join a room clicked in the ARENA or Play&Chat list), 0x1B (join by typed room number) or 0x1C (password submit). The client also shows the wait box for C2S 0x18 (create room), so 0x34 may answer that too (unverified). MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x18 / 0x1A / 0x1B / 0x1C. Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.expected_response: After result 3 the client, on user input, sends C2S 0x1C: u16 room_no, u8 room_type, str[5] password
specs.gates_and_hazards: Result 4 always searches window 0x2A (the arena list), even for play rooms. It uses [game+0x4CC]+0xF48, which the client sets on every join attempt. The client checks level/novice rules before sending 0x1A (same strings as results 6-8), so those results matter mainly for 0x1B join by number. Joining by number accepts only 1..128. No crash hazards found (all window lookups are null-checked).
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x34.py ('무투장 입장?', arena enter?) builds a room-LIST payload (count + 24-byte row). That is wrong for EN: the client would read count=1 as result 1 'Incorrect password.' and the name's first byte as room_type. PySlayer's game_server leaves the 0x34 reply to C2S 0x1A commented out. Our server consumes inbound 0x1A as a 'mob query'. In the room context C2S 0x1A is a room join (u16 room_no, u8 room_type); a mob-related C2S 0x1A may exist elsewhere, so check by context. Our server never sends 0x34.
open_questions: Which follow-up S2C packets move the client into the room after result 5
Whether result 5 is also the success reply for C2S 0x18 room creation
Exact meaning of FUN_00489960 mode 5 / FUN_00483430 mode 4 on window 0x4A (assumed: open password input)

specs.length: 6 (u32 + u8 + u8); only 4 consumed when the uid is not a scene entity

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Entity uid of the player whose arena team is set; resolved by FUN_004189f0 against scene entity list (+0x84). 0 or unknown -> the two u8 are not read
fields.dest_or_source: [2008 text, not re-derived] stack local [esp+0x1A4], passed in EDX to FUN_004189f0

fields.name: team
fields.meaning: Current team: 0=spectator, 1=Blue, 2=Red

fields.name: next_team
fields.meaning: Team subscribed for next round: 0=spectator, 1=Blue, 2=Red, 3=leave arena when the round ends (client converts 3 to entity+0x14E9=1 and stores 0)

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical; team byte is read into a local and applied through FUN_00448350 (team at entity+0x158B), next_team -> entity+0x158C (3 -> entity+0x1589 = 1 and cleared); camera scene+0xF00; team counts scene+0xF93/+0xF94.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Sets a player's current arena team (+0x14EB) and next-round team (+0x14EC). If next_team==3 the client sets the leave flag +0x14E9=1 and stores next_team=0. FUN_00428bc0 applies the state: team 0 -> +0x98=1 (spectator); team!=0 -> if +0x98 was not 3, HP +0x9C=+0x110C, MP +0xA0=+0x1110, +0x15A0=0, buff slots +0xE84 (0x1F8 bytes) and +0x107C (0x90 bytes) zeroed; then +0x98=3. Next it refreshes the local team text ('You are in blue team.', 'You subscribed to enter red team...', 'You subscribed to leave the arena...') and the scoreboard in window 0x47E. If the local player (scene+0x970) is NULL the handler ends here. Otherwise camera follow target scene+0xEE8: if local team!=0 and local+0x15B4!=0x16 -> target=local; else if updated entity team!=0 and (target NULL or target team==0) -> target=entity; else if entity team==0 and entity==target -> FUN_004305b0(game_state,0x27). Finally scene+0xF74 (red alive) and scene+0xF73 (blue alive) are zeroed and recounted over scene entities with +0x98==3, team!=0, HP>0. If the uid is unknown only the u32 is consumed and the handler jumps straight to the recount.
specs.trigger: Server broadcast to arena room members when a player picks/changes team (C2S 0x1D u8 team: 0 spectator, 1 blue, 2 red, 3 leave; 4 also sent at 0x449DDB) or when the server assigns/balances teams.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No map gate in this handler. Unknown uid: 4 bytes consumed, entity untouched, recount still runs. Entity found but local player NULL: break before camera logic and recount. HAZARD: FUN_00428bc0 overwrites +0x98 with 1 or 3 on whatever entity matches, including the local player (normally 4, required by the registration gate); sending it for the local player outside an arena can break local-player state and wipes buffs/refills HP. Leave flag +0x14E9 is never cleared here. UI helpers silently return if window 0x47E is not open.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A wrote 'u32 uid; if(entity exists){u8 team; u8 next_team} else {stop}', analyst B wrote 'u32 uid; if(entity==null){stop}; u8 team; u8 pending_team'. These are the same wire format in different notation, and both are right: 0x455EA9 reads u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8), 0x455EBD FUN_004189f0 lookup, 0x455EC6 JZ 0x455F8D skips both reads when NULL, 0x455EE2 and 0x455EFF read u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) into entity+0x14EB/+0x14EC, and 0x455F05-0x455F11 convert 3 to leave flag. I used the flat early-exit form. On semantics A is more complete: B implies the recount always runs, but at 0x455F37 a NULL local player (scene+0x970) breaks to 0x44D7AD before the camera logic and recount. That only happens when the entity was found; the NULL-entity path jumps straight to the recount at 0x455F8D. C2S team values checked in FUN_00446300: 0x44B5E3->0x44843D Add(0x1D),Add(1); 0x44B624->0x448461 Add(0x1D),Add(2); 0x44B62B->0x4483EE Add(0x1D),Add(0); 0x449DBF->0x4484AC Add(0x1D),Add(3); 0x449DDB Add(0x1D),Add(4). KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c) has no case 0x35 and PySlayer has no builder. Our server: not implemented.
open_questions: Whether the server ever sends next_team=3 or only echoes the client's C2S 0x1D 3 request; meaning of C2S 0x1D value 4 (0x449DDB, possibly cancel-leave) and how the client would treat next_team=4 if echoed (stored raw).
Meaning of entity+0x15B4 == 0x16 in camera-target logic (treated as not an active combatant).

specs.semantics: Processed only when the map control [game_state+0x4FC]+0x7C == 1 (room/arena map); otherwise nothing is read. DUNGEON (result_kind 5): round_result 1 = clear: reads the reward (u32 unused, u16 item [+ u16 tail]), closes window 0x4A5 if open, adds the item to the bag by its kind and records it in the reward window, opens window 0x4A5 (FUN_00497c70(0x4A5,3,1)), plays effect 0x144 (FUN_0042cd90) and refills local HP/MP to max. Any other round_result = failure: message box "Failed to conquer the instant dungeon." (FUN_0049ebc0); if the local player exists it reads u16 hp, u16 mp and sets them. ARENA/BATTLEFIELD (any other kind): reward u32 first, then the five round counters into scene+0xF77..+0xF7B; in mode 6 prints "%uRound ended. [Blue%d:%dRed]"; prints the winner/tie line (mode 7 tie = "Draw. Guild Battle is closing."), sets game_state+0x488 = 0x150/0x151/0x152, shows window 0x47E; final winner "Final winner: Blue/Red Team.[Blue%d:%dRed]" when round_result != 0, mode >= 6 and either side has >= 3 round wins; applies the reward; overwrites the four totals; refreshes the record panel (FUN_00443970) and scoreboard (FUN_00444220); advances the round when round_result != 0; for every scene entity refills HP/MP and clears the buff tables (+0xF24 0x1F8 bytes, +0x111C 0x90 bytes) - the 2008 per-entity team swap (team = next_team) is gone; ends with FUN_00443bc0.
specs.trigger: Arena/battlefield: server sends to all room members when a round ends. Dungeon: server sends to the party in an instance dungeon when it is cleared or failed.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Whole packet ignored unless [game_state+0x4FC]+0x7C == 1. A 2008-format arena packet (6 x u8 then 5 x u32) is now misparsed: the first byte becomes result_kind, and if it happens to be 5 (a 2008 round_result is 0..2, so normally not) the dungeon branch runs. The reward is additive (sending twice credits twice); totals are absolute. The dungeon-failure branch reads hp/mp only if the local player pointer is set - otherwise it consumes 2 bytes. Dungeon reward: the equip-kind item is only added when the equip bag holds fewer than 46 items; no reply is sent either way.

Applies a timed buff or skill effect to the entity with target_uid and plays its visuals. Steps:
(1) Look up the hii record. Unknown id: stop.
(2) Read uid and find the entity.
(3) If the entity exists and (rec+0x1C8 duration != 0 or id in 0x9CE-0x9D8/0x9E4-0x9F9) and FUN_004257a0(id)==1: read the optional ground x,y for 0xA31..0xA3B. FUN_004257a0 returns 0 for 0x187-0x191, 0x1B3-0x1BD, 0x242-0x24C, 0x78B-0x795, 0x7B7-0x7C1, 0x8BB-0x8C5, 0x981-0x98B, 0x997-0x9A1, 0xA05-0xA0F, 0xA3C-0xA67, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB30-0xB45.
(4) FUN_00424e20 then inserts the buff into the entity's 21-slot table at +0xE84. Slot layout: u16 id; u16 |rec+0x1DC|; u16 rec+0x142; u16 x; u16 y; u32 duration = rec+0x1C8, forced to 60000 for 0x9C3-0x9F9; u32 rec+0x158; u32 source uid = the target itself. Duration comes from the CLIENT's hii record, not the wire. The call returns non-zero for party-type ids (0x8E7-0x912, 0xAE3-0xAF8), which fan out stat updates to party or team members.
(5) If any stat-bonus column (rec+0x1B8..0x1C4) is non-zero, the entity's stats are recomputed (FUN_0041ace0).
(6) If the entity exists, effects and sounds play at its position by id range: 0x124-0x12E effect 0x36/sound 0x36; 0x12F-0x139 effect 0x35/sound 0x36; 0x145-0x14F 0x4A; 0x192-0x19C 0x49; 0x1D4-0x1DE 0x52; 0x8C6-0x8D0 sound 0xB4; 0x8FD-0x907 0xCD; 0x8F2-0x8FC 0xCE; 0x8E7-0x8F1 0xCF; 0x908-0x912 0xD0; 0x913-0x91D sound 0xD1; 0x934-0x93E 0xD3; 0x96B-0x975 0xD8; 0xAE3-0xAED 0x10C; 0xAEE-0xAF8 0x10D; 0xB1A-0xB24 sound 0x112.
(7) If target_uid == local uid, the full 0x25 self-use path runs as well. Otherwise, if step 4 returned non-zero, the stats panel, HP bar and party HP bars refresh; then the handler exits.
specs.trigger: When a duration/buff skill (hii type 3 with rec+0x1C8 > 0) cast via C2S 0x15 succeeds. Send it to the caster (target_uid = caster uid) and, presumably, to every other client in the map so they see the buff. For ground-placed skills 0xA31..0xA3B, append the x,y the caster sent in C2S 0x15.

specs.gates_and_hazards:
1) Unknown id: nothing is read past the id.
2) Unknown target uid (or uid 0): no buff and no visuals, but if uid == local uid the self-use logic still runs.
3) When target_uid is the local player this ALSO does everything 0x25 does: MP/HP cost from rec+0x15C/+0x158, cooldown, cast animation, clearing pending skill scene+0x258. Do NOT additionally send 0x25 to the caster or the cost is double-applied.
4) Local-target type-3 path crashes if the local entity (scene+0x970) is null; see the 0x25 hazard.
5) A full buff table (21 slots, per the grouping rules in FUN_00424e20) silently drops the buff.
6) Party buffs under mode [[0x70EED8]+0x70]==1 dereference scene+0x970 +0x14EB, a null-deref risk if the local entity is missing.
7) PySlayer's KR layout (u16, u8 flag, u32 uid, u16 time, u16 time) will MISPARSE on EN: the flag byte gets absorbed into the uid.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4, combat_skill#08, item_inventory#10/#11): THE CLIENT NEVER EXPIRES A BUFF. In field mode it decrements buff-slot +0xC every tick for type-3 AND type-4 entities, past 0 into negative values; the slot is never removed, stats are never recomputed and the icon merely blinks. The server MUST send S2C 0x43 (remove + stat recompute) or S2C 0x3C (icon only) when a Duration ends. Two more live facts: identical item buffs STACK as separate records and icons (no refresh/replace outside the listed id ranges), and a wire source_uid of 0 is stored as the TARGET's own uid, so the slot +0x14 value is not a literal copy of the wire field. The icon is the item's own icon, drawn bottom-right above the HUD buttons, one per record.

PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x3B.py ('UseBuffSkills') sends u16 skill, u8 0, u32 uid, u16 time, u16 time. PySlayer game_server.py sends it for type-3 skills with Con>0, which matches our type-3 + duration semantics.
The KR Hex-Rays handler (case 0x25/0x3B) is structurally different.
Our server (windslayer_server.py) never sends 0x3B.

The client never expires a buff by itself (it counts slot +0xC down into negative values and leaves the record and icon in place), so every timed buff granted with 0x3B / 0x41 / 0x42 must be terminated by the server: 0x43 when stats or auras must be recomputed, 0x3C when only the icon has to go.

The self echo is required: the second confirmer's final window only opens on its own echo, because its [ctx+0x24] was set earlier by the partner's 0x48. The first confirmer's final window opens when the partner's 0x48 arrives, because the client already zeroed its button 3 before sending 0x23.

FUN_00489090 dereferences [0+0x1C] if 0x4E's child list is shorter than 3.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
The packet has no payload: the handler never reads from the packet, so any trailing bytes are ignored. Steps: (1) Posts the system message "Trade has been canceled." (colour 0xFFFD4C87). (2) Hides trade window 0x4E and final-confirm window 0x291 through FUN_00483430(id,1,1). That becomes FUN_00446300(..., param_6=1), which only hides the windows (FUN_004835b0) and sends nothing. (3) If window 0x4E exists and the list of items I offered (list object at +0xAC, count/head at +0xB0) is not empty, it pops records until the list is empty. Each record is 0x38 bytes, allocated by the self branch of S2C 0x4B. The handler uses rec+0x0 = u16 item_id, rec+0x2 = 12 option bytes and rec+0xE = u16 (count/durability-like). It looks up the item definition through FUN_00404210 in [[ctx+0x10]+0xF84]. If found, FUN_00467200 restores the item by category = def+0x154. Category 0: FUN_00423b70(bag+0x5F6, bag+0x650, bag+0x6AC, id, byte bag+0x362, 0,0,0) with ECX=rec+0xE. Category 1: writes the id into the first zero u16 slot of bag+0x380 (slot count = byte bag+0x361, must be <= 0x2D) and copies the 12 bytes from rec+2 to bag+0x3DA+slot*12; rec+0xE is not used. Category 2: FUN_00423e70(bag+0x760, id, byte bag+0x363) with ESI=bag+0x7BA and EAX=rec+0xE. Here bag = [ctx+0x18]. On success the inventory UI refreshes (FUN_00465290). The record is freed either way. (4) Returns 1. The partner's offered-items list (object at +0xBC, head at +0xC0) is not touched.
specs.trigger: Send to both trade parties when either side cancels (C2S 0x24), and by server policy when a party disconnects or leaves the field mid-trade or when final validation fails.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Shared sub1 gate only. Safe to send with no trade open: the windows are simply hidden and the restore loop is skipped when window 0x4E is missing or its list is empty. The client restores offered items to its bag locally, because it removed them when S2C 0x4B (self branch, FUN_00467140) added them to the trade. The server's inventory model must still treat those items as owned. If the item definition is not found, or category 1 has no free slot (or its slot count is over 0x2D), the record is freed without a restore and the client bag loses the item until the next resync. Hiding the windows does NOT send C2S 0x24, so there is no echo loop.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the payload is empty (length 0, no fields). A wrote grammar "" and B wrote "stop". This is a difference in notation, not in wire format. The asm from 0x0046E465 to the RET 0x10 at 0x0046E53F has no CALL through any GetDataFromPacket IAT slot (0x4A4090/94/98/C8/CC/D0/D4/B0/118). None of the callees (FUN_004817d0, FUN_00483430, FUN_004830f0, FUN_00459e60, FUN_00404210, FUN_00467200, FUN_00465290) receives the packet pointer (EDI is overwritten at 0x0046E4A1) or the offset (EBP+0x10). The first packet read after this point belongs to the 0x4B block at 0x0046E550. The canonical grammar is "stop", meaning zero bytes are read. Two semantic details were checked in FUN_00467200's asm. (a) Category mapping: A was right and B was wrong. Category 0 goes to FUN_00423b70 (0x004672C9..F2), category 1 to the u16 slot array at +0x380 plus 12 option bytes at +0x3DA (0x00467249..C6), and category 2 to FUN_00423e70 at +0x760 (0x00467223..3F). B's claim that category 1 is equipment and category 2 is stackable does not match that dispatch. (b) The u16 at rec+0xE is the second stack argument (MOV SI,[ESP+0x10] at 0x0046720A). It is used by categories 0 and 2 and ignored by category 1. B mentioned it as a count and A left it out. List offsets: both are consistent. My-items list object is at +0xAC with head/count at +0xB0 (0x0046E4AF/0x0046E4C0). The partner list object is at +0xBC (0x0046E702 in 0x4B) with head at +0xC0 (0x0046E832 in 0x4A). The record size 0x38 is confirmed by PUSH 0x38/FUN_0048b484 at 0x0046E653. A's claim that the windows close without re-sending C2S 0x24 is confirmed: in FUN_00446300, case 0x4E re-enters only when param_6==2, and caseD_2 exits after FUN_004835b0 when param_6==1. Neither PySlayer nor our server implements this opcode. The companion opcode 0x4A ("Trade completed.", u64 money into [ctx+0x18]+0x228 at 0x0046E7FB) is outside this batch.
open_questions: Whether the original server also sent explicit inventory resync packets after 0x49, or relied only on this client-side restore (server policy, not visible in the client).
What exactly the u16 at rec+0xE means (count vs durability) for categories 0 and 2. It comes from the S2C 0x4B payload, which is outside this batch.
Where the partner list at +0xBC/+0xC0 is cleared. It is not cleared in this handler, and the 0x46 block does not visibly clear it either (it may happen inside FUN_0047d700 on window open).

Trade window item-added notification. All six option words form a 12-byte block (slots opt_count..4 stay zero).
