fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: UID of the player whose class changed. Matched against entity+0x84 in the scene list at scene+0x0C. uid 0 or an unknown uid means the handler stops here and ignores the rest of the packet.

fields.name: class
fields.meaning: Base class index into the 15-byte name table at 0x70C588, row 0: 0 Novice, 1 Warrior, 2 Monk, 3 Archer, 4 Rogue, 5 Mage, 6 Priest. 0 means no class change yet: FUN_00446300 at 0x4493D2 shows 'You can use [Battlefield] after class change'. The HP and MP recompute functions return early if it is 7 or more.

fields.name: class_tier
fields.meaning: Advancement tier/branch, 0..2. The name index is (tier*7+class)*15 (0x440CAE..0x440CC0). Tier-1 row: 8 Berserker, 9 Fighter, 10 Sniper, 11 Assassin, 12 Elementalist, 13 Bishop. Tier-2 row: 14 Paladin, 15 Counter, 16 BeastMaster, 17 Trapper, 18 Summoner, 19 DarkPriest, 20 empty. The quest filter indexes class*3+tier with no bounds check, so the value must be 2 or less. If 0, the client recomputes stats, HP, MP and the quest list. If not 0, it only stores the two bytes.

specs.length: 6 (4+1+1) when the uid is found; only 4 bytes consumed when it is not. Always send all 6.
specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical; class/tier -> entity+0x118/+0x119; tier==0 path: FUN_0041B830, FUN_004292A0, FUN_004294E0 (MP recalc no longer skipped at level 0), FUN_0048AC00 quest-list rebuild.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Reads the uid and looks up the entity. If it is not found, processing ends and the last 2 bytes are ignored. Otherwise it stores class at +0x110 and class_tier at +0x111. These are the same fields that 0x02 and 0x07 fill. If class_tier == 0, the client then (1) runs FUN_0041ace0 to recompute derived stats, (2) runs FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) to recompute max HP (+0x110C) and lower cur HP (+0x9C) if it is above the new max, (3) if level (+0x99) != 0, runs FUN_00427f40(0) to recompute max MP (+0x1110) and clamp cur MP (+0xA0), and (4) runs FUN_004781c0 to rebuild the local player's available-quest list. There is no popup, no sound and no reply packet.
specs.trigger: Server sends this when a character's class changes (job advancement). Send it to the player and to clients that have that entity spawned.
specs.expected_response: none (no Add/Send in the block or its callees)
specs.gates_and_hazards: No in-world gate. FUN_004189f0 returns null for uid 0 without touching the scene. For uid != 0 it dereferences scene+0x0C without a null check, so the scene object must exist. An unknown uid is silently ignored. A non-zero class_tier skips all stat/HP/MP/quest recompute, so derived stats stay stale until something else recomputes them. A class of 7 or more makes the HP/MP recompute return early and indexes past the name table. A class_tier above 2 overlaps the next class's quest flags. HP and MP are only clamped down (arg 0). The quest refresh needs the local player object ([+0x928] != 0 check at 0x4781D0). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (login_character#16): 0x58 does NOT redraw the local status window or the HUD class label - they keep the old class name until another FUN_00442510 redraw. For the owner, follow it with a packet that forces a redraw (e.g. the 0x18 job-item path or 0x74).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 @0x45760F), a lookup via FUN_004189f0 @0x457623 with JZ break @0x45762E, then u8 into +0x110 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457647) and u8 into +0x111 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457664), then a recompute gate on +0x111==0 @0x457673. They differ only in how the DSL writes it. A wrote 'if(found){u8 u8} else {stop}'. B wrote 'if(null){stop} u8 u8'. Both put the same bytes in the same order under the same condition, so neither is wrong. I chose A's explicit if/else because it maps directly onto the asm's JZ-to-break. B's field notes are also verified: the Battlefield gate at 0x4493D2 checks +0x110==0, and the quest filter at 0x4782DD..0x4782F0 uses class*3+tier. A's name-table claim is verified by dumping 0x70C588 from the exe, with one correction: the tier-2 row is not aligned with the class indexes (index 14=Paladin sits at class 0). Other references: PySlayer KR Hex-Rays case 0x58 reads u32 plus three u8 and gates on the third. EN reads two u8 and gates on the second, so EN is 6 bytes and must not copy the KR layout. PySlayer has no server builder for 0x58. Our server has no 0x58 builder, but its 0x02/0x07 builders write class/0 into the same two fields.
open_questions: Tier-2 name row at 0x70C588 is shifted by one versus the class index: (2*7+1)=15 is 'Counter' for Warrior, (2*7+0)=14 is 'Paladin' for Novice, and Priest tier 2 is empty. So either class_tier is not a simple sequential tier, or the client string table has an off-by-one. Needs a live check of which (class, tier) pairs the real server used.
Why stats, HP, MP and quests are only recomputed when class_tier == 0 is unclear.
Which C2S request or NPC flow triggers a class change in EN was not traced.

fields.name: slot
fields.meaning: 1-based active-quest slot (1..3), the index into char+0x256 u16[3]. Checked with a SIGNED test slot-1 < 3, so 0 is also accepted (hazard). A value of 4 or more ends reading with no UI refresh.

fields.name: progress
fields.meaning: Absolute progress counter for that slot (e.g. kill count), compared against quest record ReqPro (+0xDF8) and shown in the active-quest tab as progress/ReqPro.

specs.semantics:
2009 (sub2 0x489FCE): u8 slot; if (int)(slot-1) < 5 (slots 1..5; slot 0 also passes the signed test and writes char+0x269, the high byte of active slot 5 - avoid it) read u8 progress into char+0x269+slot; if the ready flag char+0x26E+slot is 0 and the quest record is now complete, set it and print "[%s] You are ready to complete the quest."; then refresh the quest window.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Updates one active quest's progress counter. The byte goes straight into char+0x25B+slot. Then, if that slot's ready flag at char+0x25E+slot is 0 and the quest record for the slot's quest id (u16 at char+0x254+2*slot) exists, the client calls FUN_00426500(ctx+0x10, record, progress, gold64 at char+0x228, bag arrays...). That function returns 1 when all of these hold: (Money >= 0, or gold >= |Money|), (ReqPro == 0, or progress >= ReqPro), and every Demand item (up to 10; types 0 and 2 counted in the bags, type 1 via FUN_00424df0, type 5 skipped) is present in sufficient count. On success the client sets the ready flag to 1 and prints "[<quest name>] You are ready to complete the quest." in green. The message appears once, because the flag suppresses repeats. The quest window is refreshed whenever slot <= 3. The ready flag only controls the message; the turn-in logic re-checks the conditions itself.
specs.trigger: Server sends it whenever a tracked quest counter changes, e.g. a monster kill counted toward ReqPro. It can also be sent with an unchanged value to re-evaluate readiness.
specs.expected_response: none (the player then talks to the ENPC, which sends C2S 0x17 turn-in)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Skipped entirely if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null. slot=0 passes the signed check and writes progress into char+0x25B, the HIGH byte of active slot 3's quest id (u16 at 0x25A). That corrupts the quest log, and the client then reads a garbage quest id from char+0x254. Only send slot 1..3. Progress is a u8 (max 255). The slot must match the client's own placement: 0x26 fills the first empty slot, and 0x27/0x38 empty the slot.
specs.references: PySlayer opcode_59: p8(random slot) + p8u(unk), which agrees on 2 bytes. Its comment 'v47 - 1 < 5' suggests the newer KR build has 5 slots; EN checks < 3. Our server's _send_quest_progress packs '<BB' slot(1..3), count, which matches. It assigns slots lowest-free in _quest_assign_slot, the same rule as the client.
open_questions: Which game events the original server counted into progress: ReqPro with the NPC field at +0xDFC, possibly a target monster id. Not decidable from this handler.

specs.semantics:

[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
First packet on the game server connection. Client installs the key (SetCodeKey), re-initialises the cash/billing sub-object at gs+0x700 (stores game_state, ui root, socket, scene+0xF84, &username), computes MD5(username) as 32 hex chars into gs+0xD0A and sets scene+0x218 = 1 if it differs from the 32-char string at scene+0x131 (else 0; later drives the 'Account transfer' text in 0x02). It then sleeps 1000 ms and sends C2S 0x01 login = str[41] username (scene+0x48) + str[21] password (scene+0x101), 62 bytes after the opcode, which matches the captured 62-byte login.
specs.trigger: Server sends immediately on accepting the TCP connection to 7022 (before any client traffic). At Fireway level it must carry the NoEncode flag and be encoded with EncodebyArray since no key exists yet (per our server/memory).
specs.expected_response: C2S 0x01 on the game socket after Sleep(1000): u8 0x01, char[0x83] from scene+0x48 (launcher SSO argument, trailing space kept), u32 scene+0x154 (value from the last S2C 0x02; 0 on first login). No password on the wire (live-verified).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate other than the global [gs+0x408]!=0 drop. Any 0x5A received mid-session re-keys the cipher (desync unless the server re-keys identically), blocks the network thread 1 s inside the receive critical section, and re-sends login (our server ignores mid-flow 0x01).
specs.references: Our GameServer._handle_fireway sends 0x5A + <i seed with NoEncode+EncodebyArray - matches. protocol.md matches (MD5, Sleep 1000, login send). PySlayer KR 0x5A handler is the same idea but the KR login it triggers carries many more fields (id + 3 more strings + 4 bytes); EN sends only username[41]+password[21].
open_questions: Origin of the 32-char string at scene+0x131 compared against MD5(username) (probably launcher/command-line supplied) was not traced; it only affects the account-transfer UI text in 0x02.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Looks up the player by uid. If not found, processing ends. Otherwise it overwrites the player's room info: u16 room number (+0xE2), u8 room type (+0xE1) and a 17-byte title (+0xD0). All three are read unconditionally, unlike the spawn record, which skips type and title when the room number is 0. With room_no != 0 the client draws a room balloon over that player, and clicking the player offers to join that room (dialog 0x133 gets the room number and type). Send room_no=0 to clear the balloon. There is no UI refresh, no sound and no reply.
specs.trigger: Broadcast to clients in the same field when a player creates, enters or leaves an arena room, play room or battle room, so others see or lose the balloon and can click to join. 0x07 can carry the same state at spawn.
specs.expected_response: none directly. If a viewer confirms dialog 0x133, the client sends a join request (not traced here).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No in-world gate. Scene must exist when uid != 0 (FUN_004189f0 dereferences scene+0x0C). An unknown uid is silently ignored. The title is used as a C string (sprintf_s '[%s] %s' at 0x44C968, Draw_Text at 0x431945); if all 17 bytes are non-NUL it runs into the room_type/room_no bytes, so always NUL-terminate. The balloon only draws when [game_state+0x4D8]+0x70 == 0 and g_ui_root+0x40 != 0. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C40, pvp_arena#25): a 0x5B carrying the RECEIVER'S OWN uid does draw the balloon over the local player (verified with a "Duel Room" balloon above the local character, cleared again by 0x5C). The server must therefore decide deliberately whether the room owner gets their own balloon.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 @0x4576D8), lookup FUN_004189f0 @0x4576EC with TEST/JZ break @0x4576F3/0x4576F5, then u16 into +0xE2 (IAT 0x4A4090 @0x45770F), u8 into +0xE1 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457729) and char[0x11] into +0xD0 (IAT 0x4A4098, PUSH 0x11 @0x45773C, call @0x457745), then JMP break. There is no condition between the three reads. They differ only in how the DSL writes it: A 'if(found){...} else {stop}' versus B 'if(null){stop} ...'. Both put the same 24 bytes in the same order, so neither is wrong. I chose A's explicit if/else form. B's extra facts are verified: S2C 0x75 writes +0xE2=0x81 at 0x457FD3; type/title are read unconditionally here but only when +0xE2 != 0 in the spawn record (0x44F03C JZ 0x44F07C); and the render gates at 0x4317B3..0x4317CD. A's render and click details are verified at 0x4317DA..0x4318F2 and 0x44C8C5..0x44C9AE. Other references: memory note project_local_player_spawn.md calls +0xE2 'marriage'; the binary shows it is the room number/balloon, though that note's read order matches. Not present in PySlayer server_packets or the KR Hex-Rays excerpt. Our server has no builder.

Reads a u8 reason. Calls FUN_0044d4b0 with ESI=game_state. If game_state+0x408==0 (window not already closing) and game_state+0x1528==0 (no disconnect already handled), it sets +0x1528=1 and shows the reason text in a modal message box (FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0)). The client does not close the socket itself here; the 5-second timer closes the whole game.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
A line of text in the Messenger 1:1 / group chat room. It is processed only while CMessenger+0xCC (the room id set by S2C 0x0F result 1, cleared on every S2C 0x03) is non-zero. Otherwise the handler returns 1 without reading anything. When processed, the client reads sender_name[17], msg_len and message[msg_len]. It then builds "%s : " from sender_name and appends it to chat-room window 0x177 via FUN_00472430. That line is colour 0xFFC766A6 if sender_name equals your own name (+0x7C), else 0xFF3277CC. Next it builds "  %s" from the message and appends it in 0xFFC8C8C8. The handler returns 1. The sender (FUN_00470120) only transmits C2S 0x35 and never appends the text locally, so the server must relay this packet to the sender as well as to the other room members.
specs.trigger: Server relay of C2S 0x35 {u8 len, bytes[len]}. FUN_00470120 sends that only when CMessenger+0x74 != 0, the text is non-NULL, +0xCC != 0 and ENGINE Curse_Engine_Clean passes. Send it to every member of the room, the sender included.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub3 entry gate: CMessenger+0x68 and +0x70 must be non-zero, or sub3 returns 0 (unclaimed). Room gate: +0xCC != 0, otherwise the packet is silently ignored with nothing consumed. The reads use CMessenger+0x74 (g_sock_game, set by FUN_0046f860 from S2C 0x03) as the CSNSocket this pointer. CRASH HAZARD 1: the message line is built with _sprintf_s(buf, 0x3D, "  %s", message), which needs strlen(message) <= 58. A longer string (a msg_len of 59..255 with no NUL inside, or a msg_len >= 61, which is unterminated inside the 61 zeroed bytes) makes _sprintf_s call the CRT invalid-parameter handler, and by default the process terminates. CRASH HAZARD 2: msg_len up to 255 writes esp0+0x100..0x1FE. That stays below the stack cookie at esp0+0x244, so there is no cookie failure, but it makes the strlen unbounded. CRASH HAZARD 3: sender_name must contain a NUL within its 17 bytes, since the local is not pre-zeroed and feeds "%s : " into the same 61-byte buffer. Rule for the server: 1..58 text bytes with no embedded NUL, and a name of at most 16 chars plus NUL.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: There is no real wire-format disagreement. Analyst A gave str[17] sender_name, u8 msg_len, bytes[msg_len] message, gated on CMessenger+0xCC != 0 with else stop. Analyst B gave the same three reads under the same gate but wrote the text as str[msg_len]. The structural-signature tool did not recognise that variable-length str, so it reported B as 'str[17] u8' only. The asm proves the layout both analysts described. At 0x47132D, CMP [EBX+0xCC],0 / JZ 0x471FF6 returns 1 before any read. At 0x471343/0x47134A, PUSH 0x11 then call [0x4A4098] reads 17 bytes into esp0+0x20. At 0x47135E, call [0x4A4094] reads a u8 into esp0+0x12. At 0x47137D/0x47138B/0x471397, MOVZX ECX,[esp0+0x12] is pushed as N for call [0x4A4098] into esp0+0x100, and no further GetDataFromPacket follows before the RET at 0x471476. A's bytes[msg_len] is the correct canonical DSL, because str[N] denotes fixed-width NUL-padded text and this field is variable-length with no terminator on the wire. B was also right to leave the sender echo as an open question, and it is now resolved: FUN_00470120 (C2S 0x35 at 0x470163: Add u8 0x35, Add u8 len, Add(text, len), Send) never appends locally, so the server must echo. On buffer size, B's 61-byte figure is the zeroed span (esp0+0x100..0x13C) and A's 64 bytes is the slot up to the next local at esp0+0x140; both agree the text must be <= 58 bytes. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x61.py (KR) builds pstr(name,17)+p8(len)+pstr(chat,len), which agrees. Its 'About normal chat?' comment is wrong: in EN this is the Messenger chat-room line (window 0x177). windslayer_server.py does not implement it.

Whether the room id in +0xCC must match anything on this packet: the packet carries no room id, so the client assumes a single active room.

Updates two text labels in the Battlefield window (UI id 0x14): control 9 gets 'Join(join_count/12)' and control 4 gets 'player_count Players'. There is no gate on game mode (unlike S2C 0x20, which checks [game_state+0x4D8]+0x70 != 1). The labels update even if the window is closed; FUN_004838c0 returns 0 if the window or control is missing. Nothing is stored in game state.
specs.trigger: Send when the Battlefield / Death Match queue counts change, and plausibly in reply to C2S 0x38 (opening the Battlefield window with the T key) so the window shows current counts.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Fireway readers bounds-check. On a short packet GetDataFromPacket leaves the destination and offset unchanged, calls CSNSockMyListener::OnError (0x4788E0), which only logs 'Error occured in Fireway (0x15/0x16)', and returns. So a short or empty 0x63 does not desync or crash, but the labels are formatted from stale stack data in the OnReceive frame (garbage text). Always send all 3 bytes. Keep join_count at 12 or below to match the /12 display. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (quest_cards_misc#06): an EMPTY S2C 0x63 (the old baseline's misroute of the client's C2S 0x63) leaves the Battlefield window's Death Match label showing garbage ("60276 Players"); only control 4 is visibly corrupted. Never answer C2S 0x63 with an empty 0x63.
specs.references: Our server (windslayer_server.py:607-608) answers C2S 0x63 with an EMPTY S2C 0x63 (b''). That triggers two Fireway short-read errors and writes garbage 'Join(?/12)' / '? Players' text into the Battlefield window; send u16+u8 (e.g. 00 00 00) or nothing instead. The same 'Join' string (0x6F6368) and 'Join(%u/12)' format are used by S2C 0x20 ('Death Match waiting list.'). Not in PySlayer server_packets or the KR Hex-Rays excerpt.
open_questions: Is S2C 0x63 the intended reply to C2S 0x63 (sent after map load on socket [game_state+0xDD0]) or to C2S 0x38 (Battlefield window open)? Static analysis shows no request/response link.
Exact meaning of player_count (queue population vs players currently inside the battlefield) is not confirmed by any other reference.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Replaces the whole client-side bank (warehouse) state. First it zeroes [game_state+0x4cc]+0x980..+0xE77 (0x4F8 bytes). Then it reads 3 tab capacities and 3 slot-ordered lists: Equipment is item u16 plus a 12-byte record of up to 5 option u16 and a trailing u16. Consumable is item u16 plus u16 qty. Misc is item u16 plus u8 qty. Last it reads the bank gold u64. FUN_00465110 (reached with ESI=this+0xD5C; that object's +0x18 points to the same block +0x48, so offsets 0x938..0xE28 in the callees match 0x980..0xE70 here) sets the gold text in window 0x1A7, resets the tab-button states and rebuilds the visible grid (FUN_00465C70). Unused slots stay zero, i.e. empty. Nothing is sent back.
specs.trigger: Server-initiated. The bank window (0x1A7) opens from local data only: bank NPC -> password dialog -> C2S 0x51 -> S2C 0x80(1,0x1A7), and no request for contents is sent. So a server should send 0x65 before the player can open the bank (e.g. at enter-world or right before 0x80 for 0x1A7). It should also send it whenever the full bank state needs to be resynced. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C32, shop_storage#03): a 0x65 sent AT ANY TIME BEFORE S2C 0x80 {1, 0x1A7} is enough - the bank window draws the block when it opens. The extra post-open 0x65 that design F3 / section 1.5 asks for is OPTIONAL; it is harmless but it resets the tab selection to Equipment.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: There is no gate; it always runs. It has no bounds checks. (1) Any list count > 60 writes past its 60-entry array: equip_count > 60 runs item ids into the record area and records past +0xCCC. Near 255 it writes past the 0x4F8-byte block into the rest of the scene/player object, which corrupts the heap. (2) option_count > 5 spills into equip_attr_last (count 6 gets overwritten by the trailing read) and into the next slot's record. For slot 59 it spills into the consumable array. Keep option_count <= 5 and every list count <= 60. (3) Capacities > 60 only affect drawing. The client's own +5 extension stops at 60. (4) Any 0x65 wipes everything, so partial updates must resend the full state.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder (server_packets has no opcode_0x65.py). The KR Hex-Rays 0x65 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c:7745) is a reworked layout: it reads the u64 FIRST, then 3 u8, then 3 lists of 48-byte records via sub_40A010, with a 0x57F8 memset. So KR does NOT carry over to EN. The EN equipment-entry encoding (u16 item, u8 n, n*u16, u16) is the same as the player-inventory equipment list in the EN 0x03 handler (+0x3C8/+0x422/+0x42C) and as PySlayer opcode_0x03 'Equipment' (p16 item, p8 5, 5*p16 enchant, p16). windslayer_server.py has no 0x65 builder, and memory notes do not mention it.
open_questions: Meaning of equip_attr_last (record +10). Worn equipment in 0x07 carries 6 fixed u16, and this looks like the 6th, but its meaning (durability/grade/upgrade?) was not traced through tooltip FUN_00484140.
Real default bank capacities (the extension item adds 5 up to 60). The initial value is unknown, and PySlayer uses 35 for the player inventory.

[RESOLVED by live verification shop_storage#03, 2026-09-17] Live: any 0x65 sent before the 0x80 {1, 0x1A7} bank-open reply is enough - the window renders from the stored block when it opens. A post-open 0x65 is optional and merely resets the tab to Equipment. Original question: "When the original server sent 0x65 (at login/enter-world vs. right before the 0x80 bank-open reply) is not provable statically. The client never requests it."
Deposit/withdraw deltas are handled elsewhere (e.g. SubHandler1 0x46CF40 reads a u64 into bank gold at +0xE70). Those opcodes are outside this batch.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Confirms moving an item from the inventory into the Bank (window 0x1A7, 'There are no empty space in Bank.'). Sets gold, looks up the item definition and branches on its type (itemdef+0x154): 0 = u16-stack item (bank tab at char+0xC84 ids / +0xCFC counts), 1 = equipment (bank ids char+0x93C, 12-byte blobs char+0x9B4; identified by an exact 12-byte opts+ext match), 2 = u8-stack item (bank ids char+0xD74 / u8 counts +0xDEC). It adds +qty to the bank, then removes qty from the matching inventory tab (inventory: equip char+0x380/+0x3DA, type0 +0x5F6/+0x650, type2 +0x760/+0x7BA). If both succeed it rebuilds the Bank and inventory windows.
specs.trigger: Server sends after a bank-deposit request. Best candidate is C2S 0x13 (u16 item_id, u16 qty, u8 n, n*u16 opt, u16 item_ext), sent from FUN_00469090 when the drag source is inventory window 9 (after an 'exceeded the amount you have' check).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No window/NPC gate in the handler. Silent no-op (gold still applied) if item id is unknown, the type is >2, a bank tab capacity byte (char+0x938/939/93A, unlocked slots) is >60, an inventory capacity byte (char+0x361/362/363) is >45, the qty is out of range, or there is no free bank slot / not enough in inventory. The bank is mutated BEFORE the inventory; if the inventory removal fails the bank change stays but no refresh happens (desync). opt_count must be <=5 (stack overflow hazard).
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Not in windslayer_server.py. Wire layout is byte-identical to our documented S2C 0x19 SellResult (u64 gold, u16 item, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16, u16 trailer).

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Reads 3 u64 values with no branches. The first one is thrown away. The second is stored as storage gold at player_info+0xE28 and the third as inventory gold at player_info+0x228. Both are then written as decimal text (%I64u) into UI labels: storage window 0x1A7 child 10 and inventory window 9 child 11. specs.trigger: Most likely the server's reply to C2S 0x3E (deposit gold: u64 amount from gold dialog 0x1AA, checked against inventory gold) or C2S 0x3F (withdraw gold: u64 amount from dialog 0x1AB, checked against storage gold). Send the new totals for both purses.

specs.references: Not in PySlayer (server_packets/__init__.py imports opcode_0x68 but the file doesn't exist). Our server has no builder. Window 0x1A7 is called storage because NPC function id 0x1A7 opens window 0x1A7 (FUN_004447d0), and it has item tabs 7/8/9 plus gold dialogs 0x1AA/0x1AB.

fields.meaning: Number of 28-byte records in THIS packet (was i32 in 2008). 0 skips the loop (TEST CL,CL at 0x46AB5E).

fields.name: cash_balance

fields.name: mileage_balance

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Record +0x04: item template id (1-based into the item table at cash-shop ctx+0x1C).

fields.name: limit_type
fields.meaning: Record +0x06: 1 = count-limited, 2 = period item (SYSTEMTIME expiry), 3 = PET record (new in 2009: +0x08.. is a pet sub-record, see pet_* fields), other = no special handling.

fields.name: unk_07
fields.meaning: Record +0x07: no reader found. Send 0.

fields.name: pet_exp
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x08: pet experience. Level thresholds (table 0x5259C4): <120 L1, <360 L2, <840 L3, <1800 L4, <3720 L5, <7560 L6, <15240 L7, <30600 L8, else L9. 0x7788 (30600) draws the pet exp bar at 100% (FUN_00442710).

fields.name: pet_summoned
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0A: 0 = the spawned pet entity is put in state 2 (entity+0x9C=2, not active); non-zero = state 4 (active) unless the local entity byte +0x158B is 0 and the map flag [map+0x7C]==1 (0x46AA5C..0x46AA77). Inferred name.

fields.name: pet_level
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0B: pet level 1..9. 0x6A OVERWRITES it client-side from pet_exp (FUN_00429680, only when pet_exp != 0); 0x6F uses the sent value as is. Drives the growth stage entity+0x9E (level<5 -> 1, <9 -> 2, 9 -> 3) and the pet window label "Level %d".

fields.name: pet_gauge_pct
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0C: shown as "%u%%" and as gauge 0x1C of the pet window (FUN_00442670). Probably satiety/stamina 0..100 (inferred).

fields.name: pet_name
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0D..+0x1B: pet name, strcpy (unbounded) into the pet entity +0x00 at 0x46A815. MUST contain a NUL inside the record (<= 14 chars).

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x08: count / remaining uses (also the stat-reset allowance, 2008 live C13).

fields.name: expire_year..expire_milliseconds
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x0A..+0x19: expiry date/time for period items (year 0 = no date).

fields.name: origin
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x1A, read as a byte (2009 shop UI FUN_00465890 line 1192): 0 = bought with cash (refund value shown), 3 = event reward.

fields.name: unk_1b

specs.semantics: Cash shop entry, now able to span several packets. Reads mode and box_count first. mode 0/1: clears game+0x16F8 (wait flag) and frees box list ctx+0x28. mode 0/3: reads cash -> ctx+0x590 and mileage -> ctx+0x594. Every mode: appends box_count 28-byte records to ctx+0x28; for pet records (limit_type 3) with non-zero exp the client overwrites record+0x0B with the level computed from exp. mode 0/3 only, after the records: rebuilds snapshot lists +0x48 (copy of +0x28) and +0x58 (copy of owned list +0x04, filled by 0x6F), ctx+0x5C0 = 0, FUN_00460590 shop UI init, FUN_00461ad0 swaps the world for ./hs/preview99_01.hmi with a preview avatar, opens windows 0x1CF/0x1FB/0x1FC/0x1FD (and 0x3F3 once), shows the first-purchase mileage message if byte ctx+0x00 != 0, and FUN_004646c0 pops the gift dialog for the head of the 0x6D queue. Other modes return right after the records. Returns 1.
specs.trigger: Reply to the client's cash-shop entry request (not re-traced for 2009). For more than 255 box records send mode 1, then mode 2 pages, then a final mode 3 page; otherwise one mode 0 packet.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 entry gate ([ctx+0x14], [ctx+0x18] non-NULL). HAZARD (as 2008): mode 0/3 unloads the world map, loads the preview map and registers a preview avatar as local player; 2008 LIVE found no working exit control, so the server must restore the world with the map-enter sequence (S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07). Send 0x6F (final page) before the 0x6A final page, because list +0x04 is snapshotted then. A mode 2/3 page without a preceding 0/1 appends to the old list (duplicates). Records are heap-allocated per entry; box_count is a u8, so at most 255 per packet. pet_name must be NUL-terminated inside the record.
specs.references: 2008 spec 0x6A (handler 0x461BDA: u32 cash, u32 mileage, i32 count, records). Strings: "Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash..." 0x52ABB8, ./hs/preview99_01.hmi (FUN_00461ad0). Pet level table 0x5259C4 {0,120,360,840,1800,3720,7560,15240,30600}. Pet record consumers: FUN_00442670 (+0x0C gauge "%u%%"), FUN_00442710 (+0x08 exp, +0x0B "Level %d").
open_questions: Which C2S requests shop entry/exit in 2009 (not re-traced).
Meaning of pet sub-record bytes +0x07 and the exact semantics of +0x0A (summoned) and +0x0C (gauge) are inferred from the spawn/UI code only.
Whether the original server ever used modes 1/2 (paging) or always mode 0.
specs.verification: 2009 asm of FUN_0046a2e0 case 0x6A (0x46AAAC..0x46AF26) read end to end with the IAT map (2009 Fireway IAT: 0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 uchar, 0x4C70F4 ushort, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7100 int, 0x4C7104 ulong, 0x4C7108 uint, 0x4C710C u64); decomp of FUN_00429680, FUN_00442670, FUN_00442710, FUN_00461ad0 checked; compared with the 2008 handler 0x461BDA and its spec. Record layout for limit_type!=3 unchanged; the limit_type 3 union was derived from the pet consumers (0x6F spawn code 0x46A6BC..0x46AA7E and the pet window helpers).
specs.diff_vs_2008: CHANGED. 2008: u32 cash, u32 mileage, i32 box_count, records. 2009: u8 mode, u8 box_count, then cash+mileage ONLY when mode is 0 or 3, then records. The list clear happens only for mode 0/1 and the shop entry only for mode 0/3 (paging). fields.name: mileage_balance

fields.name: item_serial
fields.meaning: Unique id of the bought cash item (record +0x00). Later 0x6E, 0x72 and 0x73 and C2S 0x45 find the record by this value. The next nine fields all come from ONE 28-byte buffer read at 0x462318.

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item template id (record +0x04). Ids 0x75C..0x761 (1884-1889, equipment/consumable/etc/storage slot expansions) are applied right away (+5 slots, up to 45 for inventory or 60 for bank) and are not stored.

fields.name: item_kind
fields.meaning: Record kind: 1 = counted item (quantity goes down on use, record removed at 0); 2 = duration/period item (expire_time is valid). Matches item def +0x1F6. The client only reads the low byte.

fields.name: unk_07
fields.meaning: Unused by the client (probably the high byte of a u16 kind, or padding). Send 0.

fields.name: quantity

fields.name: expire_time

fields.name: origin
fields.meaning: Source flag. 3 = event reward, which shows "Congratulation.\r\n\r\nYou received an event item.."

fields.name: unk_1b
fields.meaning: Unused by this handler; send 0

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Result of a cash-shop purchase. On success the client sets cash and mileage to the absolute values sent and redraws their labels. It shows the bonus-mileage popup if mileage went up. It reads one 28-byte cash item record. If record.item_id is a slot-expansion ticket (0x75C..0x761), the client applies it (+5 slots, with a popup) and frees the record. Otherwise it adds the record to the cash item box list (mgr+0x28), with no check for duplicate serials. Both paths then rebuild box window 0x1FC (FUN_0045b280) and inventory-side window 0x1FD (FUN_0045b360), and redraw the labels. On failure the client only shows a popup.
LIVE: the generic failure message has a second line 'Please try again in a few minutes.'; slot-extension success grows the bag from 35 to 40 slots.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x43 'C' (buy): u8 opcode, bool pay_with_mileage, u8 count, then count x u16 item_id; sent from cash shop windows 0x1F7/0x1F8/0x1FF. The server probably sends one 0x6C per bought item, since each packet carries only one record.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 returns 0 without reading if mgr+0x14 or mgr+0x18 is NULL (cash-shop manager not initialized). A repeated serial makes duplicate box entries. Result 0x0E and other non-1 values read nothing after the result byte.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer (doc/server_to_client/README.md only lists 0x6C among Packet_handler_4 opcodes). Not in windslayer_server.py. Our server's 0x80 'CashShopBalance' does not write mgr+0x588/+0x58C: in the corpus only FUN_0045ae40 (reset) and sub4 opcodes 0x6C/0x6E/0x70/0x71 write those fields. Record layout agrees with the 0x6F list parser (FUN_0045e8e0(item_id@+4, qty@+8, serial@+0); kind==2 && year!=0 -> expiry popup FUN_0045ebb0) and with FUN_00464380.

Exact meaning of record bytes +0x07 and +0x1B; is item_kind really a u16 whose high byte is unused?
Is the mileage sent here the balance after a 50% bonus? The client only compares it with the old value.

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Record +0x12 (was +0x11): gift message, copied into dialog control 4 (unbounded copy - NUL-terminate, <=90 chars).

fields.name: unk_6d
fields.meaning: Record +0x6D: alignment padding before the u16 (no reader). Send 0.

fields.name: item_id

fields.meaning: NEW. Record +0x70: item option index. 0 = "No Option"; non-zero -> dialog control 9 shows option name entry (DAT_00525450[itemdef+0x1CC]*5 + option) of the 32-byte name table at 0x5486C0, and is stored in the dialog data word +2.

specs.semantics: Adds pending received gifts to a client queue (append-only CPList ctx+0x600; one new(0x82) + one 130-byte read per record). After the loop, even when gift_count==0, it finds UI window id 3 and sets its 6th control's state +0x18 = 0 (enables the HUD gift button). The dialog 0x3EF is opened by FUN_004646c0 (end of S2C 0x6A mode 0/3, and after each dialog confirm): it takes the head record, looks up item_id and shows item name (control 1), sender (control 6), option name (control 9) and message (control 4). Button 2 with a non-empty reply sends C2S 0x4B {u16 9999, str[17] sender, str[91] reply}; the head gift is popped either way.
specs.trigger: Send when the player has pending cash-shop gifts (world entry, or right after another player's gift). For the popup, send before the 0x6A final page.
specs.expected_response: None directly; the dialog reply produces C2S 0x4B (u16 9999, str[17] sender_name, str[91] reply_text).
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 gate. Records are not zeroed: a short packet leaves heap garbage. sender_name and message are copied unbounded into the dialog controls - both MUST be NUL-terminated inside their fields. Queue-stall hazard (as 2008): a head record whose item_id is unknown, or whose def has +0x1F0 == 0 and id outside 0xCFF..0xD04, never opens the dialog and blocks the queue. 2008 LIVE C20 (same code shape): the map-change sequence resets the HUD gift button; resend with count = 0 to relight it (records are append-only).

Same 130-byte record shape as the 2009 S2C 0x78 memo record (u8, name at +1, text at +0x12, SYSTEMTIME at +0x72).

fields.name: mode
fields.meaning: NEW in 2009. Paging mode: 0 = single packet (clear + records + finalize); 1 = first page (clear + records); 2 (or any other value) = middle page (append only); 3 = last page (append + finalize). Clear = free lists +0x04/+0x38 and purge cash items from the bags (gated); finalize = inventory/period UI rebuild and pet spawn.

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Records in this packet (was i32 in 2008).

fields.name: is_equipped
fields.meaning: 1 byte per record. Non-zero: record goes to ctx+0x38 only (worn cash item; a pet record there becomes the active pet). Zero: goes to ctx+0x04 and into a bag.

fields.name: serial
fields.meaning: Record +0x00: unique cash item serial (key for FUN_0046df70 consume and the box lookups).

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Record +0x04: item template id (1-based into the item table at cash-shop ctx+0x1C).

fields.name: limit_type
fields.meaning: Record +0x06: 1 = count-limited, 2 = period item (SYSTEMTIME expiry), 3 = PET record (new in 2009: +0x08.. is a pet sub-record, see pet_* fields), other = no special handling.

fields.name: unk_07
fields.meaning: Record +0x07: no reader found. Send 0.

fields.name: pet_exp
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x08: pet experience. Level thresholds (table 0x5259C4): <120 L1, <360 L2, <840 L3, <1800 L4, <3720 L5, <7560 L6, <15240 L7, <30600 L8, else L9. 0x7788 (30600) draws the pet exp bar at 100% (FUN_00442710).

fields.name: pet_summoned
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0A: 0 = the spawned pet entity is put in state 2 (entity+0x9C=2, not active); non-zero = state 4 (active) unless the local entity byte +0x158B is 0 and the map flag [map+0x7C]==1 (0x46AA5C..0x46AA77). Inferred name.

fields.name: pet_level
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0B: pet level 1..9. 0x6A OVERWRITES it client-side from pet_exp (FUN_00429680, only when pet_exp != 0); 0x6F uses the sent value as is. Drives the growth stage entity+0x9E (level<5 -> 1, <9 -> 2, 9 -> 3) and the pet window label "Level %d".

fields.name: pet_gauge_pct
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0C: shown as "%u%%" and as gauge 0x1C of the pet window (FUN_00442670). Probably satiety/stamina 0..100 (inferred).

fields.name: pet_name
fields.meaning: limit_type==3 only. Record +0x0D..+0x1B: pet name, strcpy (unbounded) into the pet entity +0x00 at 0x46A815. MUST contain a NUL inside the record (<= 14 chars).

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x08: count / remaining uses (also the stat-reset allowance, 2008 live C13).

fields.name: expire_year..expire_milliseconds
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x0A..+0x19: expiry date/time for period items (year 0 = no date).

fields.name: origin
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x1A, read as a byte (2009 shop UI FUN_00465890 line 1192): 0 = bought with cash (refund value shown), 3 = event reward.

fields.name: unk_1b
fields.meaning: limit_type!=3. Record +0x1B: no reader found. Send 0.

specs.semantics: Rebuild or extend the owned cash item set. mode 0/1: frees lists ctx+0x04 and ctx+0x38, then for the three bags (slot-count bytes ci+0x373/0x374/0x375, ci=[ctx+0x24]) calls purge helpers that first require the slot byte <= 45 (else return 1 with nothing more read) and remove every cash item (template +0x1F0 != 0); then purges the fixed 45-slot bag ci+0x800. Every mode: per record reads bool is_equipped + the 28-byte record. Equipped -> ctx+0x38 (limit_type 3 there sets the local player entity pointer +0x1628 to the record = active pet). Not equipped -> ctx+0x04; limit_type 2 with a date -> expiry notice "[%s] will expire in %d day(s)." / "The remain time..." only; limit_type 2 without a date -> quantity set to 1 and inserted; others -> FUN_00464e00 bag insert by template category (silent failure when full or quantity 0). mode 0/3 finalize: inventory UI rebuild, period-item window rebuild, and if an active pet record exists: creates (or reuses [local+0x1638]) a pet entity next to the local player (name from record+0x0D, level +0x9D and stage +0x9E from record+0x0B, state 4, or 2 when record+0x0A==0), registers it in the scene and bumps the uid counter game+0x3FC; then FUN_004423e0 refreshes the pet UI. Returns 1.
specs.trigger: Server sends the complete owned cash item set (after world entry, and before the 0x6A final page which snapshots list +0x04). Use mode 0 when it fits in 255 records.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 gate as 0x6A. Lists are freed before the bag gate in mode 0/1, so a failed gate still wipes them. Modes 0/1 delete all cash items from the bags, so the page set must carry the full inventory. 2008 LIVE C13 still applies to non-pet records: quantity at +0x08 is also the stat-reset allowance. pet_name must be NUL-terminated inside the record (unbounded strcpy into the entity). Only the LAST equipped pet record wins (pointer overwrite). A mode 2/3 page without a preceding 0/1 appends duplicates.
specs.references: 2008 spec 0x6F (handler 0x4618EC: i32 count, bool+28-byte records, no paging, no pet). 2009 helpers: FUN_00464e00 = 2008 FUN_0045e8e0 (bag insert), FUN_00465110 = 2008 FUN_0045ebb0 (expiry notice), FUN_0046ef40 = 2008 FUN_00465290, FUN_004428b0 = 2008 FUN_00441c20. Pet entity ctor FUN_00423d00 (0x16B8 bytes), register FUN_00422fc0.

fields.name: uid

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Reads u32 uid and looks the entity up in the current scene's entity list (FUN_004189F0 walks scene+0xC nodes, matching node->entity+0x84 against EDX=uid; uid 0 returns NULL immediately). If not found, the handler breaks to 0x44D7AD without reading anything else. Otherwise it reads 17 bytes straight over the entity's name buffer (entity+0x00), so the name changes in place. If uid equals the local player uid (scene+0x220), it copies the name (inline strcpy loop) to scene+0x206 and calls FUN_00442510, which rebuilds the character-info panel labels (Lv.%u, stats, stat buttons) when scene+0x970 (local player entity) is non-null. No chat line, popup or sound in the EN build.
specs.trigger: Server broadcast to clients that have the renamed character loaded (including the renamer) after a successful rename. The requester separately receives S2C 0x73 (u8 result; result==1 is followed by a u32 and shows 'Your character name has successively changed.'; otherwise 'The name is already being used.').
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Global OnReceive gate: every packet is dropped while [game_state+0x408] != 0 (0x44D5F5). Unknown uid or uid 0 -> silently ignored; the 17 name bytes are left unconsumed (harmless as the handler ends). new_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes: the local-player copy to scene+0x206 is an unbounded byte loop that would run past entity+0x11 into following entity fields and overflow the scene name buffer. Only entity+0x00 is written; a cached nameplate record (entity+0x11DC) is not touched here, so whether the overhead name re-renders immediately is unverified. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C45, premium_cash#05): the server must NEVER send the short (4-byte) form. A 0x74 whose 17 name bytes are missing is read out of bounds by the client - live it did no visible harm, but the read is unbounded. Always send all 21 bytes, and only for a uid the receiver has loaded. (Test-tooling note: encoding this packet needs "__assume__": {"entity_with_uid_exists": true}, otherwise the client-state condition defaults to false and only 4 bytes are produced.)
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: There is no real wire-format dispute. Analyst A gave 'u32 uid; if(entity exists){ str[17] new_name }' and Analyst B gave the same plus an explicit 'else { stop }'. Both describe identical byte behavior and both are correct; B's form is adopted only because it states the early-exit path explicitly. specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
The client first reads result (u8) and mentor_name[17]. For result 0x65 or 0x66 it prints a red (0xFFFD4C87) main-chat line built from "<%s>%s" with the name and the error text, returns 1 and reads nothing else. For any other result it does the following in order. It prints the green (0xFF00C800) line '<name>is registered as your mentor.' and allocates a zeroed 0x28-byte node. It copies the 17 name bytes to node+0x00 and reads the u32 mentor_uid into node+0x18. It sets node+0x14 = result. If result == 0x64 it overwrites node+0x14 with CMessenger+0x90 (own channel) and sets status node+0x20 = 0; otherwise it sets status = 4. It sets node+0x24 = 1, appends the node to the mentor list at CMessenger+0x14 (FUN_00459df0) and refreshes the messenger UI (FUN_00470270). There is no duplicate check.
specs.trigger: Server reply to C2S 0x5C {str[17] mentor_name}, sent by FUN_0046ff70 from the name-entry dialog. The client blocks registering yourself, and FUN_00472900 only lets a novice register ('Only a novice can register a mentor.'). Send 0x65 if the target has not class-upgraded, 0x66 if they don't exist or are offline, and 0x64 or the channel number on success.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub3 entry gate: CMessenger+0x68 and +0x70 must be non-zero. No chat-room gate. Reads use CMessenger+0x74 (g_sock_game), which FUN_0046f860 sets from the S2C 0x03 handler, so send this only after S2C 0x03. mentor_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes: the local is not pre-zeroed and is formatted into a 0x80-byte buffer with _sprintf_s, where an overrun triggers the CRT invalid-parameter handler. Success appends a new node every time with no duplicate check, so don't send success twice, or after S2C 0x03 already delivered a mentor. FUN_00470780 only inspects the list head. On a same-channel success, send 0x64 rather than the numeric channel: a numeric value equal to your own channel is still stored with status 4 ('other channel'). This differs from the 0x03 block, which compares against the own channel. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#17): the 22-byte success form (result 0x64 + str[17] name + u32 mentor_uid) is accepted live - the grammar is right; the wsproto encoder dropped mentor_uid because of a hex-literal comparison bug.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: The two analysts agree on every read and its order. The structural difference is only that B spells out the terminating branch. A gave 'u8 result; str[17] mentor_name; if(result != 0x65 && result != 0x66) { u32 mentor_uid }' and B gave the same with an explicit 'else { stop }'. The asm confirms both paths. At 0x4715CD, call [0x4A4094] reads the u8 into esp0+0x13. At 0x4715DC/0x4715E3, PUSH 0x11 then call [0x4A4098] reads 17 bytes into esp0+0x20. At 0x4715E9..0x4715FA, MOVZX result, SUB 0x65 JZ 0x471742, SUB 1 JZ 0x4716F2. Both error blocks (0x4716F2..0x47173F and 0x471742..0x47178F) contain only _sprintf_s, FUN_004817d0 and RET 0x10, with no GetDataFromPacket. The success fall-through does its single extra read at 0x471690 (call [0x4A40C8], u32 into node+0x18). So B's explicit form, with 'else { stop }', is the canonical grammar and A's is equivalent. One side point: A said the matching mentor sub-block lives in S2C 0x07 at 0x44E5BA and that the client needs 0x07 first. That is wrong. 0x44E5BA is inside the S2C 0x03 handler (asm marker for 0x03 precedes it; FUN_0046f860 is called there at 0x44E52F and sets +0x74/+0x90 and clears +0xCC), as B said. windslayer_server.py _build_pyslayer_opcode_03 emits that mentor gate u32 = 0, which confirms it. Node layout, colours and status values (0x64 -> own channel, status 0; other -> status 4) were verified at 0x4716A1..0x4716C7 and match FUN_00470780 (S2C 0x7D). There is no PySlayer builder for 0x7A, and it is not implemented in windslayer_server.py.

Whether a channel value of 0 or a value >= 0x67 is ever used in practice. The client accepts any non-0x65/0x66 value as success.

[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Reply to the secondary-password (SS#) dialog. Flow: a protected action (bank NPC -> 0x1A7, cash-shop buy -> 0x1F9, or 0x235) opens dialog 0x201 with the target id stored at dialog+0x134. The user types the password. The client sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id} and closes the dialog. On S2C 0x80: if result != 1, it shows the 'Invalid password. Please check your password again.' box. If result == 1 and target == 0x1F9 (505), it calls FUN_0045E0D0: the selected cash item (this+0x700+0x5BC) is re-checked against the cash balance (+0x588). It then opens purchase confirm window 0x1F9 (mode 4) and sets its fields, or shows 'You are short of cash.'. If result == 1 and target is anything else, ui_root+0x5A4 = 1 and window <target> is opened with mode 3; for 0x1A7 that is the bank window, drawn from the data sent in 0x65. Nothing is sent back directly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C7, login_character#07): target_window_id 0x235 is the CHARACTER-DELETE confirmation window. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.trigger: Send in reply to C2S 0x51 (the password dialog submit). Echo the client's target_window_id. Send result=1 when the password matches the account's secondary password/SS#, and anything else to reject.
specs.expected_response: none directly. With target 0x1F9 the user then confirms the purchase in window 0x1F9, which triggers the cash-shop buy request (not traced here). With 0x1A7 the bank opens using the existing 0x65 data. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C32, shop_storage#03): for target 0x1A7 the bank window renders from whatever S2C 0x65 last delivered, so the 0x65 must precede this packet; no post-open 0x65 is required.
specs.gates_and_hazards: There is no state gate in the handler. The password dialog itself only opens if [game_state+0x4cc]+0x218 != 0 (set by the 0x5A handler when the account's SS# field at +0x131 differs from the default at this+0xD0A); otherwise the client shows 'no SS# in this ID...'. Sending an arbitrary target id makes the client try to open that window (FUN_00446300) and sets ui_root+0x5A4=1. Sending 0x80 unsolicited with a real window id pops that window open. Target 0x1F9 with no cash item selected (+0x5BC == 0) does nothing.

That meaning is WRONG: the u32 is a UI window id, not a balance. The function is also never called. It should instead reply to C2S 0x51 (which is not in _dispatch) by echoing the target window id. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x80.py sends p8(1)+p32u(0x4CF) (same layout, a KR window id, comment 'About Cash??'). The KR Hex-Rays 0x80 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c:7975) likewise reads u8==1 then a u32 and switches on window-like ids (0, 15/24/34, 79, 80, 153, 176...), which confirms the window-id meaning, though the KR id set differs from EN.

fields.meaning: The player's new ABSOLUTE gold total after the transfer fee, not a delta. It is shown as a %I64u string in UI window 9 control 0xB. Only present when result==1.

specs.semantics:
2009: wire identical; gold -> scene+0x278 (2008 scene+0x270); failure dialog via the shared message path.
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Result of a paid village (town) teleport. If result==1, the client overwrites its u64 gold at scene+0x270 with the value from the packet, updates the gold text in UI window 9 control 0xB and plays sound 0x29. This handler does NOT change the map or the player's position, so the actual move has to come from the normal map-change packets. If result!=1, the client shows a 'Village transfer failed. Please try again in a few minutes.' message box and reads nothing more. Both paths then break to 0x44D7AD.
specs.trigger: Server reply to the village-transfer request, most likely C2S 0x5D (u8 village_index, u16 cost), which the dialog-0x237 confirm button sends at 0x44ADBA. The server can also send it at any time to set absolute gold and play the coin sound.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No preconditions: gold is written even when the player is not in the world. On failure, do NOT add the u64, because the client reads only 1 byte and any extra bytes would just be ignored. On success the u64 is required; a 1-byte packet with result==1 would make GetDataFromPacket read past the end of the buffer. Gold is an absolute value, so sending a delta would corrupt both the displayed gold and the client-side 'short of gold' check.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts found the same reads in the same order: a u8 result at 0x452908 (IAT 0x4A4094), CMP [esp+0x7A],1 / JNZ 0x45296F at 0x45290E, and, only when result==1, a u64 at 0x452931 (IAT 0x4A4118) written straight into [ESI+0x4CC]+0x270 (scene+0x270, gold). Their only difference was the grammar text. Analyst A wrote an explicit 'else { stop }'; analyst B left the else branch out. On the wire the two are identical, and both are right. The failure path at 0x45296F only pushes the message-box arguments, calls FUN_00489DA0 and jumps to the shared break at 0x44D7AD with no GetDataFromPacket call, and the success path also ends at 0x45296A with JMP 0x44D7AD. I use A's explicit form because it records that the failure packet is exactly 1 byte. Both analysts also agree on: the FUN_004659D0 %I64u formatting into window 9 control 0xB (the sprintf of "%I64u" is confirmed at 0x4659ED), Play_Sound(0x29,0) at 0x452964, and the length (9 bytes on success, 1 on failure). B's extra lead also checks out: at 0x44ADBA in FUN_00446300 the client Adds u8 0x5D, u8 [dlg+0x40] and u16 (MOVZX SI of [dlg+0x134]), then calls Send(1), after a u64 gold >= cost check at 0x44AD6A..0x44AD7A. That makes C2S 0x5D the likely request. Other references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x81 has the same wire shape (u8 result, u64 gold on 1, UI control 7, sound 0x23, 'village move failed' text). PySlayer has no opcode_0x81 file, and our server (windslayer_server.py) has no 0x81 or 0x5D handling.
open_questions: Is C2S 0x5D (u8 village_index, u16 cost) the request that gets 0x81 back? The send site at 0x44ADBA is certain, but the pairing is inferred from the dialog flow and the gold check, not seen in a capture.
Which packets did the original server send after 0x81 to actually warp the player? Probably the usual 0x08/0x03/0x07/0x0A/0x28/0x44/0x1A map-change sequence.

specs.name: ItemStallOpenResult
specs.grammar: u8 result

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = the stall opened. 9 = 'Invalid information transaction... This violation will be recored...' warning box. Any other value = 'Item stall opening failed. Closed the stall and try again later.' box.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [ESP+0xc]; checked against 1 at 0x46D0DB and 9 at 0x46D102

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Reply to the seller's C2S 0x5E (open item stall). Note that the client already sets ctx+0x20 (selling) = 1 and ctx+0x1c (setup) = 0 right after it sends 0x5E (0x46B63B). ctx here means the window-mode controller at game_state+0xD5C, which is EBX in the handler. result==1 calls FUN_00466f20 (ESI=ctx). That sets ctx+0x20=1 and ctx+0x1c=0, calls FUN_00489320(0x259,0x19,3) to change the state of stall-window control 0x19 (the Open/Start button), disables child controls #25 and #26 (child+0x18=0), then calls FUN_00489320(0x259,0x1c,3) and (0x259,0x1d,3). This switches window 0x259 into selling mode. result==9 shows message box 0x6F6058 through FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0) and sets ctx+0x1c=1. Any other result shows message box 0x6F6470 and sets ctx+0x1c=1. On both failure paths ctx+0x20 (selling) stays 1, so the next Close click sends C2S 0x60 and needs S2C 0x84 to close the window. Reads exactly 1 byte and returns 1 (handled).
specs.trigger: Send it to the seller as the reply to C2S 0x5E (u8 item_count, str[25] shop_name, per item: u16,u16,u32,u8 n,u16*n,u16), which the client sends from 0x46B546..0x46B635 when the stall window's Start button (control 0x19) is clicked. On success the server should also send S2C 0x85 to the other players on the map.
specs.expected_response: None. The client sends nothing back.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub-handler entry gate: ctx+8 != 0 and ctx+0xc (UI root) != 0, or the function returns 0 and the packet goes on down the sub-handler chain. On failure (result != 1) ctx+0x20 stays 1, so the Close button does not close locally and sends C2S 0x60 instead. The server MUST answer that 0x60 with 0x84 result=1, or the player is stuck in the stall window (FUN_00465fe0 refuses to switch modes while ctx+0x20 != 0 and the mode is 0x259). Result 9 is the 'cheat' wording. Use it only for real tampering. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18/#19): CLIENT-SIDE ITEM DUPLICATION HAZARD. S2C 0x83 result == 1 (and S2C 0x82 with result != 1) sets ctx+0x1C = 1 WHATEVER the current window mode, so outside a real stall this latches the stall SETUP flag. FUN_004665e0's 0x259 branch then returns the listed items into the bag whenever ANY later 0x87 buyer window is closed, without checking whose list it is (observed Blue Mushroom 5 -> 15). S2C 0x84 with no window open does NOT clear the flag. SERVER RULE: send 0x83 only in reply to C2S 0x5F and 0x82 only in reply to C2S 0x5E. The old "inert outside mode 0x259" claim (design 6.1) is WRONG. RECOVERY for a client that has already duplicated: relog (the server must resync the inventory).

fields.meaning: 1 = selling stopped and the stall goes back to setup/adjust mode. Any other value is silently ignored.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Reply to the seller's C2S 0x5F (stop selling / adjust stall; opcode only). The client sends 0x5F from the stall window's control 0x1b only while ctx+0x20 (selling) != 0, and sets ctx+0x1c=0 when it sends. result==1 calls FUN_00467030 (EDI=ctx). That sets ctx+0x20=0 (not selling) and ctx+0x1c=1 (setup mode), disables child controls #24 and #25 of window 0x259, and calls FUN_00489320(0x259,0x1b/0x1c/0x1d,3). The stall window stays open with its item list so the seller can change items or prices and press Start again (C2S 0x5E). Any other result: the handler returns 1 and does nothing. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18): result == 1 sets ctx+0x20 = 0 and ctx+0x1C = 1 IN ANY MODE - the packet is not inert outside the stall window. The live probe showed ctx+0x1C latched to 1 while ctx+0 = 0 and ctx+0x20 = 0.

If result != 1, nothing tells the player, and the client keeps ctx+0x20=1 with ctx+0x1c=0 (the C2S send already cleared it), so the window is left in selling mode with setup disabled. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18/#19): CLIENT-SIDE ITEM DUPLICATION HAZARD. S2C 0x83 result == 1 (and S2C 0x82 with result != 1) sets ctx+0x1C = 1 WHATEVER the current window mode, so outside a real stall this latches the stall SETUP flag. FUN_004665e0's 0x259 branch then returns the listed items into the bag whenever ANY later 0x87 buyer window is closed, without checking whose list it is (observed Blue Mushroom 5 -> 15). S2C 0x84 with no window open does NOT clear the flag. SERVER RULE: send 0x83 only in reply to C2S 0x5F and 0x82 only in reply to C2S 0x5E. The old "inert outside mode 0x259" claim (design 6.1) is WRONG. RECOVERY for a client that has already duplicated: relog (the server must resync the inventory).

specs.name: ItemStallCloseResult
specs.grammar: u8 result

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = stall closed, so close stall window 0x259. Any other value is silently ignored.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Reply to the seller's C2S 0x60 (close stall; opcode only). The client sends 0x60 from window 0x259 control 2 or 0x1a (Close) only while ctx+0x20 (selling) != 0. When not selling it closes the window locally with FUN_00483430(0x259,1,1) and sends nothing. On send it sets ctx+0x1c=0. result==1 calls FUN_00483430(0x259,1,1) on the UI root (ctx+0xc), which sets ui+0x5a4=1 and calls FUN_00446300(0x259,0,1,0,1) to close window 0x259. FUN_00446300 is a caller of FUN_004665e0, whose 0x259 branch puts the displayed items back through FUN_00467200 and clears ctx+0x1c and ctx+0x20 to 0. Any other result: nothing happens.
specs.trigger: Send it to the seller as the reply to C2S 0x60 (0x46B6C9, sent at 0x469BA8). The server should also broadcast S2C 0x86 (owner uid) to the other players on the map.
specs.expected_response: None.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same sub1 entry gate. If the server never answers 0x60 with result=1, the client cannot leave the stall window, because the selling flag blocks both the local close and mode switches (FUN_00465fe0). This also applies after a failed 0x82 open. The server should always accept 0x60 and reply 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18): a 0x84 sent while no stall window is open does NOT clear a latched ctx+0x1C setup flag (it only closes window 0x259 when one exists), so it cannot be used to undo a stray 0x83/0x82.

fields.name: sign_sprite_id
fields.meaning: Sprite index of the stall signboard. It is the first argument of CSpriteControl::DrawSprite (DAT_0070e70c) at 0x431760. Read only when the entity exists and its stall flag was 0 (stop path otherwise).

fields.name: stall_title
fields.meaning: Stall title drawn above the sign by CIME::Draw_Text. Exactly 25 raw bytes are copied with no forced terminator. Put a NUL inside the 25 bytes (at most 24 chars), because entity+0x150E (the sprite id) follows directly. Read only on the same path as sign_sprite_id.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Opens the stall sign on another player. The client reads u32 owner_uid and resolves it with FUN_004189f0. If no entity is found (or the uid is 0), or the entity's stall flag byte +0x14F4 is already nonzero, the handler jumps to 0x46EF5A and returns 1 (handled) with nothing else read or changed. Otherwise it first sets entity+0x14F4 = 1 (0x46CFDD), then reads u16 into entity+0x150E and 25 raw bytes into entity+0x14F5, and returns 1. The per-frame routine FUN_004316b0 draws the signboard sprite and title for entities with alive state 3 (remote players) and the flag set, while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6. FUN_0044c4b0 makes the sign clickable: if no other stall or trade window is busy, clicking sends C2S 0x61 with u32 owner_uid to request the stall contents. FUN_00466e30 also checks the flag when placing a new stall, so a stall can't be opened too close to another open one. Trailing extra bytes are harmless because the offset is sub1's by-value argument copy.
specs.trigger: Broadcast to players in view on the seller's map when a stall opens successfully (after C2S 0x5E and S2C 0x82 result=1). Players who arrive later learn about open stalls from the stall sub-block of the S2C 0x04/0x07 player data, or from a 0x85 sent after that player's spawn.
specs.expected_response: None. Clicking the sign later makes the client send C2S 0x61 (u32 owner_uid).
specs.gates_and_hazards: sub1 entry gate: [ctx+0x08] and [ctx+0x0C] must both be non-null (ctx = main handler this+0xD5C). Otherwise sub1 returns 0 and the opcode falls through the rest of the chain unhandled. The owner entity must already be spawned (0x04/0x07). If the flag is already 1, the new sprite and title are silently ignored and only the uid is consumed, so to change them send 0x86 (clears the flag) and then 0x85 again. The flag is set before the u16/str reads, so a truncated packet would still leave the flag set with stale sprite/title data (how the Fireway read bounds-check behaves on a short packet was not verified). An unterminated 25-byte title makes Draw_Text run into the sprite-id bytes. The sign is never drawn for the local player (alive==4). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C48, shop_storage#09/#11, trade#16): with shop_open = 1 the client draws the stall TITLE but NO signboard sprite for sign ids 0, 1 or 0x168 on the S2C 0x04 vendor path (id 1 produced only a brief flash), so 0x168 is NOT a valid sign-sprite id. CONFLICT: on the S2C 0x05 ghost path sign sprite id 1 DID render a real sign plus an owner glow (trade#16), so the valid id set - and what distinguishes the two paths - is still unknown. Also live: an all-zero appearance block yields an INVISIBLE body (nameplate only).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts derived the same wire layout: u32 owner_uid, then on the found-and-flag-clear path u16 sign sprite and a 25-byte title, with nothing further read on the other path. A wrote the condition inverted with a bare stop, B wrote if/else with stop. The two grammars mean the same thing, so the grammar dispute is only notation, and I re-verified it from the asm. 0x46CFAA calls IAT 0x4A40C8 (u32) into [ESP+0x18]. 0x46CFB8 calls FUN_004189f0, which only walks the entity list and returns NULL for uid 0, so it reads no packet bytes. 0x46CFC3 JZ and 0x46CFD2 JNZ (flag at +0x14F4) both go to 0x46EF5A, which is MOV EAX,1 and return. 0x46CFDD sets the flag. 0x46CFEE calls IAT 0x4A4090 (u16) into +0x150E. 0x46D004 PUSH 0x19 then 0x46D00A calls IAT 0x4A4098 into +0x14F5. The two analysts differed on one cross-reference. A said the same stall block is in the S2C 0x1A spawn at 0x44F6A1. That is wrong. 0x44F6A1 is inside the handler whose marker says S2C 0x04|0x07 (asm line 1813 of OnReceive_MainTcpHandler; it loops per player and has CMP opcode,7 at 0x44F6FE). No other code in the main handler reads +0x14F4, and 0x1A is the monster/NPC spawn. B was right that it belongs to the 0x04/0x07 player block. The 0x04/0x07 block matches windslayer_server.py _build_en_opcode_07 (lines ~2293/2395), which always writes bool 0 there. A's renderer details (FUN_004316b0: scene+0xF00 in {4,5,6}, alive==3, DrawSprite(+0x150E), Draw_Text(+0x14F5, x+5, y-0x8C)) and the C2S 0x61 u32 uid send at 0x44CA2F were confirmed in the asm. PySlayer has no 0x85 builder, and our server doesn't implement it.
open_questions: Which sign_sprite_id values are valid (indices into sprite control DAT_0070e70c) is unknown. C2S 0x5E carries no sprite choice, so the server has to pick one.
Whether the original server also sent 0x85 to the seller for their own entity is unknown. It would only set the flag on the local entity, and alive==4 entities are never drawn.
The S2C 0x87 reply to the C2S 0x61 view-stall request was not re-verified here (it was only claimed by analyst A).
How a truncated 0x85 behaves (Fireway GetDataFromPacket bounds-check) was not verified. The flag is already set before the u16 read.

UNRESOLVED (shop_storage#11 vs trade#16): sign_sprite_id 0, 1 and 0x168 drew no signboard on the S2C 0x04 vendor path, yet id 1 drew a sign plus an owner glow on a 0x05 ghost. Find the valid sprite id set and what distinguishes the two paths before relying on any id.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Broadcast that a character's item stall closed. The client looks up the entity by uid. If it is missing or entity+0x14F4 == 0, nothing happens. Otherwise it clears entity+0x14F4 = 0 and entity+0x150E (sign sprite) = 0, which removes the signboard and title and makes the entity no longer clickable as a stall. The title bytes at +0x14F5 are left in place. If entity+0x84 equals ctx+4, the uid of the stall this client is browsing (written by S2C 0x87 at 0x46D2xx), the client also closes stall window 0x259 with FUN_00483430(0x259,1,1) and shows the message box 'The shop is closed or adjusting.' (0x6F6534) through FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0).
specs.trigger: Send it to the other players on the map (at least anyone browsing that stall) when the seller stops selling (C2S 0x5F / S2C 0x83) or closes the stall (C2S 0x60 / S2C 0x84), and when the seller leaves or disconnects while a stall is open.
specs.expected_response: None.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Must come before any new 0x85 for the same uid, because 0x85 is ignored while the flag is set. ctx+4 does not seem to be cleared when the buyer closes the stall window: no write of 0 was found in FUN_00469090, FUN_00466xxx or FUN_00467xxx. So a later 0x86 for a stall the player browsed earlier may still close window 0x259 and pop the 'shop is closed' message. Same sub1 entry gate.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Reply to viewing another player's item stall. Gate: if the local player's own stall is open/pending (stall ctx+0x20 or ctx+0x1c set and ctx+0==0x259) the client reads NOTHING and shows 'Open stall is opened. Close the Open stall and try again.'. On result==1 and item_count>0 the client opens the stall window 0x259 in buyer mode (FUN_00466390(0), sets ctx+0=0x259), stores owner_uid at ctx+4, writes the 25-byte stall name into control 0x1f, then for each item builds a 0x38-byte entry {item_id, 12-byte option blob, qty, price} and appends it to the window list. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C31, shop_storage#13): result == 6 shows "Open stall is opened. Close the Open stall and try again." (the same box as the local own-stall gate), and result != 1 - as well as result == 1 with item_count == 0 - shows "The shop is closed or adjusting." LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#17, shop_storage#12): the EN caption of window 0x259 is "Pedding" [sic] and its controls are Name / Goods (rows drawn as "icon, qty, <price> Gold each") / Purchase / Close.
specs.trigger: Server sends in response to C2S 0x61 (u32 target_uid), which the client sends when the player clicks another player whose entity+0x14f4 stall flag was set by S2C 0x85.
specs.expected_response: none automatically; the user may then buy via C2S 0x62 (u32 owner_uid, u16 item_id, u16 qty, u8 n, n*u16 opt, u16 item_ext), answered by S2C 0x88 (buyer) and 0x89 (seller)
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 entry requires ctx+8 and ctx+0xC non-null. Own-stall gate reads nothing. opt_count is unbounded: values >=11 overwrite the already-read price local, and >=69 reach the stack cookie at S+0xBC (process abort); send opt_count<=5. stall_name gets no forced NUL if all 25 bytes are non-zero (bytes after it on the stack are not zeroed). The list is not explicitly cleared in this block (FUN_00466390 path is assumed to reset the window). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18): if a stray S2C 0x83/0x82 has latched ctx+0x1C, closing THIS buyer window copies its listed items into the local bag (client-side duplication). Only send 0x87 in reply to C2S 0x61, and never leave ctx+0x1C latched.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder (server_packets has no 0x87). Not implemented in windslayer_server.py. The per-item layout exactly mirrors the client's own C2S 0x5E stall-open builder at 0x0046B546..0x0046B618 (u16 id, u16 qty, ulong price, u8 n, n*u16, u16 entry+0x0C), which independently confirms field order.
open_questions: Exact meaning of item_ext (slot 5 of the 12-byte option blob) and of opt slots 0..4.

[RESOLVED by live verification shop_storage#13, 2026-09-17] Live: result 6 has its own text ("Open stall is opened...") and every other non-1 result - plus result 1 with count 0 - shows "The shop is closed or adjusting.", so only 1 and 6 are distinguishable by the client. Original question: "Whether any result codes other than 1 and 6 have distinct server meaning (client treats all others identically)."

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Tells the stall owner that someone bought from their stall. Always sets gold and refreshes the inventory gold text; then finds the entry in the stall window 0x259 list with the same item_id and entry qty >= qty (for equipment also an exact 12-byte option-blob match), subtracts qty (frees the entry at 0) and prints the system chat line 'Sold %u (%s).' (qty, item name). If no entry matches, only gold changes. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C9, shop_storage#17): the handler matches whatever entries window 0x259's list STILL holds, ignoring ctx+0 and ctx+0x20 - including a STALE BUYER LIST from a 0x87 window that was already closed by 0x84 or by the Close button (the list is only freed by the next 0x87 / FUN_00466390(0)). Live: a client with no stall of its own got gold 100200 plus the floating notice "Sold 2 (Blue Mushroom)." SERVER RULE: send 0x89 only to the actual selling owner. The "no own stall -> only gold changes" expectation holds only while no 0x87 has been received since login. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.
specs.trigger: Server sends to the stall owner when another player's C2S 0x62 purchase succeeds (paired with 0x88 to the buyer).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No own-stall gate. Item id must resolve in the item table, otherwise nothing but gold is updated. This block does not remove the item from the seller's inventory. opt_count must be <=5 (stack overflow hazard as in 0x87). Live (C9): no own-stall gate exists at all - the entry match runs against whatever window 0x259 last held, so a mis-addressed 0x89 both moves gold and edits a browsed stall list on someone else's client.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Not in windslayer_server.py. The string 'Sold %u (%s).' at 0x006F7FC8 is referenced from FUN_004674f0.
open_questions: Whether stall items were removed from the seller's inventory when the stall opened (0x83 path) or need a separate inventory packet after a sale.

specs.semantics: Replaces the local Card Deck list: u8 count straight into charinfo+0xE48, then count u16 ids into charinfo+0xE4A.. (no bounds check), then FUN_0045f790 rebuilds the Card Deck window. Sent by the server after every C2S 0x63 (itself sent at the end of every S2C 0x03). Same bytes as 2008.
specs.trigger: Server-pushed; no C2S request in the EN client asks for it. Send after a successful login (S2C 0x02 success), and before or at world entry, so the deck window and the duplicate check have data. The 0x8B result-2 text "Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again." suggests the original server sent this list at login.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Ignored (no bytes consumed) until the handler object is initialized by a successful S2C 0x02 login response: SubHandler5 checks [0x70F7C4]!=0 and [0x70F7C8]!=0. CAPACITY HAZARD: ids are written in place with no bounds check. charinfo+0xE98 holds an i32 field (compared with 100/30 at 0x469189, updated by SubHandler3), so at most 51 entries fit (0xE32..0xE97). Keep deck_count <= 50/51. At about 133 or more entries the writes reach the item-table pointer at scene+0xF84 (charinfo+0xF3C), which other code dereferences. An id of 0 ends the UI list early (the count label still shows deck_count). Ids should be real item ids (category 2 card items); unknown ids just produce empty list entries.
specs.references: PySlayer: no opcode_0x8A.py exists (server_packets/__init__.py only has a try/except import stub); the KR Hex-Rays doc has no card-deck strings. Our server (windslayer_server.py): no builder and never sends 0x8A. The opcode atlas lists 0x8A only as a SubHandler5 route. The format comes from asm alone and matches the decomp.

specs.semantics: Reply to C2S 0x64 (card register). FUN_00497c70(0x16,1,1) closes the waiting box, then result is read. result 1: new_deck_count and card_item_id; if the item def exists and FUN_00470f00 removes one card from the bag, the deck count and id are stored, the Card Deck window is rebuilt and "Registered %s in the Card Deck." is printed. Any other result shows a type-3 message box. Same bytes as 2008.
specs.trigger: Send in reply to C2S 0x64 [u16 card_item_id]. The client sends 0x64 when the player confirms dialog 0x292 (button 2) after choosing to register a card item. The item must be category 2 with the card flag [rec+0x14C] set, and not already in the 0x8A deck list. After sending, the client shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' and waits for this packet. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x64 (card register). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.expected_response: none (the client consumes the card item locally on success)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Ignored (no bytes read) before the handler object is initialized by a successful S2C 0x02 login response. The waiting box is dismissed for every result. On success the client removes one card from its own inventory, so the server must NOT also send an inventory-removal packet (the card would be removed twice), but it must update its own inventory and deck records. If the client has no such item, nothing is registered client-side and no message appears, so client and server go out of sync. new_deck_count must be >= 1: with 0 the u16 id is written over charinfo+0xE30/0xE31, corrupting the count. Keep new_deck_count <= 50/51 (no bounds check; an i32 field sits at charinfo+0xE98). If new_deck_count is not old_count+1, the client's list gains gaps (a 0 id ends the UI list early) or overwrites existing entries. Category-1 items fail when inv+0x361 > 45. The chat string buffer is 64 bytes (sprintf_s).
specs.references: PySlayer: no opcode_0x8B.py and no parse for C2S 0x64 (only a try/except import stub in server_packets/__init__.py). Our server: _dispatch has no C2S 0x64 branch and there is no 0x8B builder. The UI strings (strings.tsv 0x6F5190, 0x6F517C, 0x6F5FAC, 0x6F7F50, 0x6F5FF0) confirm this is the card-deck/dictionary system. No live capture exists.
