Reads u8 result, u16 equip_item_id, u16 stone_item_id; looks up equip_item_id (FUN_00404210) and returns silently if missing (no further reads, [ctx+0x2C] not cleared). If result != 1 -> failure path with no further reads. If result == 1: reads 6 u16 option words then u16 new_option_item_id; if new_option_item_id is not a valid item -> failure path. Otherwise FUN_004241d0 scans equipment-tab slots (count u8 inv+0x361, ids u16 inv+0x380, 12-byte option blocks inv+0x3DA) for id == equip_item_id AND option block == the 12 received bytes, and stores new_option_item_id in the first zero word among option[0..4] (no change if no slot matches or all five are non-zero; success is still shown). Then FUN_00423e70 removes 1 x stone_item_id from the etc tab. Text 'Reinforcement Successful.' ("%s%s" with ' Successful.') into window 0x29B (FUN_0048A060); FUN_00465290 inventory refresh; clears list entries 4 and 5 of window 0x29B (entry+0x18=0); FUN_00483430(0x29B,4,1); window object +0x134 = equip_item_id, +0x40 = new_option_item_id; FUN_004838C0 control 4 = equip record, control 6 = new option record; [ctx+0x2C]=0. Failure path (0x46EEBB): 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.' (result 0x11) or 'ReinforcementFailed.' (no space) into window 0x29B; FUN_00489320(0x29B,5,3) and (0x29B,6,3); FUN_00483430(0x29B,4,1); FUN_00483270(0x29B, equip_item_id); FUN_004838C0 control 4 = equip record; [ctx+0x2C]=0; no inventory change.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x68 (u16 equip_item_id, u16 stone_item_id, 6x u16 option words), sent by FUN_004684d0 at 0x46869D when the 5000 ms progress window 0x293 completes with both the equipment ([ctx+0x66]) and elemental stone ([ctx+0x64]) slots filled. Send exactly once per 0x68.

specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 requires [ctx+0x8] and [ctx+0xC] non-null. Unknown equip_item_id -> stops after 5 bytes and never clears [ctx+0x2C], leaving crafting/reinforcement UI locked. With result == 1 the packet must carry all 19 bytes; the upper halves of the [ESP+0x10]/[ESP+0x14] dword slots are uninitialized, and a short packet leaves new_option_item_id garbage. The 6 option words must byte-match the client's stored 12-byte block or the option is silently not applied while the stone is still removed (desync). Client consumes exactly 1 stone locally on success only; server must not send an extra stone-removal packet. Trailing option bytes on a result != 1 packet are simply unread.

The asm order shows the item-table gate comes first (lookup at 0x46EC81, JZ 0x46EF5A exit) and only then CMP [ESP+0xC],1 / JNZ 0x46EEBB (0x46EC92/0x46EC97), with the 6-word loop at 0x46ECC0-0x46ECDB and final u16 at 0x46ECEE; the failure block 0x46EEBB..0x46EF5A contains no reads. B's two-step structure mirrors this code order, so it is adopted as canonical (A's combined condition is logically equivalent). Minor text corrections from the binary: format 0x4A630C = "%s%s", ' Successful.' at 0x6F5958 has a leading space and 'Failed.' at 0x6F5950 does not, so success text is 'Reinforcement Successful.' (B's semantics wrote 'ReinforcementSuccessful.') and failure text is 'ReinforcementFailed.' (B's field text wrote 'Reinforcement Failed.'); A had both right. C2S 0x68 layout confirmed at 0x46869D-0x4686E8 (u8 0x68, u16 [EDI+0x66], u16 [EDI+0x64], 6x u16). FUN_004241d0 decomp confirms insertion only into option[0..4]. Not in PySlayer (try-import stub only) nor our server (no 0x8E/0x68 in windslayer_server.py).

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Result of a Mining or Herb Gathering action. The client reads result (u8) and tool_item_id (u16), then looks up the tool's item def with FUN_00404210. If there is no def (id 0 or out of range included), it only clears the gather busy flag [ctx+0x28] and returns: no message, no inventory refresh, no more reads. Otherwise it always removes 1 of tool_item_id from the local inventory (FUN_00467140, tab chosen by def+0x154) before it looks at result. If result == 1: it reads reward_item_id, adds 1 of it via FUN_00440920 (chat message "you've received %s. (Count:%u)", or "You've learned skill(%s)." for skill-book items), refreshes the inventory/quest UI (FUN_00465290), clears [ctx+0x28] and returns. If result == 0x11: message "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory.". Any other result: message "Failed to obtian item.". Both failure paths then refresh the inventory UI and clear [ctx+0x28].
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x69. FUN_004684D0 sends 0x69 once the 5000 ms progress bar of window 0x295 finishes. The window is opened by FUN_00467B00 when the player uses a garden shovel (0x8A7..0x8AA) on a herb node or a shovel (0x8AB..0x8AE) on a mineral node. 0x69 carries u32 node key (roster index, stored in window+0x11C at 0x467D4B) and u16 tool item id (stored in window+0x134 at 0x467D3F).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 gate: [ctx+0x8] != 0 and [ctx+0xC] != 0, otherwise the packet goes unhandled. While [ctx+0x28] != 0, FUN_00467B00 returns at once (0x467B1E), so no new gather can start until 0x8F clears it. A UI event for window 0x295 in FUN_00446300 also clears it ([game_state+0xD84] = 0 at 0x446A2A). The client removes the tool on failure too (any result, as long as the def exists), so the server must also remove it on failure, or resend the tool, or the inventories drift apart. Send reward_item_id only when result == 1. On any other path the packet is 3 bytes, and extra bytes are ignored anyway. A tool_item_id with no item def skips the removal, the messages and the UI refresh; only the flag is cleared.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A's grammar was 'u8 result; u16 tool_item_id; if(item_def != null && result == 1) { u16 reward_item_id }'. B's was the same reads nested as if(def exists) { if(result == 1) { u16 } else stop } else stop. Both describe the same bytes in the same order, and the asm agrees with both. Reads: 0x46E91D u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) into [base+0x1C]; 0x46E931 u16 (0x4A4090) into [base+0x18]; 0x46E945 FUN_00404210 then JZ 0x46E9F9, which only clears [EBX+0x28] and returns; 0x46E963 FUN_00467140 removes the item unconditionally (stdcall RET 0xC, so the later [ESP+0x1C] still points at result); 0x46E96C CMP AL,1 / JNZ 0x46E9C3; 0x46E981 is the only other read, u16 (0x4A4090) into [base+0x0C]. None of the callees (FUN_00404210, FUN_00467140, FUN_00440920, FUN_00465290) receive the packet pointer or offset, so there are no hidden reads. B's nested form is kept because it follows the branch order in the code. On meaning, A was right that the u16 is the tool: FUN_00467B00 takes the used item id in [EBP+0x10], accepts only 0x8A7..0x8AA (garden shovel, Herb Gathering: entity+0x644 == 2, skill 0x56, map check 0x138) or 0x8AB..0x8AE (shovel, Mining: entity+0x644 == 1, skill 0x52, map check 0x139), stores it in window 0x295 +0x134 (FUN_00483270 at 0x467D3F), and FUN_004684D0 sends that same value as the u16 of C2S 0x69 (0x468584 / 0x4685A7). That settles B's tool-or-material question, and it covers both gathering types, so the name GatherResult is used rather than ItemMiningResult. The 5 s timer is confirmed: float 0x4A67AC = 5000.0. Other strings: 0x6F7FEC, 0x6F7538; 'Mining' 0x6F5F24, 'Item ' 0x6F5F3C, 'Herb Gathering' 0x6F5F2C. FUN_00440920 is the same add-item helper used by other reward packets (for example the S2C 0x18 quest reward). Neither PySlayer nor our server has this opcode.
open_questions: Result codes other than 1 and 0x11 all show the same generic failure message. The client does not show which codes the original server actually used.
The client does not check that tool_item_id in 0x8F matches the id sent in C2S 0x69. It removes whatever id the server sends, so the server should echo the tool id it received.

Not confirmed whether the programmatic close of window 0x295 in FUN_004684D0 (FUN_00483430 at 0x4685CB) reaches the FUN_00446300 path that clears [game_state+0xD84]. If it does not, a missing 0x8F leaves gathering blocked until the player closes the window by hand or the flag is otherwise reset.

Zeroes an 88-byte buffer, reads a u8 length and then exactly that many raw bytes, and appends the text to the chat log (UI window 0x0B) in orange (0xFFFF8000) through FUN_00445f00. That function measures the string with strlen, splits it into 88-byte lines, and wakes up the chat box if it has been idle more than 3000 ms. The only 0xFFFF8000 literal in the client is this handler, so the color does not reveal which chat channel it belongs to.

specs.semantics:
[carried from 2008; struct offsets in this text are 2008 values - see notes.struct_offset_map]
Applies a skill's HP effect to the whole party on the client. Steps: 1) record = skill_table[skill_id-1] (vector begin +8, end +0xC). If it is out of range or null (including skill_id 0), stop. 2) For each of the 5 u32 party uid slots at scene+0x25C, +0x260, +0x264, +0x268, +0x26C that is non-zero and matches an entity in the scene list (FUN_004189f0): spawn effect event 0x10E on that uid (FUN_0042b580(0x10E, uid, 0,0,0,1,0xA,0)), play sound 0x10E (non-positional), entity+0x9C (cur HP, i32) += record+0x158, clamp to entity+0x110C (max HP) and to >= 0. FUN_004258d0 returns 0 (skips the self-heal) for these skill_id ranges: 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x24D-0x257, 0x8C6-0x8D0, 0x8F2-0x8FC, 0x997-0x9A1, 0x9C3-0x9F9 (five consecutive 11-id blocks), 0xA5D-0xA67, 0xAF9-0xB03, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB25-0xB2F.

specs.expected_response: None
specs.gates_and_hazards: The client changes HP locally from its own skill table, so the server must apply the same delta (record+0x158) to its HP state or the HP bars will drift. Use explicit HP packets such as 0x54/0x28 to resync if needed. If the party slot list contains the local player's own uid (RegisterLocalPlayer compares the slots against the local uid, so self can be in the list), the local player may be healed twice: once in the loop, and again in step 3 for skills not excluded by FUN_004258d0. Unknown or zero skill_id does nothing. Out of party (all slots 0) only step 3 applies. Every call allocates an effect event (FUN_0042b580) per target and plays sound 0x10E. Avoid sending in bursts (the earlier lag was traced to per-hit effect events from 0x40).

The skill table identification rests on the quick-slot code (FUN_0043d8b0 -> FUN_00404210 on the same table -> FUN_0044c090 sending C2S 0x15 with record +0x154 type, +0x158 HP, +0x15C MP cost) and on the matching FUN_004258d0 gate in the 0x41/0x42 handler (0x453EEE).

Whether record+0x158 is really 'HP delta' for every skill type. It is signed: negative values are HP costs (see the 'Not enough HP.' check in FUN_0044c090).

Removes an expired premium (cash) item. The client walks the pointer vector at ctx+0x04 (begin ctx+0x08, end ctx+0x0C) from index 0. For each element whose u32 at +0x00 equals item_serial it: erases the element from the vector; looks up the item definition by the u16 item_id at element+0x04 (item table [ctx+0x1C], index id-1); if found, prints "[<item name>] is expired." to the chat log in color 0xFFFDF34C; frees the 28-byte record; and calls FUN_00441c20(1) on game_state to rebuild the inventory display. The chat line needs the chat window ([UI+0x59C] != 0); an unknown item_id still removes and frees the record, just with no message. specs.semantics:
2009: identical read sequence and conditions. entity+0x971 = (opcode != 0x9E) (2008 +0x8E4), entity+0x963 = 1 (2008 +0x8D7); command node 0x58 bytes with the same field layout; queue flush uses entity+0x13F4 (2008 +0x1354); local-target delay math uses entity+0xE3C and scene+0xF14 (2008 +0xDAC / scene+0xEFC).
[2008 description follows; struct offsets in it are 2008 values]
Uses the same handler block as 0x2A.

It sets:
- entity+0x8E4 = 0 (the SETNZ on opcode != 0x9E)
- entity+0x8D7 = 1

It builds a queue node from the bits with node+0x08 (target) = 0 and node+0x52 = 0. The node's delay is set to node[0] = 0x1E (30 ms, about one tick), and the node is appended to the entity move queue (+0x1350). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#29 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): 0x9E is NOT an immediate stop. The 30 ms is the node's OWN hold, counted only after every node already queued ahead of it has finished, so the real latency is the remaining hold of the queue (measured 750 ms behind one pending walk node); the queue drains at about 2x speed while >= 2 nodes are queued. entity+0x8E4 = 0 is written AT RECEIPT, not on dequeue. For 'stop now' use 0x2A (it flushes the queue and carries a position) or relay the stop as the next 0x1B. The queue is NOT flushed, entity+0xE48 is not reset, and no position is read. FUN_00412100 applies the node on the next ticks, which sets 94C/D80/958/8FF/8D0 etc. on the entity.

FUN_00407640 frees the current map object lists ([game+0x4FC])

specs.grammar: u16 stage_code

fields.name: stage_code
fields.meaning: Instance dungeon stage: map file ./hs/indun{code/100:02}_{code%100:02}.hmi, e.g. 105 -> indun01_05.hmi. Files named in the 2009 client: indun01_00..05, indun02_01..05, indun03_01/02/03/05.

specs.semantics: Completely new meaning in 2009 (the 2008 "Moving into Instance Dungeon"/"Failed to create" dialogs and strings no longer exist). Fades the screen out, builds ./hs/indunXX_YY.hmi from stage_code, frees the current map objects and loads that map in place (no S2C 0x08/0x03 map-change sequence), removes entities whose state byte +0x9C == 4 and that have no owner (+0x163C == 0; probably map monsters/NPCs - owned pets survive), spawns the new map's static NPCs when the map flags it, and clears the wait flag game+0x16F8. On a load failure the path is only logged and the map stays empty.
specs.trigger: Server moves the party to another stage of an instance dungeon (and presumably the first stage on entry). The creation request/flow was not traced.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate: sending it outside an instance reloads the current map object as an indun map. A stage_code whose file does not exist leaves an empty map (only logged). Monsters must be re-spawned by the server after the load (they are removed). Does not move the player; position must come from other packets.
specs.references: 2008 spec 0xA5 was InstanceDungeonCreateResult (u8 result, u32 unused) - that handler and its strings are gone. Strings: "indun" 0x4CAC90, "./hs/" 0x5268C8, "%s%s%02u_%02u.hmi" 0x52E08C, "Could not load MAP. (%s)" 0x52E0A0. Related map-object sprites: hs/indun_button, indun_gate01..04, indun_stone, hs/indun/indun_title01..03, indun_warning.
open_questions: How the client first enters an instance (whether 0xA5 alone or a normal map change to the stage-00 map is used).
Whether player position / camera need a follow-up packet after the in-place reload.
specs.verification: 2009 asm of FUN_00451960 block 0x45D72F..0x45D7FD read end to end; strings read from the exe; FUN_0043d810/FUN_00424420/FUN_00423970/FUN_00407640 decomp checked; 2008 handler 0x4581F3 and its spec compared (no common code).

u16 item_id
u8 item_option
u64 price_gold

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item offered; 1-based index into the item table [mall+0x1C]. Must be a Cash item (def+0x1F0 != 0) or 0xCFF..0xD04 (WS Gift Certificate 1000..50000 in the installed hii)
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x24]; FUN_00404750 item-def lookup; list record +0 of dialog 0x4B9; control 1 of 0x4B9 = item name (def+0)

fields.name: item_option
fields.meaning: option/grade index of the item
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x12]; list record +2 (as u16); option-name table 0x5486C0 index (row DAT_00525450[def+0x1CC], 5 names x 32 bytes) shown in control 9 of 0x4B9 when def+0x154 == 1 and the row is > 0, else 'No Option'

fields.name: price_gold
fields.meaning: asking price in gold
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x28]; sprintf('%I64u') into dialog 0x4B9 control 7. The accept button later parses this text back (_strtoi64) and compares it with gold (charinfo+0x230)

specs.semantics: Tells the receiving player that another player wants to sell them a SparkCash (cash) item, or a WS Gift Certificate, for gold. Handled in SubHandler4 (the cash-mall object, game_state+0x754): after the 4 reads, FUN_00404750 looks the item up; if the def is missing, or it is neither a cash item (def+0x1F0 != 0) nor an id in 0xCFF..0xD04, nothing else happens (bytes consumed, returns 1). Otherwise it selects dialog 0x4B9 and resets it (FUN_00490200), adds one 0x3C-byte list record {u16 item_id, u16 option} (FUN_0049e830(0x4B9,rec,1)), and fills controls: 1 = item name, 6 = seller name, 9 = option name or 'No Option', 2 = def+0x1FC formatted with thousands separators by FUN_00462d40 (+1000 when the option row applies; meaning of def+0x1FC not resolved), 7 = price. It writes the seller name into dialog 0x4BA control 1 and shows 0x4BA (FUN_00497c70(0x4BA,3,1)). Replies from the UI handler FUN_00465890: dialog 0x4B9 control 3 = accept. If gold (charinfo+0x230 u64) < the price text, the client shows 'You are short of gold.' and sends nothing. Otherwise it sends C2S 0x81 u8 0. Dialog 0x4B9 control 4, or dialog 0x4BA controls 4..5 = decline: C2S 0x81 u8 2.
specs.trigger: Server relays a seller's C2S 0x80 (built at FUN_00465890 dialog 0x4B8: u8 0x80, u16 item_id, u8 option, str[17] buyer_name, u64 price; price must be non-zero and the buyer cannot be yourself) to the named buyer.
specs.expected_response: C2S 0x81 u8 decision: 0 = accept (only if the buyer has enough gold), 2 = decline. The seller's own cancel from dialog 0x4B8 control 4 is C2S 0x81 u8 1. On success the server should send S2C 0xAA.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 gate: [mall+0x14] and [mall+0x18] must be non-NULL (set up after login), else the packet is ignored with no bytes consumed. SubHandler1..3 run first but do not claim 0xA9. An item that is not cash and not 0xCFF..0xD04 is silently dropped. seller_name should be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (it is copied with a C string copy). The price shown is re-parsed from the dialog text for the gold check, so send the real u64 price.

locations.role: item def lookup; gate def+0x1F0 != 0 or id in 0xCFF..0xD04
add {id, option} record to dialog 0x4B9 list
seller name -> dialog 0x4BA control 1; then FUN_00497c70(0x4BA,3,1) shows it
dialog 0x4B9 accept: gold check, C2S 0x81 u8 0

specs.references: PySlayer: server_packets/__init__.py only has a try/except import stub for opcode_0xA9 (no module). KR Hex-Rays doc: not in the main switch. Our server: not implemented. The 2008 client has no cash-item-for-gold trade.
open_questions: Meaning of item def +0x1FC (shown in control 2, +1000 when the option row applies).
What makes dialog 0x4B9 visible: the handler only shows 0x4BA. 0x4B9 is presumably opened from a 0x4BA button through the generic UI code. Not traced.
Whether the server also sends 0xAA to the seller (gold is absolute, so it would work for both parties).
specs.verification: Decomp of FUN_0046a2e0 case 0xA9 and its asm (0x46B3F0..0x46B5E0) read and matched field by field; the IAT slots 0x4C70EC/0x4C70F4/0x4C70F0/0x4C710C resolve to GetDataFromPacket char*/ushort/uchar/u64 (Fireway import names). Reply path confirmed in FUN_00465890 asm 0x468CF7..0x468DCD. 2008: no handler (compared with dispatch_2008_auto.json and 2008 SubHandler4 range).
specs.diff_vs_2008: new in 2009: the 2008 client has no handler for this opcode (dispatch_2008_auto.json has no entry; the 2008 primary switch ends at 0xA7 and 2008 SubHandler4 covers only 0x6A..0x9C).

fields.meaning: the receiver's new gold total (absolute, not a delta)
fields.dest_or_source: read straight into charinfo+0x230 ([mall+0x24]+0x230 = scene+0x278, the 2009 gold field; 2008 used +0x228); shown in window 9 control 0xB by FUN_0046f630

specs.semantics: Completes a cash-item-for-gold trade (see 0xA9). In SubHandler4 it first hides dialog 0x4B9 (FUN_00497c70(0x4B9,1,1)). It then reads the u64 directly into the gold field and redraws the inventory gold label (window 9 control 0xB, '%I64u'). Finally it shows the message box 'Trade is completed.\r\nEnter the SparkCash shop to verify.\r\nYou must exit and re-enter to refresh.' (string 0x529518 via FUN_0049ebc0). The cash-item lists are NOT updated. The text tells the player to re-enter the SparkCash shop, so the item appears there after the next cash-shop load.

specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 gate only ([mall+0x14] and [mall+0x18] non-NULL). No validation: the value overwrites local gold. Send the true total.

specs.name: PetEquip
specs.length: 6 (local player, or when a gate fails), 7 (remote, has_pet_info = 0) or 21 (remote, has_pet_info = 1)

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: owner entity uid (FUN_00419450 matches entity+0x88)

fields.name: pet_item_id
fields.meaning: pet item (item def type +0x154 == 6, Cash flag +0x1F0 != 0; installed hii: Picky 0x10C6, Ulie 0x10CB, ChikaPuka 0x10D0, GuriGuri 0x10D5)
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0xDC]; FUN_00427af0 writes it into the equip grid (kind 0xE, alternate grid) = entity+0x16E; the previous pet id is returned

fields.name: has_pet_info
fields.meaning: remote only: pet info follows. Also stored as the pet 'awake' flag pet_info+0xA

fields.name: pet_level
fields.meaning: remote only, if has_pet_info: pet level
fields.dest_or_source: pet_info (entity+0x1628, a 0x1C-byte block allocated here if NULL) +0xB

fields.name: pet_name
fields.meaning: remote only, if has_pet_info: pet name

specs.semantics: Puts a pet item into an entity's pet slot and spawns the pet sprite. It reads uid and pet_item_id, then gates: the entity must be found, and the item def must exist with Cash != 0 and Type == 6. On any failure the handler stops after 6 bytes. FUN_00427af0 then writes the id into the equip grid (kind 0xE, alternate grid, entity+0x16E) and returns the old pet id. FUN_004282c0 recomposes the sprite. LOCAL player (uid == scene+0x224): no more bytes are read. If the u8 at scene+0x3BB > 45 the handler stops. FUN_00425420(-1, bag scene+0x3E0/+0x43A, id) removes the item from the bag and must succeed, otherwise it stops. If an old pet was replaced, FUN_00425420(+1) returns it to the bag. FUN_00462b70(game+0x754, id) moves the cash record for the id from the cash bag list (+0x08) to the equipped list (+0x3C). If the record kind (+6) is 3 (pet), it sets local entity+0x1628 = that record, so for the local player pet_info IS the cash-item record: +0 serial, +4 item id, +8 u16 pet EXP, +0xA awake, +0xB level, +0xC HP %, +0xD name[13]. A replaced cash pet goes back through FUN_00462c00. Then the inventory (FUN_0046ef40) and the equipment window 7 (FUN_004423e0(game,1)) are refreshed. REMOTE: reads has_pet_info. If 0, only FUN_00447f40 runs (it does nothing unless entity+0x1628 already exists). If 1, it allocates pet_info if needed, reads level into +0xB and name into +0xD, and sets +0xA = 1. Both paths end in FUN_00447f40(game, entity, 0), which builds the pet as a 0x16B8-byte entity stored at entity+0x1638. The template is def+0x150 in the template list at game+0x504. The pet gets name = pet_info+0xD, position = the owner's +0x1298/+0x1328, state +0x9C = 4 (2 if not awake), +0x9D = level, and +0x9E = growth phase (1 if level < 5, 2 if 5..8, 3 if >= 9). It is added to the scene.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x82 u16 item_id (equip pet from bag, FUN_0044fe20 @0x44FFF9; refused client-side with 'Take off the equipment of your pet first.' while pet helm/wear slots entity+0x17E/+0x180 are occupied). Also broadcast to nearby players (remote form).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unknown uid, unknown item, non-cash item or Type != 6: the handler stops after 6 bytes, so do not append the remote tail in that case. The local form must NOT carry has_pet_info: the client reads nothing after pet_item_id when uid == its own uid. Local pet display needs the pet's cash record (kind 3) to exist in the cash-mall bag list before this packet arrives. Otherwise pet_info stays NULL and no pet appears, although the equip grid is still updated. The equip-grid write and sprite recompose happen BEFORE the local bag checks, so a failed bag removal leaves the pet shown as equipped without the bookkeeping.

locations.role: item def lookup; gates def+0x1F0 != 0 and def+0x154 == 6
equip into kind 0xE alternate slot (entity+0x16E), returns old pet id
local: remove pet item from bag (EAX=-1)
local: cash record bag->equipped, sets entity+0x1628 for kind-3 records

specs.references: PySlayer: import stub only. KR Hex-Rays doc has no 0xAB case in the main switch (KR numbering differs). The 2009 remote-appear handlers (0x04/0x07 and 0x05) read the same bool + u8 + str[13] pet tail. Our server: not implemented.
open_questions: Exact bag meaning of the u8 at scene+0x3BB (the <= 45 check that runs before the local bag removal).
Where the template index def+0x150 points (list at game+0x504, probably NPC/monster templates).
specs.verification: 2009 decomp (FUN_00451960 case 0xab) plus asm 0x4576FE..0x45799D, read field by field. The local/remote split is at 0x457811 (scene+0x224 == uid). FUN_00447f40, FUN_00462b70 and FUN_00427af0 were read to name the destinations. 2008: no handler; 2008 has no pet system (no 'pet' strings).
specs.diff_vs_2008: new in 2009: the 2008 client has no handler for this opcode (dispatch_2008_auto.json has no entry; the 2008 primary switch ends at 0xA7 and 2008 SubHandler4 covers only 0x6A..0x9C). The pet system is new in 2009.

specs.name: PetUnequip
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u16 pet_item_id

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: owner entity uid

fields.name: pet_item_id
fields.meaning: pet item to take off (def Type 6, Cash != 0)
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0xEC]; FUN_00427f00 removes it from the equip grid (option block zeroed)

specs.semantics: Removes a pet from an entity. The gates are the same as 0xAB (entity found, item def exists, Cash != 0, Type == 6), otherwise nothing happens. FUN_00427f00 clears the item from the grid and FUN_004282c0 recomposes the sprite. LOCAL: if the u8 at scene+0x3BB <= 45, FUN_00425420(+1) returns the item to the bag. FUN_00462c00(game+0x754, id) moves the cash record back to the cash bag list. Then the inventory is refreshed, entity+0x1628 = 0 (not freed; it points into the cash list), the equipment window is refreshed (FUN_004423e0(game,0)), the pet window 0x4CE is hidden, and FUN_00448330 releases the pet sprite (sprite +0x9C = 2, entity+0x1638 = 0, entity+0x127C = 0). REMOTE: pet_info+0xA = 0, then FUN_00448330.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x83 u16 item_id (FUN_00477000 @0x47737F, unequip a Type-6 item from the equipment window). Also broadcast to nearby players.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH HAZARD: on the remote path the client writes pet_info+0xA without a NULL check (0x457B3C). Sending 0xAC for a remote entity that never got pet info (0xAB with has_pet_info=1, 0xAD awake=1, or an appear packet with pet data) writes to address 0xA and crashes. The local path needs no pet_info.

specs.semantics: Puts a pet to sleep or wakes it up. LOCAL (uid == scene+0x224): stops if pet_info (entity+0x1628) is NULL. Otherwise pet_info+0xA = awake. If not awake, pet HP pet_info+0xC = 0. Then the equipment window is refreshed (FUN_004423e0(game,1)). REMOTE: if awake, allocates pet_info if needed and reads level and name. Then pet_info+0xA = awake. Both paths: if awake, FUN_00447f40 (re)builds the pet sprite and, if it exists, plays effect 0x14F at the pet position (FUN_0042cd90(game,0x14F,0,0,x,y,0,5,0)). If asleep, it plays effect 0x14F at the pet (when a sprite exists) and FUN_00448330 releases the sprite (entity+0x1638 = 0). Client strings: 'When pet fells asleep, feeding pet will wake it up. When you don't have food to feed, wait till pet's HP reaches 10%, Use Jingle Bell to wake it up.' and 'Pet has to have at least over 10% HP to wake up.'
specs.trigger: Server-driven. The pet falls asleep when its HP reaches 0. It wakes after feeding (C2S 0x85) or after the Pet Bell item: C2S 0x15 use-item with id 0x10B9, which the client allows only while pet_info+0xA == 0 and HP >= 10 (FUN_0044f070). Broadcast to nearby players.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH HAZARD: remote path with awake = 0 writes pet_info+0xA with no NULL check (0x457C29). Never send awake = 0 for a remote entity whose pet_info was never created. After awake = 0 the pet sprite pointer entity+0x1638 is NULL while pet_info stays. S2C 0xB0 (rename) then crashes, see 0xB0. The local form must not carry the level/name tail.

specs.semantics: Periodic status of the LOCAL player's pet (no uid). Gate: local entity scene+0x988 != NULL and its pet_info != NULL, otherwise nothing is read. It stores HP and EXP. If the pet is awake (+0xA) and HP <= 10, FUN_0046d640 auto-feeds: it looks for pet food 0x10BA, 0x10BB, 0x10BC, 0x10BD in that order (FUN_00464c10, cash list) and sends C2S 0x85 u16 food_id for the first one found (nothing if none). Then FUN_00447e10 plays pet emote 1 (hungry). It always redraws the pet HP ('%u%%' in window 7 control 0x1D and gauge 0x1C, FUN_00442670). If the pet window 0x4CE is open (state 3), FUN_00442710 redraws it (EXP gauge control 7, '%u%%' control 8, 'Level %d' control 0xB).
specs.trigger: Server tick or status change of the local pet (HP decay, EXP gain).
specs.expected_response: C2S 0x85 u16 food_item_id when HP <= 10 while awake and the player owns pet food (answered by S2C 0xB1).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Every 0xAE with HP <= 10 while awake triggers another C2S 0x85 as long as food is owned. The server should feed, or stop sending low-HP updates, to avoid a loop. Do not send it while the local player has no pet_info: the packet is then ignored without consuming bytes, which is harmless because each packet is framed separately.

specs.semantics: Sets a pet's level. The entity and its pet_info must exist, otherwise it stops after 4 bytes. It stores the level. For the local player with pet window 0x4CE open, the window is refreshed. If a pet sprite exists: sprite +0x9D = level and +0x9E = phase (1 if < 5, 2 if 5..8, 3 if >= 9). A new phase selects the grown sprite set. It plays effect 0x24 on the pet (FUN_0042cd90(game,0x24,sprite+0x88 uid,0,0,0,1,9,0)) and emote 5 (grow up) when the level is 5 or 9, else emote 4.
specs.trigger: Server, when a pet's EXP crosses a level threshold. Broadcast to the owner and nearby players.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: Level gates client features: '/Pet warning' needs >= 5 and '/Pet trick' needs >= 9 (see 0xB2). Levels 5 and 9 change the growth phase.

specs.semantics: Renames a pet on the owner and in the world. After the lookup there is a redundant check that entity+0x88 == uid, then a check that pet_info != NULL. It reads 13 bytes into pet_info+0xD and copies them (C string copy) into the pet sprite at *(entity+0x1638).

specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH HAZARD: the copy into *(entity+0x1638) has no NULL check (0x45D49F). If the owner has pet_info but no pet sprite, the client writes to address 0 and crashes. That is the case while the pet is asleep (after 0xAD awake=0 or 0xAC) and before FUN_00447f40 has built the sprite. Send only while the pet is awake and shown. The name must be NUL-terminated within 13 bytes, otherwise the copy runs past pet_info+0x1A.

specs.semantics: Guild and Guild Battle multiplexer, handled by SubHandler3 on the messenger/guild object M = *(game_state+0x508). M+0x124 = game_state, +0x128 = charinfo, +0x12C = UI root, +0x130 = socket. Guild state in M: +0x44 u16 guild_id (0 none, 1 means Game Master on the nameplate, 0xFFFF load failure; the client treats < 2 as 'not in a guild'), +0x46 name[17], +0x57 u8 level (FUN_00484ef0 from points with the cumulative table 0x5250B8, 1..5), +0x58 u16 max members, +0x5A u16 member count, +0x5C u32 guild points, +0x60/+0x64 master id/name, +0x78 member list (0x20-byte records: +0 online, +4 id, +8 name[17], +0x19 level, +0x1A job1, +0x1B job2, +0x1C grade with 5 = master), +0x88 notice[61], +0xC6/+0xC8 emblem, +0xCA/+0xCC/+0xCE battle wins/losses/draws, +0xE0 notice/application list (str[130] each). The nameplate fields on the local entity (scene+0x988) are +0x12 guild id, +0x16A1 guild name, +0x16B2 emblem (sprite 0x148, drawn on top) and +0x16B4 emblem (sprite 0x149, drawn first). The guild window is 0x4B3 (FUN_004847b0: '(%u/%u)' members, '%uRound %uWin %uLose %uDraw', '%s   Lv.%u'). Guild Battle windows are 0x4D0, 0x4D1, 0x4D2, 0x4D3, 0x4D6, 0x4D8 and 0x4D9. Message boxes use FUN_0049ebc0 and chat lines use FUN_00495e30/FUN_00447bb0 (color 0xFFFFC800). Sub-codes: 1 create result (every failure also clears M through FUN_0047a8c0): 1 = registered (M+0x44 = guild_id, M+0x64 = own name, local +0x12 = guild_id, gold -= 50,000 locally, 'Guild has been registered.', hide 0x4B3). 2 = 'You can't use this guild name...', 4 = 'Wind master can't register as guild.', 5 = 'Already in the other guild.', 7/8/9 = prerequisite failure (the text is built but the box shows the 'Wind master' string, a client bug), other = 'Fail to register the guild...'. 2 apply result: 1 'You have applied for this guild.', 6 'This guild can't recruit any more members.', 0x11 'Guild admission is being delayed.', 0x10 = one str[130] appended to M+0xE0 and HUD window 3 child #7 (+0x18 = 0) flagged. 3 full guild info: all fields into M, member list rebuilt, then chat '[Guild Master]:%s' (the notice) or '[Guild Master]:Hello. Welcome to %s guild.' when the notice is empty, and the local nameplate fields are set. 4 notice list: count x str[130] appended to M+0xE0, same HUD flag. 5 admission: 1 'Guild admission has completed.', 5 'Already in the other guild.', else 'This guild can't recruit any more members.'. 6 leave: 0 'Procedure failed...', 0xC 'You can leave the guild after 1 day.', else left (hide 0x4B3, clear local +0x12/+0x16B2/+0x16B4, chat 'You are out of this guild.'). 7 notice change: 0 'Fail to change the notice.' (clears M+0x88), 1 'Notice has been changed.'. 8 delete: 0xA 'To do this, you have to kick someone in your guild.', 0xB 'You can delete your guild after 7 days...', 1 deleted (clears all local nameplate fields, 'Your guild has been deleted.'). 9 max-member increase: ok != 0 -> gold -= cost locally, 'Max No. of guild has been increased.'; 0 -> 'Fail to increase the No. of guild member...'. 10 max members = u16 (window refresh). 11 master change: 1 'Guild master has been changed.', 8 'This member can't be the guild master.', else 'Fail to change guild master.'. 12 new master by name (FUN_00485200 swaps the master record, hides 0x4B3). 13 member joined (record appended, member count +1). 14 member removed by name (FUN_004852c0, refresh). 15 guild info failure: result 1 -> local +0x12 = 0xFFFF and 'Failed to get guild info. Please, log in again.'; any other -> local +0x12 = 0 (not in a guild). 16 grade change: 1 'The grade of this member has been changed.', 0xD 'You can only set 4 Guardians.', 0xE 'You can set 10 Vanguards.', else 'Procedure failed...'; always resets 0x4B3 controls 0x22..0x31 to state 3. 17 member grade = u8 (found by name). 18 kick: 0 'Procedure failed...', else 'Kicked that guild member.'. 19 no payload: the client immediately sends C2S 0x8A (FUN_00484550) to re-request guild info. 20 member logged in (member +0 = u8, chat '[%s] has logged in.'). 21 member logged out (member +0 = 0, points delta = new - M+0x5C, M+0x5C = new, level recomputed, chat '[%s] has logged out.' and 'Guild point(+%u : [%s]) increased.'). 22 member renamed (old name -> new name; also the master name if grade 5; ignored unless M+0x44 > 1). 23 Guild Battle registration: hides message box 0x16. 3 shows '[Guild Battle] can be played after class change.' AND continues as success. 2 'You can't use play room, battlefield, or arena due to your low manner point.'. 0 'Fail to register the Guild Battle...'. Other non-zero values are success: local entity +0xE9 = 7, +0xEC = s23_value, windows 0x4D0 and 0x4D2 shown with the roster. 24 Guild Battle invitation (needs M+0x44 > 1): shows 0x4D8 with the guild name and stores the id/value. 25 Guild Battle member result: if 0x4D0 is open, s25_reason 0xF0 adds s25_name to the roster; 2/3/4/6/7/8 show '%s can't ...' texts (low manner pts, before class change, Flea Market, cash shop, other Guild Battle, party); other values show '...using other service...'. If 0x4D0 is closed and 0x4D1 is open, the name is added to 0x4D1. 26 roster list: ok == 0 -> 'You can't play Guild Battle due to lack of empty place.'; else shows 0x4D1 and reads s26_last_index + 1 (id, name) pairs. 27: s27_value == 0 -> the same 'lack of empty place' box. 28/29 room list (28 first hides 0x4D0/0x4D2, clears the 0x4D9 list and sets a 0x4D0 value to 1, then falls through to 29): count x 0x24-byte records {u16, str[17] at +2, str[17] at +0x13} into 0x4D9, label '%u (%u %s)' = (list size, s29_value, 'In progress'), then Sleep(500) and 0x4D9 is shown. 30/31 (31 first, if 0x4D9 is open, shows 'One member left. Regroup the team.', clears 0x4D9 and falls through to 30): kind 2 hides all Guild Battle windows with 'Guild Battle registration has been stopped.'; otherwise removes the roster entry whose id == s30_member_id (0 unless kind 1) and updates '(%u/%u)'. 32 room list delta on 0x4D9: kind 1 adds a record (id, name_a at +2, name_b at +0x13; note the wire order is name_b first); other kinds remove records with id == s32_room_id or s32_room_id2. 33 challenge: if 0x4D6 is closed, 0x4D9 is open and FUN_00497b80(0x4D0) != 0, shows 0x4D6 with '[%d] %s'. 34 result 1 'You are either already on the Battle or not registered.', 2 'Same guild can't play Guild Battle.'. 35 battle record +1: 1 wins, 2 losses, 3 draws. 37 entity(uid)+0x12 = 1 (that player's nameplate becomes 'Game Master'). 185 (0xB9) item-use confirmation: flag 1 and item 0x10B8 -> the client sends C2S 0x15 u16 0x10B8 (use Guild Billboard); flag 1 with another item -> nothing; flag != 1 -> 'Guild master can only do this.'. Sub-codes 36, 38..184 and 186..255 read nothing more (return 1).
specs.trigger: Replies to the guild C2S family built by FUN_00480430 / FUN_004842xx / FUN_004845xx / FUN_004852xx (opcodes 0x87..0x98). Confirmed pairs: C2S 0x87 (create: str[17] name, ..., u16 M+0xC6, u16 M+0xC8) -> sub 1; C2S 0x8A (opcode only; sent automatically at the end of every S2C 0x03 world-info handler and after sub 19) -> sub 3 when in a guild, sub 15 with result != 1 when not; C2S 0x8F (str[61] notice) -> sub 7. Other sub-codes are server pushes (member login/logout 20/21, join 13, remove 14, notices 4) or Guild Battle flow (23..35).
specs.expected_response: Only sub 19 (client sends C2S 0x8A) and sub 185 with item 0x10B8 (client sends C2S 0x15 u16 0x10B8). All other sub-codes: none.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 gate: M+0x124 and M+0x12C non-NULL, otherwise the packet falls through to SubHandler4/5 unhandled. The guild id must be >= 2: 0 = none, 1 turns the nameplate into 'Game Master' (FUN_0043c300), 0xFFFF = load failure. Sub 1 success and sub 9 subtract gold locally (50,000 fixed / s9_cost), so the server must deduct the same. Sub 26 STACK HAZARD: s26_last_index + 1 names are written to [esp+0x68+17*i] with the stack cookie at [esp+0x220], so keep s26_last_index <= 24. At 25 or more the cookie is overwritten and the process is terminated. Sub 28/29 call Sleep(500) inside the network handler, which freezes the client for 0.5 s per packet. Sub 19 makes the client send C2S 0x8A; do not answer 0x8A with sub 19 (endless loop). Sub 3 appends to the member list without clearing it (the reset FUN_0047a8c0 runs from the S2C 0x03 world-info handler via FUN_0047a1a0, and on sub 1 failures and subs 6/8). A second sub 3 without an intervening 0x03 duplicates every member. Sub 13 and sub 3 member records use DIFFERENT field orders. Sub 32 kind 1 sends name_b (stored at +0x13) before name_a (+2). Strings are copied with C string copies: keep names NUL-terminated within 17 bytes and the notice within 61. Sub 23 result 3 shows an error AND proceeds as success (client quirk). Sub 1 results 7/8/9 show the wrong text (client bug).

specs.grammar: u32 uid

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Entity uid (matched against entity+0x88, the 2009 uid slot; 2008 used +0x84). Unknown uid => nothing else happens.

specs.semantics: Removes the guild tag from one visible character. After the entity lookup (FUN_00419450 walks the scene entity list [scene+0xC] and matches entity+0x88) it zeroes: entity+0x12 (u16 guild id), the first DWORD of entity+0x16A1 (char[17] guild name, so the name becomes an empty string; the other 13 bytes are left as they were), entity+0x16B2 and entity+0x16B4 (u16 emblem frame indices). Nothing is redrawn explicitly; the nameplate renderer FUN_0043c300 reads these fields every frame: guild id 1 draws a green "Game Master" label, guild id > 1 draws the yellow guild name (entity+0x16A1) plus emblem sprites 0x149 (frame +0x16B4) and 0x148 (frame +0x16B2), 0 draws nothing. Sibling opcodes: 0xB4 (u32 uid, u16 guild_id, str[17] guild_name, u16, u16) SETS the same four fields; 0xB6 (u32 uid) clears id and emblem but leaves the name bytes untouched. Visually 0xB6 and 0xB7 are identical because the name is only drawn when guild id > 1.
specs.trigger: Server broadcast when a character stops being a guild member (leave, kick or guild disband are the likely cases). Which 2009 guild C2S request leads to 0xB7 rather than 0xB6 was not traced; the guild C2S family is 0x87-0x92 (e.g. 0x8A and 0x8C have no body).
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate. Unknown uid (or uid 0) => only the 4 bytes are consumed. Safe to send for any entity; for the local player it does NOT clear the messenger-side guild state (messenger+0x44 guild id, +0x46 name), which the guild windows use, so a full guild leave also needs the guild (0xB3 sub-opcode) packets.

Meaning of the two emblem u16s (+0x16B2 sprite set 0x148, +0x16B4 sprite set 0x149); probably emblem symbol and emblem background chosen at guild creation (C2S 0x87 sends messenger+0xC6/+0xC8).

fields.meaning: Name of the placing character (C2S 0x88 sends messenger+0x64, which the guild-registration result fills from the local character name). Stored, not drawn.

fields.name: board_item_id
fields.meaning: Item used to place the board: 0x10B8 (4280, guild ad board, 1 h) -> sprite 0x145, 0x10B7 (4279, premium guild ad board, 24 h) -> sprite 0x146. Any other value leaves sprite index 0.

fields.name: guild_id
fields.meaning: Advertised guild id. Key for 0xB8 removal and the value sent in C2S 0x89 (join request, only if > 1).

fields.name: guild_name
fields.meaning: Guild name, drawn in green under the board.

fields.name: emblem_symbol
fields.meaning: Guild emblem frame drawn with sprite set 0x148 (same role as entity+0x16B2). C2S 0x88 sends messenger+0xC6.

fields.name: emblem_bg
fields.meaning: Guild emblem frame drawn with sprite set 0x149 (same role as entity+0x16B4). C2S 0x88 sends messenger+0xC8.

fields.name: ad_text
fields.meaning: Advertisement text typed in dialog 0x4B7, drawn in white.

fields.meaning: World X of the board (C2S 0x88 sends the local player entity+0x1298).

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: World Y of the board (C2S 0x88 sends the local player entity+0x1328).

specs.semantics: Adds ONE guild advertisement board to the Guild Plaza. Board record (0x70 bytes, zeroed, operator new): +0x00 u32 master_char_id, +0x04 char[17] master_name, +0x15 char[25] ad_text, +0x2E char[17] guild_name, +0x40 u16 guild_id, +0x42 u16 board_item_id, +0x44 u16 emblem_symbol, +0x46 u16 emblem_bg, +0x48 u32 sprite index (client-derived: 0x145 if board_item_id == 0x10B8 (4280), 0x146 if 0x10B7 (4279), otherwise left 0), +0x50 f64 pos_x, +0x58 f64 pos_y. The record is appended to the list messenger+0x114 (FUN_0045f3f0). Rendering (FUN_004330c0, called every frame): only when scene+0xF18 == 6 (in world) and the current map code [[game_state+0x4FC]+0x1C4] == 0x25E6 (9702, the Guild Plaza), each record draws sprite +0x48 at (pos_x, pos_y) minus the camera, ad_text in white, guild_name in green, and the guild emblem (sprite set 0x149 frame +0x46, then sprite set 0x148 frame +0x44, the same sets the nameplate uses for entity+0x16B4/+0x16B2). Clicking near a board (FUN_00450130, mouse-up within sqrt(3000) ~ 55 px of the board anchor or inside a small box above it) stores the record in messenger+0x190 and opens dialog 0x4B6; confirming it sends C2S 0x89 + u16 board.guild_id (send 0x482DCD) = request to join that guild, allowed only when the player has no guild (messenger+0x44 < 2) and is not a Game Master (entity+0x12 == 1 shows "Wind master can't register as guild."). The wire order is exactly the body of C2S 0x88 (place board), so the server can relay that body unchanged.
specs.trigger: Broadcast after a guild master places a board: using item 0x10B8 or 0x10B7 in map 0x25E6 opens dialog 0x4B7 (text entry, CheckString filter), which sends C2S 0x88 = u32 messenger+0x60, str[17] messenger+0x64, u16 item_id, u16 messenger+0x44 (guild id), str[17] messenger+0x46 (guild name), u16 +0xC6, u16 +0xC8, str[25] text, f64 x, f64 y (send 0x482C4D). 0xBA mirrors that layout field for field.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate; the record is kept even outside the plaza and survives map changes (the list is only cleared by 0xBB and by the messenger reset FUN_0047a1a0 run from the S2C 0x03 handler). No duplicate check: sending the same board twice draws it twice. Use only item ids 0x10B7/0x10B8, otherwise sprite index 0 is drawn. NOTE the field order differs from 0xBB (here board_item_id comes before guild_id, in 0xBB it comes after ad_text).
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 0xBA: identical read order (u32, str17 @4, u16 @66 item, u16 @64 guild, str17 @46, u16 @68, u16 @70, str25 @21, two doubles @80/@88), item 4280/4279 -> sprite 154/155 in KR. Item ids from the KR item table (_items_4001_4400.json): 4279 "premium guild ad board, 24 h, guild master only, usable in the guild plaza", 4280 "guild ad board, 1 h". Not implemented in our server.
open_questions: master_char_id/master_name: meaning inferred from the C2S 0x88 sources messenger+0x60/+0x64 (+0x64 is filled with the local character name on guild creation); the client never reads them back.
Map 0x25E6 (9702) is assumed to be the Guild Plaza from the item text; the map file name was not resolved.
specs.verification: decomp FUN_00451960 case + annotated asm of the 2009 handler; every read typed from the Fireway IAT slot it calls (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 uchar, 0x4C70F4 ushort, 0x4C70F8 double, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7108 uint) and its destination taken from the pushed address with stack-push adjustment. 2008 OnReceive 0x44D5D0 has no case for this opcode (dispatch_2008_auto.json has no entry); related 2008 handlers read for comparison as noted in diff_vs_2008. Read order/destinations from asm 0x45DAE4..0x45DBB9; renderer FUN_004330c0 and click path FUN_00450130 read to name the fields; C2S 0x88 builder in FUN_00480430 (case 0x4B7) compared field by field.

specs.semantics: Replaces the whole blacklist. FUN_0047a850 frees every node of messenger+0x34, then count records (u32 id FIRST, then the name, the reverse of the friend-list order) are appended with FUN_0045f3f0, and FUN_0047b3e0 redraws window 0x176. The blacklist is a new 2009 messenger list at messenger+0x34 (head +0x38, tail +0x3C, count +0x40; messenger = [game_state+0x508]). Each node is a 0x24-byte record from operator new (NOT zeroed): +0x00 char[17] name, +0x18 u32 char_id. The messenger window 0x176 shows it on a new tab (control 0x1D, 2008 had only the friend 0x15 and mentor 0x1A tabs): FUN_0047b3e0 lists the names and prints "(%u/10)" with the count. The client caps it at 10: C2S 0x93 (add, FUN_0047afb0) refuses at 10 ("Can't be add. Visit Frenaiga."), for the own name, for a mentor ("You can't add mentor to the blacklist.") and for a friend ("You can't add your friend to the blacklist."). Blacklisted names are also checked by friend add and mentor register ("Blacklist user can't be registered.", FUN_0047ad60/FUN_0047aef0) and by the chat invite / chat UI code ("Blacklisted user can't use this.", FUN_0047b130/FUN_004462e0).

specs.name: InstanceDungeonRoomListAppend
specs.grammar:
u8 total_rooms
u8 room_count
repeat(room_count) {
  str[17] room_name
  u16 room_no
  u8 max_players
  u8 cur_players
  u8 room_level
  u8 room_type
  u16 npc_index
  bool has_password
}

fields.name: total_rooms
fields.meaning: Denominator of the "%u/%u" label (control 0x0E of window 0x4C4); the numerator is counted by the client (rows whose room_level <= own level).

fields.name: room_count
fields.meaning: Number of room records that follow.

fields.name: room_name
fields.meaning: Room title.

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: Room number, printed as %03d; the join path copies it to scene+0xF64.

fields.name: max_players
fields.meaning: Capacity, second number of "(%02d/%02d)".

fields.name: cur_players
fields.meaning: Current players, first number of "(%02d/%02d)".

fields.name: room_level
fields.meaning: Minimum level. Printed as "Lv.%d" for type 5; rows above the local level (entity+0x9D) are added disabled, and clicking them shows "You need higher level".

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: Room type; 5 = instance-dungeon room (formats "%03d %s(%02d/%02d) Lv.%d", enables the npc_index lookup). The join path copies it to scene+0xF90.

fields.name: npc_index
fields.meaning: NEW vs the 2008 room record. 1-based index into the CNPCControl list [game_state+0x504]+0x10 (count +0x18); for type 5 the NPC record pointer is stored at row+0x50 (and CNPCControl+0x1C). Probably the dungeon NPC/definition.

fields.name: has_password
fields.meaning: Password room: joining opens password window 0x4A instead of joining directly.

specs.semantics: Appends rooms to the instance-dungeon room list without clearing it. Room rows for the instance-dungeon room list window 0x4C4 (new in 2009). Per row: operator new(0x54) zeroed, fields read as in the grammar, FUN_004455f0 formats the display text at row+0x11 ("%03d %s(%02d/%02d) Lv.%d" for type 5: room_no, name, cur, max, level; types 1-4 use the 2008 arena formats) and sets flags row+0x48/+0x4C from the type, then FUN_0049e830(0x4C4, row, enabled) adds the row with enabled = (local level entity+0x9D >= room_level). After the loop FUN_00445750(game_state, 5, total_rooms) writes "%u/%u" = enterable rows / total_rooms into control 0x0E and refreshes the window. Window 0x4C4 buttons: 8 = join by number (scene+0xF90=5, prompt "Please enter the number of the Dungeon room number to join."), 9..13 = the visible rows (level check, then scene+0xF64=room_no, scene+0xF90=room_type, password window 0x4A if has_password, else the normal room-join request). Opening window 0x4C4 sends C2S 0x2C + u8 5 (FUN_004455b0(5)); closing it sends 0x2C + u8 0.
specs.trigger: Server-pushed while window 0x4C4 is open (after C2S 0x2C with list type 5), for rooms beyond the first batch or newly created dungeon rooms. 0xC2 starts a fresh list.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate. No duplicate check (the same room twice gives two rows). Unlike 2009 S2C 0x31 (which reads npc_index only when room_type == 5), npc_index is ALWAYS on the wire here. total_rooms is re-applied to the label on every packet. If window 0x4C4 does not exist FUN_0049e830 adds to whatever dialog ui+0x5F0 points at (same pattern as 2008 lists); send only while the list is open.

locations.role: handler block (0xC2 falls through to here)
format row text / npc_index lookup for type 5
window 0x4C4 buttons: join by number / row click (level check "You need higher level")
C2S 0x2C + u8 list type (5 on open of 0x4C4, 0 on close)

specs.references: PySlayer README lists 0xC1/0xC2/0xC3 in the KR main TCP handler (same as EN 2009); PySlayer names C2S/S2C 0x34 "arena, instance-dungeon entry". 2008 analogue: 0x32 ArenaRoomListAppend. Not implemented in our server.
open_questions: What the NPC record at row+0x50 is used for (not traced beyond the lookup).
Exact join request sent from a dungeon row (LAB_0044b92b, presumably the 2008 room-join C2S 0x1B family) was not re-derived here.
specs.verification: decomp FUN_00451960 case + annotated asm of the 2009 handler; every read typed from the Fireway IAT slot it calls (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 uchar, 0x4C70F4 ushort, 0x4C70F8 double, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7108 uint) and its destination taken from the pushed address with stack-push adjustment. 2008 OnReceive 0x44D5D0 has no case for this opcode (dispatch_2008_auto.json has no entry); related 2008 handlers read for comparison as noted in diff_vs_2008. Row format read from FUN_004455f0 asm (sprintf argument order), window buttons from FUN_00448730 asm 0x44D9C9..0x44DAB3; compared with 2008 0x32/0x33 and 2009 0x31.
specs.diff_vs_2008: new opcode in 2009. Row layout = 2008 0x32/0x33 arena room record (str[17] name, u16 room_no, u8 max, u8 cur, u8 level, u8 type, bool password) PLUS a u16 npc_index inserted before has_password, and a leading u8 total_rooms before the count. Rows go to window 0x4C4 instead of the arena list 0x2A.

specs.name: RoomTeamUpdateBatch

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number of player records.

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Player uid (entity+0x88). Unknown uid: record consumed, ignored.

fields.name: team
fields.meaning: Current team (0 = spectator, 1/2 = the two teams). Written to entity+0x158B by FUN_00448350 only if it differs from the stored value AND the current map type [[game_state+0x4FC]+0x7C] == 1.

fields.name: next_team
fields.meaning: Team for the next round; stored raw.

specs.semantics: Batch form of S2C 0x35 (single-player team update). For each record: entity lookup by uid; if entity+0x158B != team, FUN_00448350(team, game_state, entity) runs (on a map of type 1: stores the team in +0x158B and, when the player has an active pet and team is 1 or 2, creates/updates the pet entity) and then FUN_0042a150: team 0 -> entity+0x9C = 1 (spectator); team != 0 -> if +0x9C was not 3, HP +0xA0 = max +0x11AC, MP +0xA4 = max +0x11B0, +0x1658 = 0 and the buff tables +0xF24 (0x1F8 bytes) and +0x111C (0x90 bytes) are zeroed; then +0x9C = 3. next_team is always written to +0x158C. After the loop FUN_00444220 rebuilds the room member window 0x47E (and may post the "System will balance number of each team members next round." / "The latest blue|red team member has moved..." notices) and FUN_00443bc0 refreshes the "You are in blue|red team..." status text.
specs.trigger: Server-pushed inside a room game (arena / play room / dungeon room) when several players' teams change at once, e.g. at a round start or auto-balance. No C2S request is tied to it.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate; all bytes are always read, so unknown uids are safe. Outside a type-1 map the team byte is NOT stored (FUN_00448350 does nothing) but FUN_0042a150 still runs on the old value. Compared with 0x35 this opcode does NOT turn next_team == 3 into the leave flag (0x35 sets entity+0x1589 = 1 and stores 0), does not update the spectator camera target scene+0xF00, and does not recount the per-team alive counters scene+0xF93/+0xF94. HP/MP refill and buff wipe happen only when the team actually changes.

locations.role: store team (+0x158B) on type-1 maps, pet handling
spectator/participant state, HP/MP refill, buff wipe

specs.references: 2008 analogue: 0x35 ArenaPlayerTeamUpdate (team +0x14EB, next_team +0x14EC; +0x98 state). PySlayer README lists 0xC3 in the KR main handler. Not implemented in our server.
open_questions: Which room modes the original server used 0xC3 for (guild battle / dungeon party start are plausible; not traced).
Meaning of map-object +0x7C == 1 (assumed: PvP/room map type, like 2008 map +0x70).
specs.verification: decomp FUN_00451960 case + annotated asm of the 2009 handler; every read typed from the Fireway IAT slot it calls (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 uchar, 0x4C70F4 ushort, 0x4C70F8 double, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7108 uint) and its destination taken from the pushed address with stack-push adjustment. 2008 OnReceive 0x44D5D0 has no case for this opcode (dispatch_2008_auto.json has no entry); related 2008 handlers read for comparison as noted in diff_vs_2008. Compared line by line with the 2009 0x35 handler (decomp case 0x35) and the 2008 0x35 spec; FUN_00448350 and FUN_0042a150 read.
specs.diff_vs_2008: new opcode in 2009: a multi-record version of 0x35 without the next_team==3 leave handling and without the camera/alive-count updates; entity offsets shifted (+0x98 -> +0x9C, team +0x14EB -> +0x158B).

specs.name: CashItemQuantityPurchaseResult

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = success; 0x0E = "You are short of cash."; any other = "You failed to buy the item.\r\n\r\nPlease try again in a few minutes." (message box 0x16).

fields.name: cash_balance
fields.meaning: New cash balance (label control 0x5F).

fields.name: mileage_balance
fields.meaning: New mileage balance (label control 0x60).

fields.name: serial
fields.meaning: Serial of the existing cash-box record to update.

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item id of that record (must also match record+0x04).

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: New quantity, zero-extended into the record's u16 quantity (+0x08). It replaces the value; it is not added.

specs.semantics: Result of buying more units of an item that already sits in the cash item box. On success the two balances are stored, the box vector mall+0x28 is scanned (FUN_0045f2e0 size / FUN_0045f2c0 at) for the first record with serial AND item_id matching, and its u16 quantity is set to the u8 value. Then (also when no record matched) FUN_00460910 rebuilds the box window 0x1FC, FUN_00462100 redraws both balance labels, and mall+0x5C0 = 1. Failures only rewrite message box 0x16.
specs.trigger: Likely reply to C2S 0x4E = u8 0x4E + bool use_mileage + u16 item_id + u8 buy_count + u32 serial (item-mall dialog 0x4DA, send 0x468706), which is sent for a selected box record; the matching (serial, item_id) pair and the "short of cash" code fit that request. Inferred, not live-tested.
specs.expected_response: none
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 gate. Quantity is a u8 on the wire (max 255) although the record holds a u16. No record matched => balances still update and the window is rebuilt. Success does not close message box 0x16 itself.

locations.role: scan box vector mall+0x28 for serial+item_id
other failure: "You failed to buy the item..."

specs.references: 2008 analogues: 0x70 CashMileageBalance (same two balances, mall+0x588/+0x58C) and 0x79 CashBoxItemAdd (28-byte box record: serial +0, item_id +4, limit_type +6, quantity +8). PySlayer README lists 0xC4 under Packet_handler_4. Not implemented in our server.

Purpose of the new flag mall+0x5C0.

Stack slots for serial/item_id/quantity recomputed from the pushes in asm 0x46B7B8..0x46B7EE and matched to the compares at 0x46B819/0x46B821.

specs.grammar: bytes[128] xtrap_challenge

fields.name: xtrap_challenge
fields.meaning: Opaque X-Trap server challenge, passed to X-Trap Step2 (FUN_0049f480 -> FUN_0049f630 -> FUN_0049f650, flags 0x13).

specs.semantics: X-Trap anti-cheat round trip. The 128 bytes are handed to FUN_0049f480(challenge, response_buf, 0x13) (the X-Trap client "Step2" entry that the live patch stubs). The client then ALWAYS sends C2S 0x9E + char[128] response (Add(uchar) 0x45DDD4, Add(char*,0x80) 0x45DDED, Send 0x45DDFB) and, if the Step2 call returned non-zero, closes the game socket (CSNSocket::Close at 0x45DE0F).
specs.trigger: Server-initiated at any time (X-Trap periodic check). No C2S request.
specs.expected_response: C2S 0x9E: u8 0x9E + 128 bytes response (from stack buffer [esp+0x1298], which is not initialised by this handler).
specs.gates_and_hazards: DO NOT SEND to the patched 2009 client. The live patch replaces the first byte of FUN_0049f480 with RET (C3), so EAX keeps its value from before the call, which is the address of the challenge buffer (LEA EAX at 0x45DDB7) and therefore non-zero. The client will reply 0x9E with 128 bytes of uninitialised stack and then close its own game connection. The server never needs to send this opcode.

locations.role: X-Trap Step2 (stubbed with RET in WindSlayer_patched.exe)
Close game socket when Step2 returned non-zero

open_questions: X-Trap buffer semantics (128-byte challenge/response) are vendor-defined; not reversed.
specs.verification: decomp FUN_00451960 case + annotated asm of the 2009 handler; every read typed from the Fireway IAT slot it calls (0x4C70EC char*+len, 0x4C70F0 uchar, 0x4C70F4 ushort, 0x4C70F8 double, 0x4C70FC bool, 0x4C7108 uint) and its destination taken from the pushed address with stack-push adjustment. 2008 OnReceive 0x44D5D0 has no case for this opcode (dispatch_2008_auto.json has no entry); related 2008 handlers read for comparison as noted in diff_vs_2008. Stub bytes of the patched exe read from the file; return-value path followed in asm 0x45DDAD..0x45DE0F.
